meta.title: Zambia Government Operating Model
meta.baseline: Government Scope Reference Model - International Baseline (14 domains, 91 SAs, 501 concepts)
meta.note: Built from the international baseline + Zambia mapping, per the answered decision register (artifact 48KKXwXqNYgkmwNDGdXg7i). The 8 grade-A entities had their source links and Act names independently opened and confirmed on 28 Oct 2026 (7 Acts verified; the pensions entry corrected to the Public Service Pensions Fund). The 5 grade-C and 3 external entities are NOT primary-verified, and whole-of-government reconciliation (Yellow Book, PACRA, cabinet gazette, Constitution, local-authority and traditional registers) remains in the validation backlog. Every entity carries its evidence grade. v1.1.0 adds the two source figures and the Zambia-structure-to-generic mapping. v1.3.0 adds the Master & Reference Data / ownership-stewardship overlay: the governance metamodel, 8 accountability roles, 9 foundational + 14 sector master-data domains, an 18-row ownership-allocation matrix, reference-data classes, the governance-artifact chain, RACI decision rights, the national registers, the data-contract spec, and the gaps/roadmap.

resolution_rules: Official statistics stewardship sits in Domain 1 (not Education/Research or Domain 14); technology platforms for statistics stay in Domain 14.
A regulator is placed in its regulated-sector domain; licensing, inspection and enforcement are mapped as capabilities, not Subject Areas.
A public enterprise uses its operating sector as primary placement; state ownership and fiscal-risk relationships are recorded separately against Domain 5.
Smart Zambia Institute is placed in Domain 14, even though its services support every domain.
The data-protection body is placed in Domain 1 (public oversight); privacy controls and incidents cross-reference Domain 14.
Traditional governance is not subsumed under local government without explicit constitutional or statutory evidence.
A ministry can change name or portfolio while its Domains and Subject Areas remain stable (entity vs mandate).

metamodel_constructs.definition: Durable jurisdiction-neutral sphere of governmental responsibility; not an organization.
Cohesive, domain-specific information grouping with a semantic boundary and stewardship home.
Stable noun or phenomenon about which government records facts.
Governance classification grouping reusable master entities around a stable subject (e.g. Person or Land). References concepts from several Subject Areas but does not replace them.
Identifiable, reusable entity with lifecycle, identifiers, attributes, relationships and cross-process reuse.
Context in which an entity participates (Taxpayer, Employer, Patient, Supplier). A role should not automatically become a separate master domain.
Controlled codes, classifications, permissible values, hierarchies or mappings used to classify, constrain or interpret data.
Legally or administratively recognized source for a defined entity, attribute, status or code set.
Operational system designated to preserve authoritative records for a specified scope. One system need not be authoritative for every attribute.
Trusted, possibly composite representation from identity resolution, source precedence and provenance; not automatically the legal record.
Institution or executive accountable for meaning, lawful purpose, quality expectations, release and authoritative-source decisions.
Function legally empowered to establish the entity, identity, status, registration, license or controlled value.
Maintains definitions, values, rules, data quality, exceptions, mappings and lifecycle changes.
Accountable for the business operation of the designated System of Record.
Operates storage, access, security, backup, integration, monitoring and recovery.
Technically publishes the authoritative data product or approved extract; may differ from the Data Owner.
Governed, consumable representation with owner, semantics, quality rules, service expectations, access controls and lifecycle.

roles.definition: Senior executive accountable for the data domain and its appropriate use.
Establishes and authorises official master or reference lists (e.g. national registers, code lists).
Ensures business quality, fit for purpose and ongoing maintenance.
Operates the authoritative source system(s) for the data.
Provides secure access (e.g. APIs, data products) and technical operations.
Accountable for appropriate use of data in their domain or service.
Sets direction, policy, standards and oversight for government data.
Ensures legal, privacy, security and classification requirements are met.

policies.title: Public Finance Management Act
policies.entity: Ministry of Finance and National Planning
principles: Public finance rests on efficiency, effectiveness, transparency and accountability in the generation and use of public revenue (s.20(b)).
Revenue must be properly forecast within the macro-economic framework (s.20(a)).
The Treasury promotes and enforces transparency and effective management of revenue, expenditure, assets and liabilities of public bodies (s.5(1)(f)).
Controlling officers and controlling bodies owe fiduciary duties: utmost care to protect the assets and records of the public body, fidelity, honesty and integrity (s.12(1)).
Public funds are consolidated: public monies are credited to the Consolidated Fund and spent only as authorised by the Constitution and this Act (ss.21, 22(1), 76).
Accountability runs from accounting officers to controlling officers to the Secretary to the Treasury and onward to the Auditor-General and the National Assembly (ss.6, 10-13, 70, 73).
Where the Act conflicts with another law on managing public funds, the Act prevails (s.3).
Financial misconduct (wilful or negligent unauthorised, irregular or wasteful expenditure, misapplication, theft) attracts personal liability, surcharge and offences (ss.49-54, 76, 82).
management_intent: Establish the Treasury as the central authority that prescribes uniform norms, standards, accounting and budget classification systems and financial management systems for all public bodies, and monitors compliance (s.5(2)).

Make named office holders personally accountable for the proper management of public monies, assets and stores: Secretary to the Treasury as chief controlling officer, controlling officers, accounting officers (ss.6, 10, 11, 13).
Require controlling officers and accounting officers to use the financial management information systems the Treasury determines or prescribes (ss.11(9), 13(3)(h)).

Give the Treasury, internal auditors and the Auditor-General statutory access to accounts, records and financial and ICT systems in electronic or any form, with limited exclusions for defence, security and Cabinet matters (ss.7(2), 16(2), 73).
Centralise cash through the Treasury Single Account and require Treasury written approval for opening, closing, overdrawing or transferring between bank accounts holding public monies (ss.25, 32).
Keep specified registers and separate books and records (assets and stores, advances, aided project accounts, investments in SOEs) so that stewardship can be audited (ss.38, 40, 41, 63).
Drive timely, consolidated financial reporting to Treasury, the Auditor-General and the National Assembly under prescribed deadlines (ss.11(1)(f), 58, 70).

Criminalise failure to keep proper records, concealing or destroying required information, false statements, and altering or divulging data, while leaving detailed record-keeping, forms and the manner of documents (hard copy or electronic) to regulations (ss.82(1), 85, 90(2)).

controls.name: Treasury-prescribed norms, standards and uniform classification systems
controls.clause: s.5(2)(i)-(ii); s.2 (applicable accounting reporting framework); s.70(6)
controls.statement: The Treasury prescribes uniform treasury norms and standards and enforces prescribed standards of budgeting, accounting and internal auditing and uniform classification systems in public bodies. 'Classification' here means accounting and budget classification (heads, votes, accounts), not data-sensitivity classification; financial reports must follow the applicable accounting reporting framework and Government Accounting Guidelines.
evidence: Treasury-issued norms and standards, circulars and accounting guidelines
Prescribed uniform chart of accounts / budget classification code list with version
Applicable accounting reporting framework issued by Treasury
Treasury compliance assessment of the public body against prescribed standards

controls.name: Prescribed financial management systems and Treasury review of systems and controls
controls.statement: The Treasury oversees the design and implementation of financial management systems in all public bodies, prescribes those systems, monitors and assesses compliance, and reviews financial management and internal control systems. The Secretary to the Treasury must ensure compatible, effective and transparent financial management information systems exist in ministries, departments, agencies, local authorities and projects.
evidence: Treasury instrument prescribing financial management systems
Treasury compliance monitoring and assessment reports on the public body
Records of Treasury review of financial management and internal control systems
Evidence of administrative action or referral for breach (s.5(2)(vi))

controls.name: Mandatory use of Treasury-determined financial management information systems (IFMIS)
controls.statement: A controlling officer shall use the financial management information systems determined by the Secretary to the Treasury, and an accounting officer shall ensure the prescribed systems are used in performing accounting duties. The Accountant-General is responsible for maintaining compatible, effective and transparent electronic or non-electronic financial management information systems in a public body.
evidence: Secretary to the Treasury determination of the financial management information system(s) to be used
System access and user role listing for controlling and accounting officers
Evidence that transactions are recorded in the prescribed system (extracts, reconciliations)
Accountant-General records of system maintenance for the public body

controls.name: Statutory access for Treasury and internal audit to accounts, records and systems
controls.statement: The Secretary to the Treasury (or an authorised office holder) may inspect and access accounts, documents, books and records in electronic or any form of any public body. Internal auditors shall at all reasonable times have access to accounts, records, vouchers, and financial and non-financial management systems, and may require information from the controlling officer; the Controller of Internal Audit may conduct ICT and forensic audits. Failing to provide information or obstructing access is an offence.
evidence: Written authorisation by the Secretary to the Treasury for inspecting officers
Appointment letters of internal auditors by the Civil Service Commission
Access logs or audit requests and the responses supplied
Internal audit reports to Controller of Internal Audit, controlling officer and audit committee (s.16(3))
ICT audit reports (s.15(1)(e))
sop: Internal auditor submits reports to the Controller of Internal Audit, the controlling officer and the audit committee, copied to the Minister, Accountant-General, Secretary to the Treasury, Auditor-General and the appropriate Minister (s.16(3)).

controls.name: Auditor-General access to books, records and ICT systems
controls.statement: The Auditor-General and authorised office holders, agents or specialist consultants have access to all books, records, returns, reports, other documents and financial management systems in electronic or any other form, to premises, to responsible persons, and to all information and communication technology systems used in managing public monies. Controlling officers must disclose material facts to the Treasury, Auditor-General or National Assembly on request.
evidence: Auditor-General audit access requests and the public body's responses
Auditor-General authorisation of agents or specialist consultants (s.74)
Management letters and audit queries with responses (s.11(6))
System access provisioning records for external auditors

controls.name: Restricted access for agents and consultants, with Presidential consent
controls.statement: The Auditor-General shall not authorise an agent or specialist consultant to access records, ICT systems or premises of the Defence Force or the Zambia Security Intelligence Service, or other access likely to prejudice security, defence, international relations or investigations, or to disclose secret Cabinet matters. Where an audit requires it, access may be authorised only after the written consent of the President.
evidence: Written consent of the President for each restricted authorisation
Auditor-General authorisation naming the agent or consultant and the scope of access
Register of consultants authorised and the systems or premises accessed
sop: Auditor-General obtains the written consent of the President before authorising an agent or specialist consultant to access restricted records, ICT systems or premises (s.73(3)).

controls.name: Integrity of records and data: offences for false, concealed, destroyed, altered or divulged data
controls.statement: A person commits an offence if, wilfully and without lawful authority, they fail to keep proper records, conceal or destroy information required to be recorded, give false or misleading information or documents required under the Act, or alter or divulge data in electronic or other form. Controlling officers and controlling bodies must exercise utmost care to protect the assets and records of the public body and must not use confidential information for personal gain.
evidence: Controls evidencing authorised change to financial records (audit trail, change log)
Access control and user-privilege records for financial systems
Incident or breach reports on altered or disclosed records and action taken
Controlling officer certification of correctness of accounts (s.11(1)(g))

controls.name: Record-keeping, forms of accounts and document format left to regulations; no retention period set
controls.statement: The Act does not set how long financial records are kept; the Minister may make regulations on the keeping of records, books and accounts, and on the forms of accounts, books, records and other documents. The manner and form of documents under the Act is as prescribed and may be hard copy or electronic, and accounting officers keep such books and render such accounts as prescribed or directed by the Accountant-General.
evidence: Regulations made under s.90 on records, books, accounts and document forms
Accountant-General directions to accounting officers on books and accounts
Prescribed forms and templates in hard copy or electronic form
Records retention schedule of the public body (the Act itself states no period)

controls.name: Register of public assets and stores, inspection and annual reporting
controls.statement: A controlling officer shall keep a register of the public assets and stores for every head of expenditure, have them inspected with written condition reports, secure public properties with title deeds, account for them each financial year as the Secretary to the Treasury specifies, and report on them to the Treasury one month after year end. Stock verifiers verify Government stock and assets, and the Accountant-General issues guidelines for recording and reporting assets and liabilities. Negligent failure to account for assets is financial misconduct.
evidence: Register of public assets and stores per head of expenditure
Written inspection and condition reports on assets and storage facilities
Title deeds for public properties
Annual assets and stores report submitted to Treasury within one month of year end
Stock verification reports
Accountant-General guidelines on accounting, recording and reporting of assets and liabilities
sop: Controlling officer causes assets and stores to be inspected and prepares written condition reports (s.41(3)).
Controlling officer submits reports on public assets and stores to the Treasury one month after the end of the financial year (s.41(6)).

controls.name: Advances account and separate Treasury account for recoverable advances
controls.statement: Where the Secretary to the Treasury authorises advances of public money, separate records (an 'advances account') shall be maintained and the Treasury shall keep a separate account for advances to persons. An advance cannot be made in anticipation of an appropriation, and any balance outstanding at financial year end is not charged to an expenditure vote unless the Secretary directs otherwise.
evidence: Advances account (register of advances, recipients, amounts, repayment or charge status)
Secretary to the Treasury written authorisation of each advance
Separate Treasury account for advances (s.38(2))
Year-end listing of outstanding advance balances

controls.name: Records of investments and Treasury approval of investment of public funds
controls.statement: The Secretary to the Treasury shall cause a record to be maintained of monies invested in statutory corporations and state owned enterprises. A controlling officer may invest public funds only with the Secretary's approval, and details of investments made from public funds must be copied to the Auditor-General; investments authorised under s.34 form part of the Consolidated Fund.
evidence: Record of monies invested in statutory corporations and state owned enterprises
Secretary to the Treasury approval of each investment of public funds
Copy of investment details furnished to the Auditor-General
Dividend and yield records for SOEs
sop: Controlling officer copies details of investments made from public funds to the Auditor-General (s.28(4)).

controls.name: Aided project books, records and project accounts
controls.statement: Monies received for aided projects (loans, grants, donations) are public monies paid into the Consolidated Fund and disbursed to the appropriate project bank account. The Secretary to the Treasury shall cause separate and proper books and records to be kept for projects, include audited statements in the financial report, and ensure project assets are recorded, accounted for and handed over within the agreed period or six months after completion; unexpended balances six months after completion go to the Consolidated Fund absent contrary instructions.
evidence: Separate books and records per aided project
Project bank account statements and Consolidated Fund disbursement records
Audited project financial statements included in the financial report
Project asset handover records within the agreed time or six months of completion
Records of loans, grants or donations receivable in kind and their valuation (s.40(4))
sop: Project assets are handed over within the time frame in the agreement, or within six months of project completion where none is provided (s.40(6)(b), (7)).
Any unexpended balance of a project account six months after completion is paid into the Consolidated Fund absent instructions to the contrary (s.40(8)).

controls.name: Approval of bank accounts for public monies, transfers, and dormant or idle accounts
controls.clause: s.32(1)-(9); s.82(1)(a); s.2 (dormant account, idle funds)
controls.statement: No person may open or close a bank account for public monies, overdraw it, or transfer public money between accounts without the written approval of the Secretary to the Treasury, and banks may not permit these without that approval. Banks must supply statements to account holders and the Accountant-General on request. An account with no transactions for six months is dormant and the Treasury may close it and transfer the funds to the Consolidated Fund; idle funds (unutilised for six months or more) are likewise transferred.
evidence: Written Secretary to the Treasury approvals to open, close, overdraw or transfer between accounts
Register or listing of bank accounts holding public monies
Bank statements furnished to account holders and the Accountant-General
Dormant and idle account reviews and transfer records to the Consolidated Fund
sop: Treasury closes a dormant account of which it becomes aware and transfers the funds to the Consolidated Fund (s.32(6)).
Treasury transfers idle funds to the Consolidated Fund (s.32(7)).

controls.name: Deposit of public monies received by the next business day
controls.statement: All monies received by an accounting officer or collecting office holder shall be deposited into the Consolidated Fund not later than the next business day after receipt, unless the Secretary to the Treasury directs otherwise. General revenues collected by appointed agents are transmitted as the Treasury prescribes, and failure to deposit or account without reasonable cause is financial misconduct or an offence.
evidence: Receipt records and daily deposit records for monies collected
Bank deposit slips or electronic transfer confirmations to the Consolidated Fund
Appointed agent remittance reports and Treasury prescription of transmission
Secretary to the Treasury directions varying the deposit rule
sop: Deposit all monies received into the Consolidated Fund not later than the next business day following receipt, unless the Secretary to the Treasury directs otherwise (s.28(2)).

controls.name: Controlling officer and accounting officer reporting and its timeliness
controls.statement: A controlling officer must submit a financial report for the head of expenditure to the Secretary to the Treasury within one month of the end of the financial year, prepare quarterly action-taken reports on audit observations and quarterly revenue performance reports, and prepare a statement of revenue and appropriation accounts for Auditor-General certification. Accounting officers compile monthly, quarterly, biannual and annual financial management reports for the controlling officer; the committee of survey reports disposals within thirty days of year end.
evidence: Annual financial report per head of expenditure with submission date to Treasury
Quarterly action-taken reports on internal and external audit observations
Quarterly revenue performance reports (s.29(2)(c))
Statement of revenue and appropriation accounts submitted for audit certification
Monthly, quarterly, biannual and annual accounting officer reports
Committee of survey report on disposals
sop: Controlling officer submits a financial report to the Secretary to the Treasury within one month after the end of the preceding financial year (ss.11(1)(f), 70(5)).
Controlling officer, upon Auditor-General certification, immediately submits the statement of accounts to the Secretary to the Treasury for the financial report (s.11(5)).

controls.name: Financial Report of the Republic: consolidation, standards and publication
controls.statement: The Treasury prepares a financial report for each financial year, and the Secretary to the Treasury consolidates the controlling officers' financial statements within two months of receipt, using the applicable accounting reporting framework and Government Accounting Guidelines. Statements are submitted to the Auditor-General for examination and certification, financial statistics are compiled to international standards and published in the Gazette, and the public-body financial year runs to 31 December.
evidence: Financial Report of the Republic with notes
Consolidated statement of assets and liabilities and consolidated revenue statement
Auditor-General certification of the statements
Gazetted financial statistics aggregation
Record of receipt dates of controlling officer statements and consolidation date
sop: Secretary to the Treasury consolidates financial statements into the Financial Report of the Republic within two months of receipt from controlling officers (s.70(2)).
Secretary to the Treasury submits the consolidated statements to the Auditor-General for examination and certification (s.7(1)(d)).

controls.name: Statutory corporation and state owned enterprise annual and monthly grant reporting
controls.statement: Boards of statutory corporations and state owned enterprises must send financial statements prepared under the applicable accounting reporting framework to their auditors within one month of year end, and the annual report, audited statements and auditors' report to the Secretary to the Treasury within four months, with the Minister laying them before the National Assembly within five months. Boards acknowledge each monthly grant and submit monthly returns on its application in the prescribed format, and the annual financial report must include risk management and corporate governance reporting.
evidence: Annual report, audited financial statements and auditors' report with submission dates
Statement of intended grant use submitted before release (s.60(1))
Grant receipt acknowledgements and monthly returns in the prescribed format
Risk management and corporate governance report in the annual financial report
Minister's laying of the report before the National Assembly
sop: Board submits financial statements to the auditors within one month after the end of the financial year (s.58(2)(b)).
Board submits the annual report, audited financial statements and auditors' report within four months of year end (s.58(2)(d)).
Minister lays the report and statements before the National Assembly within five months after the end of the financial year (s.58(4)).

controls.name: Named accountable roles: controlling officer, accounting officer, Accountant-General
controls.statement: The Secretary to the Treasury, as chief controlling officer, designates a controlling officer for each head of revenue and expenditure and any variation must be copied to the Auditor-General. The controlling officer is responsible and accountable for public monies, stores and assets, defines in writing the functions delegated to accounting officers, and accounting officers are appointed by the relevant Commission and must implement financial management and internal control systems, safeguard assets and account for them. The Accountant-General is responsible for compiling accounts and for the custody, safety and integrity of public monies and stores.
evidence: Designation of controlling officer per head of revenue and expenditure
Secretary to the Treasury approval or withdrawal of alternative controlling officer, copied to the Auditor-General
Written delegation by the controlling officer to accounting officers with directions (s.11(2))
Accounting officer appointment records
Declarations of conflict of interest by controlling officers (ss.12(3), 89)
sop: Secretary to the Treasury provides a copy of any approval, instruction or withdrawal designating another functionary as controlling officer to the Auditor-General (s.10(2),(4)).
Controlling officer defines in writing, in consultation with the Treasury, the extent to which functions may be exercised by an accounting officer (s.11(2)(a)).

policies.title: Movable Property (Security Interest) Act
policies.entity: Ministry of Finance and National Planning
principles: A single, electronic, publicly searchable Collateral Registry is the sole registration regime for security interests in movable property (ss.11(1), 26).

Accuracy sits with the submitter: the secured creditor must ensure the financing statement is complete and certify by statutory declaration that it is true, while the Registrar does not verify, scrutinise or answer for accuracy or legality (ss.12(5), 13(1), 11(3)).

The Registrar and officers may not alter or remove information in a registered financing statement (s.8(4)); changes are made only by the secured creditor's amendment or discharge or by court order (ss.21, 24).

Retrieval depends on correct identifiers: debtor name and identification or registration number, and collateral serial number, are the critical data elements and errors in them invalidate registration (ss.11(4), 17).
Registrations have a bounded life of at most five years, renewable by amendment, and must be discharged within stated timelines when obligations end (ss.13(1)(h), 19, 22, 23).
Filing is electronic only, and fees are paid electronically (ss.11(1), 14).
Registry integrity is protected by criminal offences and administrative penalties for false, fraudulent or altered entries (ss.93-98).
The Collateral Registry Office is a reporting entity under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (s.101).
The Agency is responsible for the registration system and must restore it after a malfunction (s.25).
management_intent: Make security interests in movable property effective against third parties through one transparent, low-cost electronic registration regime, to widen access to secured credit.
Keep the registry open to any person who wants to search it, so priority and encumbrances can be discovered before credit is extended.
Place responsibility for the truth of registered information on the secured creditor and keep the Registrar neutral and unable to alter registered content.
Keep the register current by limiting registration life, requiring timely discharge and amendment, and invalidating registrations with defective debtor or serial-number data.
Deter abuse of the registry through offences for fraudulent, false or malicious filings.

controls.name: Electronic Collateral Registry and Registrar's operational functions
controls.statement: The Collateral Registry Office is established in the Patents and Companies Registration Agency (the Agency) under the general direction of the Board and is responsible for the Collateral Registry (s.7). The Collateral Registry is an electronic registry that stores information and records in accordance with s.13 (s.11(1)-(2)). The Registrar's functions are to manage and facilitate electronic access by users, process fees, oversee the operation and maintenance of the registration system, and gather statistical data (s.8(2)). The Registrar may delegate in writing to officers appointed by the Board (ss.9, 10). The Act does not state where the registry is hosted.
evidence: Registry system architecture and hosting description, including location of servers and backups
Written delegations from the Registrar to officers
Registrar's statistical reports on registrations, searches and fees
Fee processing records and reconciliation
Board appointment records for officers of the Collateral Registry Office

controls.name: Public electronic search of the Collateral Registry
controls.statement: The Collateral Registry Office shall be open to the public at reasonable working hours, and any person may search the Collateral Registry electronically and obtain a copy of the search results, in accordance with the Act and regulations made by the Minister, on payment of the prescribed fee. 'Search' is defined as an electronic examination of the records in the Registry. The Act places no condition on who may search or for what purpose. Because financing statements for natural persons hold name, date of birth, identification number and address (s.13(1)(a),(c)), the public-search right exposes personal data, and the Act contains no masking or purpose-limitation rule for that data.
evidence: Search regulations and prescribed search fee schedule
Search interface specification showing which fields are returned to a public searcher
Search logs recording searcher, search key and results returned
Data protection or privacy impact assessment for public search of personal identifiers
Registry opening hours notice

controls.name: Registry indexing and search keys
controls.statement: The Collateral Registry shall contain the information provided in financing statements as specified in s.13, indexed in a manner that a debtor, a secured creditor and the serial number of the collateral can be identified and easily retrieved by a search. The Minister shall issue regulations on the storage and indexing of information in the Registry. The retrieval keys are therefore the debtor and creditor identity (for a natural person, name, date of birth and identification number; for a body, name and registration or incorporation number) and the serial number of the collateral.
evidence: Regulations on storage and indexing of Collateral Registry information
Registry data dictionary and index design showing debtor, secured creditor and serial-number keys
Search test results showing retrieval by each key
Rules for name normalisation or matching used in search

controls.name: Mandatory content of a financing statement
controls.statement: A secured creditor who intends to register a financing statement shall ensure it contains: for a natural-person debtor, name, date of birth, identification number and address; for a corporate or unincorporated debtor, name, address, registration or incorporation number and the name or job title and contact details of the person acting for it; the corresponding particulars for the secured creditor; a description of the collateral; the date of effectiveness, perfection or any prior registration under another law; the maximum amount for which the secured obligation may be enforced; the term of effectiveness (not more than five years); a statutory declaration; and any other information prescribed (s.13(1)). Collateral not described by prescribed serial number is described as in the security agreement (s.13(2)), which must describe it so as to allow reasonable identification (ss.34(1)(d), 35). The financing statement is a document in the prescribed form.
evidence: Prescribed financing statement form and regulations on format (s.32(2)(b))
Registry schema or data dictionary mapping each s.13(1) element to a field, type and mandatory flag
Sample registered financing statements for natural-person and corporate debtors
Prescribed serial number formats for collateral types that require serial numbers
Security agreements supporting a sample of registered collateral descriptions

controls.name: Submitter accountable for accuracy, certified by statutory declaration
controls.statement: The secured creditor shall ensure the financing statement contains the required information, and each financing statement must include a statutory declaration certifying that the information registered is true and complies with the Act. Oaths, affirmations and declarations are made in accordance with Zambian law on affirmations or declarations (s.30). Accuracy and compliance are therefore attested by the submitter, not by the registry.
evidence: Statutory declaration filed with each financing statement (sample)
Secured creditor procedure for verifying debtor identity and collateral details before filing
Data-entry or upload audit trail identifying the submitting user and secured creditor
Registry rule rejecting a financing statement that lacks the declaration

controls.name: Registrar does not verify or alter; modification routes
controls.statement: The Registrar or an officer shall not verify whether authorisation for registration has been properly granted (s.11(3)). The Registrar shall not conduct any scrutiny of the information in a financing statement or be responsible for its accuracy or legality (s.12(5)). The Registrar or an officer shall not alter or remove information in a registered financing statement or amendment (s.8(4)). A person aggrieved by a decision of the Registrar may appeal to a court within thirty days of notification (s.29). Where relief sought includes modifying Registry information, the Registrar may appear and be heard, and must appear if the court directs, and may file a signed written statement (s.31). Any data-quality validation therefore has to be designed into the filing system and by the submitter, not performed by the Registrar.
evidence: Registry system audit trail showing no staff-initiated alteration or removal of registered content
Role and permission matrix for Registry staff showing no edit rights over registered financing statements
System validation rules at filing (format, mandatory fields), documented as the only registry-side checks
Register of appeals under s.29 and court proceedings under s.31, with outcomes
Registrar's written statements filed in proceedings

controls.name: Debtor authorisation of registration
controls.statement: A debtor who enters into a security agreement automatically authorises registration of a financing statement and any amendments (s.12(1)). A creditor or its agent may register before or after the security agreement is made (s.12(3)), and the debtor may authorise registration in writing before a security agreement is concluded (s.12(4)). One financing statement may cover several security interests between the same parties (s.12(2)). The consent for listing a debtor's personal data on the public register is therefore deemed by operation of law, and the Registrar does not check it (s.11(3)).
evidence: Security agreements showing the debtor's agreement, as the trigger for automatic authorisation
Written pre-registration authorisations from debtors (s.12(4))
Registered financing statements filed before the security agreement, with the authorisation on file
Secured creditor procedure for retaining authorisation evidence

controls.name: Electronic-only filing and conditions for non-registration
controls.statement: A financing statement shall not be registered if it is not processed electronically in the prescribed manner or form, if it does not contain the information specified in s.13, or if the prescribed fee for registering the financing statement or an amendment has not been paid electronically. The registration regime is therefore electronic end to end, with machine-checkable preconditions for acceptance.
evidence: Online filing portal specification and prescribed form
Validation rule set that blocks submission when s.13 elements are missing
Rejection log with reason codes (not electronic, missing information, fee unpaid)
Electronic payment records linked to each registration or amendment

controls.name: Registration effective time and unique registration number
controls.statement: Registration of a financing statement is effective from the date and time when the information is entered into the Collateral Registry and a registration number is assigned to it. The system must therefore time-stamp each entry and assign a registration number, and the time-stamp determines priority between registrations under s.52(b)(i).
evidence: Registration number generation rule and uniqueness constraint
System timestamp records for each registration, with clock source
Sample registered statements showing date, time and number
Priority disputes or searches that relied on the registration time-stamp

controls.name: Confirmation statement and copy to debtor
controls.statement: On registration of a financing statement or an amendment, the Registrar shall provide a confirmation statement electronically to the person who registered it. The secured creditor shall, not later than fourteen working days after receiving the statement, give a copy to the debtor. Section 16(2) calls the document a 'verification statement' while s.16(1) and s.2 use 'confirmation statement'; the two are treated here as the same document.
evidence: Confirmation statements issued for a sample of registrations and amendments
System log of electronic transmission of confirmation statements to the registrant
Secured creditor records of copies given to debtors, with dates
Template of the confirmation statement
sop: Registrar provides a confirmation statement electronically to the person who registered the financing statement or amendment.
Secured creditor gives a copy of the statement to the debtor not later than fourteen working days after receiving it.

controls.name: Validity rules: critical identifiers and material errors
controls.statement: A registration is invalid if the registered financing statement or amendment has a defect, irregularity, omission or error in the debtor's name and identification number, or in the collateral serial number where one is required. Invalidity is limited to that debtor or that collateral. A correct serial number keeps the registration valid for that collateral even if the debtor's name or ID is wrong (s.17(3)). An error in the collateral description other than the serial number invalidates the registration for that collateral if it may seriously mislead a person (s.17(4)). Errors in the secured creditor's name, ID or address, in the debtor's address, or in voluntarily entered information do not invalidate (s.17(5)). It is not necessary to prove anyone was actually misled (s.18(2)). The fee is not refunded if registration is invalidated (s.17(6)). The critical data elements are therefore debtor name, debtor identification or registration number and collateral serial number.
evidence: Data-quality rules for the debtor name and identification number fields and for serial numbers
Format and checksum validation for identification numbers at the point of entry
Records of registrations challenged or held invalid under s.17, with outcomes
Classification of registry fields into critical elements (invalidating) and non-critical elements
Fee non-refund notice shown at filing

controls.name: Five-year maximum registration life and renewal
controls.statement: The term of effectiveness stated in a financing statement shall not exceed five years. A registered financing statement remains valid for the specified term (not more than five years), or for five years from the date of registration, or until the date of discharge and removal from the Registry (s.19(1)). The period may be extended or renewed before expiry by registering an amendment stating a new period of validity not exceeding five years (s.19(2)). The Act does not state how long expired or discharged records are retained in the Registry.
evidence: Registry rule enforcing a maximum term of five years at filing and on renewal
Expiry report listing registrations approaching or past expiry
Renewal amendments registered before expiry (sample)
Registry retention and archiving policy for expired and discharged registrations
Notification to secured creditors of impending expiry, if operated

controls.name: Amendment and transfer of registered financing statements
controls.statement: Where all or part of a registered security interest is transferred, the transferor shall register an amendment within fourteen days of the transfer, describing the collateral transferred (s.20(1)-(2)). A secured creditor may amend or discharge a registered financing statement at any time before expiry (s.21(1)). Amendments that add collateral, add a new debtor or increase the maximum secured amount are effective only from the date of registration of the amendment (s.21(2)). If a debtor's name and identification number change so that the statement can no longer be retrieved by search, the interest is not effective for collateral acquired more than thirty days after the change, but remains effective for existing collateral and collateral acquired within the thirty days (s.21(3)). A secured creditor may also amend a statement to indicate an obligation or privilege arising from another commercial document or from written law (s.88(1)).
evidence: Amendment records with date of transfer and date of registered amendment, to test the fourteen-day rule
Registry version history showing each amendment as a separate dated entry
Process for detecting debtor name or ID changes that affect retrievability
Amendments registered under s.88 with the commercial document referenced
sop: Transferor registers an amendment to the registered financing statement within fourteen days of the transfer.
The amendment includes a description of the collateral that has been transferred.

controls.name: Discharge of registrations, debtor demand and court order
controls.statement: Where a registered financing statement relates exclusively to consumer goods, the secured creditor shall discharge it within fourteen days after all obligations under the security agreement have been performed, unless the registration expires first; the discharge is lodged in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee (s.22). A debtor may send a written demand to amend or discharge where part of the collateral is released, the statement includes property that is not collateral, obligations are performed with no commitment to future advances, no security agreement exists, or the security interest is extinguished (s.23(1)). The secured creditor shall, if it has no objection, register the amendment or discharge within fourteen days of receiving the demand (s.23(2)). If the creditor fails to comply, the debtor may apply to a court for an order to amend, discharge or maintain the statement, and the creditor must comply and inform the debtor (s.24).
evidence: Discharge records with date of final performance and date of registered discharge for consumer-goods registrations
Written debtor demands and the secured creditor's response dates
Court orders under s.24 and the resulting registry changes
Registry report of consumer-goods registrations past the fourteen-day discharge deadline
Registry flag distinguishing consumer-goods registrations
sop: Secured creditor discharges a consumer-goods registration within fourteen days after all obligations under the security agreement have been performed.
On receiving a debtor's written demand to amend or discharge, a creditor with no objection registers the amendment or discharge within fourteen days of receipt.
If the secured creditor fails to comply, the debtor applies to a court for an order to amend, discharge or maintain the registration.

controls.name: Enforcement notice and extinguishment registered in the Registry
controls.statement: A secured creditor shall, before enforcing its rights, register an enforcement notice in the Collateral Registry in the prescribed manner, identifying the debtor, the secured creditor and the collateral against which enforcement is sought (s.71). Where collateral has been disposed of in accordance with Part VI and subordinate security interests are extinguished, the secured creditor shall register the extinguishment in the prescribed form (s.80(2)). The Registry therefore carries lifecycle events beyond registration and discharge.
evidence: Enforcement notices registered, with dates relative to enforcement action
Prescribed forms for enforcement notice and extinguishment
Registry record types or status codes for enforcement and extinguishment events
Search results showing enforcement status for a sample collateral

controls.name: Administration and restoration of the registration system
controls.statement: The Agency is responsible for the administration of the registration system. Where a system malfunction occurs, the Agency shall restore or have the system restored. The Act gives no recovery time or point objectives, backup requirement or hosting location.

controls.name: Certified copies, extracts and certificates of status
controls.statement: A copy of or extract from a financing statement certified by the Registrar as a true copy is admitted in proceedings as of equal validity to the original and is conclusive evidence of the information stated in it (s.27). On request and payment of the prescribed fee, the Registrar may issue a certificate of status of a registered financing statement, which is conclusive evidence of the information in the Registry at the date and time of issue, and shall provide a certified copy of any stored document to a secured creditor or other person (s.28).

Log of certified copies and certificates of status issued, with requester and fee

controls.name: Offences and administrative penalties protecting registry integrity
controls.statement: It is an offence to fraudulently lodge a financing statement (s.93), to lodge one for a frivolous, malicious or criminal purpose (s.94), to make or cause a false entry in the Collateral Registry or issue or tender a false copy of an entry (s.95), to alter, deface, add to, partly remove or erase a document issued by the Registrar (s.96), and to deceive or influence the Registrar or an officer or make a false statement knowing it to be false (s.97(1)). A person who innocently makes a false statement and, on becoming aware of the falsity, fails to advise the Registrar forthwith also commits an offence (s.97(2)). Offences carry a fine not exceeding two hundred thousand penalty units, with imprisonment up to two years for most (ss.93, 95-97, 99). The Registrar may also impose a daily administrative penalty for failure to comply with the Act, recoverable by civil action (s.98).
evidence: Register of suspected fraudulent, false or malicious filings and referrals
Procedure for a submitter to notify the Registrar of an innocent false statement
Administrative penalty register, with amounts prescribed by the Minister and penalties imposed
Registry audit logs supporting investigation of false entries
Notice to filers of the offences and penalties
sop: A person who innocently made a false statement and later becomes aware of its falsity advises the Registrar forthwith.

controls.name: Collateral Registry Office as a Financial Intelligence Centre reporting entity
controls.statement: The Collateral Registry Office is a reporting entity for the purposes of the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2010 (Act No. 46 of 2010). The Registry Office therefore carries the reporting and record-keeping obligations that Act places on reporting entities. The obligations themselves are in the FIC Act, not in this Act.

Anti-money-laundering and suspicious transaction reporting policy
Log of reports filed with the Financial Intelligence Centre
Staff training records on FIC Act obligations
Record-keeping schedule aligned to the FIC Act

controls.name: Debtor's right to information from the secured creditor
controls.statement: A debtor may request the secured creditor to send or make available to a specified person a summary of the security agreement, a statement of current indebtedness and payment terms, a written approval or correction of an itemised list of collateral, or a statement of account showing the pay-off amount. Where the creditor no longer holds the interest, it shall disclose the name and address of the immediate (or latest known) successor or transferee. The creditor shall comply within fourteen days of receipt, may charge only reasonable costs, and the debtor is entitled to one response free of charge every three months.
evidence: Log of debtor information requests and response dates, to test the fourteen-day rule
Copies of statements of account, summaries and collateral lists issued
Fee policy for information requests and record of the free quarterly response
Records of successor or transferee disclosures
sop: Secured creditor responds to the debtor's request within fourteen days of receipt.

controls.name: Collateral classification categories determined at conclusion of the security agreement
controls.statement: Whether goods are consumer goods, equipment, farm products or inventory is determined when the security agreement is concluded, and the secured creditor may rely on the debtor's representations as to intended use. This classification drives other duties in the Act: the fourteen-day discharge obligation applies only to registrations relating exclusively to consumer goods (s.22(1)), and a description of collateral as consumer goods without specific description is inadequate (s.35(3)). The four categories form a small controlled list for collateral type.
evidence: Controlled code list of collateral categories (consumer goods, equipment, farm products, inventory)
Security agreements recording the classification and the debtor's representation of intended use

Procedure for secured creditors to record the category at conclusion of the agreement

policies.title: BoZ Cyber and Information Risk Management Guidelines
principles: Apply-or-explain: all regulated entities (financial service providers, payment systems, payment system businesses, credit reference agencies) must apply the Guidelines; larger and more complex entities are expected to apply them in full, and those that cannot must explain how they otherwise manage the cyber and information risk (cl. 4).
Controls are organised on the NIST Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover functions (cl. 5).
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of information assets must be preserved (cl. 3, 9).

Governance is commensurate with the size, complexity and diversity of the entity, with an explicit risk governance structure (board, board risk committee, senior management, management risk committees, risk function, CISO) (cl. 7).
Risk is managed under the three lines of defence principle (cl. 8.4.1).
Assets, including data, are managed in proportion to their importance to business objectives and risk strategy (cl. 8.1.1).
Information is classified, and protection measures (encryption, media handling) follow the classification (cl. 9.3, 9.6).
Least privilege, segregation of duties and 'never alone' govern access to information assets (cl. 9.1.1.5).
The regulated entity remains accountable for its own responsibilities when functions are outsourced to third parties (cl. 9.1.9).
Policies must be consistent with relevant laws and with international cyber and information risk standards and best practice (cl. 7.3).
management_intent: The board sets the tone from the top, approves the cyber and information risk appetite, framework and policies, and provides senior management with the authority and resources to execute the strategy (cl. 7.1).
Senior management implements the framework, assigns and communicates roles, keeps the board informed of adverse developments and designates a CISO independent of day-to-day IT operations (cl. 7.2).
Cyber and information risk policies are board-approved, regularly reviewed, backed by detailed procedures and verified through compliance processes (cl. 7.3).
Regulated entities know what information and technology assets they hold, where they are (on-site, off-site, with a provider), how data flows and how critical each is (cl. 8.1, 8.2, 8.3).
Sensitive information is classified, inventoried, encrypted, managed through its lifecycle and securely destroyed (cl. 9.3, 9.4, 9.6).
Event and transaction logs are kept, protected from tampering and available for investigation and forensic purposes (cl. 9.1.7, 9.6, 10.2).
Outsourced and cloud arrangements are risk-assessed, contractually controlled, auditable and reversible, with data returned or irreversibly deleted on exit (cl. 9.1.9).
Incidents are classified, recorded in a repository, and medium or high severity incidents are reported to the Bank immediately, with a root-cause report after investigation (cl. 11.1).
Residual cyber risk, control effectiveness and audit results are reported to senior management and the board to support informed decisions (cl. 8.3, 8.4).

controls.name: Data classification scheme
controls.statement: The regulated entity must classify information and data in line with its own data classification scheme. The text does not prescribe the classification levels; each entity defines its scheme, and encryption and media handling are then tied to it (9.3.2, 9.6.8, 9.6.16).

controls.name: Inventory of sensitive information wherever held
controls.statement: The entity must maintain an inventory of all sensitive information stored, processed or transmitted by its technology systems, including on-site, off-site and at a remote service provider (9.3.3). Information assets that support critical functions must also be inventoried and risk-classified for criticality (8.2.8, 8.3.4).

controls.name: Asset and third-party system inventory
controls.statement: Data, personnel, devices, systems and facilities must be identified and managed according to their importance to business objectives. An inventory of physical devices, applications and systems must be maintained and updated regularly, and third-party information systems must be catalogued (8.1.1-8.1.3). A further inventory of user, system, privileged and remote-access accounts is required (8.2.11).

controls.name: Data flow mapping and network topology
controls.statement: Communication and data flows must be mapped to cyber risk roles and responsibilities (8.1.4), and a network topology of existing infrastructure supporting critical functions, including external links, must be created and maintained (8.2.9). A baseline of network operations and expected data flows must also be established for detection (10.1.2).

controls.name: Information asset lifecycle management
controls.statement: Information assets must be formally managed throughout their lifecycle (9.3.5), and the entity must implement a System Development Life Cycle and configuration change control (9.4.4, 9.4.5). Data must be destroyed according to policy (9.4.11). The text sets no retention periods.

controls.name: Data destruction and secure disposal
controls.statement: Sensitive information must be destroyed before electronic devices are disposed of (9.3.6), data destroyed according to policy (9.4.11), and media securely disposed of using formal procedures (9.6.9). Virtual images and snapshots also carry destruction rules (9.1.6.3).

Evidence that sensitive data was wiped before disposal

sop: Destroy sensitive information before electronic devices are disposed of (9.3.6)

controls.name: Encryption of data at rest and in transit by classification
controls.statement: Cryptographic mechanisms must protect sensitive or confidential data on all devices at rest and in transit (9.3.4), and information must be encrypted in transit and at rest in accordance with its classification (9.6.16). Confidential information in digital financial services must be encrypted before network transmission (9.1.7.6).

Configuration evidence of encryption at rest and in transit for sensitive systems

Protocol and transmission security configuration (9.6.17, 9.6.18)

controls.name: Removable media and media handling per classification
controls.statement: Removable media must be protected and restricted by policy, and managed according to the information classification scheme (9.6.6-9.6.7). Media containing information must be protected against unauthorised access, misuse or corruption in transport (9.6.10), and clean desk and clear screen policies apply (9.6.11).

controls.name: Log retention, protection and independent review
controls.statement: Entities offering digital financial services must retain sufficient and relevant transaction logs for investigations and forensics in line with relevant laws (9.1.7.18). Event logs must be maintained, protected against tampering, mirrored in real time to a separate system, reviewed by independent personnel, and not writable or deletable by day-to-day IT operations staff (9.1.2, 9.6.2-9.6.3, 10.2.3-10.2.4). The text sets no numeric retention period.

Log management configuration showing real-time mirroring to a separate system

Privileged user activity log reviews (9.6.4)

controls.name: Outsourcing and cloud arrangements
controls.statement: Before a material outsourcing arrangement the entity must conduct risk assessment and due diligence and obtain Bank approval (9.1.9.1). Data held by a third party in the cloud must be logically segregated from other customers' data (9.1.9.4). Contracts must secure audit and assurance rights, safeguard customer and proprietary information, and provide for return and irreversible deletion of data on termination (9.1.9.6-9.1.9.11).

controls.name: Incident management process and incident repository
controls.statement: The entity must define an incident management process aligned to the enterprise process. It must include a designated team, forensic capacity, classification of incidents, timely handling with recorded progress, protection of evidence and logs, post-incident root-cause analysis, escalation of improvements to the CISO, and a cyber and information risk incident repository (11.1.2, 11.1.4).

controls.name: Incident notification and reporting to Bank of Zambia
controls.statement: The entity must inform the Bank immediately when a medium or highly classified incident is discovered and before any media interaction, and submit an incident report after investigation that includes root-cause analysis and corrective actions (11.1.5, 11.1.6). controls.name: Chief Information Security Officer role
controls.statement: Senior management must designate an appropriately qualified CISO, independent of day-to-day IT operations, who is responsible and accountable for executing the cyber and information risk framework with sufficient authority and resources, and for overseeing and enforcing policies and regulatory requirements (7.2.8-7.2.10).

controls.name: Board-approved cyber and information risk policies and procedures
controls.statement: Cyber and information risk policies must be board-approved, regularly reviewed, consistent with laws and international standards, and supported by specific procedures that are reviewed as the threat landscape changes. Senior management must run compliance processes to verify the policies are enforced (7.3.1-7.3.11; 7.1.9-7.1.10).

controls.name: Identity, access rights and privilege reviews
controls.statement: All users, devices and systems accessing information assets must have unique identifiable credentials that are issued, managed, verified, revoked and audited. Access rights follow roles under least privilege, segregation of duties and 'never alone', and user access privileges are regularly reviewed (9.1.1.2-9.1.1.5, 9.1.3.6).

controls.name: Backups and environment segregation for data protection
controls.statement: Backups must be conducted and maintained both off-site and on-site, protected from unauthorised access and tested periodically (9.4.3, 9.1.3.5, 9.1.10.6). Development and test environments must be separated from production (9.3.9).

controls.name: Digital financial service transaction data integrity and traceability

controls.name: Risk assessment of critical and sensitive information assets
controls.statement: The entity must assess risk across critical functions, key roles, processes, information assets, third parties and interconnections to determine, classify and document their criticality, and remedy vulnerabilities affecting critical and sensitive information assets in a timely manner (8.3.4, 8.3.6). controls.name: Internal audit and assurance over cyber and information risk
controls.statement: An adequately resourced internal audit function with technology audit competence must provide assurance over cyber and information risk, using external independent auditors where internal capacity is inadequate. Cyber audits are performed at planned intervals commensurate with system criticality (8.4.4, 8.4.5).

policies.title: Zambia Interbank Payment and Settlement System (ZIPSS) Rules
principles: The BoZ is the System and Technical Operator of the ZIPSS with legal responsibility for controlling, managing and operating the system, and for the security of system data, software and infrastructure (s.1.1).

The BoZ warrants that the system is designed and implemented to a high standard of security and reliability, with the objective of maintaining the integrity, availability and confidentiality of all data handled by it (s.8.1).
The BoZ must keep strict confidentiality of all information provided by Participants and/or processed through the system (s.8.1).
Each Participant is individually responsible for the quality of the data it sends and for compliance with the agreed message formats (s.4.1).

Participants conduct business with one another in the utmost good faith and integrity, and ensure the integrity, compliance and functionality of their systems and of the data received and transmitted to the ZIPSS (s.4.1.1).
Payment messages follow the ISO 20022 standard as published on the ZIPSS MyStandards and Readiness Portal (s.1.2, s.10.1).
Settlement is final and irrevocable once settlement accounts are credited and debited, and the point of Technical Acceptance is the handover point between Participant and ZIPSS (s.4.1.3, s.5.2).

The system processes instructions as submitted; it is not designed to detect errors in transmission or content, and the BoZ is not liable for verifying the accuracy of Participant data or instructions (s.1.6, s.8.1.2).

Only authorised and uniquely identified users, holding BoZ-issued e-tokens, may access the system, with segregation of duties between business and security-administration functions (s.4.1.5, s.8.1.5, s.9.1).
Participants must assess and certify their compliance with the Rules, and the BoZ oversees adherence and may take supervisory action (s.1.1, s.13).
Transaction and accounting data are retained in line with Zambian law, with the previous 10 years of data accessible on-line in real time (s.15.3).
Participant data is shared with auditors or other legal entities only on the Participant's written authority (s.15.1), and with third parties only under the consent in s.8.1.1 or as required by law.
The BoZ is transparent about system activity by publishing monthly and annual statistics on payment volumes and values (s.15.2).
The Rules are subject to Zambian law and are aligned to the BIS Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (s.16, s.19.1).
management_intent: Define the operating rules, responsibilities and obligations of all ZIPSS Participants, including the BoZ as System Operator and Participant, under the National Payment Systems Act No. 1 of 2007 (s.1.0).

Provide a final, irrevocable, real-time gross settlement system for high-value and time-critical payments and for the net positions of clearing houses, the LuSE, Government payments and the CSD (s.1.3).
Migrate ZIPSS to the data-rich ISO 20022 standard (v4.0 live 14 October 2023) in line with global trends, and leverage it to develop new use cases for ZIPSS users (s.1.2).
Make STP the standard for outgoing and incoming payment messages between Participant core banking systems and the ZIPSS (s.2.0, s.5.7).

Safeguard data integrity, availability and confidentiality and cyber security through BoZ system-level controls and mandatory Participant measures based on the NIST Framework and ISO/IEC 27001/2 (s.1.6, s.8.1.4-8.1.6).
Keep a record of all transactional data according to relevant Zambian law and give Participants and auditors comprehensive audit trails (s.1.1, s.15.1).
Maintain business continuity through layered connectivity channels (Swift, Gateway, Payment Originator, ASA) and a contingency framework for business disruption events (s.3.0, s.16).
Review the Rules and Materials every two years or as deemed necessary, with Participant consultation and 30 calendar days notice before changes take effect (s.1.5, s.21).
Enforce compliance through penalties, administrative fees, supervisory action under the NPSA and suspension or removal of Participants (s.4.1.6, s.7.2, s.13, s.14).

controls.name: Participant duty for quality of data sent and message-format compliance
controls.statement: Participants are individually responsible for the quality of the data they send and for compliance with the message formats agreed upon, and must ensure the integrity, compliance and functionality of all their systems, including hardware, software, human resources and the data received and transmitted to the ZIPSS. The BoZ is not liable for verifying the accuracy of any data or instructions provided by a Participant or third party, so accountability for accuracy sits with the sending Participant.

sop: Participant issues payment instructions to the ZIPSS in accordance with the Rules.
Participant takes responsibility for the quality of the data it sends and for compliance with agreed message formats.
Participant ensures the integrity, compliance and functionality of its systems and of data received and transmitted to the ZIPSS.

controls.name: ISO 20022 as governing message standard with published usage guidelines
controls.statement: For ZIPSS payment messages Participants must comply with ISO 20022 formatting rules as published on the ZIPSS MyStandards and Readiness Portal. The STP Message Format Specifications published on the BoZ MyStandards and Readiness Portal form part of the technical documentation (Annex 3), and the usage guidelines on the portal define the agreed additional data for ZRA and currency-order payment messages. The standard and its usage guidelines are therefore the governing schema for ZIPSS data exchange, and the Rules do not state a version number.

STP Message Format Specifications listed in Annex 3

Change log of usage-guideline updates communicated to Participants

controls.name: Permitted ZIPSS ISO 20022 message-type set
controls.statement: The Rules enumerate the ISO 20022 message types permitted in ZIPSS: admi.004, admi.007, camt.007, camt.008, camt.025, camt.029, camt.046, camt.047, camt.048, camt.049, camt.050, camt.052, camt.053, camt.054, camt.056, camt.060, camt.103, pacs.002, pacs.004, pacs.008, pacs.009, pacs.010 and pacs.029. Messages of any other type are rejected as unsupported (INVMTTYPE, Annex 10). This is a closed code list that serves as the system's data dictionary entry point.

Participant message-type subscription configuration (camt.053, camt.054 and billing statement options per Annex 14)

controls.name: Immediate validation and controlled return/rejection code lists
controls.statement: Payment instructions sent by Participants are immediately validated by the ZIPSS, and the sender receives an acceptance or rejection message. The point of Technical Acceptance (validated as correctly formatted and accepted for settlement, with an acknowledgement) is the handover point between Participant and ZIPSS. Annex 10 sets out the controlled lists of 35 High Value Payment return codes (for example INVDATEFMT, DUPREF, INVSIG, INVFMT, CANFCO) and six rejection reasons (AGNT, CURR, CUST, CUTA, DUPL, UPAY), which give structured, machine-readable data-quality outcomes. Annex 10 also gives rules such as duplicate detection, past-date and future-date limits, currency validity and schema-rule failure.
evidence: Annex 10 code lists (return codes and rejection reasons) in current version
Sample of acceptance/rejection acknowledgements and pacs.002 status reports sent to Participants
Rejection and return code statistics per Participant and per period
ZIPSS validation rule configuration or message flow and technical specification documents
Participant procedure for handling rejected or cancelled messages

A message is sent to the sending Participant stating whether the instruction is accepted or rejected.
At Technical Acceptance an acknowledgement message is sent to the sending Participant.
Error codes are those listed in Annex 10.

controls.name: Transaction Type Codes and message priority reference table
controls.statement: Participants assign priorities by default using Transaction Type Codes (TTCs), which determine how messages are processed and settled. Annex 17 lists TTC codes (for example 0010 ZECHL, 1030 pacs.008 default, 4000 ILF drawdown, 9999 emergency funds transfer) with default priority and permitted range, and Annex 13 defines the priority ranges by message type. NSIs have the highest priority followed by BoZ payments. Pending-queue order depends first on priority, then on validation time (FIFO). The tables contain apparent inconsistencies (for example a Reserve Operation range printed as 51 to 20), so the reference data needs a controlled owner and version.
evidence: Current TTC reference table (Annex 17) and priority range table (Annex 13) with version and approval record
Reconciliation of Annex 13 to Annex 17 and to ZIPSS system configuration
Participant-type to TTC permission matrix (INVTTCPARTTYPE rule)
Log of priority modifications on pending payments
Rejection statistics for INVDEFPROCTTC, INVTRANTYPEFORTTC and CANINVTTC
sop: Participants assign message priorities by default using the TTCs.
NSIs have the highest priority, followed by BoZ payments.
A Participant may modify the priority of a pending payment by assigning a higher priority code.
Pending payments are settled first by priority and second by time validated, FIFO within each priority.

controls.name: Participant, beneficiary and payment-reference identifiers (BIC, PRN, unique reference)
controls.clause: s.2.0, s.5.4, s.5.7, Annex 4, Annex 7, Glossary (BIC)
controls.statement: Every Participant must have a Swift Business Identifier Code (BIC), or an unlisted BIC assigned by the BoZ, and the Participant BICs are specified in Annex 4. The Payment Reference Number (PRN) must always be used in the appropriate element for all ZRA payment messages. Incoming funds must be applied to beneficiary accounts on the core banking system by reference to at least account name and account number. ASA transactions carry a unique reference number (maximum 13 additional characters). Duplicate messages are rejected (DUPREF).

Participant addition or modification forms (Annex 14) showing BIC and licence number
Sample of ZRA payment messages showing PRN population
Core banking STP configuration showing account name and number matching on incoming messages

sop: Each Participant holds a BIC issued by Swift, or an unlisted BIC assigned by the BoZ.
Use the PRN in the appropriate element for all ZRA payment messages.
Apply incoming payment funds on the core banking system by reference to the account name and account number at a minimum.

controls.name: Correction of erroneous payments with traceable return message
controls.statement: Where a Participant makes a payment in error (duplicate, misdirected, incorrect amount), it must request the receiving Participant in writing to reverse the funds. A receiving Participant that learns of an erroneous credit must inform the sender immediately and reverse as a new instruction using a pacs.004 Return Message that includes the original reference for reconciliation, made to the remitting account. If the error is reported before 12:00 and not reversed the same day, the sender may claim interest at the BoZ overnight lending facility rate. The ZIPSS does not detect content errors or name and number discrepancies, so error correction relies on Participant records and bilateral resolution.

Bilateral dispute correspondence (s.8.1.2) and escalation records under s.19.2

controls.name: System-generated transaction and user-level audit trail (system log)
controls.statement: The ZIPSS generates comprehensive audit trails that Participants can access. At Participant level they record the details of all transactions relating to that Participant, and at user level they record all accesses to the system and the actions of users (the technical audit trail known as the system log). Audit tools include the facility to list all transactions in the ZIPSS for the past ten years and the facility to request defined audit reports from statistical and other tables in the database (BoZ may charge for special reports). Per the Glossary, Participants can view the audit trail of individual transactions and only the BoZ can view the full audit report. The ZIPSS also provides intraday position, settlement account position, account transactions and pending-queue reports (s.11).

controls.name: Transaction record retention and 10-year on-line accessibility
controls.statement: The BoZ, as System Operator, keeps a record of all transactional data according to relevant Zambian law. The BoZ and Participants must comply with Zambian laws and regulations on conservation and archiving of documents; all transactions and accounting data are stored for a period in accordance with relevant Zambian law, and all current transactions and data for the previous 10 years must be accessible on-line in real time. The Rules do not name the specific statute or fixed total retention period beyond the 10-year on-line window.

controls.name: Confidentiality of Participant information and consent-based third-party sharing
controls.statement: The BoZ must maintain strict confidentiality of all information provided by Participants and/or processed through the system. By consenting to the Rules, Participants authorise the BoZ to transfer information relating to them to third parties selected by the BoZ for confidential use in providing services (including data processing), and the BoZ and those third parties may transfer information as required by any law, court, legal process or requesting authority. Materials supplied by the BoZ are confidential, and security procedures, devices, codes and passwords are highly confidential. The BoZ may delegate operational tasks to third parties without affecting its responsibilities (s.1.1). The sharing basis is a blanket contractual consent, with no stated list of recipients, purposes or data categories.

controls.name: Written authority required for auditor and third-party access to Participant data
controls.statement: Where an auditor or any other legal entity wishes to access data about a Participant, the BoZ requires a written instruction from the Participant's authorised signatory or a certified copy of a board resolution of that Participant authorising the auditors, the BoZ or the other legal entity to access the data. A Participant whose access is suspended, disabled or removed retains the right to access its own data outside the system via a request to the BoZ.

controls.name: Operator liability for data integrity, availability and confidentiality
controls.statement: The BoZ's liability as Technical Operator is limited to making the system available, ensuring its cyber security, maintaining data integrity, availability and confidentiality, timely resolution of ZIPSS challenges, and help desk support during operating hours. As Technical Operator it is responsible for the security of system data, software and infrastructure, including managing backups and business continuity. The BoZ is liable only for failure to act in good faith or exercise reasonable care, and is not liable for verifying data accuracy or for failures caused by incorrect Participant use, software errors or communication infrastructure failures.

controls.name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework with ISO/IEC 27001/2 mapping and minimum Participant security measures
controls.statement: Participants must implement, within their overall Cyber Security Policy and Strategy, measures and capabilities based on the NIST Framework for Improving Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity (CSF), with correlative mappings to ISO/IEC 27001/2 controls, and at minimum in line with the Cyber Security Guidelines issued under Gazette Notice 668 of 2023 (19 May 2023). Minimum measures are restricted physical access (including fallback sites), segregation of duties, e-token certificate management, password management (minimum eight characters, mixed case plus number or symbol, 90-day default validity, three login attempts), cyber security awareness training, an incident response plan with recovery and assurance, and a communication and information-sharing strategy. Participants must also adopt the BoZ-issued password policy administered at system level and maintain internal security procedures that safeguard data integrity, availability and confidentiality.
