controls.name: 24-hour cyber incident reporting, fraud notification and technical failure notice
controls.statement: Participants must report major cyber security breaches on their systems and networks to the BoZ and the Cyber Security Incident Reporting Team (CIRT) within 24 hours of discovering the breach, by email to the ZIPSS help desk. All fraudulent activity, whether by staff, customers or anyone else, must be reported to the Director - Payment Systems immediately on becoming aware of it, with as much information as possible and all reasonable assistance. A technical failure preventing the Participant from generating or receiving payments for more than 30 minutes during the day, and any constraining event, must be notified to the BoZ immediately, in writing or by secure email. The Annual Audit Form (Annex 11) asks Participants to confirm whether fraud or cyber attacks occurred and were reported, and whether outages were recorded in a Contingency Event log.

controls.name: Participant Security Administrators and authorised-user lifecycle
controls.statement: Each Participant designates at least two Participant Security Administrators (PUSAs), who set up, amend and remove users, review users, submit the quarterly audit certificates, and manage e-token and certificate issue; the BoZ maintains the list of PUSAs. Access is permitted only to authorised and uniquely identified users named on a signed e-token application form (Annex 15), submitted at least two business days before creation, with the user trained beforehand. Revocation or modification needs a dated, signed written request (Annex 16), normally processed within one business day, and Participants must disable users immediately when they leave. Profile assignment is under dual control and users are reviewed regularly to curtail inactive accounts. The BoZ Administrators alone create user profiles including PUSA profiles, and a PUSA cannot have access to payment entry, management and enquiry functions (Glossary).

controls.name: Quarterly and annual compliance audit certificates and information requests
controls.statement: Each Participant must assess its compliance with the functional, technical, organisational and security provisions of the Rules and submit quarterly and yearly compliance audit certificates to the BoZ on the Annex 11 forms. The quarterly certificate is due six days after quarter end (s.13) and the annual certificate for the preceding year by 31 March. Both are signed by the Chief Operating Officer and the PUSA (s.13), and Annex 11 forms show signature blocks for the Head of ICT and the Participant User Administrator, and describe the quarterly deadline as six business days after month end. Material errors attract a penalty. The BoZ may require system audit reports and working documents, and Participants must provide any requested ZIPSS operations information within five working days; the BoZ may examine controls and contact the Participant's auditors.

controls.name: BoZ publication of ZIPSS monthly and annual payment statistics
controls.statement: The BoZ publishes monthly and annual statistics on its website concerning the volumes and values of payments exchanged through the ZIPSS. The Rules do not define the statistical tables, the aggregation or disclosure-control method, or the publication date, and do not describe the format of the published data.

controls.name: Version control of the Rules, Annexes and Materials with consultation and notice
controls.statement: The Rules include each annex and attachment, supplemented by Materials (user manuals, system documents and other documentation), which may be reviewed and amended every two years or as deemed necessary; where an annex conflicts with the Rules, the annex prevails for the relevant service. The BoZ amends the Rules, Annexes and technical specifications after giving Participants the opportunity to comment, gives 30 calendar days notice before implementation, and may issue complementary instructions that form part of the Rules. Pricing changes are communicated 30 days before implementation. This governs the standard and reference-data versions on which the other controls depend.

controls.name: Approved location and operating characteristics of primary and fall-back facilities
controls.statement: Any primary or fall-back connection linked to the ZIPSS must be located only in a location deemed suitable and approved by the BoZ. A Participant wishing to change the location or operational characteristics of its primary or fall-back facility must present a plan and obtain BoZ written approval in advance, and the BoZ may require changes where the plan poses a risk to ZIPSS operational integrity. Webstations must meet the Annex 5 minimum configuration at all times, and the primary and fall-back IT equipment must be operated by qualified and authorised personnel. The Rules do not state an in-country requirement, so hosting location is controlled by BoZ approval rather than by jurisdiction.

policies.title: Zambia Electronic Clearing House (ZECH) Rules
principles: The Rules set the terms for clearing and settlement of payment instruments and instructions through ZECH for Member/Participating Banks, govern ZECH operations, and standardise the CIC and DDACC payment streams (cl. 1.1-1.3).
The requirements are mandatory ('must' and 'shall'), and no departure from the Rules is allowed (cl. 1.4, 2).

ZECHL is a limited liability company jointly owned by the Bank of Zambia and the Bankers' Association of Zambia (BAZ); BoZ must agree in writing to any new or changed payment system rules and may require changes (cl. 3.66, 11.2, 11.6.2).
DDACC is used only to collect or pay Kwacha within Zambia, and participating banks must not accept foreign exchange amounts for collection (cl. 1.8).
Every interchange of Eligible Items through ZECH is final and irreversible, and items are deemed properly cleared once ZECH declares the clearing closed (cl. 16.1, 21.1).
Eligible Items are subject to the laws of Zambia and BoZ operating circulars (cl. 24.1); damages for violation of law are determined under Zambian law (cl. 23.1).

ZECHL is not liable for a participant's loss except for its own negligence or misconduct, nor for inaccurate transmission and deliveries; claims between participants are resolved directly between them (cl. 18.1-18.5).
Direct Debit is a method of collecting payments; banks are not responsible for any underlying contract between the Service Provider and the Payer (cl. 44.2.1, 64.9.2, 80.3.3).
Payers are protected by the Direct Debit Guarantee: immediate refund of errors, advance notice before collection, and the right to cancel the mandate at any time (cl. 64.6.1).
ZECH must be seen to be independent of individual banks or groups of banks (cl. 10.1.10).
Each Presenting Bank is responsible for ensuring that data files sent to ZECH are complete and accurate in all aspects (cl. 46.1.8).
The Rules are monitored and reviewed by BAZ and BoZ; complaints and suggestions are made in writing to BAZ (cl. 22.3, 26.1).
management_intent: The ZECHL Board appoints a Committee from participants to ensure operations conform strictly to the Rules, and the Management Committee enforces them (cl. 4.2, 4.3).
The daily business of ZECH is conducted under ZECHL supervision, which is responsible for the discipline of participants' representatives and ZECH staff (cl. 4.4).

New participants must have adequate facilities, policies and procedures, business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements, a dedicated PC and software for EFT and CIC, scanners and dedicated fibre connectivity, and must pass an on-site inspection and full file-transmission testing (cl. 8.2.2, 8.2.5-8.2.17).
Banks must deposit and maintain collateral with BoZ as a precondition of membership, with a defined failure-to-settle escalation and timetable (cl. 15, 16, Sch X).

Participants must keep contingency plans and alternate processing sites, notify ZECH in writing of system emergencies, and revert to manual clearing if the whole system fails; ZECHL invokes its Business Continuity Plan if communication and system both fail (cl. 20.1-20.4, 27).
ZECH operates in Lusaka with Kitwe as the disaster recovery site, and participants clear through LECH and, as contingency, KECH (cl. 3.26, 5.4, 5.5).
ZECH must ensure that the sum of all participants' Net Settlement Positions always equals zero and that each settlement statement is signed by an authorised ZECH official (cl. 9.4).

Service Providers must be sponsored and monitored by their Banks, BoZ reviews DDACC operations, and non-compliance carries a rectification period, daily penalties and possible exit (cl. 64.17, 85-88).
ZECHL penalises non-compliant clearing conduct under a scheduled penalty regime (cl. 43, Sch VII).
Disputes escalate from branch managers to Head Offices, then to ZECHL for interpretation, the BAZ Technical Committee and a BAZ-appointed Adjudicator (cl. 17.2, 17.3).
Banks must retain records to reconstruct any clearing or Eligible Item for ten years (cl. 25.1).

controls.name: Participant admission and register of Members and Participating institutions
controls.statement: Membership is restricted to licensed commercial banks that hold shares in ZECHL (7.1.1). Only commercial banks or non-bank financial institutions licensed by BoZ may apply for direct participation (7.2.3.1). The applicant applies in writing to BAZ naming its Settlement Sponsor Bank (8.1.1); BAZ approval takes no more than 90 calendar days, with the applicant told of any extension (8.1.2). A new entrant gives ZECHL a copy of its banking or financial institution licence (8.2.1), undergoes an on-site inspection (8.2.2), and BoZ confirms collateral in writing (8.4.2). ZECH confirms admission in writing to all participants and notifies BoZ and participants of the commencement date (8.4.3, 8.4.5, 8.5.2). Rule 44.3.3 lists Member and Non-Member Participating Banks.

controls.name: Register of branches and branch sort-code maintenance
controls.statement: Banks give ZECHL fourteen days written notice of a branch opening or closure (12.1) and advise BAZ and BoZ; ZECHL circulates the notice to all participants within seven days (12.2). The bank applies in writing to add or delete the branch (12.3). ZECH adds or deletes the branch and its sort code in the system and advises the bank, BoZ and BAZ in writing (12.4), records the change in the register of branches and advises the other participants (12.5). The bank sort code is a mandatory element of bank stamps (30.22.1.4).

controls.statement: Schedule II lists bank branch sort codes as Bank, Area and Branch code components (two-digit columns), and the sort code is carried as six digits in the file layouts (App I, App II). controls.name: Return reason code lists and return/dishonour notice data
controls.statement: Unpaid items must carry the appropriate return reason code on the electronic record, and only answers listed in the Schedule of Standard Answers may be used (32.8.3, 32.8.4). Direct Debits may be returned only with the reason codes in Schedule XI; if the Paying Bank omits the code the Collecting Bank rejects the item with 'failure to include reasons for return by Paying Bank' (58.1, 58.1.1). The code lists are: CIC codes 000 to 086 with 086-199 reserved (App III A, App VIII 2.3, with an applicable-to-unpaid Y/N flag); EFT codes 001 to 082 with 083-199 reserved (App III B, App VIII 3.2, with applicable-to-unpaid and unapplied flags); and Direct Debit codes 01 to 42 with circumstances and special instructions (Sch XI). Reason codes are subject to review (58.2). Dishonour advice (YUFIG) carries eleven stated items (reason, processing date, bank stamp date, collecting clearing centre, collecting branch, amount, cheque serial number, payee name, paying branch, drawer name, signature) with date format DDMMYYYY (32.11.2, 32.11.3). A Yufig sender must send the cheque image within 48 hours of deposit or the collecting bank treats the cheque as paid (32.12.1). Three points need reconciling: Schedule XI uses two-digit DD codes while Appendix VIII uses three-digit EFT codes for the same reasons (for example 'No mandate' is 29 in Sch XI and 070 in App VIII); clauses 57.4.5 and 59.2.6 cite 'Schedule 1' for codes; and code 003 reads 'Free - matched' in the CIC list but 'Free - Discrepancy - Amount Correctly Captured' in the discrepancy file (App I 3.3).

controls.name: Record, file-type, currency, voucher, EFT transaction-type and charge code lists
controls.statement: Appendix VIII defines the reference code lists used in ZECH files: record codes 00 (Header), 88 (Control Voucher) and 99 (Trailer); control voucher types 50-59 (EJ presentment, EJ unpaids, EFT direct credits, direct debits, unpaids, unapplieds, and the four reversal types); file types 30-41 (Electronic Journal 30, EJ Reversal 32, Discrepancy 33, EFT Debit 34, EFT Credit 35, EFT Debit Reversal 36, EFT Credit Reversal 37, Interbank Net Settlement 38, Consolidated Net Settlement 39, EFT ZRA 40, EFT RTGS 41); currency codes 60-69 (ZMK, USD, GBP, EUR, ZAR, BWP, MWK, MZN, NAD, ZMW) with 70-79 reserved; charges and fines codes 400-407 with 408-450 reserved; CIC presentment types 300 (Normal) and 301 (Re-presentment); voucher transaction codes 01-19 (for example 01 Government Cheques, 10 Personal, 11 Corporate, 12 Banker's Payment, 15 Zambian Travellers Cheque, 18 Promissory Notes); and EFT transaction types 200-230 (Salary through School Bill) with 231-299 reserved. ZECH validates that the transaction code is valid (50.4.1.3) and validates Participant Codes against the Transaction Types signed up for (65.5.2). Two gaps: clause 61.7 requires unapplied credits to use 'transaction code 97', which is not in the listed ranges; and the currency table includes foreign currencies although DDACC is Kwacha-only (1.8).

controls.name: CIC electronic journal file layout, naming standard and record formats
controls.statement: Collecting banks must make electronic data files conform to the formats in Appendix I, and the MICR coding, Header Record and file must follow the ZECH-prescribed format (30.16, 30.21.10); batch time and date appear on the file (30.21.12, 30.21.13). Files are named RCRB-YYYYMMDDSSNN-TTT-PCPB (receiving clearing centre code, receiving bank acronym of 5 characters, processing date, session number, two-digit sequence 00-99 so at most 100 files per file type per session, file type, presenting centre code, presenting bank name of 5 characters); file types are EJL, DFL and EJR (App I 1). An EJ file is binary/fixed width with a maximum of 2000 records, structured as File Header (type 00), Control Voucher (88) with cheque presentments, Control Voucher with unpaid cheques, and File Trailer (99); every record is 300 bytes except the trailer, which carries a 48-character SHA384 hash after position 300 (App I 3.1). The header holds file type, YYYYMMDD processing date, presenting and receiving clearing centre sort codes (6 digits each) and an 18-digit file serial number that is unique for a data file within a clearing centre for one month regardless of type (Notes 1, 2). The presentment record holds presentment type (300 or 301), presenting bank sort code, voucher code, currency code, 15-digit left-zero-padded value, amount entry method (0-3), check digit, 13-digit account number, 6-digit bank sort code, 6-digit cheque serial number, a 50-character collection account detail, an 18-character bank reference generated by the core banking system, three image sizes and three 48-character signatures, and an old/new cheque flag; images follow as blobs from position 301. Unpaid records must match the original presentment in fields 2 to 23. A parent bank that clears for another bank appears in the header while the child bank appears in the records.
evidence: Published CIC file specification (Appendix I) with version in use
Sample EJ file, with header, control vouchers, presentments, unpaids and trailer
Data dictionary or schema for the 23-field presentment record
File naming rule configuration and a sample of file names
Rejected-file log showing format errors
Test results from full CIC transmission testing (8.2.16)

controls.name: EFT (DDACC) file layout, naming standard and record formats
controls.statement: DDACC files and instructions must conform to Appendix II (46). The input file is ASCII coded text, in Binary/Fixed Length format with Header Record, Voucher Control Records, DDACC transactions and Trailer Record (46.1.2); a file contains one batch only, holding either credits or debits (46.1.3). EFT files have a maximum of 100,000 records and use the same file-name pattern as CIC with file types DCL, DDL, RCL and RDL (App II 1.1). Every record is 300 bytes except the trailer, which has a 48-character SHA384 hash after position 300. The header carries file type, processing date, presenting and receiving clearing centre sort codes and an 18-digit file serial number. Direct debit and direct credit transaction records carry a 3-digit EFT transaction type, 13-digit destination and originating account numbers, 6-digit destination and originating bank sort codes, 2-digit currency code, 15-digit left-zero-padded total value, 50-character beneficiary name, YYYYMMDD value date, 10-digit Participant ID, 20-character Service Provider customer's account number, 18-character bank reference generated by the core banking system, and a mandatory 70-character transaction details reference. Unpaid and unapplied records begin with a 3-digit return reason code; reversal files add the original file serial number and filename. The trailer holds value and count totals for transactions and unpaids/unapplieds, total record count and the SHA384 hash.
evidence: Published EFT file specification (Appendix II) with version in use
Sample EFT debit, credit, reversal, unpaid and unapplied files
Data dictionary or schema for the 15-field transaction record
File naming rule configuration and sample file names
Rejections for non-ASCII or non-compliant field content (50.4.5)
Test results from full EFT transmission testing (8.2.16)

controls.name: Batch and file integrity: control totals, batch limits and SHA384 hash
controls.statement: Each CIC batch has a maximum of 2,000 items and holds either debit or credit items only (30.21.6, 30.21.7). The Collecting Bank balances the cheque images in each batch with the Batch Control Record in the electronic data file and gives each BCR a distinct ID number (30.21.8, 30.21.9); it corrects unbalanced batches and returns them within the specified time (30.5). In DDACC, transactions must balance with the Voucher Control Records and Trailer, and an out-of-balance file is rejected and returned for correction and retransmission (46.1.7). Presenting banks confirm the validity of the extracted DDACC file and, on receipt of the Validation File, verify its contents, rename it and retransmit it to confirm validity (46.1.9, 46.1.10). Every file trailer carries total values, item counts, total record count and a SHA384 hash generated by the participating bank at file generation to prevent the contents being changed (App I trailer Note 1, App II trailer).
evidence: Batch balancing reports (images versus BCR, VCRs and Trailer)
Evidence that SHA384 hash is generated and checked per file
Logs of out-of-balance files rejected and corrected
Validation File exchange records (receipt, verification, rename and retransmit)
Batch size and debit/credit mix checks (2,000 items; credits or debits only)
BCR ID numbering records
sop: Collecting Bank balances the cheque images in each batch with the Batch Control Record (30.21.8).
Collecting Bank corrects unbalanced batches and returns them within the specified time (30.5).
On receipt of the Validation File, the Presenting Bank verifies the contents, renames the file and retransmits it to ZECH to indicate the input file is valid (46.1.10).

controls.name: ZECH receipt validation and rejection of CIC and DDACC files
controls.statement: ZECH checks for online transmission of the Electronic Data Files and matches the cheque image with the Electronic Data File; where there are no errors it processes and stores the files, and where there are errors or omissions it rejects the file and advises the Collecting Bank with an Error File (31.1-31.4). For DDACC, ZECH validates that all fields are in the prescribed format, that the bank code component is a valid bank and that the transaction code is valid (50.4.1). Validation is at control level (file type and business date) and checks batch content, interface details and that credit and debit control totals reconcile (50.4.2, 50.4.3). If any batch fails, the entire file is rejected and none of its transactions enter the net-settlement position (50.4.4). Rejection reasons include non-ASCII format, non-compliant field content and item totals that differ from the VCRs and Trailer (50.4.5, 50.4.6); no further validation is permitted (50.4.7). ZECH advises and returns the rejected file and does not correct files (50.4.8, 50.4.9). A charge applies for incorrect or incomplete data files (50.5.1).
evidence: ZECH validation rule set for CIC and DDACC files
Error Files and rejection advices sent to presenting banks
Log of rejected files by reason, with bank and date
Evidence that rejected transactions were excluded from net-settlement positions
Schedule VII charge records for incorrect or incomplete data files
sop: ZECH checks online transmission of the electronic data files (31.1).
ZECH matches the cheque image with the Electronic Data File (31.2).
If error-free, ZECH processes the file and stores it for settlement; otherwise it rejects the file and advises the Collecting Bank with an Error File (31.3, 31.4).
For DDACC, ZECH checks field format, bank code validity and transaction code validity, then control-level and batch-level checks (50.4.1-50.4.3).
A file with any failed batch is rejected in its entirety and returned to the Presenting Bank without correction (50.4.4, 50.4.8, 50.4.9).

controls.name: Value limits, Kwacha-only scope and clearing session cut-offs
controls.statement: ZECH clears items not exceeding K100,000.00 for Cheque Image, K100,000.00 for Direct Credits and K50,000.00 for Direct Debits, or as decided by BAZ from time to time (5.2, 45.1). Collecting banks must not include vouchers above K100,000.00 in batches; cheques above the threshold are returned to payees with the answer 'Exceeds ZECH limit' and a penal charge applies (30.21.1-30.21.3). In DDACC a credit above K100,000.00 or a debit above K50,000.00 causes rejection with the answer 'Batch items exceed set limit' (46.1.4-46.1.6; Sch XI code 42 'Exceeds ZECH limit'). DDACC is for Kwacha within Zambia only (1.8). Schedule IV sets DDACC clearing sessions (minimum three daily, increasing to a maximum of twelve per 45.5.1, with session four restricted to credits), CIC transmission and settlement times, and BoZ confirmation times. ZECH may extend a session closing time for an industry problem (5.13) and allow up to fifteen minutes grace in exceptional cases (9.5).
evidence: Configured thresholds in the clearing system and the BAZ decision or notice that last changed them
Rejection log for items above the limits, with answer text used
Penalty or charge records for non-compliance with the limit (30.21.2)
Currency checks showing only Kwacha items were accepted in DDACC
Current Schedule IV session timetable and records of any session extension or grace period granted

controls.name: Cheque image standards, Document Reference Numbers and digital signatures
controls.statement: Each cheque captured in the collecting bank's truncation system is allocated a unique Document Reference Number (DRN) and an authenticating digital signature of the front and back images (30.14). Three images are captured: front black and white TIFF G4 at 200 dpi, front grey scale JPEG and back grey scale JPEG both at 100 dpi and JPEG quality 80 (30.25.1-30.25.3). Image size must not exceed 100 kilobytes in the body of the Rules (30.25.4), whereas Appendix I 2.4 says approximately plus or minus 100 kilobytes per cheque. Each image carries a digital signature (30.24.2, App I 2) and the EJ record holds size and signature for each image (App I 3.2). Public keys are exchanged between ZECH and participating banks (30.21.11). Scanners with MICR encoding must have it disabled and users may enter only Amount and Payee's Name (30.20). Paying Banks verify digital signatures and return images that fail with an appropriate answer (32.1.3), and return unpaid images with their digital signatures (32.8.1). Where a cheque image is issued to a third party, participating banks give undertakings that the images are true copies (30.13). Return codes cover image defects and signature failures (for example 024-029, 031-038, 047-049).
evidence: Image capture configuration (formats, dpi, JPEG quality, size limit)
Evidence of unique DRN allocation per captured cheque
Digital signature generation and verification records
Public key exchange records between ZECH and participating banks
Scanner configuration showing MICR encoding disabled and restricted entry fields
Returns for image-quality and signature-failure reason codes
Undertakings that issued images are true copies (30.13)
sop: Paying Bank verifies the digital signature accompanying each image file (32.1.3).
If an image fails digital signature verification, the Paying Bank returns it with an appropriate answer (32.1.3).
Paying Bank returns unpaid item images with their digital signatures within the agreed times (32.8.1).

controls.name: Discrepancy, recall and reversal file handling
controls.statement: A Discrepancy File corrects a wrongly captured amount; it contains the Discrepancy Amount and the Correct Amount with the Codeline Data and Cheque Image, is not time limited, and must be preceded by written notice giving eight stated data items (amount of discrepancy, captured amount, correct amount, date processed, cheque number, drawee branch, drawer's name, payee's name) (36.2-36.5). It holds a 002 record (amount wrongly captured) and a 003 record (corrected) between a header and trailer, with file type 33 (App I 3.3). A Recall removes an entire erroneous file within the same session before closure, with no formal notice to the Destination Bank and a recall notice to ZECH via the messaging facility (37.2, 37.3, 47.2, 47.3). A Reversal File is sent after session close to reverse an entire file or affected transactions; it carries the exact details of the original except the File Type in the Header Record (38.2, 38.3.3, 38.3.4, 48.3.3, 48.3.4) and, per Appendix I, the original file serial number. Reversal files go within 5 days and later reversals need formal notification before the correcting file (38.3.1, 38.3.2, 48.3.1, 48.3.2); 3.52 says there is no validation beyond 5 days, but App I 3.4 says EJ reversal files are rejected if sent more than 3 days after the original, which conflicts. An original file and its reversal file cannot participate in the same session (38.3.5, 48.3.5). Banks process verified reversals without seeking account holder authority (38.3.6, 48.3.6).
evidence: Discrepancy files with written notices containing the eight required items
Recall notifications sent through the ZECH messaging facility
Reversal files and the originals they reverse (file serial numbers, filenames, file type codes)
Formal notifications for reversals sent after 5 days
Evidence that originals and reversals were in different sessions
Penalty records for sending discrepancy transactions as unpaids (43.16)
Resolution of the 3-day versus 5-day reversal rule
sop: Discrepancy: send formal notification to the paying or collecting bank, then send the discrepancy file with discrepancy amount, correct amount, codeline data and cheque image (36.2, 36.3).
Recall: recall the entire file within the same session before it closes and send a recall notification to ZECH via the messaging facility (37.2, 37.3.2).
Reversal: send the reversal file or transaction within 5 days of the original; after 5 days send formal notification to the destination bank and ZECH first (38.3.1, 38.3.2).

controls.name: Ten-year retention of clearing records, cheque archive and mandate dormancy period
controls.statement: Collecting Member/Participating Banks must retain all pertinent records necessary to reconstruct any clearing or individual Eligible Item for ten years beyond the date of the original 'Outwards' clearing (25.1). Each participating bank maintains a cheque archive of all cheques in its custody for a 'statutory period of ten years' (30.15); the text does not cite the statute. Until a National Archive is established, the collecting bank retains physical cheques after capture and presents images to the paying bank (30.11). Paying Banks hold Payer DDM details on file for a minimum of 13 months from lodgement if no collections occur, or from the date of the last payment (73.1); longer periods require guidance from the Bank and are not approved where mandates might lapse by agreed suspension (73.2). Where collection is suspended beyond the dormancy period a new DDM is required (73.3).
evidence: Records retention schedule showing ten years from original outwards clearing
Cheque archive inventory and sampling of reconstruction of a clearing item
Paying bank DDM records showing 13-month dormancy handling
Requests and bank decisions on dormancy periods greater than 13 months
Statutory citation supporting the ten-year period (not given in the Rules)

controls.name: ZECH archive, backup and in-country disaster recovery
controls.statement: ZECH archives all data and images and backs up all databases (31.6.3, 31.6.4). ZECH provides hard copies of images of processed Eligible Items on written request of a Member/Participating Bank (9.2). ZECH operates in Lusaka with Kitwe as the disaster recovery site (3.26, 5.4) and participants clear through LECH and, as contingency, KECH (5.5). If both communication and system fail, ZECHL invokes the ZECHL BCP to complete the day's DDACC and CIC (27). ZECHL is to establish an archive facility for physical Eligible Items under rules agreed by participants and added as an addendum (41.1, 41.2). Cheques are prepared sorted bank-wise and date-wise with a listing, and cheques submitted without listings for paid cheques are rejected (41.3, 41.4). The text does not state the archive retention period for ZECH's own copy or backup frequency.
evidence: ZECH data and image archive configuration and inventory
Database backup schedule and restore test results
Disaster recovery arrangements for the Kitwe site and recent DR test results
ZECHL Business Continuity Plan
Written requests for image copies and ZECH responses
Physical archive addendum rules and archive listings

controls.name: Communication protocol, encryption, authorised signatories and interface-directory access
controls.statement: Each participant enters into a communication agreement with ZECH and follows the Communication Protocol for transmission and delivery of files (6.1). The protocol includes the encryption and decryption applied at both bank and ZECH and the authorised representatives who may access the participant's database at ZECH, transmit and receive files, confirm transmission, authorise processing, receive messages on incorrect files and correct and retransmit rejected files (6.2). Each participant gives ZECH a list of authorised signatories (6.3) and advises in writing the level of authority of each representative (30.23.4). Electronic Data Files are encrypted using ZECH-specified software and sent over a dedicated network, exceptionally by removable media delivered by the bank's representative with a letter from an authorised signatory in a sealed envelope (30.23.2, 30.23.3, 30.24.3). Public keys are exchanged as an additional security feature (30.21.11). Each participant is allocated a directory on the ZECH database controller; only the Presenting Bank and ZECH have access to its interface directory and output files are available only to the account-holding participant in its own directory (49.2, 50.1, 50.4.11). Paying banks retrieve inward files through authorised officers (32.1.2). The text does not define a data classification scheme.
evidence: Signed communication agreements with ZECH
Communication Protocol document with encryption and decryption specification
Lists of authorised signatories and written level-of-authority letters
Directory access control lists showing only the owning bank and ZECH
Public key exchange records
Removable media delivery letters and sealed-envelope records for exceptional deliveries
sop: Authorised signatory letter and removable media are placed in a sealed envelope when files are delivered on removable storage (30.24.3).
The bank's representative delivers external media to ZECHL under exceptional circumstances (30.23.3).

controls.name: Confidentiality of Service Provider and Payer information and permitted disclosure
controls.statement: Under the Direct Debits Agreement the Bank and each appointed agent treat information relating to the Service Provider as confidential, but (unless consent is prohibited by law) the Service Provider consents to transfer and disclosure to and between the Bank's branches, subsidiaries, representative offices, affiliates and agents and selected third parties, wherever situated, for confidential use in providing the DD services and for data processing, statistical and risk analysis purposes; the Bank may also disclose as required by any law, court, regulator or legal process (App VII 10.4). The Paying Bank does not read the text in the Service Provider's 'official use only' box on the DDM (65.7.5). Paying Banks may confirm Payer details to a Service Provider but are not obliged to, or to disclose additional information about the DDM or Payer's bank details (66.16.5). Transaction and report files are available only to the account-holding participant in its directory (50.4.11). The Rules do not mention personal-data protection legislation or Payer consent for data sharing.
evidence: Executed Direct Debits Agreements containing the confidentiality and consent clause
Register of agents and third parties receiving Service Provider information, with location
Log of disclosures made to courts, regulators or legal process
Policy on confirming Payer details to Service Providers
Access control evidence for participant directories
Analysis of the Rules' disclosure basis against applicable data-protection law

controls.name: Direct Debit Mandate content, advance notice data and mandate lifecycle records
controls.statement: A Paying Bank must hold a valid customer mandate before accepting a direct debit (52.1). The DDM (Form DD 8) must hold eleven stated items: Service Provider name and address, the heading, the Payer's bank name and address, Payer's branch sort code, bank account number, Payer's reference number, Service Provider's bank sort code and account number, the instruction with signature and date, the amount (fixed, or variable subject to a stated maximum) and the payment date in DDMMYY format (65.7.2); additional content is limited to an official-use box and logo (65.7.4), and Appendix V sets form design rules. The Paying Bank validates the DDM, records accepted details in its customer Direct Debit records, and returns rejected DDMs within 3 working days (66.16.1-66.16.3, 66.14.1); an acknowledgement is returned within 3 working days (67.2.1). Each DDM is registered as a Power of Attorney (66.13.3). The Advance Notice (Form DD4) holds total amount, due date, frequency, reference number, notice period and Service Provider name (66.4.1), with a default minimum of 14 working days, in written or electronic form (66.5.1, 66.6.1). Amendment or cancellation takes effect when the Paying Bank or Service Provider receives written notice (64.12.1); a Payer gives the bank written authority at least four business days before payment date (79.1) or the Service Provider at least 10 business days before (79.19.1). A debit returned unpaid three times before the next due date leads the Paying Bank to cancel the DDM and advise Payer and Service Provider (57.5). Service Providers must keep Payer records of DDM lodgement, amendments, cancellations and amounts and dates collected (68.4.1), and apply advices immediately or within 3 working days (79.4, 79.13).
evidence: DDM forms and bank written approval of the design before issue (65.7.1)
Paying bank mandate register (Payer, account, Service Provider, amount, date, status)
Rejected DDM returns and acknowledgements with timings
Advance notices with required contents and proof of issue (not proof of receipt)
Amendment and cancellation advices and their processing dates
Service Provider Payer records covering lodgements, amendments, cancellations and collections
Unpaid count per mandate and cancellation after three returns
sop: Payer completes the DDM and returns it to the Service Provider, who lodges it with the Payer's account-holding branch (66.11.1, 66.12.4).
Paying Bank validates the DDM that the Payer is a customer and it was properly executed, then records it or returns it within 3 working days (66.16.1-66.16.3).
Service Provider allows at least 14 working days from despatch before presenting the first collection (66.15.1).
After three unpaid returns the Paying Bank cancels the DDM and advises Payer and Service Provider (57.5.2).

controls.name: Service Provider onboarding, Participant Codes and indemnity records
controls.statement: An organisation joins DDACC through its Bank, which assesses contractual capacity, financial standing and quality of internal controls (65.4.2), and only corporate bodies may use DDACC (65.2). The Service Provider needs a registered address in Zambia and a local currency account with a commercial bank that participates in interbank clearing (65.4.3); its account is in its own name and held by the Collecting Bank (65.4.7.1). It executes the standard Indemnity (Form DD 1) with a certified authorising resolution (Form DD 2); the liability is unlimited as to time and amount for debits originated before written notice of termination (65.6). Participant Codes identify all Service Providers in DD and those that generate multiple direct credits (65.5.1): the Bank applies to ZECH, ZECH allocates the code and advises all Participating Banks (65.5.3), ZECH validates codes against the Transaction Types signed up for (65.5.2), and the Originating Bank must use the correct Transaction Types for each code (65.5.4). The file layout carries a 10-digit Participant ID. A Service Provider must advise the Bank of changes in legal status and obtain new DDMs (65.6.8, 87.1.1); exit requires one month's written notice from the last input file, with the Bank advising all banks in writing (88.2, 88.3.1.3).
evidence: Register of Service Providers with Participant Code, sponsoring bank and Transaction Types
Bank assessment file (capacity, standing, controls) for each Service Provider
Executed Form DD 1 Indemnity and certified Form DD 2 resolution
ZECH Participant Code allocation requests and advice to participating banks
Records of validation of Participant Codes against Transaction Types
Termination notices and bank advice of termination to all banks
sop: Bank formally applies to ZECH for allocation of a Participant Code to the Service Provider (65.5.3.2).
ZECH allocates the Participant Code and advises all Participating Banks of the code (65.5.3.3).
Service Provider executes the Indemnity only after the authorising resolution is passed and returns both to its Bank (65.6.7, 65.6.11.1).
On exit the Service Provider's Bank withdraws it and advises all banks in writing (88.2).

controls.name: Monitoring of DDACC data originators and rectification of non-compliance
controls.statement: Banks monitor DDACC to ensure required standards are achieved and maintained by Service Providers (64.17.2, 85.6); the Service Provider's Bank satisfies itself of adherence and approves communications literature and technical specification of DDACC submissions (85.1-85.3). Paying Banks check samples of direct debits presented against the operational standards and the lodged mandate (85.8.1.1). BoZ also monitors and reviews DDACC operations (64.17.3). Where BoZ finds non-compliance and allows rectification, the Bank or Service Provider has 14 working days, during which a penalty of up to 50,000 penalty units applies per day, quoted as K180.00 per penalty unit (64.17.4); clause 15.2.11 gives K0.180 per penalty unit for the same unit, which is inconsistent. The Collecting Bank must confirm adherence to ZECH when called upon and monitor Service Providers that fail to settle Indemnity Claims (86.1, 85.8.3.2). Service Provider controls include an individual item limit and a random audit trail on the input report (74.2.1, 74.2.2). Persistent errors lead to exit (87.1.4, 88.4).
evidence: Bank monitoring plan and monitoring reports on Service Providers
Sample checks of presented direct debits against mandates (85.8.1.1)
BoZ review reports and rectification notices with 14-day deadlines
Penalty calculations and clarification of the penalty-unit value
Service Provider item limit settings and audit trail reports (74.2)
Warnings and exit decisions under 88.4
sop: Service Provider passes its DDACC communications literature to its Collecting Bank for approval (85.2).
Bank liaises with a non-conforming Service Provider, sets a time frame for changes and monitors progress (86.2).
Service Provider applies requested changes within the agreed time frame and provides evidence they were made (87.1.3).

controls.name: Net Settlement Positions, consolidated statements and settlement data
controls.statement: ZECH nets cleared Eligible Items to determine Net Settlement Positions (5.6), nets DDACC and CIC separately (5.7, 45.4.1, 10.1.2) and transmits positions to BoZ for each session at designated times (5.9, 5.10, 10.1.4, 50.6.1). ZECH is responsible for consolidating positions (9.3) and must ensure the sum of all participants' Net Settlement Positions always equals zero, with each settlement statement signed by an authorised ZECH official (9.4). ZECH generates electronic reports: NSP for BoZ, NSP for each participant, and reports of NSP, presentments and unpaids (31.7.2), and notifies each participant's designated Head Office office of its position (31.8.1). The CIC NSP statement is the authority for BoZ to credit or debit accounts on delivery date and the DDACC statement is authority immediately on receipt, with participants indemnifying BoZ against incorrect figures from ZECHL (10.1.5-10.1.7, 11.4.1). ZECH advises beneficiary and paying banks of confirmed settlement (50.6.2). Appendix I 1.9 lists CIC reports (returned items, inter-bank clearing statement, statistical, post settlement).
evidence: Signed Consolidated Net Settlement Statements per session
Reconciliation showing the sum of Net Settlement Positions equals zero
Separate CIC and DDACC netting reports
BoZ settlement confirmations and times against Schedule IV
Participant NSP reports, presentment and unpaid reports
Records of the authorised ZECH signatory for settlement statements
sop: ZECH generates the net CIC positions for all sessions (31.7.1).
ZECH transmits Net Settlement Positions to BoZ for settlement at designated times (5.9, 5.10).
BoZ confirms whether each participant has sufficient balances to settle (11.5.1).

policies.title: BoZ Certification Authority Rules
principles: Single-purpose PKI: certificates are used only to authenticate subscribers to the BOZ ZIPSS/CSD system and to digitally sign messages on it; any other use is prohibited (1.1, 1.4.1-1.4.2).
Participants act as Registration Authorities, validate their own subscribers and are responsible for, and may not repudiate, the actions of those subscribers (1.3.2-1.3.3, 4.2.1, 9.2).
No anonymous or pseudonymous subscribers; enrolment is on real names and every subscriber name is unique within a Participant (3.1.1, 3.1.4, 3.1.6).
The CA application and environment are treated as 'Top Secret' under the BOZ Information Security Policy (6.5.2).
Private keys never leave the hardware e-token and are neither backed up, archived nor escrowed (6.1.2, 6.2.2-6.2.4, 4.11).
Dual control and segregation of duties apply to certificate, profile and user administration (four-eyes principle) (3.2.2, 10.2.5, 11.4.5, 11.5.5).
Compliance with the Rules is independently verified by external audit, and all parties must correct deficiencies found (8.1-8.5).
Personal information on subscribers is not published beyond the enrolling Participant (9.4).
management_intent: Provide a trusted, standards-based (RFC 3647) PKI that authenticates every user of the national payment and securities settlement system (ZIPSS/CSD) and makes their transactions non-repudiable (1.1, 10.2.6).
Keep the Bank of Zambia as sole Certification Authority and tightly control who can request, approve and issue certificates (1.3.1, 3.2.2, 10.5).
Maintain a complete, permanent record of issued certificates and CA activity so that disputes and audits can be resolved (5.5, 6.3.1, 10.2.8, 11.3.1).

controls.name: CA environment classified 'Top Secret'
controls.statement: The CA application and its environment shall be assigned the information classification 'Top Secret' and treated accordingly as defined in the BOZ Information Security Policy. Access to PKI information and confidentiality of information used by the CA follow that Policy.
evidence: BOZ Information Security Policy (classification scheme and handling rules for 'Top Secret')
CA asset/classification register showing the CA application and environment as 'Top Secret'
Access control list for PKI repositories held by the ICT Department

controls.name: Permanent retention of certificates and archiving of CA activity logs
controls.statement: All certificates and their public keys, including expired certificates, shall be kept permanently in the CA database. All CA activity logs shall be logged, reviewed by BOZ Internal Audit, backed up under normal BOZ procedures, and archived for the retention period stipulated in the BOZ Information Security Policy. A separate token log register is kept per Participant so that a full history is retained for every token. Audit trails show operator, date and time of every action and are kept on the live system and at the DR site.
evidence: CA database extract showing issued and expired certificates with public keys
CA activity logs and Internal Audit review records
Archive/backup schedule and the retention period set in the BOZ Information Security Policy
Per-Participant token log registers
DR-site replica of audit trail logs
sop: Log every activity on the CA
Internal Audit reviews the CA logs
Back up logs under normal BOZ backup procedures
Archive logs and maintain them for the retention period in the BOZ Information Security Policy
Keep a separate log register for each Participant recording all events for each token

controls.name: Participant-ID code list and subscriber User-ID format
controls.statement: Each Participant has a controlled 3-character ID/code (e.g. BOZ, BBZ, FNB) drawn from the list in 3.1.2. A Subscriber User ID shall be {PARTICIPANT-ID/}{initial of first name}{surname} with the Participant ID in UPPERCASE and the username in lower case; a middle initial is used to resolve name conflicts. All subscriber names enrolled by a Participant shall be unique. In the certificate DN, OU holds the three-character Bank Identification Code, CN the assigned username and C the country code 'ZM'.
evidence: Participant ID/code list (3.1.2) as maintained by BOZ
User ID listing per Participant showing format conformance and uniqueness
Sample issued certificates showing OU, CN and C fields
Completed User Information Request Form CA01 and e-Token Application Form CA02
sop: Form the User ID as the 3-character Participant ID in UPPERCASE, a slash, the first-name initial and the surname in lower case
If two users in the same Participant clash, add the middle initial to differentiate
Set OU to the three-character Bank Identification Code, CN to the assigned username and C to ZM in the certificate DN

controls.name: Cryptographic standards: RSA-2048, SHA-256 and FIPS 140-2 hardware
controls.statement: User certificate keys shall be 2048-bit RSA with SHA-256 as the accepted signature algorithm. Subscriber key pairs shall be generated on e-token cryptographic hardware certified to FIPS 140-2 Level 2 and 3. Key usage for all certificates is digital signature, non-repudiation and key encryption, plus client or server authentication as applicable.
evidence: e-token vendor FIPS 140-2 certificates (Level 2/3)
CA software configuration showing key size and signature algorithm
Sample subscriber and server certificates showing key length, algorithm and key usage extensions

controls.name: Certificate and CRL format standards (X.509)
controls.statement: All certificates shall be X.509 version 3 or later and CRLs shall be created in X.509 v2 or later format. The Rules are based on RFC 3647. Subscriber and Server certificates shall contain the prescribed content fields (subscriber name, Participant organisational identity, public key, country code, issuing CA, signature, algorithm, validity period and serial number). All issued certificates shall comply with the stipulated standard.
evidence: Sample certificates and the current CRL parsed to show X.509 version
Certificate profile configuration in the CA software (EJBCA)
Mapping of the Rules to RFC 3647

controls.name: Subscriber enrolment data provided only by the enrolling Participant
controls.statement: Subscribers are enrolled only by Participants, on real names, with no anonymous or pseudonymous subscribers and no subscriber information in the system that was not provided by the enrolling Participant. Each Participant maintains at BOZ a list of at least three authorised signatories, conveyed by secure methods for physical documents, and two signatures from the list are required on any request to the CA. BOZ accepts a valid application as meaning the Participant has established the subscriber's identity and takes responsibility for that person's actions.
evidence: Register of authorised signatories (minimum three) per Participant held at BOZ
Completed e-Token Application Forms (CA02) bearing two registered signatures
Enrolment records showing the enrolling Participant for each subscriber
sop: Participant identifies its applicant, determines the level of access and requests it using the relevant forms
Two signatories from the registered list sign the request to the CA
CA validates the request for consistency and contacts the Participant if unsure of authenticity
CA logs the request in a database

controls.name: Privacy: no publication of subscriber lists
controls.statement: The CA shall not publish lists of Subscribers to anybody except the enrolling Participants. No other party shall be notified of certificate issuance, and Participant Security Administrators can only access the profiles of their own Group.
evidence: Records of any subscriber-list disclosures, showing recipients limited to the enrolling Participant
Group-level access configuration showing Participant administrators restricted to their own Group
Distribution list for certificate issuance notifications

controls.name: Annual external compliance audit
controls.statement: Compliance with the Rules shall be audited at BOZ by external auditors on an annual basis to give independent assurance, and Participants are expected to have their RA and subscriber enrolment functions audited by their own external auditors. The audit verifies that the policies and procedures are being followed; logs, configuration files and the entire CA system are regularly checked by auditors. All parties must correct any deficiency found.
evidence: Annual external audit report on the CA and PKI
Participant external audit reports covering RA and enrolment functions
Deficiency tracker and corrective-action closure evidence
sop: Appoint BOZ's external auditor annually to audit CA compliance
Participants audit their RA and enrolment functions through their external auditors
Assess whether policies and procedures in the Rules are being followed
All parties correct any deficiency found by the auditor

controls.name: Dual control and segregation of duties in user, profile and certificate administration
controls.statement: Adding, modifying, removing, disabling or activating users and profiles requires approval by a Security Officer different from the one who made the entry (four-eyes principle); until approved a profile cannot be assigned. Certificates may be generated by only one of two authorised ICT staff, the CA Approval Manager approves token requests before the CA Security Administrator issues them, and revocation requires approval by the User Approval Officer and the CA Approval Manager. Users cannot both enter and approve transactions, and token providers must not be system users.
evidence: System user and profile audit trail showing maker and approver are different
Signed e-Token Application (CA02) and Revocation (CA03) forms with Approval Manager sign-off
List of the two staff authorised to generate certificates
Profile and role matrix showing segregation of transaction entry and approval
sop: Security Officer enters or modifies the user or profile, which is placed in APPROVE status
A different Security Officer approves or rejects (rejected profiles go to REPAIR)
CA Approval Manager approves the request before the CA Security Administrator issues the certificate and e-token
Revocation is approved by the User Approval Officer and then the CA Approval Manager before the token is revoked

controls.name: Certificate lifecycle: issuance log, 12-month validity, renewal and revocation
controls.statement: Subscriber certificates are valid for 1 year and the CA's own certificate for 10 years; certificates must be renewed every 12 months, with a 2-week advance warning from the PUSA and spread-out renewal dates. Certificates are not re-keyed, modified or suspended, only revoked. Revocation is processed by the end of the business day received with no grace period, the CRL is updated on each revocation and reloaded and replicated to the DR site before next-day start-up. The CA Security Administrator logs each issue with bank name, authorising person, common name, issue and expiry dates, token serial number, certificate ID, issue and renewal numbers.
evidence: Token log register with issue/expiry dates, token serial, certificate ID, issue and renewal numbers
Signed Renewal Request and Revocation (CA03) forms
CRL publication history and DR replication confirmation
Report of certificates approaching expiry and renewal warnings issued
sop: Participant tracks certificate expiry and requests renewal before expiry using the Renewal Request form
CA checks subscriber information in the CA database, then issues a new certificate with new keys on an e-token
Participant returns the expired e-token to BOZ through the authorised delegated person
On revocation, CASA reloads the CRL onto the system in time for next-day start-up and replicates it to the DR site immediately
Username is immediately disabled when a token is revoked
Lost or damaged tokens have their certificate revoked and a new token re-issued, with the issue number updated in the token log

controls.name: Private key protection: no backup, archival, escrow or export
controls.statement: The private key shall never leave the e-token hardware module where it is generated. The CA does not back up, archive or escrow private keys. On renewal the previous certificate is deleted along with its keys and the old keys are placed in the CRL. e-tokens may only be inserted into BOZ ZIPSS/CSD workstations and certificates are used only with the user ID and password issued to the individual Subscriber.
evidence: CA configuration confirming no private key backup or escrow function is enabled
e-token vendor specification showing non-exportable private keys
Records of expired token returns and certificate deletion on renewal

controls.name: Physical, network and business continuity protection of the CA
controls.statement: The CA server shall be hosted in the BOZ ICT Server Room, a controlled 'Red area' with access limited to authorised management, computer operators and security personnel, and supervised access for auditors, suppliers, cleaners and premises staff. Network access controls follow the ICT Security manual, and the CA setup is backed up under the BOZ Business Continuity Plan. The ZIPSS/CSD system is fully duplicated at a DR site and every transaction is logged and replicated to it. Operator passwords are individual, complex, minimum 6 characters and renewed at least every 3 months.
evidence: Server Room access control list and visitor log
BOZ Business Continuity Plan covering the CA
DR site replication status reports
ICT Security manual network access rules and password policy configuration
sop: Supervise computer room access by auditors, cleaners, suppliers' engineers and premises staff at all times by a computer operator or BOZ management

policies.title: Microfinance Regulations
principles: The Bank of Zambia is the regulatory authority for microfinance institutions under the Banking and Financial Services Act (Cap. 387) (reg 4).
A microfinance institution and its staff shall conduct all transactions in strict confidence and maintain customer confidentiality (reg 44).
Microfinance institutions conduct business with integrity, prudence and professional skill and engage only in bona fide transactions (reg 28).
Borrowers must be told the cost of borrowing in writing at the time credit is provided (reg 30, Form MF5).
Only licensed institutions may conduct microfinance business; licences are issued, displayed and revoked by the Registrar under defined conditions (regs 6-13).
Institutions report to the Bank of Zambia in prescribed formats and frequency and disclose audited financial statements or management accounts (regs 38-39).
Documents that are false in a material particular, and obstruction of inspection or destruction of documents, are offences (regs 43, 37(3), 47).
management_intent: Protect low-income and small-enterprise customers of microfinance institutions through disclosure, display of rights and confidentiality (regs 30, 31, 44).
Give the Bank of Zambia the information it needs for supervision, through returns, inspections, vital statistics on key persons and power to call for operational details (regs 5, 37, 38, 45).
Keep a regulated, licensed microfinance sector in which ownership, management and category changes are approved in advance (regs 18-19, 34-36).

controls.name: Customer confidentiality of transactions
controls.statement: A microfinance institution and its staff shall ensure that all transactions are conducted in strict confidence and that the confidentiality of customers is maintained.
evidence: Institution confidentiality policy and staff confidentiality undertakings
Access control listing for customer and loan records
Register of any customer-information disclosures and their legal basis
Staff training records on customer confidentiality

controls.name: Vital statistics (personal data) of persons required by the Bank of Zambia, Form MF6
controls.clause: Reg 45; First Schedule Form MF6; Form MF2
controls.statement: The Bank of Zambia may require a person to submit vital statistics in Form MF6. The form collects personal data including name, date of birth, identity card, passport/NRC and work permit numbers, residential and business addresses, marital status, number of children, spouse, next of kin, parents' names, education, employment record and employer reference. The Directors' Questionnaire (Form MF2) is marked confidential and not available for inspection by the public.
evidence: Completed Form MF6 submissions held by the Bank of Zambia and the institution
Completed Form MF2 Directors' Questionnaires
Access restrictions applied to the MF2/MF6 files
Register of persons for whom vital statistics were requested

controls.name: Written disclosure of cost of borrowing, Form MF5
controls.statement: A deposit-taking microfinance institution that provides credit facilities to a customer shall, at the time of providing the service, disclose to the customer in a written statement the cost of borrowing, in Form MF5. The statement carries 19 prescribed items, including lender and borrower name and address, security and collateral, principal and charges financed, interest rate per annum and factors that vary it, loan term, total cost of borrowing, each charge financed, prepayment terms, default charges, date of statement, and the name and signature of the institution's representative.
evidence: Signed Form MF5 disclosure statements for a sample of loans
Loan agreements and disbursement records matched to MF5 date and amounts
MF5 template showing all 19 prescribed content items
Customer complaints log on disclosure
sop: Provide the written MF5 statement to the customer at the time the credit facility is provided
Complete all 19 prescribed items in the statement, including date and the name and signature of the institution's representative

controls.name: Prescribed reporting formats and frequency of returns
controls.statement: The Bank of Zambia prescribes reporting formats and the frequency of reporting for a microfinance institution, including balance sheets, income statements, computation of capital, computation schedules, liquidity statements, loan repayment schedules and other information it considers necessary. The Bank may also require an institution to furnish details of any of its operations, and every institution must maintain liquid assets in ratios determined by the Bank. Failure to comply is an offence with a daily penalty for continuing breach.
evidence: Bank of Zambia returns templates and reporting calendar for microfinance institutions
Submitted returns with date-stamped acknowledgement of receipt
Liquid asset ratio computations
Correspondence on information calls under reg 5

controls.name: Audited financial statements and management accounts disclosure
controls.statement: A microfinance institution that is a company shall submit an audited financial statement or management accounts to the Bank of Zambia, its shareholders and other interested persons; a non-company shall submit management accounts and, where available, audited accounts. A deposit-taking institution shall display its balance sheet and income statement on its business premises. Auditors named in the licence application are subject to the Bank of Zambia's approval, and the institution must notify the Bank 30 days before any significant business arrangement or joint venture.
evidence: Audited financial statements or management accounts submitted for each year
Evidence of distribution to shareholders and the Bank of Zambia
Photograph or inspection record of the balance sheet and income statement displayed at the premises
Bank of Zambia approval of the institution's auditors

controls.name: Licensing records and public notice of licence status
controls.statement: A person intending to establish a microfinance institution applies to the Registrar in Form MF1 with prescribed documents; the Registrar considers a complete application within 180 days and issues a licence in Form MF3 on approval and payment of the fee. The licence names the licensee and place of business and is displayed at premises and branches. On revocation the licensee surrenders every displayed copy and the Registrar publishes a notice of revocation in the Gazette and a newspaper of general circulation. The Regulations do not expressly require a public licence register to be kept.
evidence: Form MF1 application files with the MF2 questionnaires and attachments
Issued MF3 licences with licence and serial numbers
Registrar decision records and the 180-day processing log
Gazette and newspaper notices of revocation
Licence displayed at premises and certified copies at each branch
sop: Applicant files Form MF1 with incorporation evidence, voting rights designation, head office addresses, MF2 questionnaire, business plan, auditor and banker details
Registrar considers the complete application within 180 days and approves or refuses
On approval and payment of the fee, Registrar issues the licence in Form MF3
On revocation, licensee surrenders each displayed copy and the Registrar publishes the notice in the Gazette and a newspaper of general circulation

controls.name: Notification and approval of changes in branches, ownership and key persons
controls.statement: A microfinance institution shall give the Bank of Zambia written notice within 14 days of opening a branch and at least 60 days before closing a place of business, apply 90 days ahead on Form MF4 to change licence category, and obtain prior written approval for changes to shareholders, directors, chief executive officer, chief financial officer or any manager. Persons may not acquire control above 25 percent (deposit-taking) or 50 percent (non-deposit-taking company) of votes without approval, and directors and senior managers must satisfy the fit-and-proper criteria.
evidence: Branch opening and closure notices to the Bank of Zambia with dates
Form MF4 category-change applications and board resolutions
Bank of Zambia approvals for shareholder and management changes
Fit-and-proper vetting files for directors and senior management
Shareholder register showing voting percentages
sop: Notify the Bank of Zambia in writing within 14 days of opening a new branch, stating its location
Notify the Bank in writing at least 60 days before closing a place of business
Apply in Form MF4 ninety days prior to an intended change of licence category

controls.name: Inspection access to books and records
controls.statement: The Bank of Zambia or a person it authorises may inspect any microfinance institution and its books or accounts at any time at any place of business; the institution shall produce its books and accounts and ensure staff furnish reasonably required information. Obstructing an inspector, destroying, mutilating or hiding a document with intent to evade the Regulations, or issuing a document that is false in a material particular are offences.
evidence: Inspection reports and requests for information
Books, accounts and loan records produced to inspectors
Record retention practice demonstrating documents are not destroyed or altered
Sign-off or certification on documents issued to the regulator

policies.title: Bureau de Change Regulations
principles: The Bank of Zambia is the regulatory authority for the Regulations, and the Registrar may delegate powers (regs 3-4).
Only a bank or a company licensed as a bureau de change may deal in foreign exchange (reg 8).
Every purchase and sale of foreign exchange is covered by an accurate official receipt in the prescribed form, and receipts are never issued for any other purpose (reg 21).
All transactions conducted by the bureau or its staff are done and maintained in the strictest confidence (reg 38).
Complete records and registers of the foreign exchange business are kept, and books, accounts, records and registers are retained for at least six years from the date of the transaction (reg 31).
The bureau reports to the Bank of Zambia through monthly, weekly and quarterly returns and annual audited accounts (regs 29-30), and furnishes transaction details when called for (reg 5).
The bureau acts with integrity, prudence and professional skill, engages only in bona fide transactions and avoids transactions that may involve or facilitate money laundering (reg 23).
Counterfeit foreign exchange is recorded, reported at once to the Bank of Zambia and the police, confiscated and handed to the police (reg 33).
Documents required under the Regulations must be true: issuing or signing a document that is false in a material particular is an offence (reg 32).
management_intent: Bureau management maintains adequate accounting and control systems and keeps complete records and registers relating to its foreign exchange business (reg 31(1)).
Bureau management keeps its books, accounts, records and registers for at least six years from the date of each transaction (reg 31(2)).
Bureau management and staff keep every transaction in the strictest confidence (reg 38).

The bureau submits a monthly return of all purchases and sales, a weekly return of sales, purchases and open position, quarterly financial statements within ten working days of quarter end, audited accounts within three months of year end, and any other return the Bank of Zambia requires (regs 29-30).
The bureau produces its books and accounts to Bank of Zambia inspectors and ensures staff furnish the information inspectors reasonably require (reg 28(2)).
The bureau conducts its business with integrity, prudence and professional skill, accepts only bona fide transactions and exercises care and caution to avoid money laundering (reg 23).
The bureau records every counterfeit foreign exchange case, reports it immediately to the Bank of Zambia and the police, and hands the counterfeit to the police (reg 33).
The bureau obtains prior Bank of Zambia approval before changing its shareholding, directors, senior management or name, or opening or moving a place of business (regs 25-26).
The bureau keeps within the open foreign exchange position and the transaction limits the Bank of Zambia prescribes (regs 6-7).

controls.name: Six-year retention of books, records and registers
controls.statement: A bureau must maintain adequate accounting and control systems and keep complete records and registers relating to its foreign exchange business (reg 31(1)). It must keep its books, accounts, records and registers for at least six years from the date on which the transaction to which they relate takes place (reg 31(2)). With intent to evade the Regulations, destroying, mutilating, secreting or removing a document is an offence (reg 39(f)). The Regulations do not say what happens to personal data on the records after six years.
evidence: Records retention policy stating the six-year minimum and that the period runs from the transaction date
Index of books, accounts, records and registers held, showing transaction dates
Sample of records more than five years old, retrieved on request
Destruction log showing no destruction of records younger than six years
Description of the accounting and control systems used for the foreign exchange business

controls.name: Official receipts capturing customer identity and transaction data
controls.statement: A bureau must issue an accurate official receipt in the prescribed form for every sale and purchase of foreign exchange (reg 21(1)), and must not issue a receipt for any purpose other than covering an actual purchase or sale (reg 21(2)). The identity data is set by the prescribed forms in the Schedule rather than by the text of regs 21-22: the receipt forms (V, VI, VIII, VII) carry a serial number, bureau name and stamp, date, currency, amount, rate and kwacha equivalent, the customer's name, nationality, ID or passport number, permanent residential address and signature, the bureau official's signature, and (cash purchase and travellers cheque forms) the declared use or source of the foreign currency and (travellers cheque and bank draft forms) the cheque or draft number and issuer. Source inconsistency: reg 21 refers only to Form V, while four receipt forms appear in the Schedule.
evidence: Receipt books or electronic receipt system with serial number control
Sample of receipts of each form type showing all fields completed, including ID or passport number and address
Reconciliation of receipt serial numbers to the transaction ledger and to the returns submitted to the Bank of Zambia
Register of voided or spoiled receipts
Evidence that receipts are not issued except for an actual purchase or sale

controls.name: Displayed exchange rates and commissions, and transacting within them
controls.statement: A bureau must display exchange rates in a conspicuous place at every premises in accordance with Bank of Zambia guidelines (reg 22(1)), must buy and sell at or within the displayed rates (reg 22(2)), and must display any commission or other charge clearly and prominently (reg 22(3)). Subject to the anti-money-laundering duty in reg 23, it may not refuse to buy or sell at or within the indicated rates where the foreign exchange is available (reg 24). Contravening reg 22 is an offence (reg 22(4)). The Bank of Zambia guidelines on display are not in the supplied text.
evidence: Dated record or photograph of the displayed rate board and commission notice at each premises
Rate history log showing displayed buying and selling rates by date and time
Reconciliation of rates on receipts to the displayed rates at the time of the transaction
Copy of the Bank of Zambia display guidelines applied
Refusal-to-trade log with the reason, including any reg 23 basis

controls.name: Strict confidentiality of transactions
controls.statement: A bureau and its members of staff must conduct and ensure that all transactions conducted by the bureau or any staff member are done and maintained in the strictest confidence (reg 38). The Regulations define no classification levels and no exceptions to the duty; the only disclosures they expressly require are to the Bank of Zambia (regs 5, 28-30, 33) and, for counterfeit foreign exchange, the police (reg 33). Contravening a duty imposed by the Regulations is an offence (reg 39(g)).
evidence: Confidentiality policy and staff confidentiality undertakings
Access control list for receipts, transaction records and registers, showing who may view customer identity data
Disclosure log showing each disclosure of transaction information and its legal basis (Bank of Zambia request, police report)
Staff training or briefing records on reg 38
Physical and electronic safeguards for stored receipts

controls.name: Periodic returns and audited accounts to the Bank of Zambia
controls.statement: A bureau must submit a monthly return of all purchases and sales of foreign exchange in Form VII (reg 30(1)); a weekly return of sales, purchases and open foreign exchange position, not later than close of business on the first working day of the week after the week reported (reg 30(2)(a)); quarterly balance sheet, profit and loss account and cash flow statement within ten working days after quarter end, in the form the Bank of Zambia prescribes (reg 30(2)(b)); and any other return the Bank of Zambia requires (reg 30(2)(c)). It must also submit audited accounts within three months after its financial year end (reg 29(1)), and furnish details or returns of its transactions in a format the Bank of Zambia prescribes when required (reg 5). Late or missing returns attract a fine plus a daily fine (regs 29(2), 30(3)). A document required under the Regulations that is false in a material particular is an offence (reg 32). Source inconsistency: reg 30(1) names Form VII, but Form VII in the Schedule is a sale-of-foreign-currency receipt and no monthly return form appears in the supplied text.
evidence: Monthly, weekly and quarterly returns as submitted, with submission timestamps and Bank of Zambia acknowledgements
Compliance calendar showing weekly, ten-working-day and three-month deadlines
Reconciliation of each return to the transaction ledger and receipts
Audited accounts and the date they were lodged with the Bank of Zambia
Bank of Zambia prescribed formats for the returns, and any ad hoc return requests and responses
Sign-off record for the accuracy of each return
sop: Submit the weekly return of sales, purchases and open position not later than close of business on the first working day of the following week (reg 30(2)(a))
Submit the quarterly balance sheet, profit and loss account and cash flow statement within ten working days after the end of each quarter (reg 30(2)(b))
Submit audited accounts not later than three months after the end of the financial year (reg 29(1))

controls.name: Bank of Zambia inspection access and information requests
controls.statement: The Registrar, the Bank of Zambia or a person they authorise may at any time inspect any bureau and its books of accounts at any place where it conducts business (reg 28(1)). The bureau must produce its books and accounts to the inspector and ensure its staff furnish the information the inspector reasonably requires (reg 28(2)). Obstructing or hindering an inspection is an offence (reg 28(3)), as are obstructing a person exercising powers under the Regulations and failing to provide required information (reg 39(b), (e)).
evidence: Inspection authorisations presented by inspectors and the inspection access record
Record of books and accounts produced and of staff information supplied
Findings and responses from past inspections
Log of Bank of Zambia information requests and the dates answered
sop: Produce the books and accounts to the inspector (reg 28(2))
Ensure staff furnish the information the inspector may reasonably require (reg 28(2))

controls.name: Anti-money-laundering care and transaction limits
controls.statement: A bureau must conduct its business with integrity, prudence and professional skill, engage only in bona fide transactions, and exercise care and caution to avoid transactions that may involve or facilitate money laundering (reg 23). The duty to buy and sell at the indicated rates is subject to this duty (reg 24). The Bank of Zambia may prescribe maximum or minimum amounts for over-the-counter cash transactions (reg 6), and purchases or sales outside those limits are an offence (reg 39(c)). The Regulations prescribe no customer due diligence steps, thresholds or suspicious transaction reporting procedure and name no anti-money-laundering statute; those must come from other instruments.
evidence: Anti-money-laundering policy and procedures, with the governing law and version named
Bank of Zambia prescribed transaction limits currently in force and evidence they are applied at the till
Records of refused or escalated transactions with the reasoning
Staff training records on money-laundering risk
Transaction monitoring or review records

controls.name: Counterfeit foreign exchange register and immediate reporting
controls.statement: A bureau must record any case involving counterfeit foreign exchange and immediately, as the case occurs, report it to the Bank of Zambia and to the police (reg 33(1)). It must confiscate any counterfeit foreign exchange that comes into its possession and immediately hand it to the police (reg 33(2)). The Regulations prescribe no form for the record and no data elements; the six-year retention in reg 31(2) applies to the register.
evidence: Counterfeit register with an entry for each case (date, instrument, amount, how detected, action taken)
Reports to the Bank of Zambia and the police for each case, with timestamps showing immediacy
Police handover receipts for confiscated counterfeit instruments
Nil-case confirmation or review record where no cases arose
sop: Record the counterfeit foreign exchange case (reg 33(1))
Report the matter immediately to the Bank of Zambia and to the police (reg 33(1))
Confiscate the counterfeit foreign exchange and immediately hand it over to the police (reg 33(2))

controls.name: Applicant and officer vetting data, and approval of changes
controls.statement: A licence application must be accompanied by documents including certified copies of directors' passports, the vital statistics form (Form II) and the directors' questionnaire (Form III) (reg 9(3)).
