Form II collects personal data such as date and place of birth, passport or NRC number, marital status, number of children, spouse, parents, next of kin, immigration and work permit numbers, education and employment record. Form III is marked 'Confidential and not available for inspection by the public', and its declaration commits the director to notify the Registrar of material changes to the information within 21 days. No person may be appointed director, officer or manager unless fit and proper and not otherwise disqualified (reg 34). A bureau may not change its shareholding, directors, senior management or name without prior Bank of Zambia approval (reg 26). The Regulations set no retention period for application files.
evidence: Licence application files with Forms II, III and IX and the supporting documents
Fit and proper assessment record for each director, officer and manager against reg 34
Bank of Zambia prior approvals for changes in shareholding, directors, senior management or name
Notices of material change to Form III information, with receipt dates against the 21-day undertaking
Access controls and storage arrangements for the confidential forms
Retention and disposal decision for application files

controls.name: Open foreign exchange position and capital computation
controls.statement: The maximum open foreign exchange position a bureau may hold at close of business on any day, being foreign exchange on hand plus balances in foreign exchange accounts with banks, may not exceed a percentage of the regulatory capital prescribed by the Bank of Zambia, and any excess must be sold (reg 7). The Bank of Zambia prescribes minimum primary and regulatory capital by Gazette notice (reg 18(1)), and the bureau's capital is computed on the Form X schedule (paid-up capital, reserves, deductions, primary capital, eligible secondary capital, minimum required and excess or deficiency). The percentage in reg 7(1) and the Gazette capital notice are not in the supplied text, and the open position is also reported in the weekly return (reg 30(2)(a)).
evidence: Daily open position calculation (foreign exchange on hand plus bank balances in foreign exchange accounts)
Completed Form X capital computation with supporting balances
Gazette notice prescribing minimum capital and the Bank of Zambia instruction setting the open position percentage
Records of sales of excess foreign exchange to bring the position within limit
Reconciliation of the weekly return open position to the daily calculation

policies.title: Banking and Financial Services (Classification and Provisioning of Loans) Regulations
principles: 'Classification' in these Regulations means credit classification: a loan is graded by repayment quality (Pass, Substandard, Doubtful, Loss) to drive non-accrual treatment and provisioning (regs 17-18). It is not data or information classification and creates no confidentiality or sensitivity levels.
The Board is responsible for the loans policy and for a written loan review system, which it reviews and approves at least once a year (regs 4, 5).
All loans are regularly evaluated using an objective grading system consistent with the Regulations (reg 5(2)(c)).
Loans that have, or are likely to have, a problem are identified, classified and placed on non-accrual status in accordance with the Regulations (reg 5(2)(d), regs 7-12).

The Allowance for Loan Losses Account is kept at the best possible estimate of probable loan-related losses on and off the balance sheet, and meets the minimum provisioning percentages (regs 13, 15, 18).
A loan loss or recovery goes through the Allowance for Loan Losses Account and never directly to retained earnings or any other capital-related account (reg 14).
Reasonable records supporting the evaluations and entries are kept at all times and made available to the Bank of Zambia for inspection and review (regs 6(6), 19).
The Bank of Zambia may vary a provisioning level only in exceptional circumstances, with its prior written approval, for not more than one year (reg 18(4)).
management_intent: The Board adopts a loans policy that specifies at a minimum the standards for loans and extensions of credit, the lending and approving functions, delegation of responsibilities and the process for reviewing loan quality (reg 4).

The Board establishes in writing a loan review system that identifies risk, assures the adequacy of the Allowance for Loan Losses Account and reflects the result properly in the financial statements (reg 5(1)).
Executive management and the Board are at all times adequately informed about portfolio risk (reg 5(2)(b)).

A Loans Review Committee of at least three Board members, including the Chief Executive Officer, reviews the quality and collectability of all loans at least every calendar quarter and reports in detail directly to the Board, which takes appropriate action (reg 6).

Every loan is classified into one of the prescribed grades, and adverse classification can be warranted even for a current loan where repayment terms were too liberal or a delinquency was cured by modification, refinancing or additional advances (reg 17).
Management maintains an allowance it considers adequate to absorb all credit-related losses and that at least meets the minimum provisioning requirements (reg 15(1)).
Management determinations that a loan is collectable are supported by a current, well-documented credit evaluation and the borrower's historical repayment performance (reg 9(5)).
The bank or financial institution reports its loan classification and provisioning position to the Bank of Zambia within ten days after the end of every month (reg 20).

controls.name: Board-adopted loans policy
controls.statement: The Board must adopt a loans policy specifying, at a minimum, the standards for loans and extensions of credit, and the institution's lending and loan-approving functions, delegation of responsibilities and the process of reviewing loan quality.
evidence: Board-approved loans policy with approval date and version
Board minute adopting or reviewing the policy
Delegation of authority matrix for lending and loan approval
Description of the loan quality review process

controls.name: Written loan review system, approved annually by the Board
controls.statement: The Board must establish a written loan review system that identifies risk, assures the adequacy of the Allowance for Loan Losses Account and reflects the result in the financial statements. At a minimum it must ensure the portfolio conforms to the loans policy, keep management and the Board informed of portfolio risk, evaluate all loans regularly using an objective grading system consistent with the Regulations, identify and classify problem loans and place them on non-accrual status, make timely provisions and write-offs, and reflect allowances and provisions in the financial statements (reg 5(1)-(2)). The system must be reassessed regularly and submitted to the Board at least once a year for review and approval (reg 5(3)).
evidence: Written loan review system document with version and approval date
Board minute showing annual review and approval of the system
Documented objective grading methodology used to evaluate loans
Management reports on portfolio risk sent to the executive and the Board
Reassessment record showing review against current circumstances
sop: Reassess the loan review system on a regular basis in the light of current circumstances (reg 5(3))
Submit the loan review system to the Board at least once a year for review and approval (reg 5(3))

controls.name: Loans Review Committee and quarterly portfolio review
controls.statement: Every bank or financial institution must have a Loans Review Committee of not less than three members, appointed by the Board from among its members, with the Chief Executive Officer as a member (reg 6(1)-(3)). Through the committee it must, at least once every calendar quarter, review the quality and collectability of all loans in the portfolio including accrued and unpaid interest (reg 6(4)). The committee must immediately afterwards make a detailed report of the review directly to the Board, which must take appropriate action (reg 6(5)).
evidence: Board resolution appointing the committee and its member list showing the Chief Executive Officer and at least three members
Quarterly review papers covering the whole loan portfolio and accrued and unpaid interest
Detailed committee report to the Board for each quarter, with date against the review date
Board minutes recording the action taken on each committee report
sop: Review the quality and collectability of all loans, including accrued and unpaid interest, at least once every calendar quarter (reg 6(4))
Immediately after the review, make a detailed report directly to the Board (reg 6(5))
Board takes appropriate action on the report (reg 6(5))

controls.name: Loan grade code list (credit classification)
controls.statement: Every loan must be classified by the institution into a prescribed grade (reg 17(1)). Note that 'classification' here is credit classification of loan quality, not data classification. The grades are: Pass (current, performing and fully protected by the borrower's worth and paying capacity or collateral, reg 17(3)); Substandard (at a minimum, in arrears 90 days or more but under 120 days, reg 17(4)(b)); Doubtful (all substandard weaknesses and collection in full highly questionable; at a minimum, arrears of 120 days or more but under 180 days, reg 17(5)); and Loss (fully provisioned when identified, reg 18(3); 180 days and over in the First Schedule). An adverse classification can be warranted even where a loan is current (reg 17(2)). Source inconsistencies to resolve before the grades are used as a controlled code list: reg 17(4)(a) introduces a 'standard' category for inadequately protected loans that does not appear in the First Schedule; Loss has no definition in reg 17 and is defined only through reg 18(3) and the First Schedule.
evidence: Loan grading methodology mapping each of Pass, Substandard, Doubtful and Loss to the criteria and days-in-arrears thresholds
Loan-level extract showing the grade field and days past due for each loan
Reconciliation of recorded grades to days-past-due minimum thresholds
Log of adverse classifications applied under reg 17(2) with reasons
Definition of how 'standard' in reg 17(4)(a) is treated in the institution's own grade list

controls.name: Minimum provisioning percentages by grade and exemptions
controls.statement: The minimum provisioning percentages in the First Schedule apply to the corresponding loan grades: Pass at bank discretion; Substandard 20 per cent (90-119 days); Doubtful 50 per cent (120-179 days); Loss 100 per cent (180 days and over) (reg 18(1)). Any loan or portion fully secured by cash, a segregated deposit in the lending bank or a security issued by the Government of Zambia is exempt (reg 18(2)). A Loss loan or portion must be fully provisioned when the loss is identified (reg 18(3)). The Bank of Zambia may vary a provisioning level only in exceptional circumstances, with prior written approval, for not more than one year (reg 18(4)).
evidence: Provisioning computation by loan and grade against the First Schedule percentages
Reconciliation of required provisions to the balance in the Allowance for Loan Losses Account
List of loans or portions treated as exempt under reg 18(2), with the cash, segregated deposit or Government security evidence
Record of Loss loans showing the date the loss was identified and the date full provision was made
Bank of Zambia written approval for any variation of a provisioning level, with its terms and expiry

controls.name: Non-accrual status, interest reversal and restoration
controls.statement: A loan must be placed on non-accrual status where collectability of principal or interest is in reasonable doubt, a specific provision exists, it has been written off (other than a restructured loan), or principal or interest has been in default 90 days or more (or the account has been inactive 90 days with insufficient deposits to cover capitalised interest) (reg 7). Previously accrued uncollected interest must be reversed by the end of the quarter of transfer, current-quarter interest against that quarter's income, and other periods' interest charged to the Allowance (reg 8). Cash received is applied first to due principal (reg 9). Restoration to accrual requires payments to be fully current with senior management finding no reasonable doubt, or the loan to be well secured and in the process of recovery (reg 10), and a renegotiated loan returns to performing status only at a market-equivalent rate with documented management determination (reg 11). When one loan to a borrower is non-accrual, the others must be evaluated (reg 12). Any determination that a loan is collectable must rest on a current, well-documented credit evaluation and the borrower's repayment history (reg 9(5)).
evidence: Non-accrual loan listing showing the trigger criterion and the transfer date for each loan
Journal entries reversing accrued interest, with quarter-end timing
Cash application records for non-accrual loans
Restoration approvals with the documented credit evaluation and repayment history
Renegotiated loan register with rate comparison and management determination
Evidence of review of other loans to the same borrower
sop: Reverse previously accrued but uncollected interest by the end of the quarter in which the loan was placed on non-accrual status (reg 8(a))
Apply cash payments first to reduce the principal outstanding and due (reg 9(1))
Where one loan to a borrower meets the non-accrual criteria, evaluate all other loans to that borrower (reg 12)

controls.name: Allowance for Loan Losses Account and provision accounting
controls.statement: The institution must keep at all times in the Allowance for Loan Losses Account the best possible estimate of probable loan-related losses on and off the balance sheet (reg 13(1)). On-balance-sheet allowances appear as a deduction from the asset, and acceptances and off-balance-sheet items such as guarantees or letters of credit appear as a separate item with other liabilities (reg 13(2)). Additions and reductions go through the Provision for Loan Losses Account in the income statement, write-offs and recoveries are charged or credited directly to the Allowance, and no loan loss or recovery may be charged directly to retained earnings or any capital-related account (reg 14, reg 15(2)). In estimating potential loss the institution must consider historical loss experience, current economic conditions, delinquency trends, the effectiveness of lending policies and collection procedures, and the timeliness and accuracy of the loan review function (reg 16).
evidence: Allowance for Loan Losses roll-forward showing provisions, write-offs and recoveries
Journal entries showing the provision charge in the income statement and write-offs against the Allowance
Loss estimation workings covering the five factors in reg 16
Balance sheet presentation of the Allowance and the off-balance-sheet allowance liability
Evidence that no loan losses or recoveries were posted to retained earnings

controls.name: Supporting loan-loss records available to the Bank of Zambia
controls.statement: The institution must at all times maintain reasonable records in support of its loan evaluations and of the entries that keep the Allowance for Loan Losses Account adequate (regs 6(6), 19(1)). These records and entries must be made available to the Bank of Zambia for inspection and review as and when it requests, so that it can assess management's estimation procedures, the reliability of the information the estimates rely on, and the adequacy of the Allowance (reg 19(2)). The Regulations set no retention period for these records.
evidence: Index of loan files, credit evaluations and provision workings kept in support of the Allowance
Bank of Zambia requests for records and the institution's responses with dates
Records retention schedule covering loan evaluation and provisioning records
Custodian assignment for the supporting records

controls.name: Monthly loan classification and provisioning return to the Bank of Zambia
controls.statement: Within ten days after the last day of every month, or another reporting period the Bank of Zambia sets, the institution must submit to the Bank of Zambia a balance sheet reflecting an adequate Allowance for Loan Losses Account, an income statement reflecting the provision charge, details of its loan portfolio classification in the Second Schedule form, and any other information the Bank of Zambia requests in its format and time (reg 20). The Second Schedule return gives, in K'000, total gross balances, total specific and general provisions and net balances by grade, with accounts of K10 million and above listed by name and smaller accounts by number. Its notes require total gross balances to agree to the loans account balance and net balances to agree to loans less the Allowance in the balance sheet. The Loss section is labelled (V) in its heading but its sub-total is labelled (IV), a numbering inconsistency in the supplied form.
evidence: Monthly submissions with transmission date against the ten-day deadline
Completed Second Schedule return for each month
Reconciliation of return totals to the balance sheet loans account and Allowance, as the form notes require
List of named accounts of K10 million and above in each return
Bank of Zambia acknowledgement or any query on the return
Any other information requests received under reg 20(d) and the responses
sop: Submit the balance sheet, income statement, loan classification details and any requested information to the Bank of Zambia within ten days after the last day of every month (reg 20)
Ensure total gross balances agree to the loans account in the balance sheet and net balances agree to loans less the Allowance (Second Schedule notes)

policies.title: Overnight Lending Facility Guidelines
principles: The OLF provides short-term liquidity assistance to commercial banks with clearing accounts at the BoZ, on a repo basis against eligible securities (1.2, 2.1, 4.1).
OLF applications are made electronically in the BoZ CSD system, and settlement is same-day (T+0) with the cash leg in ZIPSS on DvP Model 1 (3.1, 6.1-6.3).
The OLF rate is set as a margin over the BoZ Policy Rate and is published through the OMO Statistical Release (5.1, Section 8).
BoZ reserves the right to change eligibility, collateral, application limits and the CSD timetable, and will communicate any change to participants (2.3, 3.2, 4.6, App 2 note).
management_intent: Support price and financial system stability by giving banks an orderly overnight liquidity window while encouraging active inter-bank trading (1.1, Section 8).
Keep the Guidelines current through periodic review (Section 9).

controls.name: Electronic OLF applications in the CSD system
controls.statement: Applications to access the OLF shall be made electronically in the BoZ CSD system. Participants may submit more than one application per day before the OLF window closes and if securities suffice; BoZ may restrict the number of applications. Approval is made only from 15:00 to 16:00 (OLF Authorisation Window), and no withdrawal is possible once approved; a withdrawal must be requested in writing before approval. Participants can check status and access the Individual Results Report from the CSD.
evidence: CSD application records with timestamps for OLF applications
BoZ approvals within the 15:00-16:00 OLF Authorisation Window
Written withdrawal requests received before approval
Individual Results Reports issued to participants
sop: Submit the OLF application electronically in the CSD any time from start of Business Day, before the OLF window closes
BoZ approves applications only between 15:00 and 16:00
Make a written request before approval if an application needs to be withdrawn

controls.name: CSD timetable, daily back-up and archiving
controls.statement: The CSD operates to a fixed timetable: start of day 08:00, start of business day 08:15, intraday auction cut-off 16:00, DVP cut-off 16:20, FoP cut-off 16:25, end of business day 16:30 and end of day 16:35. At end of day the CSD system closes and back-up and archiving can take place; housekeeping, including maintenance of parameters, participant details and user maintenance, takes place at start of day. BoZ may change the timetable as deemed necessary. The Guidelines do not state an archive retention period.
evidence: CSD timetable parameter configuration
End-of-day back-up and archive job logs
Change records for CSD timetable parameters and participant details
sop: At start of day, move the business date to the current system date and carry out housekeeping such as parameter, participant and user maintenance
At end of day (16:35) close the CSD system and carry out back-up and archiving

controls.name: Publication of the OLF rate in the OMO Statistical Release
controls.statement: The OLF rate is determined by adding a margin to the BoZ Policy Rate, with the margin set and changed by BoZ according to its monetary policy stance. The OLF rate is available on the OMO Statistical Release and BoZ communicates it to commercial banks through that release on the Reuters and Bloomberg Information Systems.
evidence: OMO Statistical Release showing the OLF rate on each business day
Record of the margin over the Policy Rate and its approval
Publication log for the Reuters and Bloomberg feeds
sop: Determine the OLF rate by adding the margin to the BoZ Policy Rate
Communicate the OLF rate to commercial banks through the OMO Statistical Release on Reuters and Bloomberg

controls.name: Collateral eligibility, haircut and valuation parameters
controls.statement: All loans are on a repo basis with Treasury bills, Government bonds or qualifying BoZ OMO term deposits as security. Only instruments with more than 7 days to final maturity are eligible, with a 5 percent haircut over market value for Treasury bills and Government bonds. The required market value and face value of collateral are computed by the prescribed formulas using the yield from the most recent Treasury bill or Government bond auction. In default, the repoed securities covering the loan, including the haircut, are forfeited to BoZ.
evidence: Collateral eligibility list and haircut table maintained in the CSD
Collateral valuation computations for sampled OLF loans
Auction yield rates used in the face value calculation
Notices to participants of any collateral changes
sop: Compute margin cover as loan amount multiplied by one plus the haircut margin
Compute required face value from market value using the yield on the most recent auction

controls.name: Two-yearly review of the OLF Guidelines
controls.statement: The Operating Rules and Guidelines for the OLF shall be reviewed every two years or when deemed necessary. Changes to eligibility, application limits and collateral arrangements are communicated to commercial banks. The contact offices for the Guidelines are in the Financial Markets Department.
evidence: Dated review records for the Guidelines at two-year intervals
Version history of the Guidelines (Revised August 2018)
Notifications to commercial banks of changes

policies.title: Payment System Oversight Framework
principles: The Bank's oversight of the National Payment System is guided by the CPMI-IOSCO Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMIs), formally adopted in February 2015 (Foreword, 1.4).
Oversight is risk-based, focused on systemic importance, and all SIPS and other FMIs (CSDs, SSSs, TRs, CCPs) must observe the PFMIs that apply to them (3).
Transparency: the Bank sets out publicly its oversight policies, standards and the criteria for deciding which systems they apply to (General oversight principle A, 4.1, 5 Public statements).
Consistency: oversight standards apply consistently to comparable systems, including those operated by the Bank itself (General oversight principle D, 4.1).
The oversight function is separate from operations, resourced with qualified staff, and subject to internal audit (6).
The Bank cooperates with other authorities, such as the Securities and Exchange Commission, and with other central banks on cross-border systems, without delegating its responsibilities (4.1, 4.2).
management_intent: Enhance the safety, efficiency and resilience of the National Payment System, contain systemic risk and support monetary and financial stability (II, 1.4).
Build public confidence in the National Payment System by disclosing oversight policy and practice (1.2, 5).
Protect consumer interests, promote fair access and financial inclusion alongside safety and efficiency (1.4).

controls.name: Adoption of the PFMIs as the oversight standard
controls.statement: The role of the Bank as overseer is guided by the CPMI-IOSCO PFMIs, formally adopted by the Bank in February 2015. Developments in the Zambian National Payment System must comply with the PFMIs and other relevant international standards, all SIPS and other FMIs shall observe the principles that apply to them, and the Bank may require non-systemically important systems to comply with the PFMIs. Oversight of critical service providers to an FMI is conducted in line with the PFMIs.
evidence: Bank of Zambia record of formal PFMI adoption (February 2015)
Mapping of each PFMI principle to the FMI category it applies to
Oversight requirements issued to each SIPS and FMI citing the PFMIs
Decisions on whether NSIPS are required to comply with the PFMIs

controls.name: Designation of systemically important payment systems and FMIs
controls.statement: Payment systems are designated as SIPS or NSIPS. Large-value payment systems are designated systemically important by their nature (ZIPSS/RTGS is designated). A retail payment system is designated systemically important where at least 3 of 7 criteria are met, including 75 percent market share, processing more than 10 percent of RTGS value, a participant net debit concentration above 70 percent and cross-border activity, and the Bank may designate on other factors. Systems are reviewed periodically for designation. The Zambia Electronic Clearing House and the CSDs for government securities and for bonds and shares are designated systemically important.
evidence: Register of designated payment systems and FMIs with designation category and date
Designation assessment against the seven SIRPS criteria for each retail system
Records of periodic designation reviews
Designation decisions for ZIPSS, the Zambia Electronic Clearing House and the CSDs
Consultation records with the Securities and Exchange Commission on CSD designation
sop: Assess each retail payment system against the seven criteria
Designate a retail payment system as systemically important where a minimum of three criteria is met
Review systems periodically to determine whether they qualify for designation

controls.name: Oversight monitoring information sources
controls.statement: To carry out oversight, the Bank shall obtain information on the design and operation of systems from a wide range of sources, which may include public information, official system documentation (rules, member documentation, business continuity plans), regular or ad hoc reporting of volumes, values, operating performance and financial position, internal board and audit reports, self-assessments of compliance, bilateral and multilateral contacts, on-site and off-site inspections, expert opinions, information from other regulators and customer feedback. The Bank also continuously monitors other systems, instruments, channels and payment service providers.
evidence: Inventory of information sources received per overseen system
Periodic activity and performance reports received from operators (volume, value, operating performance)
Official system documentation held on file (rules, business continuity plans)
On-site and off-site inspection reports
Information-sharing records with other regulators

controls.name: Oversight assessments and self-assessment by overseen systems
controls.statement: The Bank conducts an Overall National Payment System Assessment and an Individual System Assessment for systems in scope. The individual assessment combines self-assessment by the system, emphasising its responsibility to meet relevant standards, with independent assessment by the Bank on all available information. Oversight standards are applied consistently, including to systems operated by the Bank, and the oversight function is itself subject to internal audit by the Internal Audit Department.
evidence: Self-assessments of compliance submitted by each overseen system
Individual System Assessment reports prepared by the Oversight Division
Overall National Payment System Assessment report
Internal Audit report on the oversight function and its procedures
Assessment of Bank-operated systems such as ZIPSS and the CSD against the same standards
sop: Use information gathered through monitoring to conduct the Overall National Payment System Assessment and the Individual System Assessment
Combine the system's self-assessment with the Bank's independent assessment based on all available information
Subject the oversight procedures to internal audit by the Internal Audit Department

controls.name: Public disclosure of oversight policy and publication of statistics
controls.statement: The Bank shall publish its oversight objectives and any specific policy requirements or standards prescribed for payment systems and FMIs, together with the criteria for determining which systems they apply to, to promote market discipline. The Bank may use dialogue and moral suasion backed by the publication of statistics and other results of monitoring and assessment, and treats publication of performance information as an instrument of compliance enforcement. The Framework does not name a publication calendar or channel for payment statistics.
evidence: Published Payment System Oversight Framework (2026) on the Bank website
Published oversight standards and designation criteria
Published payment system statistics and performance information with release dates
Publication calendar or release log, if one exists

controls.name: Statutory powers to require change and enforcement
controls.clause: 5 (Statutory power to require change; Enforcement and sanctions); 1.1
controls.statement: The Bank may invoke statutory powers under the National Payment Systems Act and the Bank of Zambia Act to require compliance. These extend to powers to obtain information and carry out on-site inspections, grant initial approvals to operate a system, approve changes to system rules and procedures, issue cease and desist orders, suspend or revoke licences, and penalise or prosecute operators and participants.
evidence: Register of system approvals and approved rule changes
Records of information requests and on-site inspections
Record of cease and desist orders, suspensions, revocations and sanctions
Licence register for payment system operators and service providers

controls.name: Separation and capacity of the oversight function
controls.statement: A dedicated Oversight Division has been institutionalised within the Payment Systems Department, separated from the operational division, with qualified personnel and drawing on Legal, Financial Markets, Prudential Supervision, Financial Stability, Financial Conduct Supervision, Internal Audit and ICT. The Division coordinates oversight and exchanges information with other competent authorities for FMIs also subject to their mandate, and the Bank shall endeavour to engage cooperating partners in reviewing its oversight procedures.
evidence: Organisation chart showing the Oversight Division separate from operations
Staffing and qualification records for the Oversight Division
Memorandum of Understanding with the Securities and Exchange Commission
Reports of any external or cooperating-partner review of oversight procedures

policies.title: Bank of Zambia Act
principles: The Bank must formulate and implement monetary and supervisory policies that maintain price and financial-system stability (s.4(1)), and must licence, supervise and regulate banks and financial institutions so that the financial system operates safely, soundly and efficiently (s.4(2)(a)).

Statutory secrecy: every person appointed under the Act or employed by the Bank takes an oath of secrecy, and information that comes to a person's knowledge in the course of their duties may not be published or disclosed except in the course of duties, under a court order, or with the written consent of the Board (ss.22-23).

Accountability to the Minister: proper books of account are kept in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles, the accounts are audited annually, and a report on the Bank's activities with audited statements goes to the Minister within six months of the financial year end (ss.24-27).

Public transparency through the Government Gazette: a return of assets and liabilities each month (s.28), a policy statement every six months (s.9), and notices on coin specification, currency recall and liquidity requirements (ss.31(2), 34, 41).
The Bank may require any person to provide information it specifies, and may require data it believes to be inadequate or inaccurate to be audited by an auditor it approves (s.54).
Banks and financial institutions are inspected periodically, or when the Bank considers it necessary, in accordance with the Banking and Financial Services Act (s.55).

All the powers of the Bank vest in the Board (s.12(1)); minutes are kept of every Board and committee meeting (s.16(9)) and a director's declared private interest is recorded in the minutes (s.20(3)).

The Act as supplied also reproduces subsidiary legislation (Foreign Currency Regulations, Credit Guarantee Scheme Regulations, Call-in and Surrender of Currency Regulations) that places return, record and inspection duties on bureaux de change and on approved lending institutions.
management_intent: The Board causes proper books of account and other records of the Bank's accounts to be kept in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles, open at all reasonable times to inspection by the directors or a person authorised by the Minister (s.25).
The accounts are audited every year by an auditor the Board appoints (s.26).

The Board submits an annual report to the Minister not later than six months after the financial year end (the financial year ends on 31 December, s.24), covering financial affairs and appending an audited balance sheet, an audited statement of income and expenditure and any other information the Minister requires (s.27(1)-(2)). The Board complies with any written ministerial request for further certified reports, returns or statements (s.27(3)).

The Bank delivers a return of monthly assets and liabilities to the Minister whenever he requires it (s.28(1)), and within thirty days after the last working day of each month makes up a return as at close of business that day, publishes it in the Gazette and delivers it to the Minister (s.28(2)).

The Bank publishes a policy statement in the Gazette every six months, in consultation with the Minister, setting out the monetary policies to be followed, the guiding principles and a review of the previous period; the Minister lays it before the National Assembly (s.9).

The Bank obtains the information it needs from regulated persons and has doubtful data independently audited (s.54), and inspects banks and financial institutions periodically or as it considers necessary (s.55).

Directors and others at Board or committee meetings disclose any private interest as soon as practicable, abstain from the matter unless the Board directs otherwise, and the disclosure is minuted (s.20).
Information obtained in the course of duties is protected by oath and by the statutory prohibition on disclosure, with release only through a court order or written Board consent (ss.22-23).

controls.name: Oath of secrecy for appointees and staff
controls.statement: Every person appointed under the Act or employed by the Bank must take and subscribe, before a Commissioner for Oaths, an oath of secrecy as set out in the Official Oaths Act (Cap 5) (s.22(1)). Acting or failing to act in contravention of the oath is an offence (fine up to thirty thousand fine units or imprisonment up to two years, or both) (s.22(2)). The Act does not require a register of oaths and sets no retention period for the oath records.
evidence: Signed oath or affirmation of secrecy for each director, Governor, Deputy Governor and staff member, with the Commissioner for Oaths attestation
Reconciliation of the current board and staff list to the oath records, with the oath date against the appointment or employment date
Onboarding or appointment procedure that includes the oath step
Records custodian and storage location for the signed oaths

controls.name: Prohibition on disclosure of information to unauthorised persons
controls.statement: No person appointed under the Act may publish or disclose to any person, otherwise than in the course of that person's duties, the contents of any document, communication or information which relate to and came to their knowledge in the course of their duties, except in compliance with an order of a court of competent jurisdiction or with the written consent given by or on behalf of the Board (s.23(1)). Knowing contravention is an offence (s.23(2)), and a person who knowingly passes on information disclosed in breach commits a separate offence with a higher maximum penalty (s.23(3)). The Act defines no classes of information and no classification levels; the duty covers information 'whatsoever' arising from the person's duties.
evidence: Disclosure policy that names the lawful gateways (course of duties, court order, written Board consent)
Register of written Board consents to disclose, with date, recipient, scope of information and approver
Court orders received and the disclosures made in response
Staff acknowledgement of the s.23 duty
Information-sharing arrangements with other agencies or regulators showing the legal basis for release

controls.name: Books of account and records, open to inspection
controls.statement: The Board must cause proper books of account and other records relating to the Bank's accounts to be kept in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles (s.25(1)). The books and records must at all reasonable times be open for inspection by the directors or any person authorised by the Minister (s.25(2)). The Act names no specific accounting standard or version and sets no retention period for the books and records.
evidence: Chart of accounts and general ledger extract
Accounting policy manual stating the accounting framework applied and its version
Written authorisation from the Minister for any non-director inspector, and the inspection access record
Board approval or oversight record showing the Board caused the books to be kept
Records retention schedule covering the books of account

controls.name: Annual audit and annual report to the Minister
controls.statement: The accounts of the Bank must be audited annually by an auditor appointed by the Board (s.26). The financial year runs for twelve months ending on 31 December (s.24). As soon as practicable, and not later than six months after the end of each financial year, the Board must submit to the Minister a report on its activities, including information on its financial affairs, with an audited balance sheet, an audited statement of income and expenditure and any other information the Minister requires appended (s.27(1)-(2)). On written request the Board must also give the Minister other reports, returns or statements certified by an auditor (s.27(3)).
evidence: Board resolution appointing the auditor for the year
Signed audit report and audited financial statements (balance sheet and statement of income and expenditure)
Annual report as submitted to the Minister, with the transmittal date against the six-month deadline
Written ministerial requests under s.27(3) and the certified responses
Evidence of the auditor's certification date, which also starts the sixty-day profit payment period in s.7(2)
sop: Submit the annual report to the Minister not later than six months after the end of the financial year (s.27(1))
Include financial affairs and append the audited balance sheet, the audited statement of income and expenditure and other information the Minister may require (s.27(2))
Comply with the Minister's written request for other auditor-certified reports, returns or statements (s.27(3))

controls.name: Monthly assets and liabilities return, published in the Gazette
controls.statement: Within thirty days after the last working day of each month the Bank must make up a return of its assets and liabilities as at the close of business on that day, cause it to be published in the Gazette and deliver it to the Minister (s.28(2)). The Bank must also deliver a return of its monthly assets and liabilities to the Minister whenever he so requires (s.28(1)). The supplied text of s.28(2) is grammatically defective ('the bank make up'); the operative duty is read as above.
evidence: Gazette notice for each month showing the return and the publication date
Delivery acknowledgement from the Minister's office for each return
Reconciliation of each published return to the general ledger balances at the close of business on the last working day of the month
Compliance calendar showing the thirty-day deadline for each month-end
Ministerial requests under s.28(1) and the returns delivered in response
sop: Make up a return of assets and liabilities as at close of business on the last working day of each month (s.28(2))
Publish the return in the Gazette and deliver it to the Minister within thirty days after that day (s.28(2))
Deliver a return of monthly assets and liabilities to the Minister whenever he requires (s.28(1))

controls.name: Power to call for information and to have it audited
controls.statement: For the purpose of carrying out its functions the Bank may require any person to provide such information as it may specify (s.54(1)). Where the Bank believes that information or data supplied is, or may be, inadequate or inaccurate, it may by written notice require the information or data to be audited by an auditor approved by the Bank (s.54(2)). A related power lets the Bank require any bank or financial institution to furnish information needed to confirm compliance with the liquidity and reserve requirements (s.41(6)). The Act does not prescribe a format, schema or deadline for the information; the Bank specifies these in each request.
evidence: Register of information requests issued under s.54(1) and s.41(6), with addressee, information specified, date issued and due date
Responses received, with date of receipt
Written notices requiring audit under s.54(2), the approval of the auditor and the resulting audit reports
Documented criteria or review record showing why data was judged inadequate or inaccurate
Templates or data specifications issued with information requests

controls.name: Inspection of banks and financial institutions
controls.statement: The Bank must inspect any bank or financial institution, periodically or at such times as it considers necessary, in accordance with the Banking and Financial Services Act (s.55). The Bank itself is not subject to that Act except where it imposes a duty on the Bank (s.61). The inspection procedure sits in the Banking and Financial Services Act (Cap 387), which is not part of the text supplied, so no inspection steps are stated here.
evidence: Inspection programme or plan showing periodic coverage of banks and financial institutions
Inspection authorisations or mandates for each inspection
Inspection reports and the records of information examined
Evidence of the version of the Banking and Financial Services Act applied

controls.name: Board minutes, seal register and recorded disclosures of interest
controls.statement: The Board must cause minutes to be kept of the proceedings of every Board meeting and of every meeting of any committee it establishes (s.16(9)). A person at a meeting who, or whose spouse, has a direct or indirect private interest in a matter under consideration must disclose it as soon as practicable and may not take part in the discussion or vote unless the Board directs otherwise, and the disclosure must be recorded in the minutes (s.20(2)-(3)). The seal may be affixed to an instrument only on the authority of a Board resolution and in the presence of at least two directors who sign the instrument (s.17(3)). The Act sets no retention period for the minutes.
evidence: Minute books for the Board and each committee, with dates and attendance
Minuted declarations of interest and the recusal record for each affected item
Seal register or record of instruments sealed, with the authorising Board resolution and the two director signatures
Committee establishment resolutions (s.18)
Records retention schedule covering minutes

controls.name: Statutory publication in the Government Gazette
controls.statement: The Bank must publish a policy statement in the Government Gazette every six months, containing the monetary policies to be followed in the next six months with reasons, the principles for the next two years (or other period the Minister decides) and a review of implementation in the previous period; the Minister lays it before the National Assembly at its next first sitting (s.9). Other items are also published: the standard weight, composition and remedy of coins (s.31(2)), prior notice and cut-off dates when notes or coins are called in (s.34(1), (3)), the conditions for exchanging mutilated notes (s.36(2)), and liquidity ratios, reserve balances and qualifying assets and liabilities, which are fixed by Gazette notice (s.41(1)-(3)). The Bank may determine and make public its rates for discounts, rediscounts and advances (s.43(1)).
evidence: Gazette notices for each policy statement and each other statutory notice, with publication dates
Publication calendar showing the six-month cycle for the policy statement
Record of the Minister laying the policy statement before the National Assembly
Current published liquidity ratio and reserve requirement notice with its effective date
Published rates schedule for discounts, rediscounts and advances
sop: Publish a policy statement in the Gazette every six months, in consultation with the Minister (s.9(1))
Include the policy description and reasons, the guiding principles and the review of the previous period (s.9(1)(a)-(c))
Give prior notice in the Gazette before calling in notes or coins, and publish the cut-off dates (s.34(1), (3))

controls.name: Returns, accounts and inspection under the reproduced subsidiary regulations
controls.clause: Credit Guarantee Scheme Regs 17(3), 17(9), 19-21; Foreign Currency Regs 16-17
controls.statement: Credit Guarantee Scheme Regulations (as amended by S.I. 86 of 1989): the Bank must send the Minister a quarterly income and expenditure account of the scheme with a written performance report (reg 19(1)); approved institutions must submit Form CGS 9 particulars of guaranteed advances as at 30 June and 31 December, and quarterly Forms CGS 8 and CGS 10, no later than thirty days after the end of the period, and failure discharges the Bank's liability under the affected guarantees (reg 20(2), (4), (5)); the Bank inspects approved institutions' accounts (reg 21); and notices of default must attach the correspondence with the borrower (reg 17(3)). The returns carry borrower names and addresses. Foreign Currency Regulations (S.I. 44 of 1994): a bureau must submit returns of purchases, sales and open position in the form the Bank determines (reg 16) and produce its books for inspection (reg 17). The Bureau de Change Regulations 2003 (S.I. 38 of 2003, reg 42(2)) refer to the repeal of the 1994 Foreign Currency Regulations, so the bureau duties here appear superseded; they are assessed under the Bureau de Change Regulations policy.
evidence: Quarterly income and expenditure account and performance report sent to the Minister
Forms CGS 8, CGS 9 and CGS 10 received from each approved institution, with receipt dates against the thirty-day deadline
Late-return log and the Bank's decision on guarantee liability under reg 20(5)
Inspection reports on approved institutions' scheme accounts
Notice of default files with the attached borrower correspondence
Register of Guarantee Certificates issued, endorsed, discharged and cancelled
sop: Submit returns to the Bank not later than thirty days after the end of the period to which they refer (Credit Guarantee Scheme reg 20(4))
Remit the Bank's share of recoveries not later than seven days after the date of recovery (Credit Guarantee Scheme reg 17(9))
Submit to the Minister every quarter an income and expenditure account of the scheme with a written performance report (Credit Guarantee Scheme reg 19(1))

policies.title: Statistics Act
principles: The United Nations Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and the African Charter on Statistics apply for the purposes of the Act (s.3).
Official statistics are produced and compiled in a transparent and impartial manner (long title; s.21(3)(b)-(c)).
Protection of personal data and of the confidentiality and identity of data sources is mandatory for statistical compilation (long title; s.21(2); s.30).
Official statistics must be relevant, accurate, reliable, timely, objective, comprehensive, impartially disseminated, accessible, standards-compliant and disaggregated by important domains (s.21(3)).
The Agency is the sole designated entity responsible for publication of official statistics, and no one else may publish them without its approval (s.7(1); s.21(4)).
The Statistician-General is professionally independent: no person may interfere with how and when collections are done or with the form, extent and timing of releases (s.11(4)).
Common concepts, definitions, nomenclatures and standards are used across the National Statistical System so that it is integrated and comparable (s.7(2)(f); s.17(4)(b)).
Duplication in statistical collection is minimised to reduce the burden on suppliers of data (s.15(3)(c); s.17(4)(c)).
Professional and ethical standards apply to all members of the National Statistical System (s.17(1); s.7(2)(l)).
Release of statistics is predictable and publicly accountable through a published calendar (s.27).
management_intent: Establish an integrated National Statistical System of data producers, data suppliers, users, research institutions, higher education institutions and the media (s.14).
Re-constitute the Central Statistical Office as the Zambia Statistics Agency and make it the coordinator and sole publisher of official statistics (long title; s.5; s.7).
Give effect to the UN Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics and the principles of the African Charter on Statistics (long title; s.3).
Require other statistical agencies to supply administrative data and metadata to the Agency for official statistics and data quality assessment (s.26).
Promote the use of statistics for evidence-based decision making, policy making and monitoring and evaluation at all levels (s.15(3)(d); long title).
Standardise record keeping and metadata documentation by Gazette notice (s.20(a)(vi)).
Build sustainable capacity for production and use of statistics, including professional standards for statisticians (s.7(2)(i), (s); s.15(3)(e)).
Enforce compliance through directives, administrative penalties, offences and penalties (s.31, s.34-s.38).

controls.name: Statistical confidentiality (five disclosure states)
controls.statement: Returns, forms, answers, and any report or document that allows identification of a respondent must not be published, admitted in evidence or disclosed to anyone not performing a function under the Act, except for prosecution under the Act. The text yields five states: (1) protected by default, (2) disclosable with the respondent's written permission, (3) outside restriction where the respondent has itself published or built a computerised dataset for general access, (4) publishable without consent where the person or business is the only one in its sphere and costs, capital or profits cannot be identified, and (5) de-identified unit records released for research (see C02). The Agency must also protect the confidentiality and identity of the source of data it designates as official statistics.
evidence: Confidentiality classification scheme with the five states and release rules for each
Written respondent permissions for any identifiable disclosure
Disclosure control and statistical disclosure limitation procedure for outputs
Log of disclosures made and the s.30 state relied on
Pre-publication confidentiality check records for official statistics
sop: Do not publish, admit in evidence or disclose identifiable returns, forms, answers or documents except for prosecution under the Act or with the written permission of the respondent.
Apply the sole-business rule only where the published particulars do not allow identification of costs of production, capital employed or profits.

controls.name: Release of de-identified unit records for research
controls.statement: The Agency may release unit records on electronic media with all identifications removed if the Statistician-General is satisfied they will be used for genuine research, obtains a written undertaking against onward release without consent and a written undertaking to share the research findings, or is satisfied the records cannot be identified to a person, undertaking or business. Requirements and protocols for access to micro-data for research are set by Gazette standard.
evidence: Micro-data access request with stated research purpose
Signed recipient undertakings on non-onward release and sharing findings
Statistician-General approval record
De-identification and re-identification risk assessment of the released file
Register of micro-data releases and recipients
Gazetted micro-data access protocol
sop: Statistician-General satisfies himself or herself that the records will be used for genuine research.
Obtain from the recipient a written undertaking not to release the records to any other person without the Statistician-General's written consent.
Obtain a written undertaking to provide a copy of the research findings to the Agency.
Remove all identifications before release.

controls.name: Staff secrecy, oath and misuse of statistical data
controls.statement: Board and committee members, the Statistician-General and staff take an oath on appointment, and must not disclose information learned in their duties without written Board consent. Using pre-release information for personal gain, unauthorised communication of information and knowingly compiling false statistics are offences.
evidence: Signed oaths under the Official Oaths Act for members, committee members, Statistician-General and staff
Confidentiality undertakings and onboarding records
Access-control list for pre-release statistics
Incident register for unauthorised disclosure and investigation outcomes

controls.name: Metadata definition and gazetted metadata-documentation standard
controls.statement: The Act defines metadata as the range of generally textual information that fosters understanding of the context in which statistical data was collected, processed and analysed. The Agency may, after Board approval, issue by Gazette notice standards on record-keeping including the manner in which metadata is documented, and on the capture and publication of spatial-data metadata.
evidence: Gazette notice issuing the metadata documentation standard
Metadata template or schema applied to each statistical collection
Completed metadata records for published official statistics
Spatial data metadata records and publication location
Metadata-completeness check at designation or release

controls.name: Gazetted statistical standards
controls.statement: After Board approval the Agency may issue Gazette standards on designation criteria and certification, methods of converting data into statistics, documents required for collection, access and receipt procedures, micro-data access protocols, record-keeping, and spatial data capture, sharing, integration and access. These standards form the controlling rulebook for data handling in the National Statistical System.
evidence: Gazette notices issued under s.20 with Board approval minutes
Register of current standards with issue date and version
Evidence of conformance by the statistical agency under assessment

controls.name: Six-part quality statement for official statistics
controls.statement: Official statistics must be (a) relevant, accurate, reliable and timely; (b) objective and comprehensive; (c) disseminated impartially; (d) accessible; (e) in accordance with appropriate national and international standards and classifications; and (f) disaggregated by important domains. Each of the six parts is a testable quality criterion for designation.
evidence: Quality statement or quality report per official statistic addressing each of the six criteria
Designation checklist evidencing a pass on each criterion
Standards and classifications used, with versions
Domain disaggregation tables
Release timeliness record versus the release calendar

controls.name: Designation of official statistics and pre-publication approval
controls.statement: The Agency may designate statistics produced from National Statistical System collections as official statistics, and is the sole designated entity responsible for publishing them. Anyone wishing to publish official statistics must obtain the Agency's approval first, and approval is based on the Agency's standard concepts, definitions and methodologies.
evidence: Register of designated official statistics with designation date and criteria applied
Agency approval records for publication requests
Publication log showing approval before release
Gazette criteria and classification procedures for designation
sop: Designate statistics or classes of statistics as official statistics against the six criteria in s.21(3).
A person wishing to publish official statistics must obtain Agency approval before publication.

controls.name: Code of Practice for the National Statistical System
controls.statement: The Agency must develop a code of practice setting professional and ethical standards for members of the National Statistical System, based on s.3 principles, and publish it in the Gazette. It must include impartial and credible ethical standards, measures for quality and comparability of official and unofficial statistics, and measures to minimise duplication.
evidence: Published Code of Practice and Gazette reference
Evidence the code is based on UN Fundamental Principles and the African Charter on Statistics
Adherence declarations by NSS members
Compliance review or assessment reports against the code
Version history of the code
sop: Develop the code of practice based on s.3 and other internationally accepted principles.
Publish the code of practice in the Gazette.

controls.name: Standard concepts, definitions, nomenclatures and classifications
controls.statement: The Agency promotes and encourages common concepts, definitions, nomenclatures and standards across collection, analysis and dissemination, and approves publication of official statistics based on standard concepts, definitions and methodologies it develops. This is the basis for controlled code lists and reference data in the National Statistical System.
evidence: Agency-maintained register of standard concepts, definitions and nomenclatures with versions
Controlled code lists and classifications (for example sector, industry and geography)
Mapping of agency-local codes to the standard classification
Conformance review of a collection against standard definitions

controls.name: Supply of administrative data and metadata to the Agency
controls.statement: A statistical agency (including the ICT Authority and other listed regulators) must provide the Agency with its administrative data and with its metadata, for production of official statistics and for assessment of data quality respectively. Administrative data is data collected by or for a public body other than the Agency for administrative purposes under other written law.
evidence: Inventory of administrative datasets held by the statistical agency
Supply agreement, MoU or data-sharing arrangement with the Agency
Transfer logs of administrative data and metadata to the Agency
Metadata packs supplied for data quality assessment
Named custodian per administrative dataset

controls.name: Respondent objection to exchange and protection of shared data
controls.statement: Where the Agency jointly collects statistics with a private body under agreement, collected statistics are exchanged between the parties except information from a respondent who objects to the exchange or sharing. The private body must protect confidential information made available under the agreement, and bodies that run an approved collection must give the Agency the datasets and report without charge.
evidence: Agreement with the private body setting out joint collection and exchange terms
Respondent objection register and flag on affected records
Exchange extracts demonstrating objected records were withheld
Private body confidentiality undertaking
Datasets and reports delivered to the Agency after a private collection
sop: Undertake collection jointly by the Agency and the private body.
Exchange collected statistics between the parties, excluding information from a respondent who objects to exchange or sharing.
The private body protects confidential information made available under the agreement.

controls.name: Official statistics release calendar
controls.statement: The Agency prepares a calendar of planned release dates for official statistics, approved by the Board. The Statistician-General must publicly notify any variation, and a new release date must be set within a reasonable time and made public.
evidence: Published release calendar with Board approval
Public notices of release date variations and new dates
Comparison of actual versus planned release dates
sop: Prepare a calendar indicating planned dates for release of official statistics.
Notify the public of any variation to planned release dates.
Set a new release date within a reasonable time and make it public.

controls.name: Statistical subject taxonomy (Third Schedule)
controls.statement: The Agency may collect official statistics on matters listed in the Third Schedule: 39 named subjects from Demographic and Population through Land use and Meteorology (including Information and Communication, item 27), plus any further matters the Minister prescribes (item 40). Sampling may be authorised for these matters.
evidence: Subject taxonomy table of the Third Schedule with item numbers
Mapping of each dataset to a Third Schedule subject
Ministerial prescription of any additional matters under item 40

controls.name: Independence of the Statistician-General
controls.statement: The Statistician-General must have prescribed qualifications and is the CEO responsible for day-to-day administration. No person may interfere with how and when a collection is undertaken, spatial data handling, the form, extent and timing of releases, discontinuation decisions, or compilation, analysis and dissemination of an official collection.
evidence: Statistician-General appointment record and qualifications
Delegations and reporting lines showing separation from ministerial direction on release
Record of any attempted interference and how it was handled
Release decisions signed by the Statistician-General

controls.name: Approval of statistical collections and data collection instruments
controls.statement: The Agency approves instruments for national-level data collection, including census frame, register, sample design and questionnaire, and reviews all national data-collection initiatives. No one may start, vary or discontinue an official statistical collection without Agency approval, and a private body proposing a national census or survey must furnish particulars, with the Agency deciding within thirty days.
evidence: Agency approval of each questionnaire, sample design and register or census frame
Register of approved official statistical collections
Private body proposals and the Agency decision notice with date
Gazette exemption notices under s.18(3)
Gazetted findings of approved private-body surveys
sop: Private body furnishes particulars of a proposed national census or survey to the Agency before conducting it.
Agency considers the proposal within thirty days of receipt and approves or rejects it, notifying the private body.
On approval, Agency, subject to Board approval, publishes the findings in the Gazette.

controls.name: Disaggregation of data by important domains
controls.statement: The Agency must ensure the procedure for collecting and processing statistics in the National Statistical System provides for disaggregation by important domains, a domain being a sub-group of the population for which a separate estimate is calculated. Official statistics must be disaggregated by important domains.
evidence: List of important domains and disaggregation dimensions used
Collection and processing procedure showing domain variables captured
Published tables disaggregated by domain
Data dictionary entries for domain variables

controls.name: Statistical records registry, library and electronic database
controls.statement: The Agency must establish and maintain a documents registry, library services and an appropriate electronic database, and the National Statistical System must develop a national statistical management information system along with sector systems to ensure reliable, comprehensive and harmonised information.
evidence: Documents registry and library catalogue
Electronic statistical database inventory with owner and content
Description of the national and sector statistical management information systems
Access and storage arrangements for statistical data

controls.name: Integrity of statistical records, directives and penalties
controls.statement: Knowingly compiling false statistics, making untrue statements in returns, and concealing or falsifying records are offences. The Agency may issue a directive for non-compliance stating the addressee, issues, provisions breached, enforcement measures, report form and deadline, and may impose an administrative penalty for each day of continued failure.
evidence: Directives issued with the eight required content elements
Responses and reports submitted to directives
Register of administrative penalties imposed and recovered
Audit or verification records for returns and statistical outputs
Prosecution or referral records
sop: A directive must state who it is addressed to, the issues, supporting documents, provisions contravened, details of the contravention, intended enforcement measures, form and time frame of the report, and the submission address.
A person who fails to comply with a directive is liable to pay an administrative penalty, recoverable by civil action if unpaid.

policies.title: Information and Communication Technologies Act
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Tariffs must be transparent, non-discriminatory and based on the cost of providing the service; cross-subsidies are eliminated (s.47(2)).
Interconnection, access and co-location are negotiated in good faith, on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms, with Authority determination where parties fail to agree (ss.41, 43, 44).

Spectrum and numbers are assigned in line with the national frequency and numbering plans, in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner, using objective criteria made known in advance (s.54(3), s.54(7)).
The numbering plan must be non-discriminatory and consist of a scheme of identification that ensures communications are correctly and efficiently directed (s.55(2), s.55(4)).

Technical standards for electronic communications equipment are set with public submissions and account of international standards, including those of the International Telecommunication Union (s.64(2)).
Standards for equipment aim at network integrity, proper functioning of connected equipment, inter-operability, avoiding harmful interference and protecting public safety and health (s.65(2)).

Interconnection agreements must not pose an unnecessary risk to the protection of personal data, the confidentiality of information processed, transmitted or stored, or the protection of privacy (s.41).
Information obtained in interconnection or co-location negotiation that was not previously known or publicly available may be used only for the purpose for which it was supplied (s.41, s.44(9)).
Persons must not disclose information that comes to their knowledge in the course of their duties under the Act without written consent of the Board (First Schedule, para 9).
Persons must not gain access to, modify, intercept or obstruct programs, data or functions of electronic communications networks or services without lawful authority (s.77(2)).
Guidelines issued by the Authority bind all persons regulated under the Act once published in a daily newspaper of general circulation (s.7(2)-(3)).
Licensees must provide detailed billing information so consumers can verify they have been billed correctly (s.47(9)).
management_intent: Continue the Communications Authority as the Zambia Information and Communication Technology Authority and provide for the regulation of information and communication technology (long title, s.4).
Facilitate access to information and communication technologies and protect the rights and interests of service providers and consumers (long title).
Regulate the provision of electronic communication services and monitor sector performance, including investment, availability, quality, cost and standards of services (s.6(1)).
Implement and administer licensing and assignment schemes, provide national frequency and numbering plans and set standards for the sector (s.6(2)(a)-(b)).
Administer the country code top level domain and electronic addresses (s.6(2)(j)).
Keep public registers of licences, interconnection agreements, access agreements, co-location agreements and approved tariffs, open to public inspection (ss.26, 42, 43(7), 44(8), 47(7)).
Maintain a central numbering database recording the status of all number ranges, codes and blocks, supported by licensee returns on all numbers including prepaid subscribers (s.55(5)-(6)).

Track and control electronic equipment through registration of original equipment manufacturer identification and mobile device IMEI numbers, with disabling of unapproved or unregistered devices (s.64).
Ensure only type-approved equipment is used, supplied or sold in connection with electronic communications (s.66).
Ensure compliance through inspection by telecommunications officers and through information returns that licensees must furnish (ss.76, 82, 90).
Remain autonomous, subject only to general directives from the Minister (ss.5, 6(3)).
Account for performance through an annual report to the Minister within ninety days after the financial year end, with audited accounts (First Schedule, Part II, para 4).

controls.name: Register of licences and rejected applications
controls.statement: The Authority must keep and maintain a Register in which it enters the names and other details of licences, information on applications it rejected together with the reasons, and any other information it considers necessary. The Register is kept at places the Authority determines and is open to public inspection at such times and on such conditions, including payment of inspection fees, as the Authority determines. Where the Authority rejects a licence application it informs the applicant and gives reasons, and it publishes any suspension or cancellation of a licence in a daily newspaper.
evidence: The Register of licences maintained under s.26
Register entries for rejected applications showing the reasons recorded
Authority decision determining where, when and on what conditions the Register is open to public inspection
Schedule of inspection fees for the Register
Written rejection notices to applicants stating reasons
Newspaper notices publishing licence suspensions or cancellations
sop: Authority grants or rejects a licence application within sixty days of receipt; failure to decide within that period is a deemed grant (s.11(2)-(3)).
Where an application is rejected, inform the applicant and give the reasons (s.11(4)).
Enter the licence names and details, and rejected-application information with reasons, in the Register (s.26(1)).
Make the Register open to public inspection at times and on conditions the Authority determines (s.26(2)).
Publish any licence suspension or cancellation in a daily newspaper of general circulation (s.18(8)).

controls.name: Interconnection agreement filing, approval and public register
controls.statement: Interconnection agreements must be in writing and in English, must not be implemented without the Authority's prior written approval, and the Authority decides within sixty days, giving reasons for any refusal; failure to decide within sixty days is treated as approval. The Authority must maintain a register of all interconnection agreements that contains the terms and conditions of each agreement and is open to public inspection on terms the Authority determines. Licensees holding a dominant position must publish an approved reference interconnection offer in a format readily accessible to other licensees and keep separate accounts for interconnection. Requests and refusals for interconnection must be in writing, sent by registered post and copied to the Authority.
evidence: Register of interconnection agreements maintained under s.42
Each interconnection agreement as filed with the Authority (written, in English)
Authority's written approval or reasons for non-approval for each agreement
Reference interconnection offer of each dominant licensee, as approved and published
Separate account for interconnection activities showing revenue and cost elements and basis of calculation
Written requests and refusals for interconnection copied to the Authority
Interim charge agreements or Authority-determined interim charges under s.45
sop: Licensees negotiate in good faith; where they fail to agree within the prescribed period either may refer the matter to the Authority for determination (s.41).
Parties submit the written agreement to the Authority; the Authority decides within sixty days and gives reasons if it does not approve (s.41).
Where approval is withheld, parties may re-submit a modified agreement within the prescribed period (s.41).
A dominant licensee submits a reference interconnection offer for approval and, after approval, publishes it in a format readily accessible to other licensees (s.41).
Authority records the terms and conditions of each agreement in the register of interconnection agreements and opens it to public inspection (s.42).
Where interconnection is established before the agreement is executed, parties agree interim charges within sixty days, failing which the Authority determines them (s.45(1)-(2)).
Send requests and refusals by registered post and copy the Authority (s.46).

controls.name: Confidentiality of information obtained in interconnection and co-location negotiation
controls.statement: Information that a party to an interconnection or co-location negotiation obtains as a result of that negotiation, that was not previously known to it and is not publicly available, may be used only for the purposes for which it was supplied for as long as it remains publicly unavailable. Interconnection agreements must also not pose an unnecessary risk to the protection of personal data, the confidentiality of information processed, transmitted or stored, or the protection of privacy.
evidence: Licensee policy or procedure restricting use of negotiation information to the purpose supplied
Register or log of negotiation information received from counterparties with the stated purpose of supply
Access controls limiting negotiation information to staff working on the negotiation
Confidentiality clauses in interconnection and co-location agreements
Assessment of each interconnection agreement against personal data, confidentiality and privacy risk

controls.name: Access agreements filing and public register
controls.statement: An access agreement must be in writing and filed with the Authority. The Authority must maintain a register of all access agreements that, without revealing the terms and conditions, contains the names of the parties, a general description of the matters governed and the date of the agreement, and is open to public inspection on terms the Authority determines. Dominant licensees must offer access on reasonable and non-discriminatory terms, in particular on price, and of the same technical quality as on their own networks. The Minister may prescribe matters for inclusion in access agreements.
evidence: Register of access agreements maintained under s.43(7)
Each access agreement as filed with the Authority
Register fields showing party names, general description and date, with terms withheld
Authority determination on referred access disputes
Statutory instrument prescribing matters for inclusion in access agreements, if issued
Written access requests and refusals copied to the Authority
sop: Licensees negotiate access in good faith; where they fail to agree within the prescribed period any party may refer the matter to the Authority for determination (s.43(1)-(2)).
Put the access agreement in writing and file it with the Authority (s.43(5)).
Authority enters party names, a general description of the matters governed and the date of the agreement in the register, without revealing terms and conditions (s.43(7)(a)).
Authority opens the register to public inspection on terms it determines (s.43(7)(b)).

controls.name: Co-location agreements filing, consultation and public register
controls.statement: A co-location agreement must be in writing in English and must not be implemented unless it is filed with the Authority and the consultation process is complete. A licensee's refusal to negotiate co-location must be in writing, set out the reasons in sufficient detail and be approved by the Authority. Third parties resident in the area and public authorities with control over it must be informed of the filing by newspaper publication at the parties' expense and afforded an opportunity to make submissions. The Authority must maintain a register of all co-location agreements containing, without revealing terms, the names of the parties, a general description of the matter and the date, open to public inspection.
evidence: Register of co-location agreements maintained under s.44(8)
Each co-location agreement as filed with the Authority
Written refusals to negotiate co-location with reasons and the Authority's approval of the refusal
Newspaper notices of the filing of co-location agreements
Submissions received from third parties and public authorities and the Authority's consideration of them
Authority orders to modify, cease or not undertake a co-location on public safety grounds
