sop: Licensees negotiate co-location in writing in English; where they fail to agree within the prescribed period either party may refer the matter to the Authority (s.44(1)-(3), (6)).
Put any refusal to negotiate in writing with reasons set out in sufficient detail and obtain the Authority's approval of the refusal (s.44(5)).
File the agreement with the Authority and complete the consultation process before implementing it (s.44(7)).

Inform third parties and public authorities of the filing by publication in a daily newspaper of general circulation in the area at the parties' expense and afford them an opportunity to make submissions (s.44(10)).
Authority enters party names, a general description and the date in the register and opens it to public inspection (s.44(8)).

controls.name: Tariff approval, publication and register of approved tariffs
controls.statement: A licensee must submit proposed tariffs with justification to the Authority for approval before introduction; the Authority approves or rejects within thirty days and gives reasons for rejection. After approval the licensee must publish the tariffs in at least two daily newspapers at least seven days before introduction, provide services only at approved tariffs and not vary them without prior written approval. The Authority must maintain a register of approved tariffs open to public inspection and may review tariffs for conformity. Licensees in a dominant position in a retail market must obtain prior approval with detailed justification, and holders of individual licences must price, rate, bill and denominate services in local currency. Exceeding approved tariffs or imposing an unauthorised charge is an offence.
evidence: Register of approved tariffs maintained under s.47(7)
Tariff submissions with justification filed by the licensee
Authority approval or rejection decisions with reasons within thirty days
Newspaper publications of approved tariffs at least seven days before introduction
Written approvals for any tariff alteration or variation
Authority tariff review reports under s.47(8)
Billing and rating configuration showing services priced and denominated in local currency
sop: Licensee submits the intended tariffs including the justification to the Authority for approval before introduction (s.47(3)).

controls.name: Detailed billing information for consumer verification
controls.statement: A licensee must, for electronic communications services provided to the public, provide detailed billing information so that consumers can verify whether they have been billed correctly. The Authority may carry out reviews of tariffs to ensure conformity with the section, which depends on billing records being accurate against the approved tariff.

controls.name: Central numbering database and licensee number returns including prepaid subscribers
controls.statement: The Authority must maintain and manage a record of the status of all number ranges, codes and blocks of numbers comprising the numbering plan in a central numbering database system. Every holder of an individual service licence and every holder of an individual network licence must submit to the Authority information on all numbers, including numbers of pre-paid subscribers, allocated under the licence. The numbering plan consists of a scheme of identification ensuring communications are correctly directed and must be non-discriminatory; regulations address surrender of unused numbers, number portability and subscriber complaints and remedies.

controls.name: Assignment of numbers and electronic addresses with annual class-assignment registration
controls.statement: Numbers and electronic addresses may be used only under an individual assignment or a class assignment, and use without an assignment is an offence. The Authority assigns individually in accordance with the national numbering plan, transparently and non-discriminatorily, choosing successful applicants by objective criteria made known in advance. Holders of a class assignment must submit an updated class assignment registration form fourteen days before each anniversary, failing which they are de-registered. Assigned numbers or electronic addresses may not be transferred to a third party without prior written consent of the Authority.

Obtain the Authority's prior written consent before transferring rights to use assigned numbers or electronic addresses (s.61).

controls.name: Registration of equipment manufacturer identification and mobile device IMEI numbers
controls.statement: An importer or supplier of any electronic equipment must register the original equipment manufacturer's identification with the Authority in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee. An importer or supplier of any mobile device must register the device's International Mobile Equipment Identification number with the Authority in the prescribed manner. Contravention is an offence. The Authority may, with the Minister's approval, appoint agents to undertake registration on its behalf, and the Minister may prescribe the registration fees.

controls.name: Mobile phone and SIM registration, personal particulars, disabling of unregistered equipment and IMEI integrity
controls.statement: The Authority must disconnect or disable any device or electronic equipment that is not approved or registered under the Act. Regulations may provide for registration of electronic equipment including mobile devices and subscriber identification modules for quality assurance and tracking, for the obligations of licensees, for identifying and disabling unregistered or irregularly obtained equipment on a licensee's network, and for the relevant personal particulars of a person coming on to the licensee's network. Licensees offering mobile phone services must register the phones on their network with the Authority. Interfering with the programming of a mobile handset, including modifying its IMEI number, is an offence.

controls.name: Publication of technical standards and public access to incorporated standards
controls.statement: The Authority is responsible for the establishment and publication of technical standards for all electronic communications equipment intended to be used in Zambia, seeking public submissions and taking account of international standards including those of the ITU. Where the Minister's regulations incorporate a technical standard by reference to its number, title and year of issue, the Authority must keep the text of each incorporated standard and every amendment or substitution, open it to public inspection during normal office hours and, on payment of the prescribed fee, furnish a copy. An incorporated standard that is amended or substituted by a competent national body is treated as referring to the amended standard unless otherwise stated.

controls.name: Type approval of electronic communications equipment
controls.statement: A person must not use, supply, sell, offer for sale, lease or hire any type of electronic communications equipment or apparatus, including radiocommunications equipment, unless it has been approved by the Authority. The Authority determines the types of equipment and circumstances in which approval is not required, conducts type approval tests and issues type approval certificates subject to procedures and fees, and must comply with the technical standards it has formulated when doing so.

controls.name: Confidentiality of information held by Authority members and staff
controls.statement: A person must not, without the written consent of or on behalf of the Board, publish or disclose to any unauthorised person, otherwise than in the course of that person's duties, the contents of any document, communication or information whatsoever which relates to or has come to that person's knowledge in the course of their duties under the Act. A person who knowingly publishes or communicates information disclosed in contravention commits an offence, as does the original disclosure.

controls.name: Inspection access to licences, agreements, accounts, books and records
controls.statement: A telecommunications officer, on production of the certificate of appointment, may demand production of and inspect or copy a licence or assignment, any agreement concluded or accounts kept under the Act. All books, records and documents that a licensee is required to keep are open to inspection at all reasonable times by a telecommunications officer or police officer, who may seize any book, record or document reasonably suspected to afford evidence of an offence. Failing to give information, or giving false or misleading information, to a telecommunications officer or police officer is an offence, as is obstructing an officer.

controls.name: Returns and information furnished to the Authority
controls.statement: The Authority may request any licensee to furnish, within a period the Authority determines, such documents and other information as it requires for the better carrying out of its functions, and failure to furnish is an offence. Failing or refusing to furnish a return or information in the manner and time prescribed, or furnishing a false or misleading return, is an offence. Licence conditions may require the licensee to furnish documents, accounts, returns, estimates and other information. The Authority determines and publishes annually, by 31 December, the list of regulated markets and licensees holding a dominant position, relying on the information it collects.

Verification or reconciliation of returns for accuracy
sop: Authority requests a licensee to furnish documents and other information within a period it determines (s.90(1)).
Licensee furnishes the return or information in the manner and time prescribed, and does not furnish false or misleading returns (s.82(a)).
Authority determines and publishes in the Gazette, not later than 31 December each year, the list of regulated markets and dominant licensees for the following year (s.40(1)).

controls.name: Protection against unauthorised access to and modification of programs and data, and of communications content
controls.statement: Without lawful authority, a person must not cause an electronic communications network or service to perform any function to secure access to any program or data held in it, do an act known to cause unauthorised modification of any program or data, secure access to or obstruct or intercept a network or service function, disclose any password, access code or other means of gaining access, or cause a network or service to cease to function. Offences carry a fine up to two million penalty units or imprisonment up to fifteen years, or both, and wilful removal, destruction or damage of installations, software, hardware or plant is separately punishable. A person employed in connection with a radiocommunication service must not unlawfully disclose or use for personal purposes the contents or existence of a message not of a public character, and disclosure is lawful only if compellable under law or for administration of justice.

Access control, privileged access and credential management records for network and service systems
Audit and security logs of access to and changes of programs and data
Incident records for unauthorised access, interception or modification
Staff confidentiality undertakings for personnel in radiocommunication services
Procedure for lawful disclosure of message contents (compelled by law or for administration of justice)

controls.name: Binding guidelines published in a daily newspaper
controls.statement: The Authority may make guidelines for the better carrying out of the Act. It must publish all guidelines in a daily newspaper of general circulation in Zambia, and they do not take effect until so published. Guidelines bind all persons regulated under the Act; consumer complaint-handling guidelines bind licensees and persons exempt from holding licences, and may include procedures on the protection of consumer information. The code of conduct for licensees takes effect from its publication in a daily newspaper. Contravening a guideline or decision of the Authority is an offence.

Newspaper publication notices for each guideline, showing publication date
Effective date of each guideline recorded against its publication date

policies.title: National Public Key Infrastructure Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: The Guidelines apply to Service Providers licensed under section 28 of the ECT Act (cl. 4) and are read as one with the Act, licence terms and other NPKI guidelines and standards (cl. 2).

ZICTA acts as National Root Certification Authority and regulates the National PKI, to foster trust in digital transactions and safeguard the integrity and confidentiality of critical information (cl. 1.2, 5.1).
Trust is tiered by Level of Assurance (LoA 1 to 4) across CA, RA, VA and TSA roles, and a provider may serve only providers of similar or lower LoA (cl. 15).
A risk management approach covers all protective security activity, aligned to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NIST SP 800-30 (cl. 7.1, 8.4).
Information assets are classified and protected in proportion to value, importance and sensitivity, and access follows classification and legal obligations (cl. 8.8.1).
PKI artefacts follow named open standards (RFC 5280, RFC 3647, RFC 5019, RFC 6960, RFC 3161, RFC 3628) and only NPKI-approved cryptographic algorithms (cl. 9.1.1, 11.1.1, 16).
Identity proofing must establish uniqueness, legitimacy, operation over time, linkage to the person and absence of known fraud (cl. 10.1.2).
Privacy is a precondition for evaluation: a Privacy Impact Assessment is mandatory for PKI systems handling personal information (cl. 6.1).
Separation of duties between the IT security adviser and the IT security manager (cl. 8.2.2).
Legislation or regulation on identity proofing takes precedence over the Guidelines (cl. 10.1.5).
management_intent: Service Providers maintain NPKI approved documents (Information Security Documentation, CPS and Certificate Policy, RA Operations Manual as applicable) and review them annually or on change (cl. 7.1, 7.2, Table 1).
Providers appoint security officials, develop security policies, risk plans and DR/BCP, and vet staff (cl. 8.2-8.7).
Information is security-classified, with access control, development and operational security matched to the classification (cl. 8.8).
A Privacy Impact Assessment precedes audit evaluation, and staff receive guidance on the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 (cl. 6.1, 8.1.1).
An independent audit of all PKI systems is undertaken annually and reported to the National Root CA with non-compliances and remediation (cl. 6.2).
CA, TSA and VA operations conform to the named RFCs and only approved algorithms are used (cl. 9.1, 11.1, 12.1, 16).
Lifecycle, security and access events are logged and retained for at least seven years after the action is completed (cl. 9.13, 11.6).
Key archives are protected to the CA's level of assurance, limited to recoverable encryption keys, and every recovery is logged and alerted (cl. 9.11).

Registration Authorities verify identity against primary and secondary evidence and authoritative sources (PACRA, Immigration Department), recording and securely transmitting certificate information to the CA (cl. 10).
Service continuity and orderly migration of subscribers are ensured when a CA, RA, TSA or VA terminates (cl. 9.12, 10.7, 11.5, 12.5).

controls.name: Security classification of information assets
controls.statement: The Service Provider must implement policies and procedures for security classification and protective control of electronic and paper information assets that match their value, importance and sensitivity (8.8.1a). The text does not list the classification levels.
evidence: Information classification policy and procedures
Classified information asset register
Evidence of classification labels applied to electronic and paper records
Information Security Documentation referencing classification

controls.name: Access control tied to classification and legal obligations
controls.statement: Access control rules for all information, ICT systems, networks (including remote access) and applications must be based on business requirements and assessed or accepted risk, and be consistent with information classification and legal obligations (8.8.1c). Security measures must apply through all stages of system development and implementation (8.8.1d).
evidence: Access control policy and rule sets
Mapping of access rules to classification levels
Access reviews and remote access records
System development security measures and implementation checklists

controls.name: Mandatory Privacy Impact Assessment
controls.statement: A Service Provider must undertake a Privacy Impact Assessment for all PKI-related systems that collect, process, store or disclose personal information, and before an evaluation by an Auditor (6.1.1). ISO/IEC 29134:2017 or another internationally recognised standard may be used (6.1.2).
evidence: Privacy Impact Assessment report per PKI system handling personal information
Inventory of PKI systems that collect, process, store or disclose personal information
PIA methodology reference (ISO/IEC 29134:2017 or equivalent)
Evidence PIA was completed before the audit evaluation (dated)
sop: Undertake a PIA for all PKI systems that handle personal information (6.1.1a)
Complete the PIA before an evaluation by an Auditor (6.1.1b)

controls.name: Data Protection Act guidance and security awareness training
controls.statement: The Service Provider must give staff and contractors relevant information and security awareness training and guidance on the relevant sections of the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 (8.1.1). Personnel doing identity verification must also receive PKI skills training and records of that training must be retained (9.3.1, 10.6).
evidence: Training programme covering security awareness and Data Protection Act guidance
Training attendance records for staff and contractors
Training records for verification personnel (retained)

controls.name: Standards conformance register (RFC profiles)
controls.statement: A CA must conform certificates and CRLs to RFC 5280 (CRLs to X.509 v2 profiles), CPS and Certificate Profile to the RFC 3647 framework, and OCSP responses to RFC 5019 and RFC 6960; non-conforming extensions must be marked non-critical (9.1.1, 9.1.2). TSAs follow RFC 3161, RFC 3628 and RFC 5280 (11.1.1); VAs process X.509 v3 certificates, CRLs per RFC 5280 and OCSP per RFC 5019 (12.1.1).
evidence: Register of applicable standards with version or RFC number per artefact
Conformance test results or certificate profile validation reports
Certification Practice Statement structured per RFC 3647
Sample certificates and CRLs showing critical/non-critical extension handling

controls.name: Approved cryptographic algorithms
controls.statement: A Service Provider must use encryption products that implement NPKI-approved algorithms: asymmetric (DH, ECDH, DSA, ECDSA, RSA), hashing (SHA-2 family) and symmetric (AES 128/192/256, 3DES) (16.1.1-16.1.4). Table 6 gives certificate validity limits by key entropy.
evidence: Cryptographic algorithm register mapped to the approved list
Key and algorithm configuration of CA, RA, VA and TSA systems
Cryptographic product specifications

controls.name: CA logging and seven-year log retention
controls.statement: A CA must record key lifecycle events, certificate and subscriber lifecycle events, CRL/OCSP generation and security events (access attempts, privilege changes, outages, firewall activity, facility entry and exit), and retain the logs for a minimum of seven years after the action is completed (9.13.1-9.13.5).
evidence: Logging policy listing event types captured
Log extracts for each category (key lifecycle, certificate lifecycle, CRL/OCSP, security events)
Evidence of seven-year retention (archive configuration or oldest retained record)
Facility entry and exit logs
sop: Record key lifecycle management events (9.13.1)
Record CA and subscriber lifecycle events (9.13.2)
Record CRL and OCSP generation (9.13.3)
Record security events (9.13.4)
Retain logs for at least seven years after the action is completed (9.13.5)

controls.name: TSA logging and seven-year log retention
controls.statement: A TSA must log time stamping unit key and certificate lifecycle events, clock synchronisation to UTC and loss of synchronisation, TSA key lifecycle events, token generation and security events, and retain logs for at least seven years after the action is completed (11.6.1-11.6.3).
evidence: TSA logs for token generation and clock synchronisation to UTC
Security event logs for TSA systems
Evidence of seven-year retention
sop: Record the listed time stamping and security events (11.6.1, 11.6.2)
Retain logs for at least seven years after the action is completed (11.6.3)

controls.name: Key archive and recovery
controls.statement: The key archive must be protected commensurate with the CA's protection and level of assurance, archive only encryption keys that enable data recovery (never authentication or signature keys), hold all private keys encrypted, and log, audit and alert every key recovery instance (9.11.1). Subscriber non-repudiation keys must not be backed up or escrowed (9.2.1h).
evidence: Key archive design and access controls
List of archived key types showing only recoverable encryption keys
Key recovery log and alert/audit records
Evidence that non-repudiation keys are not escrowed
sop: Archive only encryption keys that enable recovery of encrypted data (9.11.1c)
Log, audit and alert all key recovery instances (9.11.1f)

controls.name: Identity proofing process and objectives
controls.statement: A Registration Authority must verify the sufficiency and accuracy of identity documentation, accurately record and securely transmit certificate information to the CA, securely store applicant and subscriber information, and notify the CA and request revocation where an identity error is found (10.1.1). Proofing must address uniqueness, legitimacy, operation in community over time, linkage to the person and absence of known fraud (10.1.2).
evidence: Identity proofing procedures mapped to the five objectives
Completed proofing records per subscriber (documents verified, method, outcome)
Record of transmission to the CA
Error notifications and revocation requests
sop: Verify the sufficiency and accuracy of identity documentation (10.1.1a)
Accurately record and securely transmit certificate information to the CA (10.1.1b)
Promptly notify the CA and request revocation when an identity proofing error is found (10.1.1d)

controls.name: Authoritative sources for individual identity (Immigration, primary and secondary evidence)
controls.statement: Proofing methods include interviews, biometric comparison, verified documents and information from authoritative sources such as the Zambia Immigration Department (10.1.3). Individual evidence is weighted as Primary (government-issued, with photograph) or Secondary, as listed in Table 3 (10.2), with the LoA-specific verification checks in Table 7.
evidence: Register of accepted primary and secondary evidence types (Table 3)
Proofing records showing the document or source verified
Records of checks against Immigration Department or other authoritative sources
Biometric comparison or interview records where used

controls.name: Organisation identity proofing against PACRA register
controls.statement: For organisations, the RA must verify the organisation, its Authoriser and the Certificate Manager. The Authoriser's association with the organisation is evidenced by an authoritative public register such as PACRA or by legal or regulatory documents (10.3.4, 10.4.3). Table 4 requires the PACRA notice bearing the entity name and TPIN with online verification linking the TPIN to the business name.
evidence: PACRA registration notice (original or certified copy) showing business name and TPIN
Record of online PACRA verification linking TPIN to business name
Authoriser and Certificate Manager appointment documents
Record of removal of Certificate Manager privileges (10.3.7)
sop: Provide original or certified PACRA notice showing business name and TPIN (Table 4, Option 1)

controls.name: Registration Authority operations manual and identity information storage
controls.statement: An RA must develop an Operations Manual covering roles, identity proofing procedures, logging, RA-CA interactions, incident response (including data spills), audit requirements, backup and archive, access control, and storing identity information collected (10.5.2-10.5.4). Retained applicant and subscriber information must be stored securely per Approved Documents (10.1.1c). No retention period for identity information is stated.
evidence: RA Operations Manual
Procedure for storing identity information collected
Backup and archive procedures
Access control procedures for RA facilities

controls.name: Annual independent PKI audit
controls.statement: A Service Provider must have all PKI-related systems audited by an Auditor annually and report outcomes, including areas of non-compliance and corrective measures, to the National Root CA (6.2.1). Audits use document review, onsite evidence gathering, staff interviews, evidence against the Cyber Baseline Operation Security Expectations Guidelines and review of NPKI approved documents (6.2.2).
evidence: Annual PKI audit report
Audit report submission to the National Root CA
Non-compliance remediation tracker
Audit evidence pack (documentation review, interviews, onsite evidence)
sop: Undertake an annual audit of all PKI-related systems using an Auditor (6.2.1a)
Report audit outcomes to the National Root CA (6.2.1b)

controls.name: NPKI approved documents and annual review
controls.statement: A Service Provider must develop and maintain the Information Security Documentation and, by provider type, the CPS, Certificate Policy and RA Operations Manual (7.1, Table 1), and review them annually or when threats, risks or the operating environment change (7.2). The risk management plan is likewise reviewed annually (8.4.1b).

Document version history and annual review records
Security risk management plan and its review record

controls.name: Certificate repository and revocation list availability
controls.statement: A CA must generate, maintain and publish a list of revoked certificates accessible to relying parties through standard protocols, respond within ten seconds under normal conditions, and restrict write access to the publication location (9.8.1). A VA must maintain the same list and response time (12.4).

Response time test results (ten seconds or less)

Published CRLs conforming to RFC 5280

controls.name: Certificate content accuracy and certificate profile
controls.statement: When generating a certificate, the CA must ensure information from the RA is accurately transcribed, other generated information is accurate, and the certificate contains all elements required by its Certificate Profile (9.4.1). The profile must specify key usage and the Key Usage extension must not be marked both Critical and Mandatory (9.2.1d, 9.2.1g).

controls.name: Certificate revocation process and grounds
controls.statement: A CA must provide a subscriber revocation process, publicly disclose how to report fraud, misuse or key compromise, revoke promptly per the Certificate Profile, and revoke on the grounds in 9.10.1 (such as key compromise or inaccurate information). Table 6 sets maximum revocation times by LoA (96, 72, 48 and 24 hours for LoA 1 to 4).

Revocation log with request and action timestamps
Revocation timeliness measurement against the LoA limit
sop: Provide in the CPS a revocation process allowing a subscriber to request revocation (9.9.1a)

controls.name: Security officials and separation of duties
controls.statement: A Service Provider must appoint an IT security adviser and an IT security manager, who may not be the same person (8.2.1, 8.2.2). It must also identify positions of trust requiring access to security-classified assets (8.3.1e) and vet and clear personnel with access to PKI resources and subscriber or relying party information (8.6).

Register of positions of trust

Organisation chart showing separation of the two roles

controls.name: Level of Assurance categorisation of service providers
controls.statement: Service Providers are categorised by Level of Assurance 1 to 4 (Table 5). Each LoA is tied to the value of information handled and the security of the environment, and a provider may serve only providers of similar or lower LoA (15.1.1, 15.1.2, 15.2.2-15.2.5).

Mapping of services to LoA requirements (Tables 6 to 9)
Evidence that counterparties are of similar or lower LoA

policies.title: Quality of Service Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: QoS parameters are measured and reported from the end-user's perspective; network performance parameters are reported from the perspective of QoS achieved by the licensee (cl.3(c)).
Monitored parameters must relate to aspects of service that affect users as a whole, not those with minimal usage (cl.3(a)).
QoS is defined across four perspectives from ITU-T G.1000: consumer requirements, QoS offered, QoS achieved, QoS perceived (cl.3(b)).

Measurement and definitions are anchored to international standards (ITU-T E.800, E.804, G.1000, P.800, P.863, Y.1540; ETSI TS 102 250-2, EG 201 769-1, EG 202 057-1, TR 103 219) rather than locally invented methods.
Targets are numeric, measurable and tied to a prescribed measurement method; a failure to meet a target value is a breach (cl.1, cl.9(a)).
Only KPIs designated Enforceable are legally binding; Non-Enforceable KPIs are monitored but not sanctionable until designated (cl.1, Schedule 4).
Due process: the licensee is notified of findings, may validate results, and is given an opportunity to show cause before any determination or sanction (cl.9).
Transparency: QoS results, determinations and coverage maps are published for the consumer's information (cl.13).
Proportionality: sanctions take account of seriousness, post-contravention conduct and prior record (cl.10(b)).
Consumer safeguard in both retail and wholesale markets is the stated purpose of the Guidelines (Preamble).
management_intent: Give effect to ICT Act s.67(1) by specifying and publishing the minimum QoS standards that service providers must meet, with methods of measurement and sanctions for breach (Preamble).
Safeguard consumers of ICT services and products in retail and wholesale markets (Preamble).
Enable the Authority to monitor sector performance, including availability, quality, cost and standards of electronic communication services, under ICT Act s.6 (Preamble).
Let the Authority designate any KPI enforceable without revising the Guidelines, so that targets can be hardened over time (cl.1 Non-Enforceable definition).
Allow the Authority to require licensee information to monitor and enforce QoS and consumer protection, and to compile aggregate information for sectoral planning and reporting (cl.8(a)).
Maintain a verifiable audit trail by requiring licensees to keep QoS data for 24 months and submitting that data and procedures to Authority audit (cl.14, cl.15).
Create a deterrent through graduated sanctions and statutory penalties for contravention (cl.10, cl.17).

controls.name: KPI definition structure (parameter register)
controls.statement: Every QoS parameter is defined with the same structure: service function, category, parameter name, description, measurement method or formula, source standard, published measurement, target and (in Schedule 4) enforceability status. The text and Schedule 4 differ on the critical transmission/cluster fault repair target (3 hours in cl.4.3, 4 hours in Schedule 4), so the register needs one authoritative value.
evidence: Parameter register listing each KPI with description, formula, source standard, published measurement, target and status
Schedule 4 summary tables of targets as currently in force
Reconciliation note for text-versus-schedule target differences
Version history of the Guidelines and any Authority notice revising a target

controls.name: Enforceability designation of KPIs
controls.statement: Each KPI carries an Enforceable or Non-Enforceable status, and the Authority may designate a Non-Enforceable KPI enforceable without revising the Guidelines. The status is the control point that determines whether a missed target is a prescribed contravention.
evidence: KPI status column (Enforceable / Non-Enforceable) for all 41 numbered parameters
Authority notices designating a KPI enforceable, with effective date
Change log showing status transitions per KPI

controls.name: Measurement method, measurement systems and NPMS
controls.clause: cl.2, cl.3(c)(iii), cl.5.1.3, cl.5.2, cl.10(c), Schedule 3
controls.statement: QoS is assessed at network performance, end-to-end and quality-of-experience levels using prescribed methods: network counters via the Network Performance Monitoring System, drive/walk/stationary tests, and surveys or POLQA. Licensees must establish measurement systems consistent with the Guidelines, and availability must come from an automatic data collection system based on the fault management system with timestamped alarms.
evidence: Description of the licensee's measurement systems and NPMS configuration
NPMS counter definitions mapped to each network performance KPI
Type-approval record for end-to-end measurement tools
Fault-management alarm and event logs with out-of-service and restored timestamps
Drive/walk test plans and raw test logs

controls.name: Reporting area, reporting period and measurement granularity
controls.statement: Measurements are taken and recorded once for each reporting area, parameter and service in a defined reporting period. The Authority measures QoS at national, provincial, district, township, site or cell level and may sanction at each level, so records must carry the area and period dimension.
evidence: Measurement dataset showing reporting area, reporting period, parameter and service keys
Geographic hierarchy used for reporting (national to cell)
Sample sanction or finding tied to a specific area level

controls.name: Documented measurement exclusions and counting rules
controls.clause: cl.4.1(b), cl.4.2(b), cl.4.3(b), cl.5.1.1 (Call Drop Rate note)
controls.statement: The Guidelines prescribe what is excluded from a KPI, for example cancelled orders, customer-side faults, fully automatic services, emergency services, calls ended by depleted credit and requests the operator cannot fulfil. Licensees must apply and be able to show these exclusion and counting rules (such as one request per site) when reporting.
evidence: Exclusion rules register per KPI
Reconciliation of raw counts to reported figures showing excluded records and reasons
Order, fault and call-centre extracts with exclusion flags

controls.name: Quarterly quality-of-experience assessment
controls.statement: The Authority or its appointee conducts a quarterly QoE assessment of customer satisfaction with availability, accessibility, reliability, billing performance and help/support services, each with a target above 90%. QoE is determined by customer satisfaction surveys or by POLQA/MOS (ITU-T P.863).
evidence: Quarterly QoE survey instrument and sampling method
QoE results per parameter against the 90% target
MOS/POLQA test records
Appointment letter for any third party conducting the assessment

controls.name: Licensee quarterly QoS report
controls.statement: A licensee submits a quarterly QoS report to the Authority within the first two weeks of the following quarter, and the Authority may ask for a report at any time. The report must contain the reporting period, performance findings, QoS performance and analysis, and mitigation measures.
evidence: Submitted quarterly QoS reports with submission date stamps
Report template showing the four required content elements
Evidence of any ad hoc report requested by the Authority and the response
Register of submissions against the two-week deadline
sop: Submit the quarterly report within the first two weeks of the following quarter.
Include reporting period, performance findings, QoS performance and analysis, and mitigation measures.

controls.name: Provision of information to the Authority
controls.statement: The Authority may require a licensee to provide information to monitor and enforce QoS, consumer protection and competition rules, assess fees, support efficient use of scarce resources and compile aggregate sector data. A request must carry detailed specifications, a contact person and a response period.
evidence: Information request with specification, named contact and deadline
Licensee response and transmittal record
Log of information requests and fulfilment dates
sop: Authority provides detailed specifications of the request and identifies a contact person.
Authority specifies the period within which the licensee must respond.

controls.name: Transmission service SLA filing
controls.statement: A transmission service provider must enter into an SLA with its customers (including a Mean Time To Repair target) and file the SLA and any variation with the Authority within 14 days. A licensee also reports the QoS performance of its transmission provider within the first two weeks of the following quarter.
evidence: Signed SLAs with filing receipt showing the 14-day timeline
Filed SLA variations or amendments with dates
Transmission provider QoS performance submission
SLA register with MTTR targets and uptime commitments
sop: File the SLA with the Authority within 14 days of signing.
File any SLA variation or amendment within 14 days of the variation.
Submit the transmission provider's QoS performance within the first two weeks of the following quarter.

controls.name: QoS reporting, validation and enforcement procedure
controls.statement: A failure to meet a QoS target in Part II is a prescribed contravention. The Authority may produce quarterly QoS reports, notify the licensee of findings, validate results with the licensee within ten working days, allow three days to show cause, and make a determination within ten working days.
evidence: Authority QoS report and findings notice with dates
Validation meeting record or correspondence
Show-cause notice and licensee response
Determination document with timeline from report to decision
Case file showing whether the licensee responded in time
sop: Authority notifies the licensee of QoS findings and may validate the results with the licensee within ten working days of the report.
Where targets are missed, give the licensee three days to show cause why enforcement action should not be taken.
Make a determination within ten working days, based on findings and the licensee's submission.
If the licensee fails to respond in the specified period, proceed to determination or sanction.

controls.name: Sanctions and statutory penalties
controls.statement: Sanctions for a prescribed contravention include public apology, refund, compensation, warnings (after the second, suspension), fines compounded under ICT Act s.88, variation of licence conditions, review of tenure, and suspension or revocation. Offences carry fines and imprisonment under ICT Act s.79(1) and s.67(1)(a), and the sanction chosen must weigh seriousness, conduct and prior record.
evidence: Sanction decision record with reasoning on seriousness, conduct and prior record
Register of warnings, fines and licence actions per licensee
Refund and compensation proofs
Compounding of offence record under ICT Act s.88

controls.name: Publication of QoS results and determinations
controls.statement: The Authority publishes QoS measurement results quarterly (or at the end of each monitoring period) on its website or in a daily newspaper. All determinations are published unless publication would not be in the public interest.
evidence: Published quarterly QoS results page or newspaper notice with date
Published determinations register
Record of any determination withheld and the public-interest reason
sop: Publish QoS measurement results quarterly or at the end of each monitoring period, on the Authority website or a daily newspaper.
Publish all determinations unless it is not in the public interest to do so.

controls.name: Coverage map publication by technology
controls.statement: A licensee submits to the Authority and publishes on its website, in all service outlets and in mass media, up-to-date coverage maps by technology in the prescribed manner. The maps must depict coverage per technology using the stated signal thresholds, and coverage targets include 80% composite population coverage and 85% of trunk roads.
evidence: Coverage maps per technology (2G, 3G, 4G, 5G) with date and version
Radio planning model inputs and drive-test validation
Evidence of publication on website, in outlets and in mass media
Coverage statistics: geographic and population, by technology and composite
sop: Submit up-to-date coverage maps by technology to the Authority.
Publish the maps on the licensee's website, in all service outlets and in mass media in the manner the Authority prescribes.

controls.name: 24-month QoS record retention
controls.statement: A licensee must retain QoS data, measurements and related records it collects for at least 24 months after the end of the reporting period. This is the retention basis an auditor will test.
evidence: Retention schedule showing a 24-month minimum from end of reporting period
Sample QoS records from 24 months back, retrievable on request
Storage and archive configuration for QoS data
Disposal log showing nothing deleted before 24 months

controls.name: QoS audits and trouble-ticket system access
controls.statement: The Authority audits the licensee's QoS measurements, reporting and record-keeping procedures, conducts technical audits of parameters, network interfaces and elements, and may access the licensee's trouble-ticketing system for service provisioning and complaints. The licensee must therefore keep these systems auditable and accessible.
evidence: Audit notices, scope and findings
Access arrangements or credentials to the trouble-ticketing system
Trouble-ticket extracts for provisioning and complaints
Documented QoS measurement, reporting and record-keeping procedures
Audit remediation tracker

controls.name: Appeal of Authority decisions
controls.statement: A licensee may appeal a decision of the Authority to the tribunal established under the ICT Act. Determination records must therefore be complete enough to support review.
evidence: Register of appeals lodged and outcomes
Determination file with reasoning and licensee submissions
Tribunal decisions affecting QoS determinations

controls.name: Cross-regulator precedence for digital financial service KPIs
controls.statement: For the mobile money unsuccessful-transaction resolution target of 24 hours, the Bank of Zambia target takes precedence over the Guidelines. The DFS KPIs (transfer success rate, transfer time, resolution time) are Non-Enforceable in Schedule 4.
evidence: Bank of Zambia instrument setting the resolution target
DFS KPI register showing the governing target and its source
Mobile money transaction logs with reported-unsuccessful and credited timestamps

policies.title: Digital Forensics Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Principle 1: forensics only proceeds with a documented basis (course of action, search warrant, affidavit, request letter or other documentation the Authority may determine).
Principle 2: adhere to the applicable laws and policies of the matter under investigation.
Principle 3: take reasonable effort to identify all sources of potential evidence, within the scope of the investigation.
Principle 4: prevent or limit contamination of data or device (imaging, tools that prevent data alteration); document any contamination and the changes caused.
Principle 5: access only the data targeted by the investigation, using a method compliant with Principles 3 and 4.
Principle 6: take reasonable measures to preserve the integrity of any data or device under investigation.
Principle 7: extracted and interpreted data must be tested and validated (peer review, alternative tools, hash values) to verify accuracy.
Principle 8: document all stages of the investigation to form an audit trail that a third party could repeat to obtain comparable results.
management_intent: Evidence handled in digital forensics must remain demonstrably uncontaminated and verifiable (integrity by imaging, write-blocking and hashing) so conclusions are accurate.
Every forensic engagement must leave a complete, repeatable documentary trail from authorisation through acquisition, examination, report and handover, closed by a chain-of-custody record.
Only appointed or designated persons may conduct forensics, and especially sensitive material (indecent content of children) is access-limited and referred to the relevant law enforcement agency.
The Authority supports compliance through voluntary manual endorsement and audits on invitation, rather than a licensing or registration regime.

controls.name: Documented legal basis and preliminary assessment before forensics
controls.statement: Before conducting digital forensics, the officer or person must ensure a course of action, search warrant, affidavit, request letter or other documentation determined by the Authority exists, and must carry out a preliminary assessment to fix scope and course of action (source of request, case correspondence, chain of custody, warrant and other legal authorisation, physical and operational state of the device, information sought, remote and out-of-Republic sources). Cl.9.0 allows exemption from certain parts in an emergency (threat to life, damage to property, financial loss); the exemption cross-refers to parts '5.4' and '5.7', which do not exist as separately numbered principles (the principles are numbered 5.1, 5.2 then 5.3 repeated), so the exempted scope is ambiguous.
evidence: Search warrant, affidavit, request letter or other authorising document held on the case file
Copy of the correspondence that clearly outlines the matter being examined (6.4(c)(ii))
Preliminary assessment record covering source of request, scope, device physical/operational state and information sought
Written record of the emergency (threat to life, property damage or financial loss) where cl.9.0 exemption is relied on
sop: Ensure authorising documentation exists prior to conducting forensics
Analyse the data or device to determine scope and course of action
Identify the source of the request and review case details in written correspondence
Review chain of custody, search warrant and any other legal authorisation
Determine physical state of hardware and operational status of the device
Identify the information or data sought, including remote storage and servers outside the Republic
Store the data or device subject to investigation in a secure environment

controls.name: Forensic imaging with write-blocking, clean target media and hash validation at acquisition
controls.statement: Acquisition must preserve the original data from alteration, damage or destruction. A digital forensic image must be created with specialised imaging tools producing an identical copy; software or hardware write-blockers must prevent data alteration; hashing or equivalent integrity monitoring must be applied to the image, and applied again to the image or copies after the examination concludes. The examiner's system configuration (system date, time, operating system) must be verified and documented before use, the examiner's target storage must be forensically clean, and system configuration information must be retrieved from the image.
evidence: Imaging tool and write-blocker identification and settings used for each acquisition
Hash values of the forensic image recorded at acquisition and again after examination, with comparison result
Pre-use verification record of examiner system configuration (system date, time, operating system)
Record that examiner target storage was forensically clean before use
System configuration information retrieved from the image
sop: Verify and document hardware and software configurations (system date, time, OS) of the forensic system before use
Obtain access to storage media while protecting the device from static electricity, magnetic fields and other sources of damage
Ensure the examiner's storage device is forensically clean before use as target media
Create the forensic image using specialised imaging tools to produce an identical copy
Use software or hardware write-blockers during imaging
Apply validation or integrity monitoring such as hashing to the image created
Retrieve system configuration information from the image
After examination, apply integrity monitoring such as hashing to the image or copies of the data

controls.name: Testing and validation of extracted and interpreted data
controls.statement: All extracted and interpreted data must undergo robust testing and validation using accepted methods to verify accuracy. The methods must include peer review, use of alternative tools, hash values or other relevant methods. Where results are inconclusive, examination must be repeated with alternative methods or tools, and the examination process must be reviewed in its entirety. Physical, logical and file system extraction (or other methods) are the stated extraction methods.
evidence: Peer review record for the extraction and analysis results
Record of alternative tool or method comparison, including where results were inconclusive
Validation log showing hash values used to verify extracted data
Examination review record covering extraction and analysis results in their entirety
sop: Prepare a working directory on separate storage media for recovered or extracted evidentiary files
Extract the information subject to the investigation using forensic methods and tools
Conduct analysis of the extracted data
Conduct examination using alternative methods or tools where results are inconclusive
Review the examination process considering extraction and analysis results in their entirety

controls.name: Contamination prevention, documentation and integrity preservation
controls.statement: All reasonable measures must be taken to prevent or limit contamination (compromise of integrity of data or device during the forensic process). Access must be limited to the data targeted by the investigation using a method compliant with Principles 3 and 4. Where contamination does occur, the events that led to it and the changes to the data or device must be documented.
evidence: Contamination incident record describing the events leading to contamination and the changes made to the data or device
Record of preventive measures applied (imaging, alteration-preventing tools)
Scope-of-access record showing only targeted data was accessed
sop: Take all reasonable measures to prevent or limit contamination, such as imaging and tools that prevent data alteration
Document the events that led to contamination and the resulting changes to data or device
Access only the digital data targeted by the investigation

controls.name: Documented audit trail and contemporaneous case notes
controls.statement: All stages of the investigation must be documented so as to form an audit trail describing the processes implemented, which a third party could repeat to obtain comparable results. Documentation must record all processes and observations, be complete, accurate and comprehensive, include contemporaneous notes with dates, times, descriptions and results, and retain copies of the correspondence outlining the matter and of the chain of custody documentation. No retention period for these records is stated in the Guidelines.
evidence: Examiner notes showing dates, times, descriptions and results of processes undertaken
Copy of the case correspondence outlining the matter being examined
Copy of chain of custody documentation
Evidence that a third party can repeat the documented procedure (e.g. repeat-examination or peer re-performance record)
sop: Record all processes undertaken and observations made
Ensure documentation is complete, accurate and comprehensive
Take notes during consultation and during the forensic process including relevant dates, times, descriptions and results
Maintain a copy of the correspondence that outlines the matter being examined
Maintain a copy of chain of custody documentation

controls.name: Chain of custody form completed per device
controls.statement: The chain of custody form set out in the Schedule must be completed for each device subject to investigation prior to conducting digital forensics, maintained as part of the documentation, and completed again upon handover of the report and devices. The Schedule is referenced as 'Clause 15' in its heading although the chain of custody requirement is cl.12; the form's fields are not present in the extracted text (the Schedule pages appear to be image-only), so the form's field list could not be verified.
evidence: Completed chain of custody form for each device, dated before forensics began
Chain of custody form completed at handover of report and devices
Evidence labels and evidence bag records linked to the form (7.3(j))
sop: Complete the chain of custody form in the Schedule for each device prior to conducting forensics
Review chain of custody as part of the preliminary assessment
Label seized devices, place them in evidence bags and document chain of custody
Complete the chain of custody upon handover of the report and devices

controls.name: Forensic report with 11 minimum content fields
controls.statement: A report must be produced after the forensic process containing at minimum: (i) identity of the request source and date of receipt; (ii) unique case identifier or submission number; (iii) scope; (iv) description and clear photographs of items submitted; (v) brief description of steps taken during examination; (vi) identity and signature of the examiner; (vii) technologies and tools used; (viii) findings; (ix) conclusion; (x) date of report handover; (xi) any other relevant information. The report and all devices must be handed over and the chain of custody completed.
evidence: Forensic report containing all eleven 6.5(a) fields
Photographs of items submitted for forensics
Handover record for the report and devices, with date of handover
Signed identity of the examiner who conducted the forensics
sop: Produce a report following the forensic process including the 6.5(a) content items
Hand over the report and all devices subject to investigation
Ensure the chain of custody is completed upon handover

controls.name: Evidence collection, labelling and secure handling of devices at scene and in storage
controls.statement: Before collecting evidence at a crime scene a search warrant must be ensured where necessary and appropriate personal protective equipment used; where necessary, user and account information must be gathered (user names, login names, e-mail and web mail accounts, instant message names, offsite storage, ISP, security provisions, access restrictions, destructive devices or software, and all passwords). Devices must be secured, the scene and location of evidence documented (photograph, video or sketch), evidence collected, labelled and preserved, and packaged and transported securely. Devices must be kept, stored and transported protected from magnetic sources, humidity extremes, liquids, heat, loud sound and radio frequency. Mobile devices must be signal-blocked (Faraday bag, flight mode or switch-off). The information collected under 7.1(c), notably passwords and account identifiers, is sensitive and the Guidelines state no protection or retention rule for it.
evidence: Scene documentation (photographs, video footage or sketch plan) showing device and evidence locations
Evidence labels and evidence bag records for each seized device
Completed user and account information record under 7.1(c), where obtained
Records of storage environment and transport conditions for devices
Record of signal-blocking measures applied to mobile devices
sop: Ensure a search warrant where necessary and use appropriate personal protective equipment before collecting evidence
Recognise, identify, seize and secure all devices at the scene
Document the entire scene and the specific location of the evidence found
Collect, label and preserve the digital evidence
Package and transport digital evidence in a secure manner
Block incoming and outgoing signals of mobile devices using a Faraday bag, flight mode or switching off
Record the contents of a displayed screen by photograph, video or documentation where necessary

controls.name: Restricted access and referral for indecent content of children
controls.statement: When dealing with indecent content of a child on a device subject to investigation, a person conducting forensics must limit access to that content and report the matter to the relevant law enforcement agency; a law enforcement officer must likewise limit access. The Guidelines do not define the access-limiting mechanism, the reporting timeframe or the format of the report.
evidence: Access-restriction configuration or access log for the indecent content
Report or referral to the relevant law enforcement agency, with date
List of persons authorised to access the restricted content
sop: Limit access to the indecent content of the child
Report the matter to the relevant law enforcement agency (person conducting forensics)

controls.name: Only appointed or designated persons conduct forensics
controls.statement: A person shall not conduct digital forensics unless appointed or designated by an authority or relevant law; cl.7.1 refers to persons appointed under the Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act No. 2 of 2021 or other relevant law. The Guidelines apply to law enforcement agencies and any person conducting forensics in the Republic, and allow reference to international standards such as ISO 17025 and ISO 27037 (permissive, not mandatory).
evidence: Appointment or designation instrument for each examiner, naming the appointing authority or law
Register of persons conducting forensics within the institution or laboratory
Evidence of any ISO 17025 or ISO 27037 alignment claimed

controls.name: ZICTA manual endorsement and audit on invitation
controls.statement: A law enforcement officer or person conducting forensics may submit a digital forensics manual to the Authority for review and endorsement. The Authority may, on invitation, audit institutions, laboratories and persons conducting forensics from time to time to promote compliance. Both are optional on the part of the institution; no mandatory submission or audit cycle is stated.
evidence: Digital forensics manual (and any ZICTA endorsement letter)
Invitation to ZICTA for audit and the resulting audit report
Corrective action records following an audit
sop: Submit a manual on digital forensics to the Authority for review and endorsement (optional)
Authority conducts audits on invitation to promote compliance

policies.title: ICT Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Transparent and controlled regulatory framework: innovative ICT products, services and business models are tested in a live environment under Authority oversight (cl.4).

Proportionate public disclosure: only information necessary to inform the public may be disclosed, and never commercially sensitive, proprietary, confidential or personal information without consent or legal requirement (7.2).
Participant retains ownership of intellectual property; the Authority has only a limited, purpose-bound access right (10.1-10.2).
Consumer protection is a condition of participation: consumers informed and complaints resolved (cl.11).
Participation is not a legal exemption: liability to customers and all operational, commercial and customer risks remain with the Participant (cl.18).
Participants must comply with the ICT Act, the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 and any other relevant law (cl.19).
management_intent: Allow controlled live testing of innovation while the Authority keeps supervisory visibility through reports, ad hoc information requests, on-site inspection and 24-hour adverse-incident notice.
Keep personal data and privacy risk inside the sandbox bounded by the Data Protection Act, with privacy risk identified up front in the Risk Management Plan.
Separate what the public may be told about a sandbox test from what stays confidential or personal.
Capture regulatory learning (complaints, insights, debriefing feedback) so the Authority can review its regulatory frameworks.

controls.name: Proof of legal standing and Declaration of Ownership and Responsibility
controls.statement: An application must be accompanied by documentation of legal or institutional standing to ensure accountability and traceability: certified Certificate of Incorporation for registered companies, letter of endorsement or affiliation from the hosting Zambian institution for academic or research bodies, and a certified National Registration Card (NRC) copy for individual innovators or startups under formation. All Applicants must submit a Declaration of Ownership and Responsibility executed by an authorised representative. Identity documents such as the NRC carry personal data, and the Guidelines state no handling or retention rule for them.
evidence: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and registration documents
Letter of endorsement or affiliation from hosting Zambian institution
Certified copy of NRC for individual innovators
Signed Declaration of Ownership and Responsibility from an authorised representative
sop: Apply to the Authority for authorisation with the required accompanying documents
Submit a Declaration of Ownership and Responsibility executed by an authorised representative

controls.name: Application proposal with test plan, privacy-inclusive risk plan, exit plan and compliance commitment
controls.statement: The proposal may contain: team profiles; problem and solution description; a detailed Test Plan (objectives, scope, KPIs, timeline); source of funding; a Risk Management Plan identifying all potential risks, expressly including operational, technical, consumer, financial and data privacy risks, with mitigations; an Exit Plan; a compliance commitment to sandbox rules, reporting and oversight; and a minimum viable product. The proposal content is stated as 'may contain', so the privacy-risk element is not mandatory on the face of the text, although cl.19 separately requires Data Protection Act compliance. Applicants must also meet eligibility criteria (new or significantly improved innovation, identifiable benefit, regulatory relevance, readiness to test).
evidence: Test Plan with objectives, scope, KPIs and timeline
Risk Management Plan with data privacy risks and mitigation measures
Exit Plan covering conclusion of the test and transition of remaining customers
Signed compliance commitment
Declared source of funding

controls.name: Authorisation decision, Letter of Authorisation and testing duration
controls.statement: The Authority determines a duly completed application within 30 days; the clock stops while further particulars are requested; an application lapses if mandatory requested information is not provided. On grant a Letter of Authorisation is issued with terms and conditions; rejection must be in writing with reasons; appeal lies to the tribunal under the ICT Act. Approval does not exempt the Applicant from other authorities' requirements. Testing may not exceed 12 months from commencement, extendable by at most six months on a written application at least 30 days before expiry with justification and a progress report; all testing must stay within the scale, scope and conditions of the approval.
evidence: Application register showing receipt date, particulars requests and determination date
Letter of Authorisation with terms, conditions, commencement date and duration
Written rejection with reasons (where applicable)
Extension application with justification and progress report
sop: Authority determines the application within 30 days of receipt of a duly completed application
Authority may request further and better particulars, which suspends the 30-day period until submitted
Grant the application and issue a Letter of Authorisation with terms and conditions
Inform a rejected Applicant in writing with reasons
Submit extension applications in writing at least 30 days before expiry

controls.name: Compliance with the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021
controls.statement: A Participant shall comply with the ICT Act, the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 and any other relevant law, and sandbox approval does not exempt the Participant from requirements of any other relevant authority; participation is not a legal exemption (cl.18). Because sandbox tests run in a live environment with real consumers, personal data processed during the test is within the Data Protection Act. The Guidelines do not state any additional data protection process, so the assessable evidence is the Participant's own Data Protection Act compliance posture.
evidence: Participant's data protection compliance documentation applicable to the test (e.g. registration, privacy notice, processing records)
Mapping of personal data processed in the test to a lawful basis under the Data Protection Act
Evidence of engagement with any other authority with jurisdiction over the innovation (6.7)

controls.name: Consumer information and dispute resolution
controls.statement: Compliance with consumer safeguards is a condition of participation. At minimum, a Participant must implement internal processes and controls to ensure consumers are informed of the proposed innovation, and a proper dispute resolution mechanism for consumer complaints. Liability to customers remains with the Participant.
evidence: Consumer-facing notice or disclosure describing the innovation and that it is under test
Documented consumer complaint and dispute resolution procedure
Internal process and control documentation for informing consumers

controls.name: Periodic reports including KPIs, test data and consumer complaint log
controls.statement: A Participant submits periodic reports at a frequency set in the terms of the Authorisation. The report may include progress against KPIs, key data on test parameters (e.g. number of users, transaction volumes), summary of risks and mitigations, a log of all consumer complaints received and their resolution status, and key learnings. Failure to comply may lead to revocation of approval. The report content is permissive ('may include'), so the complaint log and test parameters are not strictly mandated by the text.
evidence: Periodic reports submitted to the Authority with submission dates
Consumer complaint log with resolution status
Test parameter data (users, transaction volumes) supporting the KPI progress
Reporting frequency stated in the Letter of Authorisation
sop: Submit periodic reports at the frequency determined in the Authorisation terms and conditions

controls.name: 24-hour written notice of adverse incidents including privacy or security compromise
controls.statement: Where an adverse incident occurs, the Participant shall notify the Authority in writing within 24 hours. An adverse incident is any event during participation that results in, or has the potential to result in, compromise of information security or privacy, disruption of services, regulatory non-compliance, or any other negative impact from testing. Failure to manage risk so as to pose significant risk to consumers or the ICT ecosystem is a ground for revocation. No separate notification of affected individuals or of the Data Protection Act regulator is stated in these Guidelines.
evidence: Written adverse incident notice to the Authority with timestamps of occurrence and notification
Adverse incident log classifying events (security, privacy, service disruption, non-compliance)
Incident handling and mitigation records
sop: Notify the Authority in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of an adverse incident

controls.name: Public disclosure limited to non-confidential information, with personal data excluded
controls.statement: The Authority may publish information on approved Participants and authorised activities: Participant name, general description of the product, service or business model, duration and scope of the test, applicable safeguards and any Regulatory Relief. Disclosure must be proportionate and limited to what is necessary to inform consumers, stakeholders and the public, and must not disclose commercially sensitive, proprietary, confidential or personal information except with the Participant's consent or where required by law.
evidence: Public register or publication of approved Participants and sandbox activities
Pre-publication review showing excluded confidential and personal information
Participant consent for any additional disclosure, or record of legal requirement

controls.name: Purpose-limited Authority access to Participant information and inspection
controls.statement: Participant intellectual property (including software, source code, algorithms, data models, documentation and know-how) remains the Participant's. For supervision, monitoring, evaluation and reporting the Participant grants the Authority a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free, non-transferable access right solely to the extent necessary for its functions; the Authority may not commercially exploit, reproduce, publish, disclose or license it without prior written consent or legal requirement. The Authority may conduct on-site inspections, request ad hoc information and require meetings at any time, and may collaborate with other relevant stakeholders (cl.14), without any stated limit on onward sharing of information received.
evidence: Record of Authority information requests and inspections with stated purpose
Prior written consent for any reproduction, publication or disclosure of Participant IP
Record of any information shared with other stakeholders under cl.14 and its basis

controls.name: Disclosure and approval of collaborations
controls.statement: A Participant may collaborate with other innovators, research institutions or industry partners only if the arrangements are disclosed to and approved by the Authority. Where collaboration involves sharing consumer or test data with the partner, the Guidelines do not state the sharing conditions beyond Authority approval.
evidence: Collaboration arrangement disclosure submitted to the Authority
Authority approval of the collaboration
Data sharing terms with the partner, where data is shared
sop: Disclose the collaboration arrangements to the Authority and obtain its approval

controls.name: Exit, withdrawal, revocation and consumer offboarding
controls.statement: A Participant exits through successful completion (final comprehensive test report, then formal exit letter), voluntary withdrawal (at least 30 days' written notice with a wind-down and consumer transition plan), unsuccessful test (exit at expiry and implement the exit strategy) or revocation by written notice. Revocation grounds include material breach, failure to manage risks, violation of law, false or misleading information and insolvency. Before revocation the Authority must give notice stating grounds and allowing written representation within not more than 14 days from service. On revocation the Participant must immediately cease onboarding new consumers and activate its exit plan to offboard existing consumers under Authority supervision. No retention, return or deletion rule for consumer and test data after exit is stated.
evidence: Final comprehensive test report and formal exit letter
Written withdrawal notice and wind-down plan
Revocation notice stating grounds, and record of representations received within the 14-day window
Evidence of consumer offboarding under Authority supervision
Disposition record for personal and test data held at exit
sop: Submit a final comprehensive test report upon successful expiry of the testing period; Authority issues a formal exit letter
Give at least 30 days' written notice with a wind-down plan for voluntary withdrawal
Authority gives notice of grounds and a period of not more than 14 days for written representation before revocation
On revocation, immediately cease onboarding new consumers and activate the exit plan to offboard existing consumers under Authority supervision

controls.name: Record of sandbox insights and regulatory learning
controls.statement: As a condition of exit each Participant attends a mandatory Regulatory Debriefing giving feedback including regulatory provisions that acted as barriers and suggested reforms. The Authority shall maintain a record of the insights and feedback gathered from all sandbox tests, use the findings for periodic reviews of its regulatory frameworks, and may publish an annual Regulatory Learning Report for public consultation.
evidence: Record of insights and feedback from all sandbox tests
Regulatory Debriefing attendance and feedback record for each exiting Participant
Annual Regulatory Learning Report (where published)
sop: Participant attends a mandatory Regulatory Debriefing session as a condition of exit
Authority maintains a record of the insights and feedback gathered from all sandbox tests

policies.title: Type Approval Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Approval is mandatory: no person may use, supply, sell, offer for sale, lease or hire electronic communications apparatus without Authority approval (ICT Act s.66; SI 6 of 2011 Reg 4).
Type approval certificates are specific to a model of apparatus and remain valid unless revoked (5.2, 5.4).
An already type approved model need not be re-approved (5.3).
Conformity is verified against applicable standards through accredited test laboratory reports (5.5.2(g), Appendix 2).
Foreign approvals are accepted only from National Regulatory Authorities and Conformity Assessment Bodies with a mutual recognition agreement and published by the Authority (5.6.1-5.6.2).
Approved apparatus must carry a legible Authority-approved label evidencing conformance (cl.7).
management_intent: Only apparatus whose model has been verified against applicable standards, or accepted on recognised foreign certification, may enter the Zambian market.
Each approval is traceable through a unique certificate number tied to a specific model and displayed on the equipment label.
Approvals are kept truthful and current: false information, non-conformity, changed standards or public interest can lead to revocation, and modifications and name changes must be notified.
The applicant evidence package (form, test reports, declarations, documents) is standardised so the Authority can assess conformity consistently.

controls.name: Model-specific approval certificate with unique number, valid until revoked
controls.statement: The Authority issues type approval certificates indicating that a particular model has been approved; a certificate is specific to a model. Certificates (type approval and type acceptance) bear a unique number, remain valid unless revoked (no expiry date), and an already approved model need not be re-approved, which presupposes the Authority can look up approved models. The Guidelines do not expressly mandate a certificate register or its fields; a register of issued certificates is implied by 5.3 and by the unique number requirement. Certificate numbers follow the format ZMB/ZICTA/TA/YYYY/.. (see C02).
evidence: Register or list of issued type approval and type acceptance certificates by model
Copy of an issued certificate showing model and unique number
Status of each certificate (valid, revoked) and the date of revocation where applicable
sop: Issue a type approval certificate bearing a unique number once the Authority is satisfied requirements are met (Regulation 7 of SI 6 of 2011)
Issue an approval certificate bearing a unique number for type acceptance once requirements are met (Regulation 6 of SI 6 of 2011)

controls.name: Unique certificate number scheme ZMB/ZICTA/TA/YYYY on the label
controls.statement: The ZICTA sample label carries the registration type approval certificate number allocated by ZICTA to the equipment model, in the form ZMB/ZICTA/TA/YYYY/.. . Label presentation rules are stated: black characters on white background, blue (C100 M100 Y0 K0) and black (K100) colour codes, no character under 2mm height, the word ZICTA at least 3mm with proportions maintained. The meaning of the trailing '..' (sequence component) and any uniqueness control are not stated, so the full number format is only partly specified.
evidence: Number allocation log showing each allocated number, year and model
Sample ZICTA label conforming to Appendix 3
Check that no number is allocated twice
sop: Substitute the placeholder with the registration type approval certificate number allocated by ZICTA to the equipment model

controls.name: Standard application form (Form 1) with required data fields per model
controls.statement: Applicants apply using the approved Form 1 (obtainable at the office or on the website), in triplicate if lodged physically or one copy if electronic, with a separate form for each model. Where multiple models share technical characteristics, one application with a manufacturer's declaration of similarity is allowed (identical in circuit diagram, characteristics and performance; cosmetic differences ignored). Form 1 captures: application type (type approval, type acceptance, modification); applicant type and licence or registration number; company, contact, addresses, phone, email; manufacturer name and address; documentation checklist; equipment category and intended use; equipment details (brand, type name, model number, country of origin, frequency range, bandwidth, transmission capacity, channels, output power, channel spacing, frequency stability, modulation, ITU emission designator); antenna details; equipment licence required or not; standards compliance test report numbers (EMC, Radio, Health and Safety, Technology Specific); serial number of sample equipment; signed declaration; official-use receipt fields. Form 1's declaration refers to 'assignment/reservation' wording that does not match type approval (appears carried over from another form), and its documentation list describes the declaration of conformity as manufacturer-issued, whereas 5.5.2(g)(ii) requires one from an ISO certified independent third party laboratory.
evidence: Completed Form 1 for each model, signed by authorised persons with Power of Attorney or Board Resolution
Declaration of similarity from the manufacturer where multiple models are covered
Official-use receipt record (receipt number, date, amount, stamp)
sop: Obtain the approved application form from the Authority's office or website
Submit the form in triplicate if lodged physically, or one copy if electronic
Complete a separate application form for each model
Furnish a manufacturer's declaration of similarity where applying for several models with the same technical characteristics
Authority issues a quotation for a non-refundable fee upon receipt of a complete application
