controls.name: Conformity evidence package for type approval and Authority/independent testing
controls.statement: A type approval application must be accompanied by duly signed and dated test reports from accredited test laboratories showing compliance with Appendix 2 standards (as amended); a declaration of conformity from an ISO certified independent third party laboratory; technical and operational documents including manuals; circuit diagram, PCB layout, part list and design information; external and internal photographs; sample units where applicable; and any other information the Authority requires. Samples remain Authority property and serve as a reference for future compliance assessments. The Authority may test the apparatus itself or require testing by an independent approved laboratory at the applicant's cost.
evidence: Signed and dated test reports from accredited laboratories for each applicable standard
Declaration of conformity from the ISO certified independent laboratory
Technical documents, circuit diagram, PCB layout, parts list and photographs
Sample unit register and Authority-held samples (serial numbers matching Form 1 item 17)
sop: Submit test reports, declaration of conformity, technical documents, design information, photographs and samples with the application
Authority may undertake testing for type approval purposes
Authority may require testing by an independent approved laboratory at the applicant's cost
Samples remain the property of the Authority as reference for future compliance assessments

controls.name: Standards code list by equipment type (Appendix 2)
controls.statement: Appendix 2 sets reference standards for conformity by equipment type and service: public mobile (GSM/DCS, DECT, UMTS/IMT), private mobile (TETRA, amateur, citizen band, PMR, maritime, radar), fixed wireless (RLAN, WiMax/FWA, microwave links), short range devices, satellite, broadcasting, telecommunications terminal equipment (PSTN, xDSL, voice, leased lines, switched data), health and safety, and EMC, each with frequency bands and applicable ZS EN/ETSI/ITU/IEC/FCC standard codes. Reports must be against these 'and any other applicable standards as amended from time to time'; a change in applicable standards, or deviation from standards, is a ground for revocation. Appendix 2 contains entries without a standard (radio-navigation radar marked 'TBC'), and the extracted table text is fragmented, so row-level accuracy should be checked against the original document.
evidence: Current standards code list maintained as controlled reference data, with version and effective date
Change log recording amendments to applicable standards
Mapping of each approved model to the standards it was tested against

controls.name: Published lists of accredited laboratories and recognised foreign regulators and conformity bodies
controls.statement: An accredited test laboratory is one recognised by the Authority in line with ILAC and ISO 17025 and published on the Authority website. The Authority shall from time to time publish on its website the list of National Regulatory Authorities and Conformity Assessment Bodies it approves for the purposes of the Guidelines; type acceptance relies on approval by such a body that has entered into a mutual recognition agreement with the Authority. No update frequency is stated beyond 'from time to time'.
evidence: Published list of recognised accredited test laboratories on the Authority website
Published list of approved National Regulatory Authorities and Conformity Assessment Bodies
Mutual recognition agreements underpinning each listed body
Date of last update of each published list
sop: Authority publishes on its website the list of approved National Regulatory Authorities and Conformity Assessment Bodies from time to time

controls.name: Type acceptance on recognised foreign certificate of conformance
controls.statement: Where an apparatus is type approved by a recognised National Regulatory Authority or Conformity Assessment Body (mutual recognition agreement in place), the type acceptance process applies. The application must include a duly signed Certificate of conformance from that body; full name and mailing address of the manufacturer and of the applicant; installation and operating instructions for the user; technical and operational documents and manuals; and any other information required. The Authority issues an approval certificate bearing a unique number on being satisfied.
evidence: Signed Certificate of conformance from the recognised regulator or conformity assessment body
Manufacturer and applicant name and address record
Installation and operating instructions and technical documents
Check of the issuing body against the published recognised list
sop: Apply for type acceptance using Form 1 (Appendix 1)
Submit signed Certificate of conformance, manufacturer and applicant details, instructions and technical documents
Authority issues a quotation for a non-refundable fee on receipt of a complete application
Authority issues an approval certificate bearing a unique number when satisfied under Regulation 6 of SI 6 of 2011

controls.name: Approval of modified or rebranded apparatus and 14-day name-change notice
controls.statement: An already approved apparatus whose technical characteristics change through modification must be re-submitted under the clause 5.5 procedure; an application for modification may also be made where apparatus is renamed or rebranded. A holder of a type approval certificate that has undergone a name change must notify the Authority within 14 days of the name change. The Guidelines do not say how the Authority records the change against the certificate.
evidence: Modification applications and resulting approvals linked to the original certificate
Name-change notification with the date of the name change and date of notice
Updated certificate or register entry reflecting the name change
sop: Apply for approval of the modified apparatus following clause 5.5
Notify the Authority within 14 days of a name change of a certificate holder

controls.name: Revocation of approval including for fraud or false information
controls.statement: An approval may be revoked if obtained by fraud or submission of false information; if the model deviates from and fails to comply with relevant standards; if the Authority becomes aware of a circumstance that would have required or permitted refusal; if applicable standards change; or if revocation is in the public interest. The Form 1 declaration states that untrue or fraudulent particulars lead to revocation and forfeiture of fees. Unlike the sandbox guidelines, no notice or representation period before revocation is stated, and failure to comply is an offence under section 79(1) of the ICT Act.
evidence: Revocation notice recording the ground relied on and date
Updated certificate register showing revoked status
Signed applicant declaration of completeness and truth (Form 1)

controls.name: Conformance label on equipment, packaging and manual
controls.statement: A manufacturer, distributor, importer or supplier must ensure type approved apparatus carries a legible label approved by the Authority (Appendix 3), or one issued by the approved regulator or conformity assessment body where the type acceptance process was used. The label must be visible and legible at all times, affixed on the apparatus, packaging and user manual (or an alternative method approved in writing by the Authority where not feasible), and affixed before the apparatus is imported, supplied, sold, offered for sale or leased.
evidence: Sample of labelled apparatus, packaging and user manual showing the certificate number
Written Authority approval of any alternative label display method
Import or supply records showing label affixed prior to import or sale
sop: Affix the label on the apparatus, the packaging and in the user manual
Affix the label before the apparatus is imported, supplied, sold, offered for sale or leased

policies.title: Network Outage Credits Framework
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Protect consumers of electronic communication services against unjustified network outages (cl.1, cl.3(i)).
Compensation must be fair, timely and proportionate to the duration and severity of the outage (cl.7(i)).
Provide a predictable and standardised approach to calculating compensation, using the Schedule 1 base table and the cl.11.4 formula (cl.3(ii), cl.11).
Promote accountability and service quality among licensees; licensees keep records and non-compliance carries sanctions (cl.3(iii), cl.15).
Transparency: outages are communicated promptly to consumers and the Authority, with an RCA report and quarterly compensation reporting (cl.3(iv), cl.13, cl.14).
Where feasible compensation is automatic and driven by system records, so consumers do not need to apply (cl.7(ii), cl.11.7(iii)).
management_intent: Management is expected to run outage detection, credit calculation and crediting as a record-driven, auditable process: compensation is processed automatically from system records (cl.11.7(iii)) and records of outage incidents and related compensation must be maintained (cl.15).

Management is expected to evidence, not merely assert, any exemption relied on, for example planned maintenance notified in advance, theft or vandalism where all necessary steps were taken, and cyber incidents where all reasonable measures are demonstrated (cl.12).
Management is expected to meet the notification, 72-hour RCA and quarterly reporting timelines owed to the Authority (cl.13, cl.14).

Management accepts that paying outage credits does not give immunity from other QoS sanctions, and that non-compliance may bring a fine, review of licence conditions and public disclosure (cl.11.7(x), cl.15).

controls.name: Outage and compensation record-keeping
controls.statement: A licensee shall maintain records of network outage incidents and related compensation provided to consumers (cl.15), and compensation is processed from system records (cl.11.7(iii)). The Framework states no retention period for these records, no record format and no named record owner.
evidence: Network outage incident register (one record per incident)
Per-consumer compensation ledger linked to the incident it relates to
Records retention schedule or policy covering outage and compensation records (the Framework states no period)
Named owner or custodian of the outage and compensation records
Sample reconciliation of the incident register to the compensation ledger

controls.name: Outage duration measurement and compensation trigger determination
controls.statement: Outage duration is calculated from the time the disruption commenced until full restoration of services (cl.9). Compensation is triggered when an outage exceeds one continuous hour in a 24-hour period, or when multiple outages in a 24-hour period aggregate to the threshold (cl.5, cl.6(iii), cl.10). The risk/impact band is taken from duration in Schedule 1 (Low =1 hour, Medium 1-6 hours, High >6 hours). As written, the Low (=1) and Medium (1-6) bands both include exactly one hour, while cl.5 and cl.10 trigger compensation only above one hour.
evidence: Outage start and restoration timestamps per incident, with the source system (network monitoring or fault log)
Rule specification for 24-hour aggregation of intermittent outages
Risk/impact band assigned per incident
Sample of incidents just above and just below the one-hour threshold with the trigger decision recorded
sop: Calculate outage duration from the time the disruption commenced until full restoration of services (cl.9)
Trigger compensation when an outage lasts more than one consecutive hour in a 24-hour period, or when multiple outages in 24 hours aggregate to the threshold (cl.5, cl.10)

controls.name: Compensation calculation and Schedule 1 base compensation parameters
controls.statement: Base compensation is 2.5 voice minutes and 50 MB, with penalty multipliers of 1.25x (Low), 1.5x (Medium) and 2x (High); Outage Credit = (Base Compensation x Risk/Impact Multiplier) x Outage Duration in hours (cl.11.1-11.4). Fixed postpaid credit = (Monthly Subscription Fee / 30 / 24) x Risk Multiplier x Outage Duration; fixed prepaid uses the standard base compensation aligned to Schedule 1 (cl.11.6). Worked examples in cl.11.5 and cl.11.6 provide test values. The Framework states no rounding rule for fractional results and no version control for the Schedule 1 parameters.
evidence: Configuration of the credit calculation (base 2.5 minutes and 50 MB, multipliers 1.25/1.5/2) with version and change history
Test results reproducing the cl.11.5 examples (3.125 min + 62.5 MB; 22.5 min + 450 MB; 42.5 min + 850 MB) and cl.11.6 examples (K7.81; 225 MB; K14.63)
Recalculation by the assessor of credits for a sample of real incidents
Approval or change record for any change to the Schedule 1 parameters
sop: Select the base compensation (2.5 voice minutes and 50 MB) for the risk/impact level (cl.11.1)
Apply the penalty multiplier of 1.25x, 1.5x or 2x (cl.11.3)
Outage Credit = (Base Compensation x Risk/Impact Multiplier) x Outage Duration (hours) (cl.11.4)
Fixed postpaid: Credit Value = (Monthly Subscription Fee / 30 / 24) x Risk Multiplier x Outage Duration (cl.11.6)
Fixed prepaid: apply standard base compensation aligned with the Schedule 1 voice/data matrix (cl.11.6(b))

controls.name: Automatic crediting of affected customers from system records
controls.statement: A licensee shall automatically credit affected customers via airtime, data or bill reductions after 3 days of the outage resolution, processing compensation automatically from system records so that consumers do not need to apply (cl.11.7(i), (iii)). Credit is proportional to the services in the subscribed active package (cl.11.7(vi)); no cash or electronic money is given (cl.11.7(v)); postpaid fixed internet is credited on the next billing cycle invoice (cl.11.7(vii)); prepaid fixed internet is credited as extra data or a bundle extension valid for at least 7 days (cl.11.7(viii)). Staggering over a maximum of 30 days needs Authority approval (cl.11.7(ii)). The text says 'after 3 days' without a deadline, while the Figure 1 process flow shows compensation within 30 days, so the timing rule is ambiguous.
evidence: Credit batch logs showing each credit linked to an outage incident and a customer
Extract of affected-customer eligibility derived from system records (subscription active during the outage)
Date of outage resolution versus date credit applied, per incident
Authority approval letter for any staggered payment
Exceptions list of customers not credited and the reason
sop: Process compensation automatically based on system records; consumers do not apply (cl.11.7(iii))
Credit affected customers via airtime, data or bill reductions after 3 days of the outage resolution (cl.11.7(i))
Where staggering is needed for extensive or recurring outages, obtain Authority approval and complete payment within a maximum of 30 days (cl.11.7(ii))
Credit postpaid fixed internet customers on the next billing cycle invoice (cl.11.7(vii))
Credit prepaid fixed internet users as extra data volume or bundle extension valid for at least 7 days (cl.11.7(viii))

controls.name: Consumer notice that compensation has been issued
controls.statement: A licensee shall notify affected customers via SMS or email once compensation has been issued, and shall communicate data top-ups or validity extensions transparently via SMS or email (cl.11.7(iv), (ix)). The Framework states no required content for the notice, no deadline for sending it and no retention period for proof of notice.
evidence: Notice templates (SMS and email) for credits, data top-ups and validity extensions
Per-customer sent log with timestamp and delivery status linked to the credit record
Sample reconciliation of credits issued to notices sent
sop: Notify affected customers via SMS or email once compensation has been issued (cl.11.7(iv))
Communicate data top-ups or validity extensions transparently via SMS or email (cl.11.7(ix))

controls.name: Consumer outage notification and public apology
controls.statement: A licensee shall notify affected consumers of any network outage no later than one hour after detection and inform them once services are restored, through channels that may include SMS broadcasts, the licensee's website, daily newspapers and social media (cl.13(iii)), and shall issue a public apology within two hours following restoration (cl.13(iv)). Failure to communicate outage notifications or updates promptly is itself a compensation trigger (cl.6(ii)).
evidence: Outage notification log with detection time and notice time per incident
Copies of SMS broadcasts, website posts, newspaper notices and social media posts with timestamps
Restoration notices to consumers
Public apology publication with its time relative to restoration
sop: Notify affected consumers no later than one (1) hour after detection of an outage (cl.13(iii))
Inform consumers once services have been restored (cl.13(iii))
Issue a public apology to affected consumers within two (2) hours following restoration of service (cl.13(iv))

controls.name: Outage notification to the Authority and 72-hour Root Cause Analysis report
controls.statement: A licensee shall notify the Authority of all network outages using a risk-based approach and the timelines in the Consumer Protection and Code of Conduct Guidelines (cl.13(i)); for planned service, system upgrades or migration, inform the Authority within seven days (7) of the upgrade and once completed (cl.13(i)(a)); and furnish an RCA report within 72 hours detailing among other things the cause, time, duration and mitigation measures (cl.13(ii)). Figure 1 shows the Authority informed within 1 hour. The start of the 72-hour period is not stated, and the Consumer Protection and Code of Conduct Guidelines timelines are incorporated by reference without a version.
evidence: Outage notifications to the Authority with timestamps and acknowledgements
RCA reports with submission timestamps per incident
RCA template showing at least cause, time, duration and mitigation measures
Planned-maintenance, upgrade or migration notices to the Authority
Reference copy of the Consumer Protection and Code of Conduct Guidelines timelines applied
sop: Notify the Authority of the outage using the risk-based timelines (cl.13(i))
Furnish the Authority with an RCA report within 72 hours covering cause, time, duration and mitigation measures (cl.13(ii))
For planned upgrades or migration, inform the Authority within seven days and once completed (cl.13(i)(a))

controls.name: Quarterly network outage compensation report to the Authority
controls.statement: A licensee shall submit to the Authority a quarterly network outage compensation report including: (i) date, time and duration of outages; (ii) services affected; (iii) number of affected consumers; and (iv) total compensation disbursed (cl.14). The Framework does not define the unit of 'total compensation disbursed' (voice minutes, MB or ZMW value), the submission deadline after quarter end, or the submission format.
evidence: Quarterly reports as submitted, with submission dates
Reconciliation of each report to the outage incident register and the compensation ledger
Report template or data specification for the four content items
Authority acknowledgement of receipt
sop: Submit a quarterly network outage compensation report to the Authority covering date/time/duration, services affected, number of affected consumers and total compensation disbursed (cl.14)

controls.name: Evidence for exclusions and exemptions from compensation
controls.statement: A licensee is not obliged to pay outage credits for force majeure, civil unrest, planned maintenance communicated in advance to the Authority and consumers, subsea cable cuts, theft and vandalism where it can be proven that all necessary steps were taken, cyber security threats where all reasonable measures can be demonstrated, prolonged power outages beyond regulatory backup timeframes (case-by-case), international fibre cuts, customer-caused faults, and other circumstances determined by the Authority (cl.7(iii), cl.12). Several exemptions are conditional on the licensee proving or demonstrating the steps it took; the Framework does not say how or to whom.
evidence: Exemption determination record per incident (reason, decision, approver)
Advance notices of planned maintenance to the Authority and consumers, with dates
Evidence of safeguards relied on for theft, vandalism and cyber security exemptions
Power backup records compared with the Installation Guidelines timeframes for prolonged power outage claims
List of incidents excluded from compensation, with reasons, for each reporting period

controls.name: Customer segment and package entitlement reference data
controls.statement: The Framework applies to last-mile retail customers on prepaid and postpaid plans and does not apply to Enterprise Customers, who are governed by SLAs (cl.4). Compensation is proportional to the services in the subscribed active package (voice, data, SMS); pay-as-you-go customers receive voice and data (cl.11.7(vi)). Applying this requires a reliable customer segment and package entitlement attribute as at the time of the outage. Small Office/Home Office is defined by reference to a determination of the Authority and no threshold is stated.
evidence: Customer segment reference data (Last Mile, SOHO, Enterprise, Pay-as-you-go) with definitions
Customer-to-package entitlement data as at the outage time
Rules mapping each package to the services compensated
Sample of segment classification decisions for Enterprise and SOHO customers
Authority determination of SOHO, if any

policies.title: Private Networks Guidelines (DRAFT)
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: [DRAFT - not binding] A private network is for the exclusive use of a specified person or closed user group and is not used to provide electronic communications services to the general public (cl.2, cl.8(a)).
[DRAFT - not binding] A licence exemption relates only to the network licence and does not remove radiocommunication licensing, numbering, type approval or other obligations (cl.5.2).
[DRAFT - not binding] Spectrum for private mobile networks is shared, non-exclusive and local, protected only inside the approved coverage area (cl.6.2.3, cl.6.2.4).

[DRAFT - not binding] A private network is isolated from public networks: no interconnection without prior written approval, no roaming, and no internal signalling, addressing or numbering extended into a public network (cl.7).

[DRAFT - not binding] Core, control and management elements, and the stores of subscriber data and authentication credentials, are kept on the licensee's premises and not hosted outside Zambia (cl.8(c)).
[DRAFT - not binding] All apparatus is type-approved before installation, importation or deployment (cl.8(d)).
management_intent: [DRAFT - not binding] The draft signals that management of a private mobile network licensee would need to keep core elements and the stores of subscriber data and authentication credentials on its own premises in Zambia (cl.8(c)); the Authority has asked whether in-country data centres or remote support from outside Zambia should be allowed (consultation Q18), so the final rule may change.

[DRAFT - not binding] The draft signals that coverage-area data is expected to define a single contiguous area confined to the licensee's premises (cl.6.2.3(a)); whether a format such as WGS 84 or a GIS file will be mandated is an open consultation question (Q10).
[DRAFT - not binding] Numbering resources, including the shared Mobile Country Code 999, would be assigned for one year, renewable, and limited to the authorised private network (cl.6.3(e)-(g)).
Because the instrument is a draft for consultation, an assessment against it is a readiness view only; no statement here creates a binding obligation until the Guidelines are finalised.

controls.name: Localisation of core elements, subscriber data and authentication credentials
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] Core, control and management network elements, including where subscriber or user data and authentication credentials are stored, shall be physically located on the premises of the licensee and shall not be located or hosted outside the territory of Zambia (cl.8(c)). As drafted both conditions apply together. The text does not address remote management or support from outside Zambia, hosting in an in-country data centre or a licensed provider's core, or backups and replicas; consultation Q18 asks whether these should be permitted.
evidence: Network architecture and data-flow diagram showing the physical location of core, control and management elements
Asset register with the physical location of each element that stores subscriber data or authentication credentials
Inventory of subscriber data and authentication credential stores, including backups and replicas, with location
Hosting, managed-service or vendor contracts showing nothing is hosted outside Zambia
Inventory of remote management and support access paths from outside Zambia (not addressed in the draft text; raised in Q18)
Site inspection or location attestation for the licensee premises

controls.name: Coverage area definition and data format
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] The coverage area shall be defined by coordinate points, a vector polygon or a building footprint, delineating a single contiguous area that shall not extend beyond the premises of the licensee (cl.6.2.3(a)). The draft does not specify a coordinate reference system, file format or accuracy; consultation Q10 asks whether to specify WGS 84 coordinates or a GIS file format.
evidence: Coverage-area data submitted with the Radiocommunication Licence application (coordinates, polygon or footprint)
Proof of the premises boundary (title, lease or site plan) supporting the declared coverage area
Specification of the format, coordinate reference system and accuracy used for the coverage data
Radio access network plan with predicted coverage (cl.6.4(d)) reconciled to the declared coverage area

controls.name: Boundary field-strength limit and compliance measurement
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] A licensee shall ensure that the field strength produced by its base stations, measured at the boundary of the approved coverage area, does not exceed the limit specified in its Radiocommunication Licence (cl.6.2.3(b)). The Authority may confirm compliance by field measurement at any time after operations begin (cl.6.2.3(c)) and may vary the limit to prevent or remedy harmful interference (cl.6.2.3(d)). The limit value, measurement height and reference bandwidth are not set in the draft (Q10).
evidence: Radiocommunication Licence stating the boundary field-strength limit
Licensee boundary field-strength measurement records with method, height and reference bandwidth
Authority field measurement reports and licensee responses
Notices varying the limit and evidence the variation was implemented

controls.name: Numbering resource assignment and use
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] A person intending to establish a private mobile network shall apply to the Authority for numbering resources in Form 1 of the National Numbering Plan Regulations, 2010 (cl.6.3(a)); the Authority approves or rejects within sixty (60) days of a complete application (cl.6.3(c)); assignment is for one (1) year and renewable on application (cl.6.3(e)); use is limited to the authorised private mobile network and shall not be used for routing outside the approved network scope (cl.6.3(f)); the shared Mobile Country Code 999 may be used subject to approval and assignment by the Authority (cl.6.3(g)). The clause text does not state an assignment register, an identifier format, or how network codes are assigned (Q14 refers to network codes assigned by the Authority).
evidence: Numbering application (Form 1) and Authority approval or rejection with dates
Numbering assignment record or certificate, including MCC 999 and any network code assigned
Renewal applications compared with the one-year assignment term
Network routing configuration showing assigned numbers are not routed outside the approved private network
sop: Apply to the Authority for numbering resources in Form 1 of the National Numbering Plan Regulations, 2010 (cl.6.3(a))
Authority assesses the application for eligibility and approves or rejects within sixty (60) days of a complete application (cl.6.3(b), (c))
Numbering resources are assigned upon payment of prescribed fees where applicable (cl.6.3(d))
Renew the one (1) year assignment by application to the Authority (cl.6.3(e))

controls.name: Technical documentation accompanying spectrum and numbering applications
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] Applications for spectrum and numbering shall be accompanied by technical documentation covering: (a) a comprehensive description of all services to be delivered, including intended use cases; (b) the proposed network architecture and specifications, including the specific equipment; (c) information on the use of numbering resources; and (d) a radio access network plan covering overall radio network, spectrum usage, predicted coverage, site locations and design (cl.6.4).
evidence: Technical documentation pack submitted with the application, covering items (a) to (d)
Network architecture description naming equipment, reconciled to the type approval inventory
Radio access network plan with site locations and predicted coverage
Named author or owner of the documentation and its version

controls.name: Interconnection approval and isolation of signalling, addressing and numbering
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] A private network shall not interconnect with any public network except with the prior written approval of the Authority (cl.7(a)); roaming between a private mobile network and any PLMN shall not be permitted (cl.7(b)); and no internal signalling, addressing or numbering resources of a private network shall be advertised, routed, switched or otherwise extended into any public network (cl.7(c)). Whether ordinary internet access or corporate WAN links count as interconnection is an open question (Q15).
evidence: Written Authority approval for each interconnection with a public network
Register of interconnections and external links
Firewall, border and signalling configuration showing internal signalling, addressing and numbering are not advertised externally
Confirmation that no roaming arrangement with a PLMN exists

controls.name: Type approval and installation standards for apparatus
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] A licensee shall ensure all electronic communication apparatus used in the network is type-approved by the Authority prior to installation, importation or deployment, in compliance with the Type Approval Regulations (Statutory Instrument No. 6 of 2011) (cl.8(d)), and that construction, installation, configuration, testing, commissioning, repair and maintenance follow the Installation Guidelines 2020 (cl.8(e)). A licence exemption does not remove type approval requirements (cl.5.2(c)).
evidence: Type approval certificate for each model of apparatus in the network
Equipment inventory with the type approval number for each item
Importation and installation dates compared with type approval dates
Installation, testing and commissioning records against the Installation Guidelines 2020

controls.name: Closed user group and exclusion of general public service
controls.clause: cl.2 (Closed User Group, Private Network); cl.4; cl.7(b); cl.8(a), (b); consultation Q17
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] A private network is established for the exclusive use of a specified person or closed user group whose membership is predefined and not open to the general public, and shall not be used to offer or provide any electronic communications service to the general public (cl.2, cl.8(a)). The Authority will take enforcement action under the Act where use breaches cl.8(a) (cl.8(b)). The treatment of non-employees on site, such as residents of a company township, contractors or visitors, is an open question (Q17). A network licence is required, subject to the cl.5 exemptions (cl.4, cl.5).
evidence: Closed user group definition and membership criteria
Register of authorised users and the subscriber identity credentials (SIM or eSIM) issued to them
Records of any non-employee access and the basis for it
Network licence held (cl.4) or the exemption basis relied on (cl.5)

controls.name: Radiocommunication licence lifecycle, shared spectrum use and cross-border coordination
controls.statement: [DRAFT - not binding] Only a network licence holder deploying within its authorised market segment is eligible (cl.6.1). The applicant applies in Form 1 of the Radiocommunication Regulations 2024; the Authority performs compatibility analysis and coordination, grants or rejects within 60 days of a complete application, and issues the licence on payment of fees; the licence remains in force for the period specified unless revoked or suspended; renewal may be applied for three months before expiry (cl.6.2.1, cl.6.2.2). Spectrum is shared, non-exclusive and valid only within the approved coverage area, licensees may be required to coordinate with other users, and licensees must comply with cross-border coordination notices and any added conditions (cl.6.2.4, cl.6.2.5).
evidence: Network licence and its market segment
Form 1 application with receipt date, and the grant or rejection decision with date
Radiocommunication Licence showing period, conditions and any cross-border conditions
Renewal application dates compared with licence expiry
Coordination correspondence and cross-border notices received, with responses
sop: Apply to the Authority for a Radiocommunication Licence in Form 1 (cl.6.2.1(a))
Authority undertakes compatibility analysis and coordination on receipt of a complete application (cl.6.2.1(b))
Authority grants or rejects the application within 60 days of receipt of a complete application (cl.6.2.1(c))
Authority issues the licence upon payment of the requisite licence fees (cl.6.2.1(d))
Apply for renewal three months before expiry of the licence (cl.6.2.2)

policies.title: ICT (Satellite Licensing) Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Satellite spectrum and orbital resources are licensed in line with the ICT Act, the Radiocommunication Regulations 2024 and the ITU Radio Regulations, with the Authority acting as Notifying Administration for Zambian filings (cl.2.2, cl.4.1.2).
Licences are issued by category, and eligibility is tied to network licence status and market segment (cl.4, cl.4.3.4, cl.4.4.3, cl.4.5.3, cl.4.7.3).
Transparency of landing rights: the Authority publishes a list of satellites granted landing rights (cl.4.2.6).
The Authority retains operational control: a registered 24-hour Network Control Facility must be able to modify or cease transmissions on request (cl.4.2.5(b)).
Earth stations in motion and visiting equipment operate on a non-interference, non-protected basis within stated conditions (cl.4.3.6, cl.6).
Equipment is type approved and conforms to the First Schedule standards, and gateway arrangements support domestic routing, quality of service and lawful access (cl.10.1, cl.4.7.4, First Schedule).
management_intent: The Authority intends to publish a landing-rights list on its website with eight defined details per satellite network (cl.4.2.6), which makes the quality and currency of that list a matter of the Authority's own data governance.
Licence holders are expected to keep the Authority informed through the annual report (cl.4.1.11) and the 30-day modification notice (cl.4.2.5(a)).
The Authority expects operators to keep a registered, always-staffed Network Control Facility so that transmissions can be modified or ceased on request (cl.4.2.5(b)).
Personal identification details of visiting vessel or aircraft operators are collected for extended stays (cl.6.2(b)); the Guidelines do not say how those details are protected, shared or retained.

controls.name: Landing rights eligibility evidence
controls.statement: A Landing Rights Licence lets a Satellite Network Operator whose system was notified to the ITU through another Administration land signals in Zambia and provide capacity to network licensees; it does not include deploying an earth station or offering services directly to end users (cl.4.2.1, 4.2.2). The applicant shall hold a valid satellite licence or authorisation from its notifying administration (or proof of recognition), identify the ITU filing and show the frequency assignments are recorded in the MIFR (or notified and pending recording where permitted), and where coordination is required provide MIFR or BR IFIC findings and coordination status, or a statement of outstanding coordination (cl.4.2.3). A foreign operator may hold the licence in its own name without a Zambian corporate entity (cl.4.2.4). The Guidelines state no format or retention period for this evidence.
evidence: Application file with the notifying administration licence or proof of recognition
ITU filing identification and MIFR recording evidence (or notification pending recording)
MIFR or BR IFIC findings and coordination status, or the outstanding-coordination statement
Authority eligibility assessment record for each landing-rights licence

controls.name: Public landing-rights list and its eight-field schema
controls.statement: The Authority will publish on its website a list of satellites granted landing rights, with eight details for each satellite network or system: (a) Orbital Location; (b) Satellite Commercial Name; (c) Satellite Name (ITU Filing); (d) Satellite Operator; (e) Notifying Administration; (f) Radiocommunication Service; (g) Frequency Range of Operation (Downlink and Uplink); (h) Approval Status (cl.4.2.6). The clause gives no data types, frequency units, code lists for service, notifying administration or approval status, unique identifier, update frequency, last-updated date or machine-readable format. For non-geostationary systems orbital location is not a single value, and the clause does not say how it is recorded.
evidence: Published landing-rights list on the Authority website
Data dictionary for the eight fields (type, unit, allowed values)
Reconciliation of the published list to the landing-rights licences issued
Update log showing when entries were added, changed or withdrawn
Code lists used for Radiocommunication Service, Notifying Administration and Approval Status
sop: Authority publishes a list of satellites granted landing rights on its website with the eight listed details (cl.4.2.6)

controls.name: Annual report by Space Station licence holders
controls.statement: A holder of a Radiocommunication (Space Station) Licence shall submit an annual report to the Authority within three (3) months of the end of the preceding year, including (a) the status of all coordination exercises and their progress, (b) all interference cases encountered and how they were addressed, and (c) any major change in the business plan or project status of the satellite network (cl.4.1.11). The Guidelines do not define the reporting year, a report format, or what counts as a major change.
evidence: Annual reports as submitted, with submission dates
Coordination log supporting item (a)
Interference case register supporting item (b)
Business plan and project status change record supporting item (c)
Authority acknowledgement of receipt
sop: Submit an annual report to the Authority within three (3) months of the end of the preceding year (cl.4.1.11)
Include coordination status and progress, interference cases and how they were addressed, and any major change in business plan or project status (cl.4.1.11(a)-(c))

controls.name: 30-day notice of significant modification to a landed satellite network
controls.statement: A Landing Rights licensee shall notify the Authority of any significant modification to the satellite network's frequency assignments, orbital position or operational characteristics within thirty (30) days of the modification (cl.4.2.5(a)). 'Significant' is not defined, and the Guidelines do not say how a notice leads to an update of the published landing-rights list (cl.4.2.6).
evidence: Modification notices with the modification date and the notice date
Change log of the licensee's frequency assignments, orbital position and operational characteristics
Authority record showing the licence data updated after a notice
Comparison of the published landing-rights list to the latest notified characteristics
sop: Notify the Authority of any significant modification within thirty (30) days of the modification (cl.4.2.5(a))

controls.name: Registered 24-hour Network Control Facility
controls.statement: A Landing Rights licensee shall maintain a twenty-four-hour Network Control Facility with details registered with the Authority and ensure that transmissions can be modified or ceased within a technically feasible period upon request of the Authority (cl.4.2.5(b)). Earth stations under an Earth Station Terminals Licence operate under the control of a Network Control Facility (cl.4.3.1(b)); the Network Control Facility is a facility able to remotely monitor and control the correct operation of earth stations (cl.3). The registered details are not itemised, and the location of the facility is not restricted.
evidence: Registered Network Control Facility details held by the Authority (facility, contact points, location)
24-hour operating roster and escalation contacts
Record of Authority requests to modify or cease transmissions and the time taken to act
Procedure or test evidence that transmissions can be ceased on request
Updates to the registered details after any change
sop: Maintain a twenty-four-hour Network Control Facility with details registered with the Authority (cl.4.2.5(b))
On request of the Authority, modify or cease transmissions within a technically feasible period (cl.4.2.5(b))

controls.name: Earth station terminal parameters and licensed terminal count
controls.statement: An Earth Station Terminals Licence covers terminals that communicate with the same satellite network or system, operate under a Network Control Facility and share the same technical and operational characteristics (cl.4.3.1). Terminals are treated as similar when seven parameters are the same, lower or within range: frequency, maximum transmit power, maximum antenna gain, bandwidths and emission types, equivalent antenna diameter, antenna radiation pattern, and the satellite network communicated with (cl.4.3.2). The number of terminals shall not exceed the maximum declared in the application and specified in the licence, by class (Class A under 100 to Class F over 10,000, Second Schedule) (cl.4.3.3). The Guidelines do not state how terminal counts are reported after licensing.
evidence: Licence stating the maximum number of terminals and the fee class
Terminal inventory with a unique identifier and the seven radio parameters for each terminal
Reconciliation of active terminals to the licensed maximum
Network Control Facility terminal list reconciled to the inventory

controls.name: Foreign visiting earth stations and terminals: authorisation and personal identification records
controls.statement: A foreign-registered vessel or aircraft ESIM is exempt from licensing for a visit of up to four weeks if the cl.6.1 conditions are met. For a stay over four weeks, the ESIM operator shall apply in writing at least five days before the extended period starts, providing proof of authorisation in the country of registration, personal identification details of the responsible aircraft or vessel operator, details of the satellite service in use, the purpose of use, and the expected period of stay and address; the Authority approves or rejects within five days (cl.6.2). A foreign national may operate a mobile satellite terminal without a licence if the terminal is declared at the point of entry to immigration officials, is authorised in the home country, the satellite operator holds a Zambian landing-rights licence, and the stay is up to four weeks (cl.6.5); a longer stay requires service from a locally licensed provider (cl.6.6). The Guidelines state no retention period, legal basis, access control or sharing arrangement for the personal identification details or the immigration declarations, and do not say how declarations reach the Authority.
evidence: Extended-stay applications containing the five items required by cl.6.2(a)-(e)
Authority decision records with dates, to test the five-day determination
Procedure for handling personal identification details (access, storage, disclosure)
Retention schedule for these records (none is stated in the Guidelines)
Immigration declaration records for mobile satellite terminals and how they reach the Authority, if at all
Check that the satellite operator holds a Landing Rights Licence (cl.6.1(c), cl.6.5(c))
sop: Apply in writing not less than five days before the commencement of the extended period (cl.6.2)
Provide proof of authorisation, personal identification details of the responsible operator, details of the satellite service, purpose of use, and expected period of stay and address (cl.6.2(a)-(e))
Authority approves or rejects the application within five days after submission (cl.6.2)
Declare a foreign national's mobile satellite terminal at the point of entry to immigration officials (cl.6.5(a))

controls.name: Gateway interconnection and lawful access and monitoring
controls.statement: A holder of a Radiocommunication (Mobile Satellite Terminals) Licence providing electronic communications services to the public shall interconnect with existing public networks in Zambia through (a) a gateway earth station established and maintained within Zambia, or (b) an alternative technical arrangement approved by the Authority. The gateway or arrangement shall provide sufficient capacity and functionality to ensure optimal domestic traffic routing, compliance with quality-of-service requirements and regulatory compliance, including lawful access and monitoring (cl.4.7.4). The Guidelines do not describe the lawful access and monitoring procedure, who may request access, or how access data is protected and retained.
evidence: Location and licence of the gateway earth station in Zambia
Authority approval of any alternative technical arrangement
Gateway design showing domestic traffic routing, quality of service and lawful access and monitoring capability
Lawful access and monitoring procedure and request-handling records (no procedure is stated in the Guidelines)
Capacity and functionality assessment supporting the gateway or arrangement

controls.name: Type approval and harmonised standards (First Schedule)
controls.clause: cl.10.1; cl.4.3.5; cl.6.7; First Schedule and Notes 1-3
controls.statement: A licensee shall ensure all radio equipment is type approved by the Authority prior to importation or deployment under the Registration of Electronic Communication Apparatus Regulations 2011 and the Type Approval Regulations 2011, in conformance with the technical standards in the First Schedule (cl.10.1). The First Schedule maps each terminal type to a harmonised standard or ITU reference, frequency bands and operational limits such as maximum e.i.r.p. and antenna diameter. Compliance with a standard does not itself authorise operation (Note 1); a numerical limit in the Schedule prevails over a higher or inconsistent value in a harmonised standard or Type Approval Certificate (Note 2); a different limit in the licence prevails for the operation licensed (Note 3). Foreign type approvals are accepted on the basis of Type Acceptance (cl.6.7). The Schedule cites standards (for example EN 301 428, EN 303 979) without edition or version numbers.
evidence: Type approval certificate for each model of earth station and terminal
Mapping of each terminal type to its First Schedule row, standard and frequency band
Conformity evidence against the harmonised standard and the e.i.r.p. and antenna limits in the Schedule
Type Acceptance records for foreign visiting equipment (cl.6.7)
Record of the edition of each EN standard and ECC decision applied (the Schedule gives none)

controls.name: Licence application procedure, decision timelines and licence duration
controls.statement: An applicant applies in Form 1 of the Radiocommunication Regulations 2024 with proof of payment of the application fee; the Authority grants or rejects within sixty days of receipt, and that period starts only when payment is received and an official receipt is issued (cl.7.1(a)-(d)). Information requested must be provided within fourteen (14) days or the application is rejected (cl.7.1(e)); the Authority notifies the outcome in writing within fourteen (14) days of its decision and states reasons for any rejection (cl.7.1(h), (i)). Licences are valid for one year from issue, run concurrently with a Network Licence where held, and Landing Rights Licences are valid for the declared operational lifespan (geostationary) or ten years (non-geostationary), with renewal applied for three months before expiry (cl.9.1-9.3).
evidence: Application register with application date, fee payment date, official receipt date, decision date and notification date
Information requests with the 14-day response tracking
Written outcome notices, including reasons for rejections
Licence register with issue date, expiry date and renewal dates
Landing Rights Licences showing the lifespan or ten-year period applied
sop: Apply for a Radiocommunication Licence in Form 1 with proof of payment of the application fee (cl.7.1(a), (b))
Authority grants or rejects within sixty days of receipt, the period starting on payment and issue of an official receipt (cl.7.1(c), (d))
Applicant provides requested information within fourteen days or the application is rejected (cl.7.1(e))
Authority notifies the applicant of the outcome in writing within fourteen days of the decision, stating reasons for a rejection (cl.7.1(h), (i))
Authority issues the licence upon payment of the requisite fee (cl.7.1(j))
Apply for renewal three months before expiry (cl.9.3)

policies.title: ICT (E-Band Assignment) Guidelines
policies.entity: Zambia Information and Communications Technology Authority
principles: Transparency through a public register: the Self-Coordinated Registration Database is a publicly available reference for applicants choosing channels (cl.3).
Applicant-led coordination: in the Self-Coordinated Block the applicant must analyse and coordinate so no harmful interference is caused to links already registered (cl.6.2(a)).
First-registered priority: earlier registered links have priority in interference resolution, provided they have had no unauthorised modification (cl.10.1(a)).
Licensed and published before deployment: a self-coordinated link is deployed only after licence issue and publication in the database (cl.6.2(f)).
Time-bound decisions: 60 days to grant or reject, and fixed timelines for interference acknowledgement, resolution and determination (cl.6.1(c), cl.6.2(d), cl.10).
Equipment is type-approved and conforms to the mandatory technical requirements and standards (cl.11, cl.13, Fourth Schedule).
management_intent: The Authority intends the Self-Coordinated Registration Database to be the working reference that applicants use to select channels (cl.3, cl.6.2(a)), so the completeness and accuracy of its entries directly affect interference outcomes.
Licensees are expected to supply the minimum set of link and site parameters in the Third Schedule for coordination (cl.11(a)).
Licensees are expected to acknowledge interference notices within 24 hours and resolve interference within 7 days, with the Authority determining unresolved disputes within 21 days (cl.10.1).
The Authority reserves monitoring and inspection of equipment and installations where it deems necessary (cl.12).

controls.name: Public Self-Coordinated Registration Database
controls.statement: The Self-Coordinated Registration Database is a publicly available register maintained by the Authority containing the technical and operational details of all registered links with assignments in the Self-coordinated Block, serving as a public reference for applicants to select preferred channels (cl.3). A link is published in the updated database before it is deployed (cl.6.2(f)). The Guidelines do not state the publication format, how soon after licence issue a link is published, who in the Authority is custodian, or how corrections and withdrawn links are handled. There is no equivalent register for the Coordinated Block.
evidence: Public Self-Coordinated Registration Database (dated extract or screenshot)
Register governance document naming the custodian and the update process
Publication log: licence issue date versus database publication date for each link
Reconciliation of Self-coordinated Block licences issued to register entries
Change and removal log for register entries
sop: Publish the link in the updated Self-Coordinated Registration Database after the licence is issued (cl.6.2(f))

controls.name: Link and site parameter data dictionary (Third Schedule)
controls.clause: cl.11(a); Third Schedule Tables 1 and 2; cl.3
controls.statement: A licensee shall adhere to the minimum set of parameters required for coordination in the Third Schedule (cl.11(a)). Table 1 lists 11 link parameters: Licensee Name, Link ID, Town/District, Province, Channel Number, Path length (km), Bandwidth (MHz), Bit-rate (Mbps), Receiver sensitivity level (dBm), Polarization (H, V or Dual) and Duplexing Mode. Table 2 lists 13 site parameters: Latitude and Longitude (decimal degrees), Ground Height (m ASL), Antenna height (m AGL), Equipment manufacturer, Equipment Model Number, Equipment type approval number, Antenna manufacturer, Antenna model number, Antenna maximum gain (dBi), Antenna elevation angle (degrees), EIRP (dBW) and Transmit frequency (MHz). This is the only field-level schema in the Guidelines, but the text does not say that the published register fields equal these 24 parameters. Row numbering in Table 2 starts at 10, repeating Table 1 rows 10 and 11. Channel Number, Polarization and Duplexing Mode have no unit or stated code list in the Schedule; no data types, precision, mandatory flags or Link ID format and uniqueness rule are given; and there is no registration date, licence number or status field.
evidence: Third Schedule parameter list (Tables 1 and 2) as the schema of record
Register field list compared with the 24 Third Schedule parameters
Sample of registered links checked for completeness and unit conformity (km, MHz, Mbps, dBm, decimal degrees, m ASL, m AGL, dBi, degrees, dBW)
Code lists applied for Polarization (H, V, Dual), Duplexing Mode (TDD, FDD) and Channel Number
Validation rules for coordinates, EIRP and channel against the First and Fourth Schedules

controls.name: Deploy only after licence issue and publication in the database
controls.statement: The successful applicant in the Self-Coordinated Block shall only deploy the radio link upon issuance of the licence and publication of the link in the updated Self-Coordinated Registration Database (cl.6.2(f)). The Guidelines do not say how the Authority learns of the deployment date or how premature deployment is detected.
evidence: Licence for each link with issue date
Database entry for the link with publication date
Link commissioning or first-transmission date compared with licence issue and publication dates
Authority inspection findings on links deployed before publication, if any (cl.12)
sop: Deploy the radio link only upon issuance of the licence and publication of the link in the updated Self-Coordinated Registration Database (cl.6.2(f))

controls.name: Applicant compatibility analysis and channel selection
controls.statement: A self-coordinated applicant shall choose their preferred channel in line with the Self-Coordinated Block Channel Plan and Registration Database after conducting compatibility analysis and coordination to ensure no harmful interference is caused to existing links in the database (cl.6.2(a)). The channel shall be in accordance with the First Schedule channelling plan (cl.6.2(b)), and the applicant then applies for a Radiocommunication Licence in Form 1 (cl.6.2(c)). No method, tool or evidence format for the analysis is prescribed, and the Authority's check of the analysis is not described.
evidence: Applicant's compatibility analysis and coordination record, dated against the database state used
Database extract showing the registered links considered
Channel selection record showing the channel and bandwidth chosen against the First Schedule plan
Form 1 application referencing the analysis
sop: Choose the preferred channel in line with the Self-Coordinated Block Channel Plan and Registration Database (cl.6.2(a))
Conduct compatibility analysis and coordination so no harmful interference is caused to links registered in the database (cl.6.2(a))
Select the channel in accordance with the First Schedule channelling plan (cl.6.2(b))
Apply to the Authority for a Radiocommunication Licence in Form 1 (cl.6.2(c))

controls.name: Interference priority by registration date
controls.statement: Resolution of harmful interference within the Self-Coordinated Block is based on the priority of operational links according to their registration dates in the Self-Coordinated Registration Database: earlier-registered links have priority over later ones, provided the earlier link has not been subject to any unauthorised modification (cl.10.1(a)). The Third Schedule schema contains no registration date or modification-history field, so this rule depends on data the Schedule does not define.
evidence: Registration date held for each link and its audit trail
Modification records for each link showing authorised and unauthorised changes
Interference case files showing how priority was determined
Comparison of as-built link parameters to registered parameters

controls.name: Interference notification, response and determination timelines
controls.statement: In the Self-Coordinated Block the affected licensee notifies the interfering licensee in writing; the interfering licensee acknowledges receipt within 24 hours, investigates and cooperates in good faith, and shall resolve the interference within 7 days; if unresolved, the affected licensee may lodge a complaint with the Authority, which shall investigate and determine the dispute within 21 days of lodgement (cl.10.1(b)-(e)). In the Coordinated Block, a licensee shall ensure all cases of harmful interference are reported to the Authority for resolution within 21 days from submission of the complaint (cl.10.2); the text does not say who must meet the 21-day period or how the case is recorded.
evidence: Interference case register with notice, acknowledgement, resolution and complaint timestamps
Written interference notices and acknowledgements
Authority complaint files and determinations with lodgement and decision dates
Coordinated Block interference reports and resolution dates
sop: Affected licensee notifies the licensee of the interfering link in writing (cl.10.1(b))
Interfering licensee acknowledges receipt within 24 hours, investigates and cooperates in good faith (cl.10.1(b))
Interfering licensee resolves the harmful interference within 7 days (cl.10.1(c))
If unresolved, the affected licensee may lodge a complaint with the Authority (cl.10.1(d))
Authority investigates and determines the dispute within 21 days from the date of lodgement (cl.10.1(e))

controls.name: Licence application, decision timelines, duration and renewal
controls.clause: cl.6.1; cl.6.2(c)-(e); cl.7; cl.8; cl.9; Second Schedule
controls.statement: For the Coordinated Block the applicant applies in Form 1, the Authority undertakes compatibility analysis and coordination to select the channel, grants or rejects within 60 days and issues the licence upon payment of the licence fees (cl.6.1). For the Self-Coordinated Block the Authority likewise grants or rejects within 60 days and issues the licence on payment (cl.6.2(d), (e)). A licence is valid for one year from issue, or runs concurrently with the Network Licence where one is held (cl.8), and renewal may be applied for three months before expiry (cl.9). Fees are set in the Second Schedule (application fee ZMW 66.80; annual fee ZMW 1,666.80 per 250 MHz paired link in the Coordinated Block and ZMW 416.8 per link in the Self-coordinated Block). The Guidelines do not say when the 60-day period starts.
evidence: Application register with received date, completeness date, decision date and licence issue date
Licence register with issue, expiry and renewal dates
Fee payment records compared with the Second Schedule
Renewal applications compared with expiry dates
sop: Apply to the Authority for a Radiocommunication Licence in Form 1 (cl.6.1(a), cl.6.2(c))
Authority undertakes compatibility analysis and coordination to select the channel in the Coordinated Block (cl.6.1(b))
Authority grants or rejects the application within 60 days (cl.6.1(c), cl.6.2(d))
Authority issues the licence upon payment of the requisite licence fees (cl.6.1(d), cl.6.2(e))
Apply for renewal three months before expiry of the licence (cl.9)

controls.name: Type approval and mandatory technical requirements (Fourth Schedule)
controls.statement: A licensee shall ensure radiocommunication equipment conforms to the technical requirements and standards in the Fourth Schedule (cl.11(b)) and is type-approved by the Authority prior to installation, importation or deployment (cl.13.1), and that deployment conforms with the Installation Guidelines (cl.13.2). The Fourth Schedule sets the usable range (71.125-75.875 GHz paired with 81.125-85.875 GHz), channelling from 250 MHz to 2000 MHz (ITU-R F.2006-0), FDD only in the Coordinated Block and TDD or FDD in the Self-coordinated Block, maximum EIRP 55 dBW, minimum antenna gain +38 dBi, maximum transmit power output +30 dBm, out-of-band limits, and reference standards ETSI EN 302 217 (Radio) and EN 301 489 (EMC), cited without an edition. The type approval number is also a register field (Third Schedule Table 2).
evidence: Type approval certificate for each equipment model
Equipment datasheets showing EIRP, antenna gain, transmit power and out-of-band emission against the Fourth Schedule limits
Check that the type approval number in each register entry matches a valid certificate
Record of the edition of ETSI EN 302 217 and EN 301 489 applied (the Schedule gives none)

controls.name: Monitoring and inspection of equipment and installations
controls.statement: The Authority shall, where it deems necessary, carry out monitoring and inspections of equipment and installations to assess technical and operational compliance with the Act, Regulations or Guidelines (cl.12). The Guidelines set no inspection frequency, trigger or report format.
evidence: Inspection and monitoring plan or trigger criteria
Inspection reports with date, link ID and findings
Corrective actions and closure records
Comparison of as-built installation data (coordinates, antenna height, EIRP) to registered parameters

policies.title: Telecommunications Act
principles: Telecommunication messages are confidential: operators and their staff must not unlawfully disclose the contents or existence of a message or use its contents for their own purposes (s.17(1)).
Disclosure of a message is lawful only if compellable under any law or given for purposes of the administration of justice (s.17(2)).
Licensees' books, records and documents must be open to inspection by telecommunication officers and police officers (s.18(3)).

Licensees and applicants must furnish the Authority with documents, accounts, returns and other information the Board reasonably requires, and false or misleading returns are an offence (ss.8(2)(d), 20, 21(a),(c),(d)).
The Authority keeps proper accounts, audited annually, and reports annually to the Minister (First Schedule paras 7, 8, 10).
management_intent: Protect the privacy of communications carried on licensed telecommunication systems, with criminal sanction for unlawful disclosure or personal use of message contents.
Give the regulator visibility over licensees through inspection of records and compulsory information returns.

Note: the source is the 1994 text. It predates modern data-protection and electronic-communications regimes, contains few data controls, and specifies no retention periods or record formats. Currency of this text should be verified before it is relied on.

controls.name: Confidentiality of telecommunication messages
controls.statement: A person operating or employed in connection with a telecommunication service who unlawfully discloses the contents or existence of any telecommunication message, or makes use for his own purposes of knowledge of message contents acquired in the course of his duties, commits an offence (fine not exceeding twenty thousand penalty units, imprisonment not exceeding twelve months, or both). Disclosure is lawful only if it is compellable under any law or given for purposes of the administration of justice. The protection covers the existence of a message as well as its contents, which brings call or traffic metadata within scope. Wilful interception (s.15(1)(c)) and divulging contents of a message not intended for the person (s.21(j)) are separate offences.
evidence: Customer communications confidentiality policy covering message contents and existence of messages
Staff and contractor confidentiality undertakings
Access-control matrix for systems holding message contents and call or traffic records
Register of disclosures made under legal compulsion or for the administration of justice, with the legal basis for each
Incident register for suspected unauthorised disclosure or interception

controls.name: Licensee records and equipment records open to inspection
controls.statement: All books, records and documents required to be kept by a licensee shall be open to inspection at all reasonable times by a telecommunication officer or a police officer. These officers may seize any book, record or document they reasonably suspect will afford evidence of an offence. Failure to produce, on request, a licence or certificate, or a book, record or document relating to any telecommunication equipment in the person's possession or control, is an offence (s.21(b)). The Act does not list which records must be kept, in what form, or for how long.
evidence: Inventory of books, records and documents the licensee is required to keep under its licence and regulations
Telecommunication equipment register or asset records
Records retention schedule (the Act sets no period)
Inspection log recording requests by telecommunication or police officers and what was produced
Procedure for responding to inspection and seizure

controls.name: Information, returns and accounts furnished to the Authority
controls.statement: Licence conditions may require the licensee or any other person concerned in providing the service to furnish to the Authority, in such manner and at such times as the Board may reasonably require, documents, accounts, returns, estimates and other information (s.8(2)(d)). A licensee and any licence applicant shall furnish the Authority with the documents, accounts, estimates or other information the Board reasonably requires or as regulations prescribe (s.20(1)), and failure to comply is an offence (s.20(2)). Failing to furnish a return in the manner and time prescribed, furnishing a false or misleading return or information, or making a declaration known to be false in a licence application is also an offence (s.21(a),(c),(d)). The submitter is therefore accountable for the accuracy of the return.
evidence: Licence conditions specifying required returns, accounts and reporting timetable
Calendar and log of returns submitted to the Authority, with submission dates
Copies of returns, accounts and estimates as submitted
Internal review or sign-off record for the accuracy of each return
Licence application declarations and supporting documents

controls.name: Accounts, audit and annual report of the Communications Authority
controls.statement: The Authority's financial year ends on 31 March (para 7). The Board shall cause proper accounts to be kept of assets, liabilities, income and expenditure, and the accounts shall be audited by one or more persons publicly carrying on the profession of accountants in Zambia, appointed by the Board with the Minister's approval (para 8). The Board shall submit a report of the Authority's activities to the Minister not later than 30 September in any year, and the Minister shall lay it before the National Assembly not later than fourteen days after the first sitting after receipt (para 10). This control sits with the regulator, not with Infratel as a licensee.
evidence: Accounting records of the Authority for each financial year ending 31 March
Auditor appointment letter and evidence of the Minister's approval
Audited financial statements
Annual report as submitted to the Minister by 30 September, and proof of tabling
sop: Board submits a report of the Authority's activities to the Minister not later than 30 September in any year.
Minister lays the report before the National Assembly not later than fourteen days after the first sitting after receipt.

policies.title: Data Protection Act
policies.entity: Office of the Data Protection Commissioner
principles: Personal data is processed lawfully, fairly and transparently (s.12(1)(a)).
Personal data is collected for explicit, specified and legitimate purposes and not further processed in an incompatible manner (s.12(1)(b)).
Personal data is adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purpose (data minimisation) (s.12(1)(c)).
Personal data is accurate and kept up to date; inaccurate data is erased or rectified without delay (s.12(1)(d)).
Personal data is kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purpose (storage limitation) (s.12(1)(e)).
Personal data is processed in accordance with the rights of the data subject (s.12(1)(f)).
Personal data is processed securely, protected against unauthorised or unlawful processing, loss, destruction or damage (s.12(1)(g)).
Processing requires a lawful ground, with consent that is written, freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrable and withdrawable (s.2, s.13, s.15).
Sensitive personal data may be processed only on narrow statutory grounds and must be stored in-country (s.14, s.70(3)).
Personal data is processed and stored on a server or data centre located in the Republic unless the Minister prescribes otherwise (s.70).
Controllers and processors are accountable and must be able to demonstrate compliance to data subjects and to the Commissioner (s.50).
Controllers and processors must be registered with the Data Protection Commissioner before controlling or processing personal data (s.19).
management_intent: Provide an effective system for the use and protection of personal data and regulate its collection, use, transmission, storage and other processing (long title).
Establish the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner as the regulator of data protection and privacy in the Republic (s.4).
Require registration of data controllers and data processors and licensing of data auditors so that the Commissioner holds a public Register of regulated parties (s.4(2), s.19-37, s.80).

Impose duties on data controllers and processors: record of processing, impact assessment, security, data protection officer, breach notification, accountability, retention and processor contracts (Part VIII).
Give data subjects enforceable rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction, protection from solely automated decisions, and portability (Part IX).
Keep personal data, and in particular sensitive personal data, within the Republic, with controlled cross-border transfer conditions (Part X).
Enforce compliance through inspectors, annual audit, a complaints and appeals route, compensation and criminal penalties (Parts III, IX, XI).

controls.name: Registration as data controller or data processor
controls.statement: No person may control or process personal data without first registering with the Data Protection Commissioner as a data controller or data processor, by applying in the prescribed form on payment of the prescribed fee. The Commissioner grants or rejects the application within fourteen days and gives written reasons for any rejection; the Commissioner may exempt a person by declaration.
evidence: Registration application as submitted to the Commissioner (prescribed form)
Proof of payment of the prescribed registration fee
Commissioner's approval or rejection letter
Entry for the entity in the Commissioner's Register (s.80)
Any exemption declaration issued under s.27
sop: Apply to the Data Protection Commissioner in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee.
Commissioner grants or rejects the application within 14 days of receipt.
If rejected, Commissioner informs the applicant in writing with reasons.

controls.name: Certificate of registration: issue, display, renewal and change notification
controls.statement: A certificate of registration is issued within fourteen days of approval, must be displayed at the principal place of business (certified copy at each subsidiary premises), and must be renewed by applying three months before expiry. Any change in registration particulars must be notified to the Commissioner within seven days; surrender of registration must be notified in writing.
evidence: Certificate of registration (current, unexpired)
Photograph or inspection record of the certificate displayed at the principal premises and certified copies at subsidiary premises
Renewal application and proof of fee, lodged at least three months before expiry
Renewal decision from the Commissioner
Notice of change in registration particulars with date of change and date lodged
Register of registration expiry dates and renewal triggers
sop: Display the certificate in a conspicuous place at the principal place of business and a certified copy at every subsidiary premises.
Apply for renewal three months before the certificate expires, in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee.
Commissioner approves or rejects the renewal within 30 days; the holder may continue operating until a decision is made.
Notify the Commissioner of any change in registration particulars within 7 days of the change.
Notify the Commissioner in writing if deciding not to continue providing services (surrender).

controls.name: Personal and sensitive personal data definitions and classification
controls.statement: Datasets must be identified as personal data (data relating to an identifiable individual) and, where applicable, as sensitive personal data (race, marital status, ethnic origin, sex, genetic and biometric data, child abuse data, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, physical or mental health). Sensitive status drives stricter processing conditions and mandatory in-country storage.
evidence: Data classification scheme or policy showing personal data and sensitive personal data classes aligned to the s.2 definitions
Data inventory or catalogue with a personal/sensitive flag on each dataset and data element
Classification review records
List of anonymised or pseudonymised datasets and the method used

controls.name: Lawful basis, consent and child or vulnerable person consent
controls.statement: Processing needs a lawful ground (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public interest or official authority, legitimate interests, or data made public by the subject). Where consent is relied on it must be written, distinguishable from other matters, withdrawable at any time (with data collected after withdrawal destroyed immediately), and demonstrable by the controller; for a child or vulnerable person consent must come from a parent or guardian with age verification and parental consent mechanisms.
evidence: Register of processing activities recording the lawful basis for each activity
Consent forms and consent notices showing separation from other matters and the right to withdraw
Consent log or audit trail demonstrating who consented, when and to what
Consent withdrawal procedure and records of withdrawals actioned
Age verification and parental or guardian consent mechanism and records
Objection handling records (s.15(8)-(9))
sop: Inform the data subject of the right to withdraw consent before consent is given.
Present a consent request clearly distinguishable from other matters, in clear and plain language.
On withdrawal of consent, destroy immediately all personal data collected after withdrawal (subject to the Act).
Make every reasonable effort to verify that consent for a child or vulnerable person was given or authorised by the parent or guardian.

controls.name: Principles of processing: purpose limitation, minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation
controls.statement: Controllers and processors must ensure personal data is processed lawfully, collected for specified purposes, limited to what is necessary, accurate and kept up to date, kept identifiable no longer than necessary, and secured. Reasonable steps must be taken to erase or rectify inaccurate data without delay.
evidence: Documented purpose specification for each dataset
Data minimisation review of collection forms and fields
Data quality or accuracy procedure and correction logs
Named accountable owner for accuracy of each personal dataset
Retention schedule linked to purpose

controls.name: Collection from the data subject and information given at collection
controls.statement: Personal data must be collected directly from the data subject unless a listed exception applies (public record, consent to other source, legal obligation, and similar). When collecting directly, the controller must concurrently tell the subject its name and address, the purpose, any direct marketing objection right, intended third-country transfer and safeguards, whether the request is compulsory, recipients, and the rights of access and rectification.
evidence: Privacy notice or collection notice containing every s.64 item
Collection forms showing the notice at the point of collection
Documented source and basis for any personal data collected from a source other than the data subject
Provenance record of each personal dataset source
sop: Concurrently with direct collection, provide the data subject with the s.64 information unless it is established the subject already has it.

controls.name: Record of processing activities and metadata
controls.statement: A data controller must keep a written record of its processing activities and the metadata under its responsibility, and of all categories of processing activities, in the prescribed manner and form. The record must be made available to the Commissioner on demand.
evidence: Record of processing activities (register) in the prescribed form
Metadata record per dataset (what each dataset describes, owner, purpose, categories, recipients, retention, location)
Data dictionary or schema documentation for personal datasets
