Evidence of the record being produced to the Commissioner on demand
Record review and update log
sop: Keep and maintain the record in writing in the prescribed manner and form.
Make the record available to the Data Protection Commissioner on demand.

controls.name: Data protection impact assessment
controls.statement: Before processing that uses new technologies and is likely to pose high risk to individuals, the controller must carry out a data protection impact assessment. It is required for automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects (including profiling), large-scale processing of sensitive personal data or criminal conviction data, and large-scale systematic monitoring of public areas; it must be reviewed when risk changes.
evidence: Completed DPIA in the prescribed manner and form, dated before processing began
DPIA screening checklist applied to new projects and systems
Commissioner's published list of processing operations requiring a DPIA, and the entity's mapping to it
DPIA review record following a change in risk
sop: Carry out the impact assessment prior to the processing, in the prescribed manner and form.
Carry out a review of processing against the DPIA where there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations.

controls.name: Security of processing
controls.statement: Controllers and processors must guarantee and strictly adhere to technical and organisational security measures proportionate to the risk, including pseudonymisation and encryption, confidentiality and integrity safeguards, and protection against misuse, unauthorised access, modification, disclosure or destruction. Safeguards must be reviewed periodically per Commissioner guidelines, and controllers may use only processors that give sufficient guarantees.
evidence: Information security policy and data protection policies
Risk assessment relating to personal data processing
Evidence of encryption and pseudonymisation of personal data at rest and in transit
Access control lists and access review records for personal datasets
Periodic security safeguard review report
Processor due diligence records showing sufficient security guarantees
sop: Undertake a periodic review of security safeguards in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Data Protection Commissioner.

controls.name: Appointment of a data protection officer
controls.statement: Every data controller and data processor must appoint a data protection officer, in accordance with guidelines issued by the Commissioner.
evidence: Letter of appointment of the data protection officer
DPO terms of reference or job description
DPO contact details published or registered with the Commissioner
Evidence that the appointment meets the Commissioner's DPO guidelines
sop: Appoint the data protection officer in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Data Protection Commissioner.

controls.name: Notification of security breach within 24 hours
controls.statement: A data controller must notify the Data Protection Commissioner within twenty-four hours of any security breach affecting personal data. A processor must notify the controller as soon as practicable, and the controller or processor must notify affected data subjects as soon as practicable.
evidence: Personal data breach response and notification procedure
Breach register with detection time, notification time to the Commissioner and elapsed hours
Copies of notifications sent to the Commissioner, to the controller (by processors) and to data subjects
Breach test or simulation records
Processor contract clauses requiring prompt breach notification
sop: Data controller notifies the Data Protection Commissioner within 24 hours of any security breach affecting personal data.
Data processor notifies the data controller as soon as practicable of any breach affecting data processed on its behalf.
Data controller or data processor notifies the data subject as soon as practicable.

controls.name: Accountability, inspection access and annual audit
controls.statement: Controllers and processors must take measures to comply and keep internal mechanisms able to demonstrate compliance to data subjects and the Commissioner. The Commissioner or a licensed independent data auditor must audit a controller's policies and processing conduct annually, and inspectors with a warrant may inspect premises and records, which the controller must make available.
evidence: Compliance framework or programme mapping Act obligations to controls and owners
Latest annual data protection audit report (Commissioner or licensed data auditor) and licence of the auditor
Remediation plan and closure evidence for audit findings
Inspection access log and records produced to inspectors
Where data is stored outside the Republic, evidence the controller bore the audit cost (s.81(2))
sop: Afford an inspector access to any record or document and produce any record or document the inspector requires.
Commissioner or independent licensed data auditor audits the controller's policies and processing conduct annually.

controls.name: Personal data retention
controls.statement: Personal information must be kept for as long as it is used for its collection purpose and remains relevant to it, and for at least one year afterwards or any other prescribed period. Controllers and processors must also keep a record of the process and purpose of collection and of third parties to whom, and when, the information was disclosed.
evidence: Retention schedule with retention basis and period per dataset (minimum one year after purpose ends or prescribed period)
Evidence of disposal or archival when retention periods expire
Disclosure log recording third parties, dates and purposes
Record of collection process and purpose for each dataset
sop: Keep personal information for as long as used for its purpose and relevant, and for at least one year thereafter or other prescribed period.
Keep a record of the process, the purpose of collection, and third parties to whom and when the information was disclosed.

controls.name: Data processor contract and sub-processor authorisation
controls.statement: Processing by a processor must be governed by a contract setting out subject matter and duration, nature and purpose, type of personal data and categories of data subjects, and the controller's and processor's rights and obligations. A processor may not engage another processor without the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation and must tell the controller of intended changes.
evidence: Signed data processing contract or agreement for each processor
Register of processors and sub-processors with contract dates and scope
Written authorisation for each sub-processor engaged
Notices of sub-processor change and controller responses
Processor registration certificate
sop: Processor obtains the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation before engaging another processor.
Where general authorisation exists, processor informs the controller of intended additions or replacements so the controller can object.

controls.name: Non-disclosure of personal data and disclosure notice
controls.statement: Personal data may not be disclosed without the data subject's prior consent, except to prevent a national security threat or to investigate or prosecute a cognisable offence. Before disclosure the subject must be told when and to whom the data goes, why, what protections apply, and how to seek recourse; unlawful disclosure of sensitive personal data is an offence.
evidence: Disclosure consent records
Disclosure notices issued to data subjects covering the four s.53(3) items
Data sharing register recording recipient, purpose, date and legal basis
Records of any disclosure made under the national security or criminal investigation exceptions
sop: Before disclosing personal data, obtain the consent of the data subject.
Before disclosure, inform the data subject of when and to whom it will be disclosed, the purpose, the protective security practices and policies, and the recourse procedure.

controls.name: Joint controller agreement
controls.statement: Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing, they must enter into an agreement reflecting their respective roles and relationships towards the data subject. The agreement must be made available to the data subject and the joint controllers are jointly and severally liable.
evidence: Joint controller agreement signed by all parties
Register identifying processing operations with joint controllers and their roles
Evidence the agreement is accessible to data subjects (publication or provision on request)
sop: Joint controllers enter into an agreement reflecting their respective roles and relationships as they relate to the data subject.
Make the agreement available to the data subject.

controls.name: Notification of third-party agreements that trade on a data subject's profile
controls.statement: A data controller or processor must notify the Data Protection Commissioner of any third-party agreement that allows the third party to trade on the profile of a data subject.
evidence: Register of third-party agreements involving data subject profiles
Notifications lodged with the Commissioner and acknowledgements
Negative declaration or attestation where no such agreements exist
sop: Notify the Data Protection Commissioner of any third-party agreement that allows the third party to trade on the profile of a data subject.

controls.name: Data subject right of access and notification
controls.statement: A data subject may obtain confirmation that their data is processed and access the purpose, categories of data and recipients, storage period or criteria, the data and its source, and the logic of any automated decision. They may also be told of all third parties to whom data was disclosed; the first copy is free, access may be provided in a commonly used electronic format, and unresolved complaints go to the Commissioner.
evidence: Data subject access request procedure and request log with dates and outcomes
Response templates covering all s.58(2) items
Record of third parties to whom each subject's data was disclosed
Fee schedule for additional copies
Complaints register and Commissioner correspondence
sop: Where a request is made electronically, provide the information in a commonly used electronic format unless the data subject asks otherwise.
Provide a copy of the personal data at no cost for the initial data and a reasonable administrative-cost fee for additional copies.

controls.name: Rectification, erasure, objection, restriction and automated decision rights
controls.statement: Data subjects may have inaccurate data rectified and incomplete data completed, have data erased where it is no longer needed, consent is withdrawn, or processing is unlawful, object to processing (including direct marketing), restrict processing, and not be subject to solely automated decisions with legal or similar effect. The controller must pass rectification, erasure and restriction on to each recipient where practicable and must bring these rights to the subject's attention on first communication.
evidence: Procedures and request logs for rectification, erasure, objection and restriction requests
Erasure evidence across systems, backups and downstream recipients
Notices to recipients of rectification, erasure or restriction
First-communication notice presenting the data subject's rights clearly and separately
Inventory of automated decision and profiling processes with safeguards and human-intervention route
Direct marketing opt-out suppression list
sop: On first communication with the data subject, expressly bring the data subject's rights to their attention, clearly and separately from other information.
Communicate any rectification, erasure or restriction of processing to each recipient to whom the data was disclosed, where practicable.
Inform the data subject before a restriction of processing is lifted.
Where erased data was made public, take all reasonable steps to inform processors and third parties of the erasure request.

controls.name: Right to data portability
controls.statement: A data subject has the right to receive their personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable or otherwise legible format and to transmit it to another controller. They may have it transmitted directly from one controller to another where technically feasible.
evidence: Data portability procedure and request log
Sample export in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format
Data dictionary or schema supplied with exports so the data is interpretable
Evidence of controller-to-controller transfer capability or documented infeasibility

controls.name: In-country storage and processing of personal data
controls.statement: A data controller must process and store personal data on a server or data centre located in the Republic. The Minister may prescribe categories that may be stored abroad, but sensitive personal data must always be processed and stored in-country.
evidence: Hosting inventory listing the physical location of every server, data centre and cloud region holding personal data
Data centre or cloud contract showing in-country location
Statutory instrument or Minister's authorisation for any category stored outside the Republic
Confirmation that sensitive personal data is held only in the Republic

controls.name: Cross-border transfer of personal data
controls.statement: Non-sensitive personal data outside the Minister's prescribed categories may leave the Republic only with data subject consent plus an approved standard contract or intragroup scheme or a Ministerial adequacy prescription, or where the Commissioner approves the transfer on grounds of necessity. A controller transferring under a standard contract must certify and periodically report to the Commissioner and bears liability for transferee non-compliance.
evidence: Register of cross-border transfers (data categories, destination country, recipient, basis)
Data subject consent for the transfer
Commissioner-approved standard contract or intragroup scheme in force
Certification and periodic reports to the Commissioner
Commissioner approval or Ministerial instrument for each transfer or class of transfers
Explicit consent record for any transfer of sensitive personal data under s.71(4)(b)
sop: Where transferring under a standard contract or intragroup scheme, certify and periodically report to the Commissioner that the transfer adheres to the approved clauses and that the controller bears liability for transferee non-compliance.

policies.title: Electronic Government Act
principles: Focus on the needs of citizens and businesses in service delivery (s.4(a)).
Innovative design and transformational, integrated, streamlined, collaborative and citizen-focused business processes (s.4(b)).
Innovative solutions that reduce long-term operational costs and eliminate redundant steps and cycle times (s.4(c)).
Integrated provision of e-government services that recognises the unique roles and capabilities of public bodies (s.4(d)).
Sharing of administrative information among public bodies which avoids information duplicity (s.4(e)).
Protection of information held by a data controller, used in accordance with the law (s.4(f)).
Prudent and responsible use of public resources in e-government activities (s.4(g)).
Collaboration with the private sector for sustainable resource utilisation (s.4(h)).
management_intent: Enhance the management and promotion of electronic Government services and processes (long title).
Facilitate access to e-Government services to improve service delivery, administrative functions and productivity, and enhance citizens' access to Government services and information (long title).
Establish the Electronic Government Division in the Office of the President to coordinate e-government and ICT matters in public bodies (ss.5-6).
Ensure public data is preserved in a secure government designated area with backups in specified locations (s.6(1)(c)).

Enforce prescribed standards, generally recognised e-government and ICT practices and uniform classification systems in public bodies, monitor compliance and take administrative action for contraventions (s.6(2)(a)-(b)).
Promote paperless transactions in the public service and reduce paper documents (s.6(1)(q), s.9(2)(a)).
Hold the Division accountable through an annual report to the President within ninety days after the financial year end (s.34).

controls.name: Uniform classification systems enforced in public bodies
controls.statement: The Division must enforce prescribed standards of generally recognised e-government and ICT practices and uniform classification systems in public bodies. Public bodies are therefore expected to apply the uniform classification systems the Division prescribes.
evidence: Uniform classification scheme or standard issued by the Division
Public body's information classification policy mapped to the uniform scheme
Classification labels or tags recorded on information assets
Division compliance monitoring reports on classification

controls.name: Public data preserved in designated secure area with specified backups
controls.statement: The Division must ensure that public data is preserved in a secure government designated area and that backups are held in specified locations.
evidence: Designation of the secure government data hosting area
Backup location specification and backup schedule
Hosting location register for public-body datasets and systems
Backup restoration test records

controls.name: Consent-based retrieval of documents from another public body
controls.statement: A public body may, with the data subject's consent, retrieve required documentation directly from the issuing public body, and both bodies may collect, process and use the necessary personal data for that purpose.
evidence: Inter-body data retrieval arrangement identifying issuing and requesting bodies
Consent records linked to each retrieval
Log of documents retrieved between public bodies
Data protection assessment of the retrieval process

controls.name: Documented consent that is clear, retrievable and revocable
controls.statement: Consent may be given electronically and must be documented. The public body must ensure the data subject grants consent consciously and clearly, can retrieve the content of the consent at any time, and can revoke it at any time with effect for the future.
evidence: Consent register or store with consent text, date and data subject reference
Consent capture screens or forms showing clear wording
Facility for the data subject to view consent content
Consent revocation records and evidence that revocation stops later processing
sop: Document the consent provided by electronic means
Allow the data subject to retrieve the content of the consent at any time
Allow the data subject to revoke consent at any time with effect for the future

controls.name: Electronic record-keeping with orderly records and retention duration
controls.statement: A public body may keep records in electronic form and must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, in line with accepted technological standards, so that orderly record-keeping principles and legal requirements for the duration of maintaining records are observed.
evidence: Records management policy and retention schedule
Description of technical and organisational measures for electronic records
Records inventory showing the retention period and legal basis for each record class
Records system access and integrity controls

controls.name: Conversion of paper to electronic records and destruction of originals
controls.statement: Electronic copies of records must be kept in electronic form, and converted documents must match the paper originals in pictorial and text content when rendered. The National Coordinator may waive conversion where disproportionate technical effort is needed, and originals may be archived, returned or destroyed once retention is no longer needed on legal grounds or for conversion quality.
evidence: Document conversion procedure and quality check records
Waiver requests and National Coordinator decisions
Paper destruction or archive log with the legal retention check
Sample comparison of electronic copies to paper originals
sop: Ensure the pictorial and text content of electronic documents corresponds to the paper documents when rendered readable
Archive, return or destroy paper documents after conversion only when further retention is no longer needed on legal grounds or for conversion quality

controls.name: Written specification of a joint automated procedure before establishment
controls.statement: Public bodies may run joint automated procedures that let several data controllers process personal data in or from a database. Before establishing or substantially changing one, the public body must specify in writing the procedure, the bodies responsible for organisational and technical specifications, and the bodies responsible for legality of collecting, processing and using data.
evidence: Written joint automated procedure specification
Allocation of responsibilities for specifications and for legality of data processing among participating bodies
Change records for substantial changes to the procedure
Register of joint automated procedures
sop: Specify in writing the procedure to be applied and bodies responsible for defining, amending, developing and complying with specifications
Specify in writing the participating bodies responsible for legality of collecting, processing and using data

controls.name: Single data protection officer coordination and coordination guidelines
controls.statement: The data controllers in a joint automated procedure must appoint one participating public body whose data protection officer coordinates implementation of the section. That officer must cause guidelines for coordination of the joint procedure to be prepared and made available for inspection.
evidence: Appointment record naming the coordinating public body and its data protection officer
Guidelines for coordination of the joint automated procedure
Proof the guidelines are available for inspection
sop: Appoint one participating public body whose data protection officer coordinates implementation
Prepare guidelines for coordination of the joint automated procedure and make them available for inspection

controls.name: Data retrieval, participation limits and data subject rights across joint procedures
controls.statement: Retrieval procedures in joint automated procedures must meet this Act and the Data Protection Act, and participation must be appropriate given the data subject's legitimate interests. A data subject may assert rights against any participating body, and a body contacted must forward the matter to the responsible body.
evidence: Assessment of appropriateness of each body's participation
Data subject request handling procedure across participating bodies
Log of data subject requests forwarded to the responsible body
Instruments commissioning another body to process personal data for the procedure
sop: Forward the matter to the responsible public body when contacted by a data subject

controls.name: Machine-readable format for data published on public networks
controls.statement: Where a public body uses publicly accessible networks to make data available, it must use a machine-readable format as a general principle. A format is machine-readable when the data can be read and processed in automated mode by software.
evidence: Inventory of datasets published online with their file formats
Format policy requiring machine-readable output
Sample test showing automated processing of published data

controls.name: Metadata provided with published data and conditions of use
controls.statement: Subject to this Act and the Data Protection Act, data made available under s.18 must be provided with metadata, defined as a set of data that gives information about other data. The President, on the Division's recommendation, may make Regulations on use of the data, including commercial and non-commercial use, conditions of use and exclusion of liabilities and warranties.
evidence: Metadata records accompanying each published dataset
Metadata standard or profile applied
Terms and conditions of use for published data
Regulations made under s.18(4), if any

controls.name: Data protection measures under the Data Protection Act
controls.statement: A public body must implement data protection measures in accordance with the Data Protection Act, 2021, and data protection under this Act is enforced in accordance with that Act.
evidence: Data protection policy and measures register
Data Protection Act compliance assessment
Records of processing activities

controls.name: Identity validation before granting access to personal data
controls.statement: A data controller may grant access to confidential personal data in electronic public-sector communications only where the requester's unique identity and the authenticity of the request are validated in an electronically verifiable form. Where only a recurring identity can be validated, access is limited to data the requester made available using that identity.
evidence: Access request identity validation procedure
Electronic verification mechanism configuration
Access request log showing validation outcome
Rule limiting access to data supplied under a recurring identity

controls.name: Purpose and retention limitation for personal data
controls.statement: A public body must ensure personal data is kept and used only for the specified and lawful purposes for which it was collected and processed, and is not kept longer than necessary for those purposes or as required by law.
evidence: Documented purpose for each personal data collection
Retention schedule for personal data with legal or purpose basis
Evidence of deletion or disposal at the end of retention
Review records of personal data holdings

controls.name: Non-disclosure of information provided to a public body
controls.statement: A public body must not disclose, without lawful authority, information provided to it for or during delivery of e-government services. Contravention is an offence carrying a fine and daily fines for continuing offences.
evidence: Disclosure authorisation procedure and lawful authority register
Log of disclosures with the lawful authority relied on
Staff confidentiality undertakings

controls.name: Source identification number and citizen card unique identification
controls.statement: The source identification number identifies natural and legal persons and is the basis for sector-specific personal identifiers. The ministry responsible for national registration confirms allocation of the number to the citizen card holder, and the number must be kept confidential, with special protection, to the extent it does not contain public data.
evidence: Source identification number allocation records from the national registration ministry
Technical and regulatory protection measures for the source identification number
Citizen card scheme identity link controls
Registration of persons not required to be on a public register, at data controller request

controls.name: Public register definition and statutory register identification
controls.statement: A public register is a register required to be maintained by a public body under any other written law. Public bodies should therefore be able to identify which of their registers are public registers and cite the written law that requires each.
evidence: Inventory of public registers maintained by the public body with the enabling written law cited
Owner and custodian assignment for each register
Register of data sets flagged as statutory registers

controls.name: Information security measures and staff awareness
controls.statement: In accordance with information security standards issued by the Division, a public body must develop and enforce security measures safeguarding information used in e-government services from unauthorised disclosure, and take reasonable steps to ensure officers know of and comply with them.
evidence: Information security policy aligned to Division standards
Security measures register for e-government information
Staff awareness and training records

controls.name: Sharing information with private bodies and access by user rights
controls.statement: A public body may share information with a private body in providing Government services only in accordance with the Data Protection Act, and access to information must follow user rights and access levels as prescribed.
evidence: Data sharing agreements with private bodies
Legal basis assessment under the Data Protection Act for each sharing arrangement
Access control matrix showing prescribed user rights and access levels

controls.name: Audit of public bodies and remediation of non-compliance
controls.statement: The Division may audit a public body, by an inspector or independent auditor, to evaluate compliance with Part V. Where a contravention is found, the Division must notify the body in writing with the audit finding, required remedial action and the period for remedy.
evidence: Audit reports on the public body
Written non-compliance notices stating findings, remedial action and deadline
Remediation plan and closure evidence
Division monitoring of information systems and internal controls
sop: Notify the public body in writing of the audit finding, the action required to remedy non-compliance and the period for remedial action

policies.title: Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act
principles: Information the Minister declares critical to national security or economic and social well-being is protected as critical information (s.17).
Infrastructure containing critical information is declared and protected as critical information infrastructure (s.17(2)).
Critical information is stored on a server or data centre within the Republic unless the Minister authorises otherwise (s.18).
Controllers of critical information infrastructure are accountable for its registration, annual audit, threat detection and incident reporting (Part V).
Cyber security incidents affecting critical information infrastructure are reported to the Authority promptly and routinely (s.23).
Interception of communications is prohibited except through the lawful, judicially supervised route and the Central Monitoring and Co-ordination Centre (s.26-28).
Electronic records and data messages are admissible in evidence, weighted by the reliability of how their integrity was generated, stored, maintained and attributed (s.73).
Providers of cyber security services must be licensed (s.41).
management_intent: Provide for cyber security in the Republic and the protection of persons against cyber crime (long title).
Constitute the Zambia Computer Incidence Response Team and the National Cyber Security Advisory and Coordinating Council (s.6, s.7).
Make the Authority the cyber security regulator, with power to issue binding guidelines, codes of practice and standards for owners of critical information infrastructure (s.4, s.5(1)(g), s.88).
Facilitate identification, declaration and protection of critical information infrastructure, including a register, localisation, audit and incident reporting (Part V).
Provide cyber inspectors with powers to inspect, search, seize and require information, and to audit critical information infrastructure (Part III, Part IV).
Provide for collection and preservation of evidence of computer-related crime and the admission of electronic evidence in criminal matters (Parts X-XI, long title).
License cyber security service providers and keep a register of them (Part VII, s.5(1)(m)).

controls.name: Minister-declared critical information and critical information infrastructure
controls.statement: The Minister may by statutory instrument declare information important to national security or the economic or social well-being of the Republic to be critical information, and any infrastructure containing it is declared critical information infrastructure. Declared information and infrastructure then fall under Part V obligations, so organisations must identify which of their datasets and systems have been declared.
evidence: Statutory instrument(s) declaring critical information and critical information infrastructure
Inventory of datasets and systems mapped against the declarations, with a critical-information flag
Written determination for each system of whether it is critical information infrastructure
Data classification scheme including a critical information class

controls.name: In-country storage of critical information
controls.statement: A controller of critical information must store all critical information on a server or data centre located within the Republic. The Minister may authorise externalisation outside the Republic as prescribed.
evidence: Hosting inventory showing physical location of every server or data centre holding critical information
Hosting or cloud contracts evidencing in-country location
Ministerial authorisation for any critical information held outside the Republic
Architecture diagram showing data location and backup or replication sites

controls.name: Surrender of critical information on expiry of purpose or cessation of controller
controls.statement: When the purpose for which critical information was collected expires, or the controller ceases to exist, the critical information must be surrendered to the Authority.
evidence: Lifecycle and end-of-purpose procedure for critical information
Record of purpose and purpose-end date for each critical dataset
Surrender or transfer records to the Authority
Exit plan covering surrender of critical information on controller cessation
sop: Surrender the critical information to the Authority when its collection purpose expires or the controller ceases to exist.

controls.name: Registration of critical information infrastructure with the Authority
controls.statement: Critical information infrastructure must be registered with the Authority under the requirements and procedure the Minister prescribes by statutory instrument. The controller, being the person who controls and is responsible for the infrastructure, carries the obligation.
evidence: Registration application and acknowledgement from the Authority
Statutory instrument prescribing registration requirements and procedure
Registration number or certificate for each registered critical information infrastructure
Designation of the controller responsible for each infrastructure

controls.name: Change of ownership of critical information infrastructure
controls.statement: A person who owns critical information infrastructure and intends to change its ownership must apply to the Authority in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee. Changing ownership without applying is an offence.
evidence: Application to the Authority for change of ownership with proof of fee
Authority's decision on the application
Ownership register for critical information infrastructure assets
sop: Apply to the Authority for change of ownership in the prescribed manner and form on payment of the prescribed fee.

controls.name: Register of critical information infrastructure
controls.statement: The Authority maintains a register of critical information infrastructure containing the information that is prescribed. An entity's critical systems should appear in this register with accurate details.
evidence: Extract of the Authority's register showing the entity's critical information infrastructure entries
Reconciliation of the entity's own infrastructure inventory to the register
Statutory instrument prescribing register content

controls.name: Annual information technology audit of critical information infrastructure
controls.statement: A controller of critical information infrastructure must appoint an information technology auditor every year to audit the infrastructure as prescribed. Cyber inspectors may also audit critical information infrastructure under warrant.
evidence: Annual appointment letter for the information technology auditor
Auditor qualifications showing expertise in information security management systems
Annual audit report on the critical information infrastructure
Audit scope aligned to the prescribed audit requirements
Audit calendar showing an audit completed in each year
sop: Appoint an information technology auditor annually to audit the critical information infrastructure as prescribed.

controls.name: Authority-required audit and remediation of non-compliance
controls.statement: The Authority may at any time require a controller to perform an audit, and refusal is an offence. Where an audit reveals contravention of Part V the Authority gives written notice of the finding, the remedial action required and the deadline; failure to remediate in time is an offence.
evidence: Authority directions requiring an ad hoc audit and the controller's response
Audit findings notice from the Authority
Remediation plan with owners and deadlines
Evidence of remedial action completed within the stipulated period
sop: Authority notifies the controller in writing of the audit finding, the action required and the period for remedial action.
Controller takes the remedial action within the stipulated period.

controls.name: Reporting of cyber security incidents affecting critical information infrastructure
controls.statement: A controller of critical information infrastructure must report to the Authority, on or after occurrence, any cyber security incident affecting the infrastructure, any incident on an interconnected computer system under its control, and any other incident type the Authority specifies by written direction. Reports must be in the prescribed manner and form.
evidence: Cyber incident response and reporting procedure
Incident register with detection, classification and report dates
Copies of incident reports submitted to the Authority in the prescribed form
Mapping of interconnected systems that communicate with the critical information infrastructure
Authority written directions on additional reportable incident types
sop: Report to the Authority on or after the occurrence of a cyber security incident in respect of the critical information infrastructure.
Report incidents on any computer or system under the controller's control that is interconnected with the critical information infrastructure.
Submit the report in the prescribed manner and form.

controls.name: Monthly cyber security incident and threat report
controls.statement: A controller of critical information infrastructure must submit a monthly cyber security incident and threat report to the Authority.
evidence: Monthly incident and threat reports submitted to the Authority, one per month
Submission calendar and acknowledgement receipts
Threat log supporting each monthly report
sop: Submit a monthly cyber security incident and threat report to the Authority.

controls.name: Threat detection mechanisms aligned to Gazetted standards
controls.statement: A controller of critical information infrastructure must establish mechanisms and processes, in accordance with information security standards published in the Gazette, to detect cyber security threats against the infrastructure.
evidence: Gazetted information security standards applicable to critical information infrastructure
Threat detection architecture and tooling (monitoring, logging, alerting)
Mapping of detection processes to the Gazetted standard and version
Monitoring test results or detection coverage review
sop: Establish mechanisms and processes for detection of cyber security threats in accordance with information security standards published in the Gazette.

controls.name: Participation in national cyber security exercises
controls.statement: The Authority conducts national cyber security exercises to test readiness, and a controller of critical information infrastructure must participate when directed in writing by the Authority. Failure to comply is an offence with a daily continuing penalty.
evidence: Written direction from the Authority to participate in an exercise
Exercise participation records and attendance
After-action report and improvement actions
sop: Participate in a national cyber security exercise as directed in writing by the Authority.

controls.name: Data retention notice for internet connection records
controls.statement: Where a data retention notice is issued to an electronic communications service provider requiring it to retain internet connection records, the specific data to be retained must be stated in the notice. A provider is not required to retain data as part of an internet connection record.
evidence: Data retention notice(s) received, specifying exactly which connection record data must be retained
Retention schedule for internet connection records reflecting each notice
Evidence of retention and disposal in line with the notice
Metadata inventory of internet connection record fields (time stamp, source and destination IP, volume, URL elements)

controls.name: Inspection, search and production of records by cyber inspectors
controls.statement: A cyber inspector with a warrant may inspect computer systems and licensed provider premises, search and copy records, demand licences and registration certificates, and require written statements, records and information about a suspected cyber security incident or threat. Persons with knowledge of the system must assist, and refusal to cooperate or false information is an offence.
evidence: Procedure for responding to cyber inspector warrants and written notices
Log of inspector requests, records produced and dates
Current licences and registration certificates available for production
Named contacts able to explain system functioning and data protection measures
sop: Cyber inspector must carry and show the certificate of appointment when performing functions.
Person with knowledge of the system permits and assists a search by providing information, accessing computer data, copying it and obtaining intelligible output.

controls.name: Expedited preservation, production and traffic data disclosure
controls.statement: Where data is needed for a criminal investigation, a law enforcement officer may by written notice require the person in control of it to preserve it for up to seven days (extendable by a Judge), disclose relevant traffic data, and a Judge may order production of specified data or subscriber information. Organisations must be able to preserve and produce such data on demand.
evidence: Legal hold and preservation procedure triggered by a written notice
Preservation notices received and proof of preservation within the specified period
Judge's production orders and the data produced
Log and traffic data inventory showing what is retained and where
sop: Preserve the specified data for the period of up to seven days stated in the written notice from a law enforcement officer.
Disclose relevant traffic data about a specified communication when required by written notice.

controls.name: Integrity and provenance of electronic evidence
controls.statement: Data messages cannot be denied admissibility in legal proceedings solely because they are electronic, and are given evidential weight based on the reliability of how their integrity was generated, stored, communicated and maintained, and how the originator was identified. Records intended as evidence therefore need demonstrable integrity and provenance.
evidence: Records management and logging standards covering integrity controls (hashing, audit trails, access logs)
Evidence of how the originator of key records is identified (authentication, signatures)
Sample audit trail showing record creation, storage and change history
Digital forensic readiness procedure

controls.name: Use of licensed cyber security service providers
controls.statement: No person may provide or advertise cyber security services for reward without a licence from the Authority, except employees working on their employer's own systems. Entities that outsource cyber security work (including audits and penetration testing) should hold evidence that the provider is licensed and in good standing.
evidence: Cyber security service provider licence held by each vendor, valid and unexpired
Entry for the vendor in the Authority's register of cyber security service providers
Vendor due diligence file showing licence checked before contract
Contract with scope of the cyber security service

controls.name: Emergency cyber security measures directed by the Minister
controls.statement: The Minister may issue regulations directing a person or organisation to take specified measures or comply with requirements to prevent, detect or counter a threat to essential services, national security, the economy, public health and safety, or an electronic communication, computer or information system. Failure to comply is an offence.
evidence: Ministerial regulations or directions received and register of directions
Action plan and evidence of measures implemented in response
Responsible officer designated to receive and action directions

policies.title: Public Service Information Security Standard
principles: Confidentiality: information is accessible only to those with authorised access (s.1.0 a).
Integrity: safeguard the accuracy and completeness of information and processing methods (s.1.0 b).
Availability: authorised users have access to information when required (s.1.0 c).
Compliant use: MPSAs meet all legal and contractual obligations (s.1.0 d).
Responsible use: appropriate controls ensure users of government ICT resources do not adversely affect other users or systems (s.1.0 e).
Objective: a secure environment for ICTs that enhances user confidence and trust (s.3.0).
Classification is driven by legal requirements, value, criticality and sensitivity, is consistent across the whole organisation, and is aligned to the access control guideline (s.5.3.2).
Access is granted on a need-to-know and need-to-use basis, using role-based access control (s.5.9.1, s.5.9.3).

Standard enforced by the e-Government Division, monitored by the National ICT Standards Review Committee, with annual MPSA compliance audits and a certificate of compliance on a successful audit (Foreword).
Security is designed into all architecture layers (business, data, applications, technology), balancing security with accessibility (s.5.10.5.1.4).
management_intent: MPSAs shall develop an Information Security Guideline approved by management that sets out the institution's approach to its information security objectives (s.5.1.1.1).
MPSAs shall communicate the guidelines to employees and relevant external parties in a form that is accessible and understandable, and address regulations, legislation and contracts (s.5.1.1.1).
MPSAs shall review the information security guidelines every 2 years or on significant change, with the National ICT Standards Review Committee approving revised guidelines (s.5.1.2).
MPSAs shall have an Information Security Steering Committee and designate certified officers in charge of information security (s.5.2.1.1).
MPSAs shall implement and maintain an asset inventory, assign every information asset to an owner and identify its classification (s.5.3.1).
MPSAs shall classify information on the four-level confidentiality scheme and label classified information using physical labels and metadata (s.5.3.2).
MPSAs shall develop and document formal transfer guidelines, procedures and agreements covering all communication facilities and external parties (s.5.6.2).
MPSAs shall establish, document and review an access control guideline based on business and information security requirements (s.5.9.1).
MPSAs shall produce, keep and regularly review electronic event logs and protect log information against tampering and unauthorised access (s.5.8.4).
MPSAs shall draw up a retention schedule and issue guidelines on retention, storage, handling and disposal of records, and maintain an inventory of sources of key information (s.5.14.1.3).
MPSAs shall develop and implement a data guideline for privacy and protection of personal information in line with existing data protection and privacy laws (s.5.14.1.4).
MPSAs shall document all applicable legislative, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements and their approach to meeting them for each information system and the MPSA (s.5.14.1.1).
MPSAs shall agree and document supplier agreements that classify the information involved and set security, audit and incident obligations (s.5.12.1.2).

controls.name: Approved Information Security Guideline and review
controls.statement: Each MPSA must have a management-approved Information Security Guideline defining objectives, principles, roles and a deviation/exception process, communicated to staff and external parties and reviewed at least every 2 years or on significant change.
evidence: Approved MPSA Information Security Guideline with version and approval date
Evidence of communication to employees and external parties (awareness programme records)
Guideline review record (2-year cycle) and management review inputs
Approval record from the National ICT Standards Review Committee for revised guidelines
Documented deviation and exception handling process
sop: Define information security, objectives and principles in the guideline
Assign general and specific responsibilities to the MPSA Information Security Working Group
Define a process for handling deviations and exceptions
Review the guideline every 2 years or on significant change, taking management review results into account
Submit revised guidelines from the Working Group to the National ICT Standards Review Committee for approval

controls.name: Information security roles, steering committee and accountability
controls.statement: MPSAs must have an Information Security Steering Committee, designate certified officers in charge of information security, document and have senior management approve roles and responsibilities, and have role holders sign a consent document acknowledging them.
evidence: Steering Committee terms of reference and membership list
Senior management agendas and minutes showing information security items
Letters of designation for information security officers
Certification records for appointed officers
Documented and approved roles and responsibilities register
Signed role-acknowledgement consent documents
sop: Include information security matters on senior management agenda and minutes
Document and obtain senior management approval for security roles and responsibilities
Have employees with security roles sign a consent document stating they understand their roles

controls.name: Segregation of duties
controls.statement: No single person may access, modify or use assets without authorisation or detection, and initiation of an event must be separated from its authorisation; where segregation is hard, monitoring, audit trails and supervision must compensate.
evidence: Segregation-of-duties matrix or role conflict analysis
Compensating control records (monitoring reports, audit trails, supervision sign-offs)
Collusion risk consideration in control design documentation
sop: Separate initiation of an event from its authorisation
Where segregation is difficult, apply monitoring of activities, audit trails and management supervision

controls.name: Information asset inventory with owner and classification
controls.statement: MPSAs must maintain an accurate, up-to-date asset inventory aligned with other inventories, assigning each information asset an owner and an identified classification; the owner ensures it is inventoried, classified, protected, handled and disposed of properly.
evidence: Information asset register with owner and classification fields for every asset
Evidence of reconciliation with other inventories
Asset owner assignment records
Disposal/destruction records for assets
sop: Assign ownership of each identified asset and identify its classification
Owner ensures assets are inventoried, appropriately classified, protected and properly handled and disposed of

controls.name: Four-level confidentiality classification scheme
controls.statement: Information must be classified by legal requirements, value, criticality and sensitivity using a named, organisation-wide scheme aligned to access control, with a confidentiality scheme of four levels: (1) disclosure causes no harm; (2) minor embarrassment or minor operational inconvenience; (3) significant short-term impact on operations or tactical objectives; (4) serious impact on long-term strategic objectives or survival of the organisation at risk. The scheme must be in line with existing Public Service Security Guidelines.
evidence: Documented classification scheme showing four named levels and their harm definitions
Mapping of the scheme to the access control guideline
Classification applied to datasets, systems and records (classification register)
Evidence the scheme is consistent across the organisation and aligned with Public Service Security Guidelines
sop: Give each level a name that makes sense in the context of the scheme's application
Include classification in the organisation's processes consistently across the organisation
Classify in terms of legal requirements, value, criticality and sensitivity to unauthorised disclosure or modification

controls.name: Classification kept current across the lifecycle
controls.statement: Classification results must be updated as the value, sensitivity and criticality of information change through its lifecycle.
evidence: Classification review/re-classification log
Change records showing classification updates with date and approver
Periodic review schedule for classified assets
sop: Update classification results in line with changes in value, sensitivity and criticality through the lifecycle

controls.name: Labelling of classified information (physical label and metadata)
controls.statement: MPSAs must label classified information, using both physical labels and metadata.
evidence: Sample of classified documents and media showing physical labels
Dataset/system metadata records showing classification label field populated
Labelling procedure or guideline
Label coverage report (share of classified assets labelled)
sop: Apply physical labels and metadata to classified information

controls.name: Media handling, disposal and transfer by classification
controls.statement: MPSAs must develop procedures for removable media management in line with the classification scheme, document formal secure disposal procedures to prevent leakage of confidential information, and document and implement guidelines to protect media in transit.
evidence: Removable media management procedure referencing the classification scheme
Secure media disposal procedure and disposal/destruction certificates or logs
Physical media transfer guideline and transport records
Safe/lock access records for media holding confidential information (s.5.15.2)
sop: Manage removable media per the classification scheme
Dispose of media through documented formal secure procedures
Protect media containing information being transported
Keep media containing confidential information in safes with strictly controlled access (s.5.15.2)

controls.name: Information transfer procedures and agreements
controls.statement: MPSAs must develop formal transfer guidelines, procedures and controls covering all communication facilities, and have agreements for secure transfer of business information with external parties whose security content indicates the sensitivity of the information.
evidence: Information transfer guideline and procedures
Signed agreements with external parties covering secure transfer (data sharing agreements, MoUs, SLAs)
Agreement clauses stating the sensitivity/classification of the information
Register of external information-sharing agreements
sop: Develop formal transfer guidelines, procedures and controls for all types of communication facilities
Include in each agreement the information security content indicating sensitivity of the business information

controls.name: Electronic messaging and non-disclosure agreements
controls.statement: MPSAs must protect electronic messages commensurate with the classification scheme, obtain approval before using external public services (instant messaging, social networking, sharing), and maintain non-disclosure agreements that are regularly reviewed and that cover ownership of information and breach actions.
evidence: Electronic messaging guideline
Approvals for use of external public messaging or sharing services
Templates and signed non-disclosure agreements
NDA requirements review record
Documented breach actions and signatory responsibilities
sop: Obtain approval before using external public services such as instant messaging, social networking or file sharing
Identify, regularly review and document non-disclosure requirements
Identify responsibilities and actions of signatories to avoid unauthorised disclosure
Identify ownership of information, trade secrets and intellectual property
Document expected actions in case of a breach of the agreement
Provide forms of non-disclosure agreement for different circumstances

controls.name: Cryptographic controls and key management
controls.statement: MPSAs must implement a cryptography guideline, set protection level by risk assessment, encrypt information on mobile/removable media and communication lines, and operate a key management guideline covering generation, storage, change, compromise, revocation, destruction, logging and auditing; encryption standards and key architecture are submitted to the e-Government Division.
evidence: Cryptographic controls guideline
Risk assessment determining required encryption strength
Key management guideline and key activation/deactivation records
Key management audit logs
Minimum encryption and hashing algorithm and key length standard
Contractor submission of encryption key and architecture to the e-Government Division
SLAs or contracts with cryptographic service suppliers
sop: Consult the National Coordinator, e-Government Division for specialist advice on cryptographic controls
Define standards and secure methods for generating, issuing, storing, changing, revoking, recovering and destroying keys
Log and audit key management activities
Set key activation and deactivation dates so keys are used only for their permitted period
Analyse risks of not using effective encryption and hashing, and define the minimum algorithm and key length
Contractor submits the encryption key and architecture to the e-Government Division or its appointed agents

controls.name: Information backup and backup retention
controls.statement: The e-Government Division defines the backup guideline; backup plans must keep accurate records of copies and restoration procedures, store backups remotely, encrypt where confidentiality matters, test backups and restores regularly, and determine the retention period for essential business information including permanent archive copies.
evidence: Backup guideline
Backup catalogue and records of backup copies
Documented restoration procedures and restoration test reports with timing
Backup execution monitoring and failure records
Offsite or remote backup location record
Retention period determination for essential business information
sop: Produce accurate and complete records of backup copies and documented restoration procedures
Store backups in a remote location far enough away to escape damage at the main site
Test backup media and restoration procedures regularly against required restoration time
Encrypt backups where confidentiality is of importance
Monitor backup execution and address failures of scheduled backups
Determine retention period for essential business information, including permanent archive copies

controls.name: Event logging, log protection and clock synchronisation
controls.statement: MPSAs must produce, keep and regularly review event logs recording user IDs, activities, timestamps, access attempts, file access, privilege changes and transactions; protect logs against tampering and unauthorised access with privacy safeguards; log administrator/operator activity; prevent administrators erasing their own logs; and synchronise to a documented reference time.
evidence: Event log samples showing required fields (user ID, date/time, device, files accessed, access type)
Log review records and schedules
Log protection configuration (tamper protection, restricted access)
Administrator and operator log reviews
Evidence administrators cannot erase or deactivate logs of their own activity
Documented reference time and clock synchronisation configuration
Privacy protection measures for logs containing personal information
sop: Record user IDs, system activities, dates, times, device identity, successful and rejected access attempts, privilege changes, files accessed and transactions
Take privacy protection measures for logs that contain sensitive or personal data
Deny system administrators permission to erase or deactivate their own logs
Protect logging facilities and log information against tampering and unauthorised access
Document and implement a standard reference time and clock synchronisation approach

controls.name: Protection of test data and separation of environments
controls.statement: Operational data containing personally identifiable or other confidential information must not be used for testing; if it is, sensitive content must be removed or modified, operational access controls apply to the test system, each copy is separately authorised, erased immediately after testing and logged.
evidence: Test data guideline prohibiting use of operational PII/confidential data
Masking or anonymisation records for test datasets
Authorisation records for each copy of operational data to a test environment
Erasure confirmation after testing
Audit log of copying and use of operational information in test
Access control configuration of test systems
sop: Prohibit use of operational data containing PII or other confidential information for testing
Remove or modify sensitive details where such data is used for testing
Obtain separate authorisation each time operational information is copied to a test environment
Erase operational information from the test environment immediately after testing
Log the copying and use of operational information to provide an audit trail

controls.name: Access control guideline (need-to-know, role-based)
controls.statement: MPSAs must establish, document and review an access control guideline based on business and security requirements, using role-based access control and need-to-know/need-to-use, taking account of legislation, information dissemination authorisation, segregation of access roles, formal authorisation and periodic review and removal of access rights.
evidence: Documented access control guideline with review history
Role-to-access matrix (RBAC model)
Network and network services use guideline
Mapping between classification scheme and access rights
Archive of records of events concerning user identities and secret authentication information
sop: Base access on need-to-know and need-to-use
Link access rights to business roles using role-based access control
Segregate access request, access authorisation and access administration roles
Require formal authorisation of access requests
Archive records of all events concerning use and management of user identities and secret authentication information

controls.name: User registration, provisioning and central access record
controls.statement: MPSAs must run a formal user registration/de-registration and access provisioning process using unique user IDs, owner authorisation of access, a central record of access rights granted per user ID, and immediate removal or blocking for leavers and role changers.
evidence: User registration and de-registration procedure
Central register of access rights granted to each user ID
Access request and authorisation records signed by the system or service owner
Approved and documented shared-ID exceptions
Redundant user ID review and clean-up records
Leaver and mover access removal records
sop: Use unique user IDs so users can be held responsible for their actions
Permit shared IDs only where necessary, approved and documented
Obtain authorisation from the owner of the information system or service before granting access
Verify access level is appropriate to the access guideline and consistent with segregation of duties
Do not activate access rights before authorisation is complete
Maintain a central record of access rights granted to each user ID
Immediately disable or remove IDs of leavers and do not reissue redundant IDs

controls.name: Privileged access rights management
controls.statement: Privileged access must be allocated through formal authorisation on a need-to-use, event-by-event basis, recorded, held on separate IDs from regular business use, with expiry, regular competence review, and controlled shared admin credentials.
evidence: Register of privileged access rights per system and user
Authorisation records for privileges allocated
Separate privileged user IDs and expiry settings
Privileged user competency review records
Logs of changes to privileged accounts reviewed periodically
Controls over generic administration IDs and credential rotation records
sop: Allocate privileged rights on a need-to-use, event-by-event basis at the minimum needed for the functional role
Maintain a record of all privileges allocated and do not grant until authorisation is complete
Use a separate user ID for privileged activity and do not perform regular business from privileged IDs
Review competencies of privileged users regularly
Change shared admin credentials frequently and as soon as a privileged user leaves or changes job

controls.name: Periodic access rights review and removal

policies.title: e-Government Interoperability Standard
principles: Subsidiarity and Proportionality (s.5.1): decisions taken as close to the citizen as possible; the eGIF is the common denominator and sectors extend it for sector specificities.
Openness (s.5.2): public data should be freely available for use and reuse unless restricted (personal data, confidentiality, IPR); open specifications and open source are preferred.
Transparency (s.5.3): visibility of administrative rules, processes, data and services; interfaces to internal systems; protection of personal data.
Re-usability (s.5.4): MPSAs reuse and share solutions, information and data and cooperate on joint solutions.
Technological Neutrality and Data Portability (s.5.5): no imposed technology; data must be easily transferable between systems to avoid lock-in.
User-Centricity (s.5.6): multi-channel delivery, single point of contact, user feedback, once-only and relevant-only data collection.
Inclusion and Accessibility (s.5.7): services accessible to all, including differently abled and elderly, and in official local languages where possible.
Security and Privacy (s.5.8): guarantee privacy, confidentiality, authenticity, integrity and non-repudiation of information provided by citizens and businesses.
Administrative Simplification (s.5.9): digital-by-default and digital-first, with simplified processes.
Data Retention (s.5.10): records must be preserved, remain legible, reliable and intact, converted when media become obsolete, and be accessible subject to security and privacy.
Assessment of effectiveness and efficiency (s.5.11): interoperability solutions are evaluated on user needs, proportionality and cost-benefit.
management_intent: Facilitate seamless interconnection and exchange of data and information between Government information systems owned by different public institutions (Foreword, s.1).
Eliminate unnecessary duplication and lower the cost of service delivery by making ICT assets flexible, reusable and interoperable (Foreword, s.1, s.2).
Make shared and reusable public-sector ICT assets discoverable and usable with minimal effort (s.2(a)).
Avoid digital fragmentation of services and data through coordinated national-level efforts (s.1).
Treat data and information as a public asset that is generated, collected, managed, shared, protected and preserved appropriately (s.14.1.1).
Ensure that 'what is sent is what is understood' by preserving format and meaning of exchanged data (s.14).
Let citizens request and use public information at any time as per set permissions (s.2(e)).

Monitor the Standard through the National ICT Standards Review Committee, enforce it through the e-Government Division, audit MPSAs annually and issue certificates of compliance; non-compliance reports go to the Committee (Foreword).

policies.title: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act
principles: The Act provides a safe and effective environment for electronic transactions, facilitates electronic filing by public authorities and regulates the National Public Key Infrastructure (long title).

The Act applies to electronic transactions, communications and records, commercial and non-commercial, domestic and international, including storage of information (s.3(1)), and it binds the Republic (s.101).

No person is required to generate, retain, store or display information in electronic form, and a person may set requirements for the manner in which data messages are accepted (s.3(2)); the Act does not limit any written law that prescribes a specified method of storage or retention (s.3(3)).
Data in the form of a data message has legal force and effect (s.4(1)); a requirement for writing is met by an accessible, retainable data message (s.5).

A requirement to retain information is met by retaining a data message that is accessible and usable, is in its generated/sent/received format (or one shown to represent it accurately), and whose origin, destination and date and time of sending or receipt can be determined (s.10(1)).
A requirement for original form is met where integrity has been assessed from the time the information was first generated in final form and the information can be displayed or produced (s.8).

A data message may not be denied admissibility merely because it is a data message or is not in original format where it is the best evidence reasonably obtainable, and it carries due evidential weight judged on reliability of generation, storage, communication, integrity maintenance and originator identification (s.9).
A public body may, despite contrary law, accept filing, creation or retention of documents, issue permits, licences or approvals, and take or make payments in electronic form (s.23).

The Authority (ZICTA) acts as the National Root Certification Authority and regulates the National PKI (s.25, s.26); certification authorities and time stamping providers are licensed and cryptography service providers are registered (s.26(2), s.27, s.28, s.34).
Certification authorities must use a trustworthy system, defined as reasonably secure, available, reliable, suited to function and adhering to generally accepted security procedures (s.2, s.38).
Guidelines issued by the Authority bind all regulated persons once published (s.97).
Provisions on the .zm domain registry, intermediary liability, consumer protection and encryption (Parts VIII to XI) apply alongside the records and PKI provisions.
management_intent: Retained electronic records stay accessible and usable, in their original or an accurately representative format, with origin, destination and send or receipt time determinable (s.10).
The integrity of information is assessed from its first final form and maintained so that originality, admissibility and evidential weight can be demonstrated (s.8, s.9).

Public bodies that accept electronic filing or issue electronic documents specify, in the Gazette or on their electronic platform, the manner and format, signature type, acceptable certification authority criteria and control processes for integrity, security and confidentiality (s.24).
The Authority maintains a public Register of licensed and private certification authorities, time stamping providers, cryptography service providers and rejected applications with reasons (s.93).
Time stamping providers keep records of issued time stamps and preserve documentation to verify them (s.61).
Certification authorities and time stamping providers conduct annual information systems audits and report to the National Root CA / Authority (s.40, s.60(2), s.61(e)).
Recovery agents implement technical and organisational measures to comply with the Data Protection Act and do not disclose or use stored recovery information except as the Act allows (s.90).
Persons marketing electronically disclose their identity, offer a working opt-out and disclose the source of the addressee's personal information (s.64(2)).

controls.name: Retention of information as data messages: format and accessibility
controls.statement: Where a law requires information to be retained, retention as a data message must keep the information accessible and usable for subsequent reference (s.10(1)(a)), and the data message must be in the form or format in which it was generated, sent or received, or in a format that can be demonstrated to represent accurately the information generated, sent or received (s.10(1)(b)). The retention obligation does not extend to information whose sole purpose is to enable the message to be sent or received (s.10(2)). A writing requirement is met by a data message that is accessible and capable of being retained in a manner usable for subsequent reference (s.5). The Act states no retention period; periods come from the law that requires retention.
evidence: Records retention schedule naming the law that requires retention and the format of each retained record class
Format register or file-format policy for retained electronic records
Format migration or conversion records showing the demonstration that the converted format represents the information accurately
Sample retrieval test: retained data messages opened and read in the current environment
Records management system configuration showing storage of the original format

controls.name: Provenance of retained data messages: origin, destination, date and time
controls.statement: A retained data message must allow its origin and destination, and the date and time it was sent or received, to be determined (s.10(1)(c)). Dispatch occurs when the record enters an information system outside the control of the originator or its agent (s.15); receipt occurs when it enters the information system designated by the addressee, or otherwise an information system of the addressee through which it is retrieved (s.16). Provenance metadata therefore has to be captured and kept with the record, not only the content.
evidence: Message headers, transmission logs or audit trail retained with the record
Metadata schema or fields capturing originator, addressee, sent time and received time
Definition of the designated receiving information system used to fix time of receipt
Sample of retained records with origin, destination and timestamps shown
System clock synchronisation or time source configuration used for the time fields

controls.name: Integrity and originality of data messages
controls.statement: Where a law requires information in its original form, a data message satisfies it if its integrity, from the time it was first generated in its final form as a data message or otherwise, has passed the assessment in s.8(2), and the information can be displayed or produced to the person to whom it is to be presented (s.8(1)). Integrity is assessed by considering whether the information has remained complete and unaltered (apart from endorsements and changes arising in the normal course of communication, storage and display), in the light of the purpose for which it was generated, and having regard to other relevant circumstances (s.8(2)). The same integrity test applies to electronic production of documents (s.11(2)).
evidence: Documented integrity assessment method for records required in original form
Hash values, digital signature validation results or audit logs demonstrating the information is complete and unaltered
Change and endorsement logs distinguishing permitted endorsements from alterations
Display or production test showing the record can be presented to the requiring person
Record of the stated purpose for which the information was generated
sop: Assess whether the information has remained complete and unaltered, excepting endorsements and changes arising in the normal course of communication, storage and display (s.8(2)(a)).
Assess integrity in the light of the purpose for which the information was generated (s.8(2)(b)).
Have regard to other relevant circumstances (s.8(2)(c)).

controls.name: Admissibility and evidential weight of data messages
controls.statement: A data message may not be denied admissibility in legal proceedings merely because it is a data message, or because it is not in original format where it is the best evidence the person adducing it could reasonably obtain and the substance is the same (s.9(1)). Data messages receive due evidential weight (s.9(2)), assessed having regard to the reliability of the manner in which the message was generated, stored or communicated, the reliability of the manner in which integrity was maintained, the manner in which the originator was identified, and any other relevant factor (s.9(3)). A data message made in the ordinary course of business, or a copy, printout or extract certified correct by an officer in the service of that person, is admissible on mere production and is rebuttable proof of its facts (s.9(4)).
evidence: Documentation of how records are generated, stored and communicated and why that manner is reliable
Documentation of how integrity of stored records is maintained

sop: Assess evidential weight by reliability of generation, storage and communication; reliability of integrity maintenance; manner of originator identification; and other relevant factors (s.9(3)).
Have an officer in the service of the person certify a copy, printout or extract to be correct (s.9(4)).

controls.name: Production of electronic documents and certified copies
controls.statement: A requirement to produce a document or information is met by producing an electronic form if the method of generating it reliably assured integrity and it was reasonable to expect it to be readily accessible and usable for subsequent reference (s.11(1)); this is subject to the public body's filing requirements under s.24. Notarisation, acknowledgment, verification or oath is met by attaching the advanced electronic signature of the authorised person (s.12(1)). A certified copy of an electronic document may be a printout certified as a true reproduction (s.12(2)); a certified electronic copy of a paper document must be certified as a true copy and the certification confirmed by an advanced electronic signature (s.12(3)). Where law requires a seal and does not prescribe the electronic method, the document must indicate it is under seal and include the advanced electronic signature of the sealer (s.13(3)).
evidence: Procedure for producing electronic documents showing the integrity-assurance method used
Sample certified electronic copies carrying an advanced electronic signature
