controls.name: Electronic signature use and attribution of records to the originator
controls.statement: Where law requires a signature and does not specify its type, an advanced electronic signature meets the requirement (s.6(1)); where parties require an electronic signature and have not agreed on a type, the method must identify the person, indicate approval of the information communicated, and be reliable and appropriate in the circumstances (s.7(1)). A valid advanced electronic signature is presumed properly applied unless the contrary is proved (s.7(3)). An electronic record is the originator's if sent by the originator, an authorised person, or an information system programmed by or for the originator to operate automatically (s.18(1)); the addressee may rely on it if it properly applied an agreed authentication procedure or the record resulted from a person with access to the originator's identification method (s.18(2)). Absent an agreed procedure, the apparent originator is presumed to be the originator, subject to the exceptions in s.18(4).
evidence: Signature policy stating which signature type applies to which document class
Agreed originator-authentication procedures with counterparties
Delegation or authority records for persons sending on behalf of the originator

controls.name: Public body e-filing and issuing: acceptance, format and control specification
controls.statement: A public body that accepts the filing of documents, requires documents to be created or retained, issues permits, licences or approvals, or provides for payment may, despite contrary law, accept filing, creation or retention as a data message, issue permits, licences or approvals as data messages, and make or receive payment electronically (s.23). Where it does so, it may specify, in the Gazette, a daily newspaper of general circulation or its electronic platform: the manner and format for filing, creating, retaining or issuing data messages (s.24(a)); the signature type required (s.24(b)); how the signature is attached or associated (s.24(c)); the identity or criteria of designated certification authorities (s.24(d)); the control processes and procedures ensuring adequate integrity, security and confidentiality of data messages or payments (s.24(e)); and any other requirements (s.24(f)).
evidence: Gazette notice, newspaper notice or platform publication specifying manner and format of electronic filing and issuing

controls.name: National PKI Register of certification authorities, time stamping providers and cryptography providers
controls.statement: The Authority must establish and maintain a Register in which it enters names and other details of licensed and private certification authorities, timestamping service providers, cryptography service providers, applications rejected and the reasons, and any other information it considers necessary (s.93(1)). The Register must be kept at a place the Authority determines and be open to public inspection during normal working hours (s.93(2)). A suspension or cancellation of a licence must be entered in the Register (s.33(6)); a rejected licence application must be notified in writing with reasons (s.28(4)); the Authority also maintains the certificate revocation list and other repositories (s.26(2)(g)). The Act prescribes no entry schema or identifier format.
evidence: Extract of the Register showing entries for licensed CAs, private CAs, time stamping providers and cryptography providers

controls.name: Time stamp records, verification documentation and time stamping audit
controls.statement: A timestamp must be linked to data so that undetectable change after stamping is precluded (s.58(1)); the provider must confirm timestamps it issued when required (s.58(2)) and its systems must be unable to issue identical timestamps for a time earlier or later than the relevant point in time (s.58(3)). A timestamping service provider must make correct indications of time per Authority guidelines (s.61(a)), maintain records of issued time-stamps (s.61(b)), preserve documentation to verify issued timestamps (s.61(c)), ensure timestamps can be obtained and verified on the data communication network when required (s.61(d)), conduct an annual information systems audit and submit the results (s.60(2), s.61(e)), publicise compulsory insurance conditions (s.61(f)) and inform the authorised processor of the register of certification of any change to the public key used (s.61(g)). The Act states no retention period for the timestamp records.
evidence: Log or database of issued time-stamps
Preserved documentation enabling verification of issued timestamps
Time source and calibration records evidencing correct indication of time
Verification service availability evidence on the data communication network
Annual information systems audit report submitted to the Authority
Notification to the register processor of any change to the timestamping public key
Published insurance conditions

controls.name: Certificate content, revocation list and CA information system audit
controls.statement: A certification authority may issue a certificate only after an application, compliance with its certification practice statement including subscriber identification, and verification that the listed information is accurate and the subscriber holds a working private key (s.36). A certificate must set out the certificate number, holder name, holder personal identification or registry code, holder public key, validity period, issuer and issuer registry code, and limitations on scope of use (s.37). The CA must use a trustworthy system (s.38), maintain a certificate revocation list (s.41), publish a signed notice of suspension in the repository (s.47) and a signed notice of revocation in every repository specified in the certificate (s.50), and conduct an information system audit annually and submit the report to the National Root CA (s.40(1)).
evidence: Sample certificates showing the seven required fields
Certificate revocation list and its publication location
Signed notices of suspension and revocation in the repository
Certification practice statement
Annual information system audit report and its submission to the National Root CA
Subscriber identification and application records for issued certificates

controls.name: Recovery agents: Data Protection Act compliance and stored recovery information
controls.statement: A recovery agent must implement technical and organisational measures to comply with the Data Protection Act (the Act text reads 'Data Protection Act, 2020'; other instruments in the library cite Act No. 3 of 2021) and must not disclose stored recovery information or use it to decrypt data or communications (s.90(1)). No person may access stored recovery information from a recovery agent without authorisation (s.90(2)). A recovery agent may disclose or use stored recovery information only with the consent of the person who stored it, or that person's agent, or under a court order (s.90(3)). Releasing a decryption key or decrypting data without authorisation is an offence (s.87(1)); a key holder may release only with approval of the key owner, where necessary to the encryption service or key holding, or under a court interception order (s.87(3)). A key holder must not disclose records or personal information about a key owner except with consent or court order (s.88(1)), and a recovery agent must not disclose use of recovery information or assistance to law enforcement (s.88(2)).
evidence: Documented technical and organisational measures of the recovery agent mapped to Data Protection Act obligations
Access control list and access log for stored recovery information
Consent records from persons who stored recovery information
Court orders authorising disclosure or use of recovery information
Register of keys held or managed with owner approvals
Data protection impact or compliance assessment for the recovery service

controls.name: Electronic marketing: identity, opt-out and source of personal information
controls.statement: A person marketing by electronic communication must give the addressee its identity and contact details, a valid and operational opt-out facility, the identifying particulars of the source from which the originator obtained the addressee's personal information, and applicable privacy and other user policies (s.64(2)). Commercial communications may be sent only where the opt-in requirement is met (s.65(2)): the addressee consents, and contact details were collected in the course of a sale or negotiations, only similar products are promoted, an opt-out was offered free of charge at collection and declined, and an opt-out is offered with every subsequent message (s.65(3)). A supplier must make available on its website, application or platform its security procedures and privacy policy for payment, payment information and personal information (s.63(1)(p)). Sending to an opted-out addressee is an offence (s.65(6)).
evidence: Marketing message templates showing identity, contact details, opt-out and privacy policy
Opt-in and consent records with collection context (sale or negotiation)
Opt-out suppression list and evidence it is honoured
Record of the source from which each addressee's personal information was obtained
Published privacy policy and payment security procedures

policies.title: Network Management Standard
principles: The Standard governs design, development, utilisation and management of the Government Network Infrastructure (GNI), whose main component is the Government Wide Area Network (GWAN), and applies to all Ministries, Provinces and Spending Agencies (MPSAs) (Foreword, cl. 1, 1.1).
The e-Government Division (SMART Zambia Institute) formulates and enforces ICT standards and compliance by MPSAs is required (Foreword).

The GNI uses industry-proven technologies based on open architecture and international network standards (cl. 3(d)), is designed with confidentiality and security of data as a high priority (cl. 3(e)) and is operational, reliable and available (cl. 3(b)).
MPSAs use standard devices and architecture approved by Office Equipment and Machine Services (Ministry of Works and Supply), ZICTA and the e-Government Division (cl. 3(h)).

The Government retains governance on any connection in operation: connections conform to laws, regulations and standards; each MPSA is responsible for securing its own network; IP address allocation is administered by the e-Government Division (cl. 3.4).
Technology areas are classified as Emerging, Current Standard In-Use, Legacy or Antiquated, and only Current Standard technologies are used in new GNI development (cl. 3.2).
The e-Government Division may suspend or terminate any connection or activity on the GNI, and reinstatement needs authorisation by the National Coordinator (cl. 3.5).
Where network infrastructure and connectivity are outsourced, governance and decision making stay within the Government entity ICT team (cl. 11.1(e)).
International infrastructure standards such as ISO 27001 are implemented and end-to-end data encryption is used (cl. 11.1(f), 11.1(h)).
management_intent: All Government communication, being email, telephone communication, video conferencing and instant messaging among others, is archived legally and can be accessed for legal services (cl. 7.3).
The e-Government Division administers IP address allocation for connection links and associated equipment (cl. 3.4(c)).
The e-Government Division Network Management Team monitors the GNI, implements network security policy, handles escalations and updates network operations documentation (cl. 4).
GNI architecture, deployment, enhancements and equipment configuration are documented, regularly updated per change requests, and vendors supply original and as-built documentation (cl. 5).
Access to the GNI management console is role based and all user-driven events are logged (cl. 7, 7.1).
Network connections are audited, subjected to external ICT audit, and unauthorised changes are investigated immediately (cl. 10).
MPSAs satisfy a site feasibility study, site readiness activities and a network security assessment before joining the GWAN (cl. 12).
The e-Government Division advises on and clears Public Service ICT network infrastructure before MPSAs purchase it (cl. 13).

controls.name: Archiving of all Government communications
controls.statement: Official email exchange within the GNI is conducted over the network as needed, enforced and controlled by the MPSA network or system administrator. All Government communication, that is email, telephone communication, video conferencing, instant messaging among others, must be archived legally and accessed for legal services. The text states no retention period, archive location, format, or access authorisation process.
evidence: Archive system configuration covering email, telephone, video conferencing and instant messaging
Inventory of Government communication channels and whether each is archived
Records of legal-services access requests to the archive and approvals
Archive retention schedule (the Standard states none, so this is the assessed entity's own)
Administrator enforcement and control records for official email exchange

controls.name: IP address allocation administered by the e-Government Division
controls.statement: IP address allocation for the connection link and associated equipment is administered by the e-Government Division. All connections within the GNI are based on a standard speed determined by the e-Government Division, and the MPSA LAN termination equipment to the GNI is prescribed by the e-Government Division. Annex 2 also lists IP as the only network protocol in routers and recommends transition from IPv4 to IPv6.
evidence: IP address allocation register or IPAM extract for each MPSA connection link and associated equipment
Allocation requests and approvals by the e-Government Division
Record of the prescribed standard connection speed and termination equipment per MPSA
Evidence that no MPSA self-allocated address space for GNI links
IPv4 to IPv6 transition tracking

controls.name: Connection requests, approval, suspension and reinstatement
controls.statement: Network services over the GNI are coordinated by the e-Government Division based on MPSA needs, requested in writing by the Responsible Officer. The e-Government Division issues, certifies and revises GNI connectivity requests, standards and compliance mechanisms. Every connection must conform to the laws, procedures, regulations and standards of relevant statutory organisations, and each MPSA secures its own network. The e-Government Division may suspend or terminate any connection or activity; reinstatement is only possible after authorisation by the National Coordinator, and MPSAs are given the reasons (for example non-compliance).
evidence: Written connection requests signed by the Responsible Officer
e-Government Division certification or approval of each connectivity request
Register of active, suspended and terminated GNI connections
Suspension or termination notices stating reasons
National Coordinator authorisation for each reinstatement
sop: Request network services in writing through the Responsible Officer (3.4).
e-Government Division issues, certifies and revises connectivity requests (3.4).
On suspension, give the MPSA the reasons for the action; reinstate only after authorisation by the National Coordinator (3.5).

controls.name: Open standards, VPN prerequisite and GNI technology classification
controls.statement: GNI connections conform to defined open standards and National Network Infrastructure standards (3.3.1(a)), are built on IP/MPLS (3.3.1(e)), and each MPSA must set up a VPN before getting access to the GNI (3.3.1(f)). Each technology area is classified Emerging, Current Standard In-Use, Legacy or Antiquated (3.2); Emerging items are used only in controlled pilot or test environments. MPSAs ensure interoperability of all active devices with the GNI (3.3.1(i)) and connect only by the supported connection technologies (3.3.1(h)). Annex 2 classifies mandatory standards (SMTP for email delivery, DHCP and NAT within MPSAs, MPLS transport, redundancy by dual or shared links, TCP/IP only) and recommended ones (Government-wide DNS, central remote access, IPv6 transition). Annex 2 item 6 requires the WAN to be secure and MPSAs to assess the need to encrypt data over the network.
evidence: GNI technology standards register with classification per component (Emerging, Current, Legacy, Antiquated)
VPN set-up evidence for each MPSA before GNI access was granted
Interoperability test results for active devices
Network design showing IP/MPLS and redundancy by dual or shared links
MPSA assessment of the need to encrypt data over the network (Annex 2 item 6)
Pilot or test environment records for any Emerging technology in use

controls.name: Network documentation: architecture, configuration and as-built records
controls.statement: GNI architecture, deployment and enhancements must be documented, including equipment configuration, to foster proper management, enforce security and plan for growth. The documentation is regularly updated and maintained in accordance with change requests. GNI vendors must provide the original and as-built documentation. Methods for detailed GNI operations are defined in technical resource manuals and training, and those manuals are classified accordingly; procedures not otherwise defined are at the discretion of the e-Government Division. The Network Management Team updates documentation of network operations procedures (4(i)), and user and technical manuals are provided (3.3.1(b)). The Standard does not define the classification levels.
evidence: GNI architecture documents and network diagrams
Equipment configuration documentation for GNI components
Vendor-supplied original and as-built documentation
Change requests and the matching documentation updates
Technical resource manuals showing a classification label
Network operations procedure documents with revision history

controls.name: Role-based access to the GNI management console and event logging
controls.statement: Access to the GNI management console is protected by user IDs and passwords; the main network administrator configures each user and correlates access to role. Web access is fully SSL, TCL and Kerberos encrypted. Detailed logging must cover individual user access, login and log-off; changes to system and monitoring configuration; addition or deletion of devices; changes to policies, alerts and notifications; and access to reporting and other system functions (7(a)-(e)). Role-based management imports login information from Active Directory and LDAP and defines, by organisational function, user access to configuration management, reporting, discovery, policies, workspaces and management and monitoring of services, servers, applications and devices (7.1). Managers maintain access control lists and security mechanisms on routers, switches, IDS, IPS and firewalls and SNMP security, and provide role-based access rights (6).
evidence: User and role matrix for the management console
Active Directory or LDAP import configuration
Event logs for login, log-off, configuration changes, device additions or deletions, policy changes and report access
ACL and security configuration of routers, switches, IDS, IPS and firewalls
SNMP security settings

controls.name: Network monitoring, audits and external ICT audit
controls.statement: The e-Government Division Network Management Team monitors all aspects of connections over the GNI and uses monitoring tools to automate auditing. Audits cover the authentication database showing login entries, all entity router and network device configurations, client equipment where tampering may be suspected, bandwidth management, monitoring of access points, monitoring dashboards, monitoring of unauthorised use, and the GNI is subjected to external ICT audit (10(a)-(h)). The team investigates any unauthorised changes immediately, MPSA connections are reviewed regularly by mutual agreement, routine maintenance processes are documented and SLAs for maintenance with external service providers are agreed and adhered to.
evidence: Audit reports covering items (a) to (g)
External ICT audit report on the GNI
Investigation records of unauthorised changes
Records of regular MPSA connection reviews
Documented routine maintenance processes
SLAs with external service providers and adherence reports
Monitoring dashboards and tool outputs
sop: Audit the authentication database, router and network device configurations, suspect client equipment, bandwidth management, access points, dashboards and unauthorised use (10(a)-(g)).
Subject the GNI to external ICT audit (10(h)).
Investigate unauthorised changes immediately; review MPSA connections regularly by mutual agreement; document routine maintenance processes (10).

controls.name: Protection of Government information and network resources
controls.statement: The e-Government Division is responsible for ensuring all possible measures are taken for the integrity and privacy of Government confidential information; MPSAs are responsible for appropriate security measures to protect their private internal network and information. Measures include biometric card based login with active directories, an encryption method, and procurement of systems with adequate security features (7.6). The Government entity infrastructure is secured with end-to-end data encryption such as IP VPN and SSL (11.1(h)). ICT facilities supporting critical or sensitive Government services are secured and critical links and servers are in physically secure areas (7.7). The text does not define a classification scheme for confidential information.
evidence: Security measures register showing biometric login, encryption and security feature requirements
Encryption method documentation for data in transit and storage
Identification of ICT facilities that support critical or sensitive Government services
Physical access control records for data centres, NOC and server rooms
Procurement records showing security features were assessed
Information classification scheme for Government confidential information (not defined in the Standard)

controls.name: File exchange, Telnet and web resource access restrictions
controls.statement: Using router Access Control Lists, file exchange by FTP is restricted to designated FTP servers (7.2). Telnet access to GNI servers is prohibited and access to other internal Government hosts and devices is limited and authorised by the authority owning those hosts and devices (7.4). Access to internal web resources is provided on a need basis; the Government's public web resources are reached through normal Internet access (7.5).
evidence: Router ACL configuration restricting FTP to designated servers
Register of designated FTP servers
Scan or configuration evidence that Telnet is disabled on GNI servers
Authorisations by owners of internal hosts and devices granting access
Need-based access approvals for internal web resources

controls.name: Backup, recovery and separate siting of fallback media and continuity plans
controls.statement: Government entities implement a comprehensive backup and recovery plan so that all server and storage contents are secure and recoverable (11.1(l)). Fallback equipment and back-up media are sited at a safe distance to avoid damage from a disaster at the main site, and Business Continuity Plans and associated equipment are stored in a location sufficiently separate from the main location (7.7(b)). Backup power for equipment supporting critical Government services is regularly tested and included in contingency planning (9). Redundancy by dual or shared links is mandatory for critical components (Annex 2 item 4). The GWAN is intended to enable real-time back-up and disaster recovery services (1(g)). The text states no backup frequency, retention period or restore-test requirement.
evidence: Backup and recovery plan covering server and storage contents
Location records for fallback equipment, backup media and Business Continuity Plans
Backup job logs and restore test results
Backup power test records for critical services
Redundant link configuration

controls.name: Minimum requirements for an MPSA to join the GWAN
controls.statement: Several prerequisites must be satisfied before an MPSA is allowed to join the GWAN: a site feasibility study, site readiness activities and a network security assessment, coordinated by the e-Government Division. The site feasibility study covers satellite, copper, microwave or fibre access to the MPSA and path diversity (12.1). For site readiness the MPSA must gather and provide to the e-Government Division information on power availability, air-conditioning, current ICT infrastructure, network access points and cabling (12.2). The text names the network security assessment but gives no sub-clause setting out its content.
evidence: Site feasibility study report per MPSA
Site readiness submission covering power, air-conditioning, current ICT infrastructure, access points and cabling
Network security assessment report per MPSA
e-Government Division confirmation that prerequisites were met before GWAN connection
Register of MPSAs with GWAN join date
sop: Complete a site feasibility study (12.1).
Complete site readiness activities by providing the e-Government Division with power, air-conditioning, ICT infrastructure, access point and cabling information (12.2).
Complete a network security assessment before joining the GWAN (12).

controls.name: Procurement clearance of Public Service ICT network infrastructure
controls.statement: MPSAs are expected to obtain technical advice from the e-Government Division on the configuration of information systems suitable for the intended purpose 15 days prior to issuance of tenders. The e-Government Division has sole authority to clear all Public Service ICT network infrastructure before it is purchased by MPSAs (13). MPSAs use standard devices and architecture approved by Office Equipment and Machine Services, Ministry of Works and Supply, ZICTA and the e-Government Division (3(h)), and infrastructure components are provided by proven vendors (11.1(a)).
evidence: Technical advice requests sent to the e-Government Division at least 15 days before tender issue
e-Government Division clearance for each network infrastructure purchase
Approved standard device and architecture list
Tender documents showing the cleared configuration
sop: Obtain technical advice from the e-Government Division on the configuration 15 days before issuing tenders (13).
Obtain e-Government Division clearance before purchasing network infrastructure (13).

policies.title: Government Office Equipment Management Standards
principles: The Standards apply to all Public Bodies and cooperating partners in the procurement, registration, utilisation, transfer, maintenance and disposal of office equipment, and are anchored on SI No. 77 of 2022 (Public Finance Management (Public Stores) Regulations) (Foreword, cl. 1.0, 1.1, 1.3).
Accountability is secured by assigning ranges of Government serial numbers for inscription on equipment and by maintaining an inventory of all Government office equipment (cl. 1.0 items 3-4).

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics, through the Office Equipment and Maintenance Services Unit, coordinates acquisition, registration, maintenance, usage and disposal; the Office Equipment Controller oversees implementation (cl. 1.0, 1.1, 11.0).

The standards are minimum requirements; networking devices, computer servers, switches and software not covered are referred to the National Coordinator, Electronic Government Division (SMART Zambia Institute) (cl. 1.1).

Legal framework: Public Finance Management Act No. 1 of 2018, Public Procurement Act No. 8 of 2020, ICT Act No. 15 of 2009, Electronic Communications and Transactions Act No. 4 of 2021, Environmental Management Act No. 12 of 2011, Public Procurement Regulations 2022, Public Asset Management Policy 2020 and the Public Stores Regulations 2022 (cl. 10.0).
Utilisation, maintenance and disposal must be environmentally responsible and sustainable (cl. 1.4.8).
Equipment acquired is expected to have a useful life of not less than five years (cl. 12(i)).
A public asset is a resource the Republic owns or controls with expected future benefit, including public stores and major state assets (Working Definitions).
Non-compliance may attract disciplinary action under the PFMA No. 1 of 2018 and the Disciplinary Code (cl. 11.0).
management_intent: Every public body keeps an asset register of office equipment with make, model, manufacturer serial number, GRZ serial number and location (cl. 3.1(5)).
The Office Equipment Controller keeps a master record of all Government office equipment and assigns ranges of GRZ serial numbers (cl. 3.1(6)-(7)).
Controlling officers submit a quarterly return of office machinery to the Office Equipment Controller (cl. 3.2(2)).
All office equipment carries a visible GRZ serial number that is quoted in correspondence (cl. 3.1(1)-(3)).
Active storage devices are removed from office equipment designated for disposal, with the controlling officer's authority (cl. 7.1(2), 7.2(2)).
Thefts and losses are reported to the supervisor and Zambia Police within 24 hours and to the Office Equipment Controller within 48 hours (cl. 6.1).
Equipment custody is documented by the Office Equipment Custodian Form (OE 1) and handover-takeover notes, and inventories use Form PSR XIX (cl. 4.2, Appendices 2 and 4).

controls.name: Office equipment asset register
controls.statement: All Public Bodies must maintain an asset register of office equipment under their charge with the following details: make, model, manufacturer serial number, GRZ serial number and location (3.1(5)). All project office equipment must be recorded in the asset register of the respective Public Body (2.2(10)). Each office must have an updated Miscellaneous Form 58A visibly displayed on the door (3.1(4)). The Standard does not require asset data owner, acquisition date, cost, condition or storage-capacity fields in the register.
evidence: Asset register extract showing make, model, manufacturer serial number, GRZ serial number and location for each item
Physical verification sample matching registered items to equipment on site
Project office equipment recorded in the register
Miscellaneous Form 58A displayed on office doors
Register data dictionary or template defining the five mandatory fields

controls.name: GRZ serial number assignment, inscription and quoting
controls.statement: All office equipment and other assets, whether procured or donated, must be inscribed with GRZ serial numbers (3.1(1)), appropriately assigned before distribution to end users (2.2(8)), marked at a visible position (3.1(2)), and the GRZ serial number must be quoted in all correspondence about the equipment (3.1(3)). The Office Equipment Controller assigns a range of GRZ serial numbers to Public Bodies (3.1(7)); Public Bodies request the Controller to assign numbers to newly procured or donated equipment and furniture (3.2(1)).
evidence: Controller's record of GRZ serial number ranges assigned to each Public Body
Requests to the Controller for GRZ serial numbers on new or donated equipment
Physical inspection sample showing visible inscribed GRZ serial numbers
Correspondence samples quoting the GRZ serial number
Evidence that numbers were assigned before distribution to end users
sop: Request the Office Equipment Controller to assign GRZ serial numbers to newly procured or donated office equipment and furniture (3.2(1)).
Inscribe the GRZ serial number at a visible position before distribution to end users (2.2(8), 3.1(2)).

controls.name: Master record of Government office equipment maintained by the Office Equipment Controller
controls.statement: The Office Equipment Controller maintains a master record of all Government office equipment (3.1(6)) and an inventory of all Government office equipment in order to ensure accountability (1.0 item 4). Office equipment donated to Government must be reported to the Controller for updating of the master record (2.2(9), 2.3(5)). A Public Body transferring equipment to another Public Body must notify the Controller (4.1(5)). The Controller also maintains a record of repaired office equipment (1.0 item 2). The Standard defines no master record schema and no reconciliation step between Public Body registers and the master record.
evidence: Master record extract showing equipment by Public Body
Donation notifications to the Controller and corresponding master record updates
Inter-Public Body transfer notifications and corresponding updates
Controller's record of repaired equipment
Reconciliation of Public Body asset registers to the master record
sop: Report donated office equipment to the Office Equipment Controller for updating of the master record (2.2(9)).
Notify the Controller before transferring office equipment to another Public Body (4.1(5)).

controls.name: Quarterly return of office machinery
controls.statement: A controlling officer must cause to be prepared and submitted to the Office Equipment Controller a return of the office machinery at the end of each quarter, not later than the fifteenth day of the month after the end of the quarter. The Standard does not prescribe the return content beyond office machinery.
evidence: Quarterly returns with submission dates
Controller's acknowledgement or receipt of each return
Tracker of returns due and submitted by Public Body
Evidence of the controlling officer's preparation and sign-off
sop: Prepare a return of the office machinery at the end of each quarter (3.2(2)).
Submit the return to the Office Equipment Controller not later than the fifteenth day of the month after the quarter end (3.2(2)).

controls.name: Custody of equipment: Form OE 1, authority to remove and handover-takeover
controls.statement: No Government office equipment may be moved out of the office without prior written authority from the supervisor (4.1(2)); officers allocated movable devices are responsible for their safety and custodianship in and outside the office (4.1(3)); officers exiting a Public Body must surrender all equipment in their custody to their supervisors (4.1(4)) and complete the handover-takeover note (4.2(2)). The Office Equipment Custodian Form (Form OE 1, regulation 56 PFMA 2018) records the officer's name, position, staff number, mobile number, address, make or asset description, model, serial number, GRZ number, accessories, condition, purpose, expected return date, acknowledgement signed by the officer and authorisation by an authorising officer. Appendix 5 is a Certificate of Handing and Taking Over of Stations or Departments. Equipment is used for Government work only, not for commercial, for-profit or illegal activities (4.1(1)). The Form OE 1 has no field for data held on the device.
evidence: Completed Office Equipment Custodian Forms (OE 1) for movable devices
Written supervisor authority for removal of equipment from the office
Handover-takeover notes for exiting officers
Certificates of Handing and Taking Over of Stations or Departments
Register of equipment issued to individual custodians cross-referenced to the asset register
sop: Obtain written permission from the supervisor to use Government equipment outside the office (4.2(1)).
Complete the handover-takeover note when surrendering equipment on exit (4.2(2)).
Report any abuse of office equipment to the controlling officer (4.2(3)).

controls.name: Inventory of assets issued and received: Form PSR XIX
controls.statement: Inventories of furniture, fittings, plant, machinery, tools and equipment issued and received are kept on Form PSR XIX issued under regulation 51 of the Public Finance Management (Public Stores) Regulations, 2022. The form carries a file number, control number, date, item, signature of the receiving officer, posting checked (initials) and recorded in ledger (initials), with issues in black or blue and receipts in red. The Standards state they follow SI No. 77 of 2022 (Foreword). The source text of the form contains only field labels; Appendix 3 (form 21) has no extractable content.
evidence: Completed Form PSR XIX entries for equipment issued and received
Evidence of posting checks and ledger recording initials
Control number and file number references linking forms to the asset register
Receiving officer signatures

controls.name: Removal of active storage devices before disposal (data sanitisation)
controls.statement: Active storage devices must be removed from all office equipment that is designated for disposal (7.1(2)). Authority must be obtained from the controlling officer before active storage devices are removed from office equipment designated for disposal (7.2(2)). The Standard does not say what happens to the removed storage devices, does not set a sanitisation or destruction method, does not require a record of removal and does not mention data classification or Data Protection Act obligations; the same gap applies to equipment sent to private firms for repair (5.1(2)) and to equipment lost or stolen (6.1).
evidence: Disposal records listing each item and confirming active storage devices were removed
Controlling officer authority for storage device removal
Custody or destruction records for removed storage devices (not specified by the Standard)
Sanitisation method used before reuse, donation or disposal, if any
Disposal committee minutes referencing storage device removal
sop: Obtain authority from the controlling officer before active storage devices are removed from office equipment designated for disposal (7.2(2)).
Remove active storage devices from all office equipment designated for disposal (7.1(2)).

controls.name: Disposal of office equipment under the PFMA
controls.statement: Disposal of office equipment must be done in accordance with the Public Finance Management Act No. 1 of 2018 (7.1(1)). Disposal has been decentralised to Public Bodies, which constitute Committees of Survey or Disposal Committees in accordance with the PFMA (7.2(1)). The Office Equipment and Maintenance Services Unit identifies obsolete and unserviceable office equipment to facilitate disposal (1.0 item 7). The Standard states no requirement to update the asset register or the Controller's master record on disposal.
evidence: Committee of Survey or Disposal Committee appointment records
Disposal committee minutes and approvals
Lists of obsolete and unserviceable equipment identified by the Unit
Asset register entries showing disposal date and method
Evidence of environmentally responsible disposal (cl. 1.4.8)
sop: Constitute Committees of Survey or Disposal Committees in accordance with the PFMA No. 1 of 2018 (7.2(1)).

controls.name: Theft and loss reporting
controls.statement: All thefts and losses involving Government office equipment must be reported to the supervisor and Zambia Police within 24 hours of occurrence (6.1(1)) and to the Office Equipment Controller within 48 hours (6.1(2)). Thefts and losses while in a public officer's custody where authority was not granted by the supervisor are handled under the Disciplinary Code (6.1(3)). A public officer who loses equipment must ensure a copy of the preliminary report is submitted to the controlling officer (6.2). The Standard does not require assessment of data held on the lost or stolen device.
evidence: Theft or loss incident reports with date and time of occurrence
Zambia Police report references and timestamps
Report to the Office Equipment Controller within 48 hours
Preliminary reports submitted to the controlling officer
Asset register entries updated for lost or stolen items
sop: Report the theft or loss to the supervisor and Zambia Police within 24 hours (6.1(1)).
Report to the Office Equipment Controller within 48 hours (6.1(2)).
Submit a copy of the preliminary report to the controlling officer (6.2).

controls.name: Maintenance, repair authority and cannibalisation
controls.statement: Maintenance is done by the Office Equipment Controller or a reputable private firm registered with a professional body (5.1(1)). No equipment may be taken to a private firm for repair without prior authority from the controlling officer (5.1(2)). No public officer may remove or swap (cannibalise) any part without the controlling officer's authority (5.1(4)). The Controller conducts regular inspections (5.1(5)) after notifying Public Bodies (5.2(1)), and maintains a record of repaired equipment (1.0 item 2). The Standard does not require removal of storage devices or data sanitisation before equipment leaves for repair.
evidence: Controlling officer authority for repairs by private firms
Authority for removal or swapping of any part
Maintenance and repair records per GRZ serial number
Inspection reports by the Office Equipment Controller
Memoranda of understanding with the Permanent Secretary on maintenance (5.2(3))

policies.title: Public Asset Management Policy
principles: Equity: equitable distribution of public assets between urban and rural areas, based on need (3.3)
Citizenry participation: citizens safeguard and report vandalism, calamities and defects concerning public assets (3.3)
Coordination: stakeholders coordinate to avoid duplication and overlaps in the management of public assets (3.3)
Decentralisation: management of public assets is undertaken at the lower administrative levels or institutions where they have their effect (3.3)
Gender equity: gender equity in the management of public assets and in the award of contracts (3.3)
Integrity: honesty, reliability and uprightness in award and supervision of contracts and in selection, acquisition and use of public assets (3.3)
Non-discrimination: human rights exercised without discrimination in managing public assets (3.3)
Patriotism: citizens have a duty to protect public assets (3.3)
Sustainable development: care and maintenance throughout the asset life cycle (3.3)
Transparency and accountability: management in an open and responsible manner; assets acquired and disposed of transparently; all public assets accounted for using GAAP (3.3)
management_intent: Provide a framework for all public bodies to manage assets sustainably across identification, acquisition, valuation, utilisation, maintenance, redevelopment, accounting and disposal (1.0)
Replace uncoordinated, silo-based asset management and the absence of a consolidated electronic asset register that left some assets unaccounted for and lost (2.2, 2.3, 2.8)
Support the move from cash-basis to accrual-basis accounting through electronic financial management systems, making accounting for assets a necessity (1.0, 3.2)
Establish an electronic information management system for public assets linked to all MPSAs and a National Asset Register at national level (4.2 viii and ix)
Enable the Ministry of Finance to prepare a country balance sheet from valuation reports and annual consolidated statements of assets certified by the Auditor General (5.1.1)
Promote transparency, accountability and value for money in the acquisition, use and disposal of public assets (Foreword, 3.2, 4.1)
Verify compliance through physical inventory twice every financial year and spot checks by the Treasury and the Ministry responsible for Works and Supply (5.4)

controls.name: National Asset Register and consolidated electronic asset information system

The Ministry responsible for Works and Supply develops and maintains the consolidated register of all public assets for accountability and prepares the annual consolidated asset register for the Ministry of Finance. Cabinet Office provides oversight and guidance on the development, management and maintenance of the Electronic Asset Register. It is mandatory for all public bodies to maintain an Asset Register (2.9, citing PFMA No. 1 of 2018). The policy itself records that no comprehensive asset register for all government assets yet exists (2.9).

controls.statement: Every MPSA shall record public assets under its charge, maintain an electronic sub database of all such assets, and update asset data in the applicable Asset Management Information System as prescribed. Maintaining the Asset Register entails updating records when there is an acquisition, depreciation, impairment loss, revaluation, transfer or disposal (2.9). MPSAs also coordinate and submit capitalisation amounts and update the asset register for donated assets to the Ministries responsible for finance, works and supply, and local government (5.1.11).

controls.name: Unique government serial number, labelling and tagging of assets

Allocation of GRZ numbers is vested in the Ministry responsible for works and supply under CAP 600 and Statutory Instrument No. 122 of 1985 (2.3). Assets must be labelled and tagged and this must reflect in the asset register; MPSAs ensure all acquired assets are appropriately labelled with indelible ink (5.1.11). State land is to be on title, and MPSAs were directed to acquire title deeds (2.3).

controls.name: Databases and software recognised as intangible assets in the register
controls.clause: Working Definitions (Asset; Intangible Asset: software, database; Asset Register); 5.1.11
controls.statement: The policy defines an Asset as any tangible and/or intangible property owned by a public body to which a value can be assigned, and an Intangible Asset as an identifiable non-monetary asset without physical substance, e.g. software, database or any related asset. The Asset Register is defined as a list of assets owned by a public body containing details about tangible and intangible assets to track their value, quantity and physical location. Databases and software held by an MPSA therefore fall within the asset register obligations in 5.1.11. The Classes of Public Assets table does not name an intangible class; such assets would fall under Others, which an assessor should confirm against the MPSA register structure.

controls.name: Asset classification, valuation and depreciation basis
controls.clause: Classes of Public Assets table; Estimated Lifespan of Assets table and notes (a) to (e); 3.3 (GAAP); 4.2 (ii, iii, vi); 5.1.2 (valuation and revaluation); 5.1.11 (valuation, revaluation, technologically impaired assets)
controls.statement: Assets are classified in the Classes of Public Assets table (immovable, movable, and sub-classes such as Land, Infrastructure, Plant and Equipment, Motor Vehicles, Office Equipment which includes computers and telecommunication equipment, Financial Assets and Others). The Estimated Lifespan table gives useful lives by asset category, including computer hardware and telecommunication equipment under Office Equipment; lives of unlisted assets are assigned by the Secretary to the Treasury in consultation with the Ministry responsible for Works and Supply (note a). All assets other than land, heritage and biological assets are depreciated straight-line over useful life (note b); depreciation begins when the asset is available for use (note c) and ceases at the earlier of classification as held for sale and derecognition from the asset register (note d). Each Controlling body makes an annual provision for depreciation (note e). MPSAs ensure assets are valued in accordance with GAAP as directed by the Treasury, that revaluations of all classes are undertaken, and that information on technologically impaired assets is assessed and submitted.

sop: Depreciate assets other than land, heritage and biological assets using the straight-line method over useful life (Estimated Lifespan note b)

Cease depreciation at the earlier of classification as held for sale and derecognition from the register (note d)

Maintenance is classified as emergency, minor rehabilitation, preventive (routine or periodic) and planned (capital) maintenance. The Ministry responsible for Works and Supply coordinates the implementation of the asset maintenance management system, develops infrastructure maintenance manuals, and monitors and evaluates implementation of maintenance plans in MPSAs.

controls.name: Authorised transfer and disposal of assets with record of disposed assets
controls.clause: 5.1.11 (transfers authorised; recording assets for transfer; maintaining a record of disposed of assets; Committees of Survey or Disposal Committees); 5.1.1 (authorising disposal of obsolete assets); 2.3 and 2.9; 4.1 (v, vi); 4.3 (iv)

The Ministry of Finance authorises the disposal of obsolete assets under PFMA No. 1 of 2018, and the Ministry responsible for Works and Supply determines whether assets earmarked for disposal can be used by another user. The Public Stores Regulations guide transfer, removal and disposal to keep a correct record of assets and their location, but the policy notes they are not aligned with the current legislation (2.3). The policy states that the absence of a comprehensive register makes it hard to know which assets have been or are being disposed of (2.9).

The Treasury and the Ministry responsible for Works and Supply conduct spot checks on public assets to monitor public bodies' compliance with the policy and the legal framework and then apply appropriate interventions. The Ministry of Works and Supply undertakes inspections on public assets and monitors and evaluates utilisation of all public assets, and MPSAs monitor and evaluate utilisation of assets under their charge. The policy acknowledges that follow-up inspections after handover are rarely conducted (2.4).

controls.statement: The Ministry of Finance is custodian of all public assets, and the Ministry of Works and Supply is mandated to manage all public assets under Gazette Notice No. 836 of 2016. Each MPSA identifies public officers to oversee implementation of the asset policy under its charge, maintains a system of internal control for proper management of assets, ensures assets are safeguarded and utilised for the intended purpose, ensures adherence to the asset regulatory framework, and ensures that assets acquired are covered by an insurance policy. At the higher level, they manage the comprehensive classification, organisation and administration of information, data and knowledge assets within ICT systems undertaken by others, and implement and maintain the procedures within ICT systems to classify, categorise and manage information and how it is accessed. policies.title: National Pension Scheme Act
principles: Every member is registered by the Authority and issued a unique social security number; every contributing employer is registered and issued a unique employer account number (s.16(3), s.18(3)).
Registration decisions are made within a statutory time limit (30 days) and rejections are communicated in writing with reasons (s.16(2),(4); s.18(2),(4)).
Employers pay contributions and submit monthly returns on or before the tenth day of the month following the contribution month, in the prescribed manner and form (s.24(7), s.25).

Information that comes to a person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act is confidential and may be disclosed only with the Director-General's written consent or as permitted by written law (s.63).

Benefit entitlement depends on accurate contribution and earnings history (180 or 60 monthly contributions; average monthly earnings), so employer and member data must be complete and truthful (ss.29(3), 30(3), 39(1), 64(1)(e)).
Invalidity is established only by certification of an ad hoc medical board, and may be re-examined after award (ss.37-41).
Pensions are indexed annually using national average earnings determined from statistics and data compiled by the Zambia Statistics Agency (s.48).
The Authority may require employer electronic systems to be integrated for compliance, through regulations (s.66(2)(m)).
Inspectors have statutory access to documents, books and records to enforce the Act, and obstruction or false information is an offence (ss.59-60).
Knowingly giving the Authority a false statement or report in any material particular is an offence (s.64(1)(e)).
Members' benefits and contributions are protected against assignment, attachment and bankruptcy (ss.52-53).
management_intent: Continue the National Pension Scheme and its membership, contribution and benefit structure under the Authority's administration (long title, ss.4, 10).
Provide for the registration of employers and members and the collection of contributions as the data foundation of the Scheme (long title, ss.5(b)-(d), 16, 18, 24, 25).
Pay benefits (retirement, early retirement, pre-retirement lump sum, invalidity, survivor, funeral) strictly on the statutory conditions and prescribed claim process (Part V, s.49).
Require prudent controls over fiscal management, actuarial correctness, reporting procedures, benefit fairness and investment of the Scheme and the Fund (ss.10(4), 55(2)).
Ensure actuarial valuation of the Scheme and sub-schemes at intervals not exceeding three years and action on the actuary's recommendations (ss.12-14).
Enforce compliance through an inspectorate, offences and penalties (Part VII, ss.62-65).
Enable regulations on forms, returns, medical-board procedure and employer electronic-system integration (s.66).

controls.name: Member registration and unique social security number
controls.clause: s.15, s.16, s.17, Second Schedule para 3(2)
controls.statement: A person aged sixteen or more and below pensionable age (sixty) applies to the Authority for registration in the prescribed manner and form. The Authority approves or rejects the application within thirty days of receipt; where the applicant satisfies the prescribed requirements the Authority registers the applicant and issues a unique social security number. A rejection is communicated in writing with reasons. Membership ceases on payment of accrued benefits or death; persons who were members of the former Scheme continue as if registered under this Act.
evidence: Member registration application in the prescribed form, with age evidence
Registration decision log showing receipt date and approval or rejection date (30-day measure)
Written rejection notices stating reasons
Member register extract showing unique social security number, date of registration and status
Uniqueness or duplicate-detection report on social security numbers
Records of cessation of membership (accrued benefits paid or death)
Migrated member records carried over from the former Scheme (Second Schedule para 3(2))
sop: Applicant applies to the Authority for registration in the prescribed manner and form.
Authority approves or rejects the application within 30 days of receipt.
Where the applicant satisfies the prescribed requirements, Authority registers the applicant and issues a unique social security number.
Where the application is rejected, Authority informs the applicant in writing stating the reasons.

controls.name: Contributing employer registration and unique employer account number
controls.clause: s.18, s.23, s.3, Second Schedule para 8
controls.statement: An employer applies for registration as a contributing employer within one month of employing its first employee, in the prescribed manner and form. The Authority approves or rejects within thirty days, and where the prescribed requirements are met registers the employer and issues a unique employer account number; rejection is in writing with reasons. Failure to apply is an offence. Employers exempt under s.3 may consent to register (all or a specified number of employees) and then follow s.18. Employers registered under the repealed Act continue with their existing account number.
evidence: Employer registration application in the prescribed form with date of first employee
Registration decision log showing receipt and decision dates
Written rejection notices with reasons
Employer register extract showing unique employer account number, status and registration date
Exempt-employer consent records and the scope of employees covered (s.23(2))
Uniqueness or duplicate-detection report on employer account numbers
Mapping of legacy employer accounts to the continued account numbers (Second Schedule para 8)
sop: Employer applies for registration as a contributing employer within one month of employing its first employee, in the prescribed manner and form.
Authority approves or rejects the application within 30 days of receipt.
Where the employer satisfies the prescribed requirements, Authority registers it and issues a unique employer account number.
Where the application is rejected, Authority informs the employer in writing stating the reasons.

controls.name: Employer account lifecycle: cancellation, suspension and reactivation
controls.statement: A contributing employer that ceases to have employees or intends to cease business applies in the prescribed manner and form for cancellation; the Authority may also cancel on death, bankruptcy, winding-up or established permanent cessation. An employer intending to cease operations for more than six months notifies the Director-General, who suspends the account; the employer notifies the Director-General in writing within thirty days of resuming and the account is reactivated. The Director-General may lift a suspension where operations have not ceased or have resumed unreported, and the Authority notifies the employer in writing within thirty days with reasons. Cancellation or suspension does not relieve liability for earlier or unreported periods.
evidence: Cancellation applications and Authority decisions
Suspension notices from employers (intention to cease for more than six months) and the Director-General's suspension decisions
Resumption notices lodged within 30 days and reactivation records
Notices lifting a suspension, with written reasons, issued within 30 days
Employer account status history (active, suspended, cancelled, reactivated) with dates
Reconciliation of suspended or cancelled accounts against liabilities and unpaid contributions
sop: Employer applies to the Authority for cancellation of registration in the prescribed manner and form when it ceases to have employees or permanently ceases business.
Employer intending to cease operations for more than six months notifies the Director-General in the prescribed manner and form.
Director-General suspends the account where satisfied that the employer has temporarily ceased to operate.
Employer notifies the Director-General in writing within 30 days of resuming operations; Director-General reactivates the account.
Where a suspension is lifted, Authority notifies the employer in writing within 30 days stating the reasons.

controls.name: Notification of employee lifecycle events and retirement intention
controls.statement: A contributing employer notifies the Authority, in the prescribed manner, when an employee's contract is terminated, the employee resigns, is placed on unpaid leave, is seconded (where the employer is not responsible for earnings), or dies; contributions cease from the relevant date or for the relevant period. A receiving employer that is not exempt pays contributions during secondment. Where a member retires early (55) or late (65), the employer notifies the Authority in the prescribed manner within thirty days of the member's notification or the employer's approval. Concurrent employment by several employers is accommodated by separate contributions per employer.
evidence: Employer event notifications (termination, resignation, unpaid leave, secondment, death) with event date and lodged date
Employee-level contribution start and stop dates reconciled to notifications
Retirement intention notices (12 months before age 55 or 65) and employer approvals
Employer notification to the Authority within 30 days of the retirement notice or approval
Secondment arrangements showing which employer pays earnings and contributions
Concurrent-employment records showing each employer's contribution for the same member
sop: Employer notifies the Authority in the prescribed manner where an employee's contract is terminated, the employee resigns, is placed on unpaid leave, is seconded without the employer paying earnings, or dies.
Employer stops contributions from the date of termination, resignation or death, or for the period of unpaid leave or secondment.
Employer notifies the Authority in the prescribed manner within 30 days of a member's early or late retirement notification or approval.

controls.name: Contribution payment timeliness, deduction rules and penalty
controls.statement: A contributing employer pays the employer's and the member's contributions at the prescribed percentage on or before the tenth day of the month following the contribution month. The member's contribution is deducted from earnings; the employer's contribution must not be deducted from earnings. Late payment attracts a penalty of ten per cent of the amount unpaid for each month or part thereof, recoverable by civil action and waivable on prescribed conditions. Where a deduction was made but not paid, the Director-General may treat the contribution as wholly or partially paid for benefit purposes. Excess deductions and non-payment are offences.
evidence: Contribution receipts ledger by employer and month with date received against the 10th-day due date
Late-payment and penalty computation records (10 per cent per month or part thereof)
Penalty waiver decisions and the Minister's waiver conditions
Director-General decisions treating unpaid contributions as paid (s.26)
Third-party recovery notices and amounts recovered (s.28)
Prosecution or enforcement records for excess deduction or failure to pay
Prescribed contribution percentage and the actuarial assessment supporting it (s.24(2))
sop: Employer pays the employer's and member's contributions on or before the tenth day of each month following the month to which the contribution relates.
Member's contribution is deducted from the member's earnings to which it relates; employer's contribution is not deducted from earnings.
Employer failing to pay on the due day is liable to a penalty of ten per cent of the amount unpaid for each month or part thereof.
Authority may recover the penalty by civil action; Authority may waive a penalty on conditions prescribed by the Minister.

controls.name: Monthly return submission and return data quality
controls.statement: A contributing employer submits a monthly return to the Authority on or before the tenth day of the month following the contribution month, in the prescribed manner and form. The return is the primary source of per-member earnings and contribution data that determines qualifying contributions and average monthly earnings, so a return that is late, incomplete or false exposes the employer to the s.64 offences. The manner and form of filing are set by regulation.
evidence: Prescribed return template or file layout and its data dictionary
Return submission log by employer and month against the 10th-day due date
Acknowledgement or validation report for each submitted return
Reconciliation of return totals to contributions received per employer-month
Rejected or amended return records with correction reason
Non-filer or late-filer report and follow-up actions
sop: Employer submits a monthly return to the Authority on or before the tenth day of each month following the month to which a contribution relates, in the prescribed manner and form.

controls.name: Employer electronic-system integration for compliance
controls.statement: Regulations may provide procedures for the integration of the electronic systems of contributing employers for purposes of compliance, and for the manner and form of registering employers and members and of filing monthly returns. Where an employer system is integrated with the Authority, the interface, data format and onboarding procedure are governed by those regulations and their versions.
evidence: Regulations or statutory instrument made under s.66(2)(m) and any implementing guideline
Interface or integration specification (data fields, formats, frequency, authentication) with version number
List of employers integrated with the Authority's systems and onboarding dates
Interface test or certification records for an employer system
Exception and rejection logs for electronically submitted returns or registrations
Data-sharing or integration agreement with an employer

controls.name: Corrections: refunds of contributions paid in error and repayment of benefits improperly received
controls.statement: Where the Director-General is satisfied that an amount was paid as a contribution in error, it is refunded to the employer or applied to the employer's liability, and the Authority notifies the employer and member in the prescribed manner. A person who receives a benefit not due must inform the Authority and repay; where the Authority becomes aware of an improper payment it notifies the person in writing and may recover by deduction from a benefit. Advance payments are recovered in the prescribed manner.
evidence: Refund or offset decisions by the Director-General with the amount and basis
Notifications to employer and member of the refund or offset
Adjusted member contribution history showing the correction
Improper-payment notices to beneficiaries and repayment or deduction records
Advance payment recovery schedule and recoveries made
Audit trail linking each correction to the original transaction
sop: Director-General refunds an amount paid in error to the contributing employer or applies it to a liability owed by the employer.
Authority notifies the contributing employer and the member in the prescribed manner when it exercises the refund or offset power.
Authority notifies in writing a person to whom a benefit was improperly made, and may recover it by deducting from a benefit to which the member is entitled.

controls.name: Benefit claim, consent and calculation inputs
controls.statement: A person submits a benefit claim to the Director-General in the prescribed manner and form, and the Director-General determines it as prescribed. Entitlement turns on stored data: monthly contribution counts (180 for retirement and early retirement pension; 60 with age or contribution conditions for pre-retirement lump sum), age, and average monthly earnings computed at claim time as aggregate pensionable earnings divided by months of pensionable employment. Access to a pre-retirement lump sum requires the member's written consent and acknowledges a reduction in later benefits. Advance payment applications are approved or rejected within thirty days with written reasons for rejection.
evidence: Benefit claim forms in the prescribed manner and form
Claim determination records with the contribution count and average monthly earnings used
Member contribution statement supporting the claim
Written consent to access pre-retirement lump sum benefit (s.34(1))
Advance payment application, decision date and rejection reasons (s.50)
Calculation worksheet or system output showing application of the prescribed formula and minimum pension
Prescribed benefit rates and formulae in force (statutory instrument) with version
sop: Claimant submits a claim to the Director-General in the prescribed manner and form.
Director-General determines the claim as prescribed.
For an advance payment, applicant applies to the Authority in the prescribed manner and form; Authority approves or rejects within 30 days and informs a rejected applicant in writing with reasons.

controls.name: Invalidity benefit and ad hoc medical board health data
controls.statement: The Authority constitutes an ad hoc medical board to examine claimants or beneficiaries. A member applies to the Director-General for invalidity benefit in the prescribed manner and form; the Director-General refers the member to the board to determine whether the invalidity is permanent. Invalidity pension and invalidity lump sum are payable only where an ad hoc medical board has certified the member as invalid; the Director-General may refer a pensioner for re-examination at any time, and the pension ceases if the beneficiary fails to comply or the board finds recovery. The same board certifies a child as permanently invalid for lifetime survivor's pension. Medical examination and certification data are health data; board proceedings and reports are prescribed by regulation.
evidence: Invalidity benefit application in the prescribed form
Director-General referral to the ad hoc medical board
Ad hoc medical board constitution record and member list
Medical board certificate or report for each claimant, and re-examination reports
Prescribed medical board proceedings and report format (s.37(3), s.66(2)(e))
Access controls and classification of medical records held with the claim file
Cessation decisions after re-examination or non-compliance
Certification of permanently invalid child beneficiaries (s.44(c)(iii))
sop: Member applies to the Director-General for an invalidity benefit in the prescribed manner and form.
Director-General refers the member to an ad hoc medical board for medical examination to determine whether the invalidity is permanent.
Member qualifies only if certified invalid by the ad hoc medical board, is under pensionable age and meets the contribution conditions.

Director-General may at any time refer an invalidity pensioner to an ad hoc medical board for re-examination; the pension ceases if the beneficiary fails to comply or the board finds the beneficiary no longer permanently invalid.

controls.name: Survivor, eligible child and next-of-kin beneficiary data
controls.clause: s.2 (eligible child, parental responsibility), s.43, s.44, s.45, s.46, s.47(3)
controls.statement: Survivor's pension is payable to a surviving spouse and eligible child (biological child or child adopted under the Children's Code Act, 2022), with duration depending on stored attributes: spouse age (45), parental responsibility for a child under fifteen, remarriage, a child's age (18, or 25 in school or training) and certified permanent invalidity. A funeral grant is paid to next of kin, who include a person nominated by the member. Survivor entitlements are computed under this Act despite estate laws. Beneficiary records therefore hold dates of birth, relationship, school or training status and nomination data, including data about children.
evidence: Beneficiary registration or claim records identifying spouse, eligible children and relationship evidence
Dates of birth and age-based cessation triggers for each beneficiary
Evidence of school education or training enrolment for child beneficiaries aged 18 to 25
Remarriage and death notifications and the resulting cessation records
Member nomination of next of kin for funeral grant
Adoption evidence for adopted eligible children
Controls restricting access to children's data

controls.name: Statutory confidentiality and authorised disclosure
controls.statement: A person must not publish or disclose the contents of any document, communication or information that came to the person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act, other than in the course of those duties, without the written consent of (or on behalf of) the Director-General or as otherwise permitted by written law. Onward publication of unlawfully disclosed information is also an offence. Every dataset holding member, employer, claim or medical information is therefore subject to the Director-General's disclosure authority.
evidence: Confidentiality policy or code and staff acknowledgements
Register of Director-General written consents to disclose, with recipient, purpose and date
Delegation instrument if consent is given on behalf of the Director-General
Data-sharing agreements or memoranda with other agencies stating the written-law basis
Access control matrix and access logs for member and employer data
Incident log of unauthorised disclosures and responses
sop: Disclosure to a person other than in the course of duties requires the written consent of, or on behalf of, the Director-General, or must be otherwise permitted by written law.

controls.name: Accuracy of statements to the Authority and false-statement offence
controls.statement: It is an offence knowingly to make or cause to be made to the Authority a false statement or report in any material particular, to refuse without lawful excuse to provide information or produce a document, to deduct more than is due from wages, or knowingly or negligently to give an inspector false or misleading information. A convicted person may be ordered to pay contributions and penalty (credited to member accounts), produce documents or furnish information. Principal officers of a body corporate share liability. Data submitted by members and employers is therefore a declared-accurate record for which a named person is accountable.
evidence: Declaration or certification wording on registration forms and monthly returns
Named accountable officer for each employer submission
Data quality or validation rules applied on intake and exception reports
Referral records of suspected false statements and outcomes
Court orders under s.64(3) and the resulting member-account credits
Data-correction requests and amendment audit trail

controls.name: National average earnings and pension indexation reference data
controls.clause: s.48, s.30(2), s.39(4), s.2 (national average earnings, Zambia Statistics Agency)
controls.statement: Pensions are adjusted annually by an index based on national average earnings as prescribed by the Minister. The Authority determines national average earnings each year by applying statistics and data compiled by the Zambia Statistics Agency. The same figure sets minimum retirement pension and minimum invalidity pension at twenty-five per cent of national average earnings. The annual figure is controlled reference data sourced from an external statistical authority.
evidence: Annual national average earnings determination with the Zambia Statistics Agency data source and extraction date
Index prescribed by the Minister for pension adjustment
Reference table of national average earnings by year, versioned
Calculation of minimum retirement and invalidity pension from the figure
Data-sharing or supply arrangement with the Zambia Statistics Agency
Annual pension adjustment run record
sop: Authority determines the national average earnings annually by applying statistics and data compiled by the Zambia Statistics Agency.

controls.name: Inspectorate: appointment and access to records
controls.statement: The Authority appoints suitably qualified inspectors, each issued an identification card that is prima facie evidence of appointment and must be shown on request. Inspectors may at any reasonable time, without prior notice, access, inspect, examine and audit documents, books and records, take copies, require explanations of entries and remove documents that may be evidence, issuing a receipt and returning them as soon as practicable; owners and occupiers must produce records. Inspectors furnish the Authority a written report. Delaying, obstructing, refusing assistance, impersonating an inspector or giving false information is an offence.
evidence: Inspector appointment records and identification card register
Inspection plan and inspection reports furnished to the Authority
Receipts issued for documents or records removed and records of their return
Records of copies or extracts taken during inspections
Offence referrals for obstruction or false information
Handling rules for inspected employer data held by the Authority
sop: Authority issues each inspector an identification card; the inspector shows it to any person who requests it or is investigated.
Inspector who removes a document or record issues a receipt to the owner or person in control and returns it as soon as practicable after achieving the purpose.
Inspector furnishes the Authority with a written report and other information relating to an inspection.

policies.title: Zambia Revenue Authority Act
principles: Blanket statutory secrecy: every document, communication or information that comes to a person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act is confidential unless the Authority consents in writing (s.21(1)).
Secrecy is backed by criminal sanction, both for the original discloser and for onward publishers (s.21(2)-(3)).
Information may flow freely inside the ZRA family (Departments, Governing Board, Authority) but the Act creates no external sharing gateway (s.21(4)).
Proper books of account and records must be kept and audited annually by independent auditors (s.24).
Accountability to the Minister and Parliament through an annual report with audited statements, laid before the National Assembly (s.25).
Revenue collected is credited to the Treasury as soon as reasonably practicable (s.11(1)(b)).

Authority is exercised through documented delegation from the Board to the Commissioner-General, members and committees, and from the Commissioner-General to named officers (ss.8, 11(3), 12(5), 19(2), 20(4)).
Decisions and conflicts of interest are minuted (ss.15(9), 17(2)).
management_intent: Protect taxpayer and revenue information: nothing learned in the course of ZRA duties leaves the Authority without written consent, and breach is a criminal offence.
Keep the internal flow of tax and customs information between the Departments, the Governing Board and the Authority unobstructed so revenue can be assessed and collected.
Ensure the Authority keeps proper accounts, has them independently audited every year, and reports to the Minister and Parliament within six months of year end.
Ensure revenue collected for Government reaches the Treasury promptly and is accounted for.

Keep decision rights traceable: the Board may delegate, and the Commissioner-General may delegate to the Commissioners and Controller, so each exercise of power can be tied to an instrument of delegation.

controls.name: Statutory tax-secrecy duty over all duty-acquired information
controls.statement: No person may, without the written consent given by or on behalf of the Authority, publish or disclose to any person, other than in the course of his duties, the contents of any document, communication or information whatsoever which relates to and has come to his knowledge in the course of his duties under the Act. The wording is a blanket rule with no tiering by data type, so every record handled under the Act is treated as statutory-confidential. This is the confidentiality floor for all ZRA datasets.
evidence: Information classification or handling policy showing that all taxpayer and revenue records default to the statutory-confidential tier
Staff confidentiality undertakings or declarations of secrecy signed at appointment
Access-control matrix for tax, customs and excise systems showing duty-based access only
Disclosure log or register of disclosures made outside the course of duties
Security awareness or induction training records that cite section 21

controls.name: Written consent given by or on behalf of the Authority as the only disclosure gateway
controls.statement: Disclosure outside the course of duties is lawful only with the consent in writing given by or on behalf of the Authority. The consent must be written and must come from the Authority or a person acting on its behalf, so a delegated authority to consent must exist and be traceable. The Act does not describe any taxpayer consent route, so consent here is institutional consent, not data-subject consent.
evidence: Register of written consents to disclose, with date, requester, recipient, content disclosed and approver
