Instrument of delegation naming who may give consent on behalf of the Authority
Sample of consent letters or approvals linked to the disclosed record sets
Data-sharing requests refused or escalated, with reasons

controls.name: Criminal penalties for disclosure and onward publication
controls.statement: A person who knowingly contravenes s.21(1) commits an offence, liable to a fine not exceeding ten thousand penalty units, imprisonment not exceeding five years, or both. A person who holds information he knows was disclosed in breach and unlawfully publishes or communicates it to another is also guilty, liable to a fine not exceeding two thousand penalty units, imprisonment not exceeding three years, or both. Recipients of leaked tax information are therefore also covered, which makes onward-transfer clauses in any data-sharing arrangement relevant.
evidence: Staff and contractor notices or acknowledgements that state the section 21 penalties
Breach and incident register for suspected unauthorised disclosure, with referral outcomes
Disciplinary or prosecution referral records for section 21 contraventions
Contract clauses binding third-party processors or consultants to section 21

controls.name: Intra-ZRA information passing is exempt from secrecy; no external gateway
controls.statement: Nothing in s.21, in s.175 of the Customs and Excise Act (Cap. 322) or in s.8 of the Income Tax Act (Cap. 323) prevents the passing of information between the Departments, between the Departments and the Governing Board, or between the Departments and the Authority. The sharing exemption is limited to these internal parties, so sharing with any other agency, ministry or third party still needs the written consent under s.21(1). Any cross-entity data sharing with ZRA data must be traced to a basis outside this subsection.
evidence: Internal data-sharing register or matrix between Department of Taxes, Department of Customs and Excise, the Board and the Authority
Data-sharing agreements or MoUs with external agencies, each citing its legal basis other than s.21(4)
System integration inventory showing which ZRA datasets are exposed to external parties
Legal opinion or compliance review on external sharing

controls.name: Proper books of account and other accounting records
controls.statement: The Governing Board shall cause to be kept proper books of account and other records relating to the accounts of the Authority. The Act states no retention period, format or standard for these records, so retention and the accounting framework must be set by internal policy or another law.
evidence: General ledger, chart of accounts and sub-ledgers of the Authority
Records retention schedule showing the basis and period for accounting records (the Act itself gives none)
Board resolution or policy assigning responsibility for the books of account
Financial reporting framework or accounting policies document

controls.name: Annual independent audit of the Authority's accounts
controls.statement: The accounts of the Authority shall be audited annually by independent auditors appointed by the Authority, and the auditors' fees shall be paid by the Authority. The Act does not name the auditing standard to be applied.
evidence: Auditor appointment letter or engagement letter for each financial year
Signed audit opinion and audited financial statements
Management letter and management responses to audit findings
Evidence of auditor independence declaration

controls.name: Annual report with audited statements to the Minister and the National Assembly
controls.statement: The financial year is the twelve months ending 31 December (s.23). As soon as practicable, and not later than six months after the year end, the Governing Board shall submit to the Minister a report on its activities for the year. The report shall include information on the financial affairs of the Authority, with an audited balance sheet, an audited statement of income and expenditure and any other information the Minister requires appended. The Minister shall lay the report before the National Assembly not later than seven days after its first sitting next after receipt, and publish it as soon as reasonably practicable thereafter.
evidence: Annual report as submitted to the Minister, with date of submission
Appended audited balance sheet and audited statement of income and expenditure
Correspondence showing any additional information requested by the Minister
Proof of tabling in the National Assembly and of publication
Annual reporting calendar showing the six-month deadline from 31 December
sop: Board submits the annual report to the Minister not later than six months after the financial year ends.
Report includes financial affairs, with the audited balance sheet and audited statement of income and expenditure appended, plus any other information the Minister requires.
Minister lays the report before the National Assembly not later than seven days after the first sitting after receipt.
Minister publishes the report as soon as reasonably practicable after laying it.

controls.name: Crediting of collected revenue to the Treasury
controls.statement: The Governing Board assesses, charges, levies and collects all revenue due to Government under the laws the Minister specifies by statutory instrument, and shall ensure that all revenue collected is, as soon as reasonably practicable, credited to the Treasury. Sections 24 and 25 (books, audit and reports) apply to this function with necessary modifications. The Act gives no number of days for crediting, so the timeliness standard is 'as soon as reasonably practicable'.
evidence: Revenue collection ledger and Treasury remittance or crediting records
Reconciliation of collections to Treasury receipts, with dates
Statutory instrument(s) specifying the revenue laws administered
Internal service-level or policy defining 'as soon as reasonably practicable' for crediting

controls.name: Delegation of Board and Commissioner-General powers
controls.statement: The Governing Board may delegate to the Commissioner, to any member or to a committee the power to carry out Board functions (s.11(3)), and may delegate to the Commissioner-General, a member or a committee the power to carry out Authority functions (s.12(5)). The Commissioner-General may delegate his duties to the Commissioner of Taxes, the Commissioner of Sales Tax and the Controller of Customs and Excise as appropriate to each officer (s.8 proviso). He may, with Board approval, establish organisational structures (s.19(2)), and staff exercise functions conferred by the specified laws or delegated by the Commissioner-General (s.20(4)). Delegation therefore determines who may validly act, including who may give disclosure consent under s.21(1).
evidence: Delegation register or instruments from the Board to the Commissioner-General, members and committees
Delegations from the Commissioner-General to the Commissioner of Taxes, Commissioner of Sales Tax and Controller of Customs and Excise
Board-approved organisational structure
Board resolutions or minutes recording delegations
Role-to-system-access mapping tied to delegated authority

controls.name: Minutes of Board and committee meetings and recorded disclosures of interest
controls.statement: The Governing Board shall cause minutes to be kept of every meeting of the Authority and of every committee established by it (s.15(9)). A member or attendee with a direct or indirect private interest, or whose spouse has one, in a matter under consideration shall disclose it as soon as practicable and not take part in the discussion or vote unless the Authority directs otherwise; the disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes (s.17). The minutes are the primary evidence of delegations, disclosure consents and decisions.
evidence: Signed minutes of Board and committee meetings
Register of members' declared interests and recusals
Minute extracts showing disclosures of interest recorded
Minute book retention and custody arrangements
sop: Person present at a meeting with a private interest in a matter discloses it as soon as practicable after the meeting begins.
The disclosure is recorded in the minutes of that meeting.
The person does not take part in the consideration, discussion or vote on the matter unless the Authority directs otherwise.

policies.title: National Health Insurance Act
principles: Every citizen or established resident above eighteen is registered as a member in the prescribed manner and form and issued a membership card carrying a health insurance number assigned by the Authority (ss.13(1), 19, 2).
Employers register an employee with the Authority within thirty days of the commencement of the contract of employment (s.13(3)).

The Authority establishes and maintains registers of members, of employers, pension schemes and self-employed persons, and of accredited health care providers, and each accredited provider maintains a register of members enrolled with it (s.52).
Accredited health care providers implement a standardised and confidential patient record system to maintain accurate patient records (s.34(1)).

A person who receives information under s.34 in the course of functions under the Act keeps it confidential and may not disclose or use it except as authorised by law (s.34(3)); disclosure of Authority information to an unauthorised person needs the Board's written consent (Schedule para 6).
Accredited providers report prescribed statistical, service, staffing, equipment, medicine-stock and medical information, and the Authority may request medical records (s.32).
Providers submit claims in the prescribed manner and form and may not bill a member directly for insured services (s.33).
The Authority sets a uniform national standard schedule of fees and charges annually and a prescription drug formulary system (ss.17, 18).
The Authority and providers maintain monitoring mechanisms against over-utilisation, under-utilisation, irrational prescribing, inappropriate referral and fraud (s.39(2)).
A provider that is suspended, revoked or dispenses with accreditation transfers members' medical records within thirty days of the Authority's direction (ss.29(3), 30(7)).
Inspectors may inspect patient records and billing but must pay particular regard to ethical procedures, privacy and confidentiality (s.40(4)).
management_intent: Provide universal access to quality insured health care services through a sound financing arrangement for the national health system (long title, s.12(2)).
Establish the Authority to implement and manage the Scheme and the Fund, register and issue cards to members, accredit providers and process claims (s.5).
Keep a comprehensive, current register of members, employers and accredited providers (ss.5(t), 52).
Ensure accredited providers deliver efficient, quality services under contract, with monitoring and inspection (ss.5(m)-(o), 37-40).
Protect the confidentiality of patient information while allowing the Authority to receive the data it needs to pay claims and monitor utilisation (ss.32, 34, 40(4)).
Provide complaints and appeals routes to the Health Complaints Committee, the Board and the High Court (ss.49-50).
Provide prudent control of the Fund, annual audit and annual reporting (ss.41-44, 47-48).

controls.name: Member registration, membership card and health insurance number
controls.statement: A citizen or established resident above eighteen years is registered as a member in the prescribed manner and form, as is a self-employed citizen or established resident. On registration the Authority issues a membership card stating the health insurance number assigned to the member, replaces a lost, defaced or destroyed card on payment of a prescribed fee, and accompanies issue with information on benefits, rights and privileges and the list of accredited providers. Members and family members (registered child, spouse, dependant) access the benefit package as prescribed. The health insurance number is the member's identifier across enrolment, claims and provider records.
evidence: Member registration application in the prescribed form
Member register extract showing health insurance number, status and registration date
Uniqueness or duplicate-detection report on health insurance numbers
Membership card issue and replacement log, including fee paid
Information pack issued with the card (benefits, rights, accredited provider list)
Family member register linked to each member (registered child, spouse, dependant)
Regulation setting registration procedure and card replacement (s.57(2)(a),(d))
sop: Citizen or established resident above eighteen applies for registration as a member in the prescribed manner and form.
Authority registers the person as a member and issues a membership card on registration.
Authority replaces a lost, defaced or destroyed membership card on payment of a prescribed fee.
Issue of the membership card is accompanied by adequate information on benefits, rights and privileges, including the list of accredited health care providers.

controls.name: Employer registration of employees (30 days) and retiree registration by pension scheme managers
controls.statement: An employer registers an employee with the Authority within thirty days of the commencement of the contract of employment, in the prescribed manner and form, and pays the employer's and employee's contributions at the end of each month. The manager of a pension scheme ensures that a retiree is registered by the Authority and pays the retiree's contribution as prescribed. Failure to register, or to ensure registration of another person, within the period is an offence. The pension-scheme feed is a cross-entity data dependency: retirees paid by pension schemes must appear on the Authority's register.
evidence: Employer registration submissions for employees with contract start date and lodged date
Log of registrations against the 30-day limit by employer
Employer register extract (s.52(1)(b)) and contribution payment ledger by month-end
Pension scheme manager retiree registration submissions and payment of retiree contributions
List of pension schemes registered and the retiree data feed with its frequency and format
Enforcement records for late or missing registration
sop: Employer registers an employee with the Authority within thirty days of the commencement date of the contract of employment, in the prescribed manner and form.
Employer pays contributions to the Scheme at the end of each month.
Manager of a pension scheme ensures that a retiree is registered by the Authority.

controls.name: Membership status changes, suspension and cessation
controls.statement: A member provides updated information within a month of an employment status shift, family membership change (death, birth, arrival or departure of a family member), change in financial status, geographic relocation or other change affecting membership; death information is provided as soon as practicable and not later than four months. Membership ceases on death and family members keep benefits for four months. The Authority suspends a member who presents a false claim, materially misrepresents or fails to disclose required factual information, and may suspend benefits where required contributions are unpaid. Exemption categories (disabled person unable to work, person over 65, person classified poor and vulnerable) and foreigners' insurance are driven by recorded attributes.
evidence: Member change-of-status notices with change date and lodged date (one-month and four-month limits)
Member register history showing status transitions (active, suspended, exempt, deceased)
Suspension decisions with reason (non-payment, false claim, misrepresentation) and period
Four-month family-continuation records after a member's death
Exemption determinations, including classification by the ministry responsible for social welfare
Foreigner health insurance records on arrival (s.14)
sop: Member provides updated information to the Authority within a month after a change in employment status, family membership, financial status, location or other change affecting membership.
Updated information in case of death is provided as soon as practicable but not later than four months.
Authority suspends a member who presents a false claim, makes material misrepresentation or fails to disclose required factual information.

controls.name: Statutory registers (four registers)
controls.statement: The Authority establishes and maintains, in the prescribed manner and form, a register of (a) members, (b) employers, pension schemes and self-employed citizens or established residents, and (c) accredited health care providers. Each accredited health care provider also establishes and maintains a register of members enrolled with that provider. These four registers are the statutory masters for registration, enrolment and accreditation; accredited providers are also published annually in the Gazette and a daily newspaper.
evidence: Register of members extract and its data dictionary
Register of employers, pension schemes and self-employed citizens or established residents extract
Register of accredited health care providers extract including accreditation status and dates
Provider-level register of enrolled members for a sample of accredited providers
Prescribed manner and form of the registers (regulations)
Owner or custodian of each register and change audit trail
Annual Gazette and newspaper publication of accredited providers (s.31)
sop: Authority establishes and maintains a register, in the prescribed manner and form, of members; of employers, pension schemes and self-employed citizens or established residents; and of accredited health care providers.
Each accredited health care provider establishes and maintains a register of members enrolled with that provider.
Authority publishes annually in the Gazette and a daily newspaper of general circulation the names of accredited health care providers.

controls.name: Provider accreditation: application, 90-day decision, suspension and revocation
controls.statement: A health care provider may not provide insured services without accreditation, and the Authority does not pay for services of an unaccredited provider except in an emergency where an accredited provider is not accessible. A provider applies in the prescribed manner and form on payment of a prescribed fee; the Authority assesses the application and within ninety days grants or rejects it, giving reasons for rejection; if no decision is communicated in ninety days accreditation is considered granted. Suspension or revocation requires prior notice with reasons and an opportunity to show cause or remedy, and is published in a daily newspaper. The accreditation register must therefore carry application, decision and status dates.
evidence: Accreditation applications in the prescribed form with fee payment
Assessment record for each application against the prescribed requirements
Decision log with receipt and decision dates against the 90-day limit, and deemed-grant cases
Rejection letters with reasons
Show-cause notices, remedial measures and final suspension or revocation decisions
Newspaper publication of suspension or revocation
Emergency payments to non-accredited providers (s.26(4)) with justification
sop: Health care provider applies to the Authority for accreditation in the prescribed manner and form on payment of a prescribed fee.
Authority assesses the application and, within ninety days of receipt, grants accreditation or rejects the application.
Authority informs the applicant of the reasons where it rejects an application.
Before suspending or revoking accreditation, Authority notifies the provider with reasons and requires it to show cause or remedy the default.
Authority publishes a suspension or revocation in a daily newspaper of general circulation.

controls.name: Provider exit: surrender of accreditation and transfer of members' medical records
controls.statement: An accredited provider that is wound up or decides to dispense with accreditation notifies the Authority in writing within sixty days and surrenders the accreditation. A provider that dispenses with accreditation transfers the medical records of members in its possession to the Authority within thirty days of the Authority's direction; a provider whose accreditation is suspended or revoked transfers them within thirty days of direction to an accredited provider the Authority directs. Before directing a transfer the Authority consults the affected members on the alternative providers they wish to be enrolled with. Medical records leaving one controller for another is a regulated transfer of health data.
evidence: Provider notification of winding up or decision to dispense with accreditation, with date
Authority cancellation of surrendered accreditation and conditions imposed
Authority direction to transfer medical records, with date and destination
Transfer manifest of member records and receipt from the Authority or receiving provider (30-day measure)
Records of consultation with affected members on alternative providers
Controls applied to transferred medical records (secure transfer, inventory, access)
Updated enrolment register entries after transfer
sop: Accredited provider that is wound up or decides to dispense with accreditation notifies the Authority in writing within sixty days and surrenders the accreditation.
Authority consults affected members on the alternative accredited providers they wish to be enrolled with before directing a transfer of medical records.
Provider transfers members' medical records to the Authority, or to an accredited provider the Authority directs, within thirty days of the Authority's direction.

controls.name: Standardised confidential patient record system
controls.statement: An accredited provider implements a standardised and confidential patient record system to maintain accurate patient records and simplify the provider payment system, as prescribed by the Minister in consultation with the Authority. The provider appoints persons on its establishment responsible for managing the patient record system and for accurate and expedient claim submission. Patient records contain health information about members and are the source for claims, utilisation monitoring and inspection. Failure to implement the prescribed provider payment system is an offence (s.34(4)-(5)).
evidence: Prescribed standard for the patient record system (schema, data elements, version)
Provider's patient record system description or data dictionary
Evidence of provider conformance (assessment or inspection report)
Appointment letters or job descriptions for the person responsible for the patient record system and claims accuracy
Access controls and audit logs for patient records
Evidence of the prescribed provider payment system in operation
sop: Accredited provider implements a standardised and confidential patient record system to maintain accurate patient records and simplify the provider payment system as prescribed by the Minister in consultation with the Authority.
Accredited provider appoints persons whose responsibility is to manage the patient record system and ensure accurate and expedient submission of claims in accordance with prescribed procedures.

controls.name: Confidentiality and purpose limitation of patient and member information
controls.statement: A member must on request submit information required for the better carrying out of the Act to the Authority, an employer, an accredited provider or another authorised person. A person who receives information under s.34 in the course of functions under the Act keeps it confidential and does not disclose or make use of it except as authorised by law, which limits both disclosure and secondary use. Separately, a person must not publish or disclose Authority information to an unauthorised person without the Board's written consent, and onward publication is an offence. Inspectors reviewing patient records must pay particular regard to ethical procedures, privacy and confidentiality.
evidence: Confidentiality policy covering patient and member information
Staff and provider acknowledgements of the s.34(3) duty
Register of Board written consents to disclose, with recipient, purpose and date
Statement of authorised purposes for use of member and patient data
Data-sharing agreements with providers, employers, pension schemes and other agencies stating the legal basis
Access control matrix and access logs for medical and claims data
Incident log for unauthorised disclosure or secondary use
sop: Member submits to the Authority, an employer, an accredited provider or any other authorised person, on request, information required for the better carrying out of the Act.
A person who receives information under s.34 in the course of functions under the Act keeps it confidential and does not disclose or make use of it except as authorised by law.
Disclosure to an unauthorised person, other than in the course of duties, requires the written consent of the Board.

controls.name: Provider reporting of statistical and medical data to the Authority
controls.statement: The Minister prescribes, in consultation with stakeholders, the reporting requirements and reporting periods for accredited providers covering: statistical data on enrolled members; insured services provided and the conditions under which they were provided; number and skills of staff; type and state of equipment and infrastructure; inventory and stock levels of medicines; relationships with other accredited providers; and other administrative, financial or medical information. The Authority may request information and documents, including medical records and explanations, and the provider must disclose or submit them. Failure to comply is an offence. This is the structured data flow from providers to the Authority.
evidence: Prescribed reporting requirements and periods (regulation or guideline) with version
Reporting template or data schema for provider returns
Log of provider returns received against reporting periods
Authority requests for information or medical records and provider responses
Non-compliance records and follow-up actions
Data quality checks applied on receipt and rejected submission records

controls.name: Claims submission in the prescribed form, processing and no direct billing
controls.clause: s.33(1)-(3), s.38(2)(c), s.5(g), s.2 (billing, health care expense)
controls.statement: An accredited provider that provides a health care service to a member submits a claim in the prescribed manner and form. The Authority processes claims within the period it agrees with the provider. A provider that receives payment from the Fund does not bill a member directly for an insured service. Claims link a member's health insurance number to diagnosis, treatment and fee data and are the basis of provider payment, so claim records carry health data and must tie to the patient record and the fee schedule.
evidence: Prescribed claim form or electronic claim layout with data dictionary
Claims register showing submission date, processing date and payment date against the agreed period
Provider-Authority agreement on claim processing period
Claim adjudication rules applied and rejection or query records
Reconciliation of claims paid to Fund disbursements and to provider patient records
Member complaints or checks showing no direct billing for insured services
sop: Accredited provider that provides a health care service to a member submits a claim in the prescribed manner and form.
Authority processes a claim for payment within the period agreed with the accredited provider.
Accredited provider that receives payment from the Fund does not bill a member directly for any insured service.

controls.name: Standard fee schedule, negotiated fees and drug formulary reference data
controls.statement: Each year the Authority establishes and updates a uniform national standard schedule of fees and charges for items and services provided by accredited providers. It negotiates fair and optimal fee schedules with providers, taking into account the need for a uniform national standard, compensation reflecting expertise regardless of region, a prescription drug formulary system that encourages best-practice prescribing and discourages ineffective, dangerous or excessively costly medication, and use of generics where available. Changes to benefit packages that are not reflected in the latest summary are notified to members at least sixty days before taking effect. The schedule and formulary are controlled reference data used to validate claims.
evidence: Current and prior annual standard fee schedules with effective dates and version
Negotiated fee schedules agreed with providers
Prescription drug formulary and generics list, with version and effective date
Annual update record showing the review date
Code lists for items and services used in claims
Notice to members of material benefit package modifications issued at least 60 days before effect
Claim validation rules that reference the schedule and formulary
sop: Authority establishes and updates each year a uniform national standard schedule of the fees and charges for items and services provided by accredited health care providers.
Authority negotiates with accredited providers a schedule of fees and charges for insured health care services that are fair and optimal.
Authority gives members notice of a material modification in any benefit package or coverage not later than sixty days before it comes into operation.

controls.name: Provider contracts and fraud and over-utilisation monitoring
controls.statement: The Authority contracts with each accredited provider for provision of insured services. The Authority and the provider ensure monitoring mechanisms are in place to safeguard against over-utilisation, under-utilisation, unnecessary diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, irrational prescribing, inappropriate referral, continuation of unnecessary services, fraud and other circumstances. Making a claim for services not rendered, obtaining services by false statement or document, and making false statements in registration are offences; the Authority may impose a fine in lieu of prosecution. Monitoring depends on linked claim, patient and prescribing data.
evidence: Contract with each accredited provider, including data and reporting clauses
Utilisation monitoring rules, indicators and thresholds
Monitoring reports on over-utilisation, under-utilisation, prescribing and referral patterns
Fraud case register, investigations and outcomes
Member suspensions for false claims (s.22(2)) and fine-in-lieu certificates (s.54)
Access controls on the analytical data sets used for monitoring
sop: Authority enters into a contract with each accredited health care provider for provision of insured health care services under the Scheme.

Authority and accredited provider ensure monitoring mechanisms are in place to safeguard against over-utilisation, under-utilisation, unnecessary procedures, irrational prescribing, inappropriate referral, fraud and other circumstances.

controls.name: Inspection of providers and access to patient records
controls.statement: The Authority, in consultation with the Council and the Registrar responsible for Pensions and Insurance, appoints inspectors. An inspector may at all reasonable times enter and inspect premises used by an accredited provider, presenting an identity card on entry, and may inspect a patient's records, treatment, diagnosis and fees sheet to ascertain the validity of billing, paying particular regard to ethical procedures, privacy and confidentiality. Delaying or obstructing an inspector, refusing assistance or giving false or misleading information is not permitted. The inspector submits a written report, and non-compliance leads to written notice to the provider that the Board may suspend or revoke accreditation.
evidence: Inspector appointment records and consultation with the Council and the Registrar
Inspector identity card register
Inspection plan and written inspection reports submitted to the Authority
Record of patient files inspected with the purpose (billing validation) and safeguards applied
Written notices of violation served on providers
Records of obstruction or false information referrals
sop: Authority appoints inspectors in consultation with the Council and the Registrar responsible for Pensions and Insurance.
Inspector presents the identity card to the person in charge on entering an accredited provider's premises.
Inspector submits to the Authority a written report relating to an inspection.
Authority serves the provider with a written notice specifying the violation where an inspection report indicates non-compliance.

controls.name: Contribution exemptions, vulnerable-person classification and disability data
controls.statement: Persons who may be exempted from contributions include a mentally or physically disabled person who is unable to work, an elderly person above sixty-five, a person classified as poor and vulnerable by the ministry responsible for social welfare, and others prescribed by the Minister. The Minister may prescribe conditions under which non-eligible persons access insured services, extend categories of individuals to whom the Act applies, and prescribe different contribution rates for different benefit packages. Exemption status therefore relies on disability and vulnerability attributes supplied by, or classified by, other agencies.
evidence: Exemption determinations and the evidence used for each category
Classification list or certificates supplied by the ministry responsible for social welfare
Disability evidence held for exempt members and access controls on it
Prescribed contribution rates by benefit package and the exemption categories in force
Data-sharing arrangement with the ministry responsible for social welfare
Periodic review of exempt members' eligibility

controls.name: Complaints and appeals records
controls.statement: The Health Complaints Committee of the Board hears and resolves complaints submitted by members, accredited providers and health professionals, and hears and determines matters relating to accredited providers. The Authority develops an awareness process so that members and providers know their right to lodge complaints where a complaint is not settled internally. A person aggrieved by a Committee decision may within thirty days appeal to the Board, and a person aggrieved by a Board decision may appeal to the High Court. Complaint files can contain member and patient health information and the decisions affect accreditation and member standing.
evidence: Complaints register with received date, parties, subject and outcome
Committee decisions and reasons, and Board appeal decisions with dates
Appeal lodged date against the 30-day limit
Complaint awareness materials for members and providers
Access controls for complaint files that hold patient information
Link between complaint outcomes and changes to member or provider register status
sop: Health Complaints Committee hears and resolves complaints submitted to the Authority by members, accredited health care providers and members of the health profession.
A person aggrieved with a decision of the Committee appeals to the Board within thirty days of receiving the decision.
A person aggrieved by a decision of the Board may appeal to the High Court.

policies.title: Public Service Pensions Act
principles: Every member of the Public Service Pension Scheme and the Occupational Pension Scheme is registered by the Public Service Pensions Fund and issued a unique social security number (ss.11(3), 15(3)).
The relevant authority submits prescribed member particulars within thirty days of employing the member, and the Fund registers the member within thirty days of receipt (ss.11(1)-(2), 15(1)-(2)).
The Fund keeps and maintains a register of members in the prescribed manner and form (s.70).

Mandatory contributions and monthly returns are due on or before the tenth day of the month following the contribution month; late payment attracts a penalty at eight percent above the Bank of Zambia policy rate (ss.17(5),(7), 21).
The relevant authority notifies the Fund within thirty days of termination, resignation, unpaid leave, suspension of pensionable emoluments, secondment or death (s.19).
A member or beneficiary in receipt of a pension must confirm that the member is alive, and payment may be suspended on failure (s.71).
Medical retirement and ill-health benefits rest on a medical board or registered medical doctor's recommendation and a medical report (ss.33, 34, 47).
Benefits for spouses, children and dependants depend on relationship status, age and number of beneficiaries, including polygamous marriages (ss.2, 37-40).
A false representation affecting benefit amount, commencement or termination, or the identity of the payee permits withholding, suspension, reduction or termination of benefits (s.65).
Information that comes to a person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act may be disclosed only with the Board's written consent or as permitted by written law (First Schedule para 8).
Regulations may provide for integration of contributing employers' electronic systems for compliance (s.77(2)(l)).
management_intent: Continue the membership, contribution and benefit structure as the Public Service Pension Scheme and establish the Occupational Pension Scheme (long title, ss.9, 13).
Collect contributions from members and relevant authorities and pay benefits on prescribed conditions (ss.4(d),(e), 17, Parts VII and VIII).
Ensure prudent controls over fiscal management, actuarial soundness, fairness of benefit distribution, investment and reporting for each scheme and fund (ss.9(2), 13(2), 55(2)).
Provide for actuarial valuation at intervals not exceeding three years and Board action on the actuary's recommendations (ss.60-62).
Protect members' benefits and accounts from attachment, assignment and bankruptcy (ss.66-67).
Allow portability of contributions and fund credit between schemes (ss.25, 50).
Enable guidelines and regulations on registration, returns, confirmation of life, register of members and employer system integration (ss.75, 77).

controls.name: Public Service Pension Scheme member registration and unique social security number
controls.clause: s.10, s.11, s.12, Second Schedule para 4
controls.statement: The relevant authority submits the prescribed particulars of a public service employee (aged sixteen or more and below pensionable age) to the Public Service Pensions Fund within thirty days after employment. The Fund registers the member within thirty days of receipt of the particulars and issues a unique social security number. Defence Force and national security services employees are admitted through the same registration route. Persons who were members of the existing Fund continue as members as if registered under this Act. Membership ceases on payment of all accrued benefits, transfer of contributions (non-contributing member) or death.
evidence: Prescribed member particulars submitted by the relevant authority, with date employed and date submitted
Registration log showing particulars received date and registration date (30-day measure)
Register entries showing the unique social security number and scheme (Public Service Pension Scheme)
Uniqueness or duplicate-detection report on social security numbers
Migration records carrying existing Fund members forward (Second Schedule para 4)
Cessation records (benefits paid, contributions transferred, death)
sop: Relevant authority submits the prescribed particulars of the member to the Public Service Pensions Fund within 30 days after employing the member.
Public Service Pensions Fund registers the member within 30 days of receiving the particulars.
Public Service Pensions Fund issues a unique social security number to the registered member.

controls.name: Occupational Pension Scheme member registration and scheme assignment
controls.statement: The relevant authority submits prescribed particulars of each employee in permanent and pensionable service, aged sixteen or more and below pensionable age, within thirty days of commencement of the Act or of employing the member. The Fund registers the employee within thirty days and issues a unique social security number. A member of one scheme is not eligible for the other, except that a non-contributing member of the Public Service Pension Scheme may join the Occupational Pension Scheme; the scheme assignment is therefore a controlled attribute of each member record. Membership ceases on payment of benefits, transfer to another scheme or death.
evidence: Particulars submitted for employees in permanent and pensionable service, with dates
Registration log showing receipt date and registration date
Member register showing scheme assignment (Public Service Pension Scheme or Occupational Pension Scheme) and basis
Exception report of any person recorded in both schemes
Regulations on registration conditions and procedures for the Occupational Pension Scheme (s.14(3))
Records of non-contributing members moving to the Occupational Pension Scheme
sop: Relevant authority submits prescribed particulars of an employee in permanent and pensionable service to the Public Service Pensions Fund within 30 days after commencement of the Act or after employing the member.
Public Service Pensions Fund registers the employee as a member within 30 days of receipt of the particulars.
Public Service Pensions Fund issues a unique social security number to the employee or member.

controls.name: Register of Members
controls.statement: The Public Service Pensions Fund keeps and maintains a register of members in a prescribed manner and form. The register is the statutory master record of membership across both schemes, carrying forward existing Fund members, their accrued benefits and the continued status of existing employers. Its manner and form are prescribed by regulation.
evidence: Register of Members extract with field list, scheme, unique social security number and status
Regulation prescribing the manner and form of the register (s.77(2)(f)(v))
Custodian or owner of the register and access control list
Change log and audit trail for additions, amendments and cessations
Reconciliation of register totals to contribution returns and pension payroll
Reconciliation of existing-Fund members, accrued benefits and employers carried forward (Second Schedule)
sop: Public Service Pensions Fund keeps and maintains a register of members in a prescribed manner and form.

controls.name: Notification of employment events by the relevant authority
controls.statement: The relevant authority notifies the Fund, in a prescribed manner and form and within thirty days, when an employee's contract is terminated, the employee resigns, is placed on unpaid leave, has pensionable emoluments suspended, is placed on secondment or dies. These events change contribution obligations, membership status and, on death, benefit eligibility, so each is a dated record that the Fund must be able to tie to the member and the contribution history.
evidence: Event notifications from relevant authorities with event date and lodged date
Log of notifications against the 30-day limit by relevant authority
Member status history (active, on leave, seconded, terminated, deceased) tied to notifications
Reconciliation of notified events to contribution stop and start dates
Prescribed notification form
sop: Relevant authority notifies the Public Service Pensions Fund in a prescribed manner and form within 30 days where an employee's contract is terminated, the employee resigns, is placed on unpaid leave, has pensionable emoluments suspended, is seconded or dies.

controls.name: Mandatory contributions, monthly returns and late-payment penalty
controls.statement: The relevant authority pays the mandatory contribution (its own and the member's) to the applicable scheme on or before the tenth day of each month following the contribution month, and submits a monthly return on or before the same day in a prescribed manner and form. The member's share is deducted from pensionable emoluments; the relevant authority's share is not deducted. Failure to pay attracts a penalty at eight percent above the Bank of Zambia monetary policy rate, which the Fund may waive on prescribed terms. The contribution rate is prescribed by the President on actuarial assessment. For the Occupational Pension Scheme the relevant authority's contribution vests in the member.
evidence: Monthly returns by relevant authority with submission date against the 10th-day deadline
Contribution receipts ledger by scheme, relevant authority and month
Late-payment and penalty computation records (policy rate plus eight percent)
Penalty waiver decisions and the terms under which they were granted
Prescribed contribution rates by scheme and the actuarial assessment behind them
Prescribed return template and data dictionary
Reconciliation of return totals to payroll and register of members
sop: Relevant authority pays the mandatory contributions on or before the tenth day of each month following the month to which they relate.
Relevant authority submits a monthly return to the Public Service Pensions Fund on or before the tenth day of each month following the contribution month, in a prescribed manner and form.
Member's contribution is deducted from pensionable emoluments; the relevant authority's contribution is not deducted.
Relevant authority that fails to pay pays a penalty on the unpaid amount at eight percent above the Bank of Zambia monetary policy rate; the Fund may waive the penalty on prescribed terms.

controls.name: Contribution eligibility, refunds of contributions paid in error and post-retirement contributions
controls.statement: A member must not contribute for service before age sixteen or after attaining retirement age (early 55, pensionable 60, late 65, with earlier ages for prescribed categories). A contribution received after the applicable retirement age is treated as received in error and refunded. Where a relevant authority or member pays in error, the Fund refunds the amount or applies it to a liability and notifies the payer in writing. Ages and retirement-age elections are therefore rule-driving attributes of the member record.
evidence: Member date of birth and retirement-age election records with relevant authority consent
Exception report of contributions received for members under 16 or past retirement age
Refund or offset decisions and written notices to the relevant authority or member
Adjusted contribution history showing the correction
Prescribed categories with earlier or later retirement dates (s.26(3)-(4))
sop: Public Service Pensions Fund refunds an amount paid as a contribution in error to the relevant authority or member, or applies it to any liability due from them.
Public Service Pensions Fund notifies the relevant authority or member, in writing, of the action taken.
A contribution received after a member has attained the applicable retirement age is treated as received in error and refunded under s.24.

controls.name: Elections and special contribution bases: voluntary, temporary employment, secondment and unpaid leave
controls.statement: Contribution treatment depends on recorded elections and absences: unpaid leave contributions at the member's election; secondment contributions by the receiving employer (or by member election for an exempted receiving employer) on the substantive pre-secondment pensionable emoluments; proportional reduction when salary is reduced; non-counting of unauthorised absence or elected absence over thirty days. A member may elect within six months of public service employment to pay contributions for prior temporary employment, notifying the Fund in writing, with payment due within thirty days of notification. Voluntary contributions in the Occupational Pension Scheme are deducted on the member's instruction. Each election is a consent-type record that alters pensionable service.
evidence: Member election notices (unpaid leave, secondment to exempted employer, temporary employment, voluntary contributions)
Relevant authority consent to pay contributions for temporary employment
Date of election against the six-month limit and date contributions became payable (30 days)
Secondment records showing receiving employer and substantive pensionable emoluments used
Authorised and unauthorised absence directions affecting pensionable service
Member instruction to deduct voluntary contributions
Board determination of intervals for voluntary contributions
sop: Member notifies the Public Service Pensions Fund in writing of an election to make contributions for temporary employment; the contributions become payable within 30 days of the notification.
Member elects within six months of being employed in the public service to pay contributions for the period of temporary employment, with the relevant authority's consent.
Member who elects voluntary contributions instructs the relevant authority to deduct them from monthly pensionable emoluments.

controls.name: Transfer and portability of contributions and fund credit between schemes
controls.statement: A non-contributing member with fewer than ten years of contributions may transfer contributions (with accrued interest) to the Occupational Pension Scheme or to another pension scheme, or elect not to transfer. On separation, an Occupational Pension Scheme member notifies the Fund, which transfers the fund credit to the new employer's scheme; a member joining from another scheme may transfer the fund credit in, credited to the member's account and deemed contributions. The manner and form of transfers are prescribed. Transfers move member and balance data across scheme and organisational boundaries.
evidence: Transfer election or notification by the member
Transfer instruction to or from the receiving or sending scheme with amount and date
Fund credit and accrued interest computation
Record crediting the member's Occupational Pension Scheme account
Statutory instrument prescribing manner and form of transfers (s.50(4), s.77(2)(f)(iii))
Data-sharing or transfer agreement with the receiving scheme
Members excluded from transfer by prescribed category (s.25(5))
sop: Occupational Pension Scheme member who separates from employment notifies the Public Service Pensions Fund, which transfers the member's fund credit to the new employer's scheme.
Public Service Pensions Fund credits the member's Occupational Pension Scheme account or transfers the contributions to another pension scheme where a member elects to transfer.

controls.name: Employer electronic-system integration, guidelines and regulations governing data exchange
controls.statement: Regulations may provide procedures for integration of the electronic systems of contributing employers for compliance, and for the manner and form of monthly returns, transfers, confirmation of life and the register of members. The Fund may issue guidelines, published in the Gazette and a daily newspaper or electronic media the Fund determines, which take effect on publication and bind all persons under the Act. Employer system interfaces and prescribed data formats are therefore governed by versioned regulations and guidelines.
evidence: Regulations or statutory instruments under s.77(2)(f) and (l)
Published guidelines with publication date and medium (Gazette, newspaper, electronic)
Interface or integration specification for employer systems with version number
List of relevant authorities integrated with the Fund and onboarding dates
Interface test records and rejection logs
Data-sharing arrangement with each integrated employer
sop: Public Service Pensions Fund publishes guidelines issued under the Act in a Gazette and a daily newspaper of general circulation or electronic media it determines; guidelines take effect on the date of publication.

controls.name: Confirmation of life and pension payment validity
controls.statement: A member or beneficiary in receipt of a pension must provide, in a prescribed manner and form, confirmation to the Fund that the member is alive. Where confirmation is not provided the Fund may suspend payment. This is the statutory validity check on the pensioner population, alongside event-driven cessations: spouse pension ceases on remarriage or death, child benefit ceases at age eighteen or death, and Occupational Pension Scheme pension ceases on the member's death, a spouse's death or remarriage, or a child reaching eighteen.
evidence: Confirmation-of-life procedure and prescribed form
Confirmation records by pensioner and date, and the confirmation cycle
Register of pensioners not confirmed and the suspension decisions taken
Reinstatement records after late confirmation
Death, remarriage and age-18 cessation records and linked payroll stops
Reconciliation of pensioner payroll to confirmation status
sop: Member or beneficiary in receipt of a pension provides confirmation that the member is alive, in a prescribed manner and form.
Public Service Pensions Fund may suspend payment of a pension to a member or beneficiary who fails to provide the confirmation.

controls.name: Medical-retirement and ill-health health data
controls.statement: A member retired on medical grounds is entitled to benefits (lump sum and pension with at least ten years of contributions, lump sum otherwise). Within two years of medical retirement and before normal retirement, a medical board may certify the pensioner fit to resume duty; the relevant authority may require resumption, withhold the pension if the requirement is not met, and recover any medical-retirement lump sum from later benefits. For an Occupational Pension Scheme member, the relevant authority may retire the member for ill health on the recommendation of a registered medical doctor, and the benefit claim must be accompanied by a medical report. These processes create and depend on health data about named members.
evidence: Medical board certificates of fitness to resume duty
Registered medical doctor's recommendation for ill-health retirement
Medical report accompanying the ill-health benefit claim
Relevant authority decision to retire on medical grounds or require resumption
Pension withholding and recovery of lump sum records (s.34(2)-(4))
Classification, access control and retention approach for medical documents held with the member file
sop: Relevant authority may, on the recommendation of a registered medical doctor, retire an Occupational Pension Scheme member who is incapable of performing duties due to ill health.
Claim for a benefit by a member retired for ill health is accompanied by a medical report.
Medical board certifies a pensioner fit to resume duty within two years of medical retirement before the relevant authority may require resumption.

controls.name: Beneficiary data: spouses, children, minors, dependants and polygamous marriages
controls.clause: s.2 (child, dependant, beneficiary), s.35, s.37, s.38, s.39, s.40, s.48, s.49, s.51
controls.statement: Death benefits flow to the estate, spouse, children and dependants. A child is a person under eighteen born in or out of marriage, a step-child, adopted child or posthumous child. Where a member leaves more than one spouse of a polygamous marriage, benefits are calculated as if there were one spouse and divided equally among the surviving spouses. A child's benefit ceases at eighteen or death and is recalculated whenever the number of children changes; the Board may redirect a child's pension if the recipient fails to maintain or abandons the child. Spouse pension ceases on remarriage or death. Beneficiary records therefore need relationship type, number of spouses, dates of birth and payee identity, including data about minors.
evidence: Beneficiary claim and relationship evidence (marriage, birth, adoption, posthumous birth)
Records identifying each spouse in a polygamous marriage and the equal-division calculation
Dates of birth for child beneficiaries and age-18 cessation triggers
Recalculation records when the number of children changes
Board decisions redirecting a child's pension and recovery from the original payee
Remarriage and death notifications for spouses
Controls restricting access to children's data and identity of the payee for a minor
sop: Where a member is survived by more than one spouse of a polygamous marriage, pension or other benefits are calculated as if there were only one surviving spouse and divided equally among the surviving spouses.
A benefit payable to a child is recalculated whenever there is a change in the number of children in respect of whom the benefit is payable.
Board may terminate a child's pension payment to a person who fails to maintain, deserts or abandons the child and pay it to a person the Board determines.

controls.name: Statutory confidentiality of information
controls.clause: First Schedule para 8, First Schedule para 9
controls.statement: A person must not publish or disclose any document, communication or information that came to the person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act, other than in the course of those duties, without the written consent given by or on behalf of the Board, or as otherwise permitted by written law. Onward publication of unlawfully disclosed information is also an offence. Disclosure authority for member, beneficiary, medical and payment data therefore rests with the Board.
evidence: Confidentiality policy or code and staff acknowledgements
Register of Board written consents to disclose, with recipient, purpose and date
Delegation instrument if consent is given on behalf of the Board
Data-sharing agreements or memoranda stating the written-law basis
Access control matrix and access logs for member and pensioner data
Incident log of unauthorised disclosures and responses
sop: Disclosure otherwise than in the course of duties requires the written consent of, or on behalf of, the Board, or must be otherwise permitted by written law.

controls.name: Identity and statement accuracy, and consequences of false representation
controls.statement: Where the Fund discovers that a member made a false representation of facts that affected the amount of benefits, the commencement or termination of a payment, or the identity of the person to whom payment is made, it may withhold, suspend, reduce or terminate the benefit. The same applies on conviction for misappropriation or false representation to obtain a pension. For a discharged or dismissed member, the relevant authority may set off losses sustained by Government against refunds under ss.32 and 46. A person aggrieved by a decision of the Fund may appeal to a court. Member identity, payee identity and declared facts are accountable data with a defined enforcement consequence.
evidence: Identity verification records at registration and at claim (document types accepted)
Payee identity verification for beneficiaries and minors' guardians
Case file for each suspected false representation with decision to withhold, suspend, reduce or terminate
Set-off decisions by the relevant authority against s.32 or s.46 refunds
Appeal records against decisions of the Fund
Data correction and amendment audit trail for identity attributes

controls.name: Benefit eligibility inputs: qualifying period, pensionable emoluments and fund credit
controls.clause: s.2 (qualifying period, pensionable emolument, pensionable service, fund credit), s.28, s.30, s.41, s.43, s.52, s.42
controls.statement: Entitlement and amount depend on stored data: contribution period against the qualifying period (ten years for the Public Service Pension Scheme, fifteen for the Occupational Pension Scheme), pensionable emolument (basic salary or wages for the Public Service Pension Scheme; gross for the Occupational Pension Scheme), pensionable service, and for the Occupational Pension Scheme the fund credit (contributions plus investment returns less expenses). Benefits, factors for commutation and rates are prescribed, and are subject to constitutional provisions on pension benefits. Inaccurate or incomplete contribution history therefore directly misstates benefits.
evidence: Member contribution statement with contribution period and pensionable emoluments by month
Fund credit statements for Occupational Pension Scheme members with returns and expense deductions
Benefit calculation worksheet or system output for a sample of claims
Prescribed benefit rates, commutation factors and formulae in force with version
Interest-rate computation basis (s.77(2)(g)) and the actuarial assessment behind it
Commutation elections by members before payment commences
sop: Member of the Public Service Pension Scheme entitled to a pension may, before payment commences, elect to receive a prescribed percentage of the pension as a lump sum, calculated by multiplying the pension to be commuted by a prescribed factor.

policies.title: Zambia Centre for Accountancy Studies Act
principles: Information that comes to a person's knowledge in the course of duties under the Act is confidential unless the Board consents in writing (s.17(1)).
Unauthorised disclosure and onward publication are criminal offences (s.17(2)-(3)).
The Board keeps proper books of account and other records and has its accounts audited annually by independent auditors (s.20).
The Board is accountable to the Minister through an annual report with audited statements, laid before the National Assembly (s.21).
The Centre collects and disseminates accountancy and financial information, and conducts surveys and research on accountancy manpower and training (s.8(2)(c),(e)).
management_intent: Keep information obtained in the course of ZCAS duties confidential unless the Board has consented in writing, with criminal liability for breach.
Keep proper accounting records, independently audited each year, and report to the Minister within six months of year end.
Support the public-benefit mandate of collecting and disseminating accountancy and financial information, including reports, journals and research.
Note: the Act is thin on data. It has no provisions on student or learner records, no retention periods and no data-protection safeguards for survey data.

controls.name: Confidentiality of information acquired in the course of duties without Board consent
controls.statement: No person shall, without the written consent given by or on behalf of the Board, publish or disclose to any person, otherwise than in the course of his duties, the contents of any document, communication or information whatsoever which relates to and has come to his knowledge in the course of his duties under the Act. A person who knowingly contravenes this commits an offence, liable to a fine not exceeding one thousand two hundred and fifty penalty units, imprisonment not exceeding three years, or both. A person holding information he knows was disclosed in breach who unlawfully publishes or communicates it commits an offence with the same maximum penalty. The blanket wording covers all ZCAS information, including any student, member, client or employee records.
evidence: Information classification or confidentiality policy showing that duty-acquired information defaults to confidential
Staff and contractor confidentiality undertakings or declarations
Register of Board consents to disclose, with date, recipient, content and approver
Delegation instrument naming who may give consent on behalf of the Board
Access-control matrix for student, finance and HR systems
Incident register for suspected unauthorised disclosure

controls.name: Proper books of account and records, audited annually
controls.statement: The Board shall cause to be kept proper books of account and other records relating to its accounts. The accounts shall be audited annually by independent auditors appointed by the Board with the approval of the Minister, and the auditors' fees shall be paid by the Board. The Act specifies no retention period or auditing standard for the records.
evidence: General ledger, chart of accounts and sub-ledgers of the Board
Records retention schedule for accounting records (the Act gives no period)
Auditor appointment letter and evidence of the Minister's approval
Signed audit opinion and audited financial statements for each financial year
Management letter and management responses

controls.name: Annual report with audited statements to the Minister
controls.statement: The financial year is the twelve months ending 31 December (s.19). As soon as practicable, and not later than six months after year end, the Board shall submit to the Minister a report on its activities, including its financial affairs, with an audited balance sheet, an audited statement of income and expenditure and any other information the Minister requires appended. The Minister shall lay the report before the National Assembly not later than seven days after the first sitting next after receipt. Unlike the ZRA Act, this Act does not require the report to be published.
evidence: Annual report as submitted to the Minister, with date of submission
Appended audited balance sheet and audited statement of income and expenditure
Correspondence showing any additional information the Minister requested
Evidence of tabling before the National Assembly
Annual reporting calendar showing the six-month deadline from 31 December
sop: Board submits the annual report to the Minister not later than six months after the financial year ends.
Report includes financial affairs, with the audited balance sheet and audited statement of income and expenditure appended, plus any other information the Minister requires.
Minister lays the report before the National Assembly not later than seven days after the first sitting after receipt.

controls.name: Collection and dissemination of accountancy and financial information, and related research
controls.statement: The Board shall collect and disseminate accountancy and financial information, including the publication of reports, journals and other documents and literature relating to the work of the Centre, and shall conduct surveys and research relating to accountancy manpower and training as may be required to develop effective national policies. The Act sets no standards for the provenance, ownership or accuracy of this information, and no safeguards for personal data gathered in surveys.
evidence: Catalogue or register of ZCAS publications, reports and journals
Survey and research datasets on accountancy manpower and training, with methodology notes
Data-source and provenance documentation for published statistics
Publication approval or editorial review records
Consent or anonymisation records for survey respondents

edges.note: Taxpayer data carries the statutory tax-secrecy basis as a Level 3+ floor.
Tax secrecy (ZRA Act s.21): record-level taxpayer data shared only under written authority; aggregates otherwise.
Statistical confidentiality (Statistics Act s.30) and respondent objection (s.19(2)(b)) govern release.
Identifiable returns and sole-entity particulars handled under s.30 confidentiality states.
Patient-record confidentiality (NHI Act s.34) sets a Level 3+ floor for claims data.
All member and claims health data treated as special-category by default; non-compensable privacy gate applies.
